task_description: The script calculates the maximum NDVI value from Landsat 8 imagery over a specified region between 2018 and 2019, groups it by elevation-based zones (1000, 1100, 1200 meters), and computes mean NDVI per zone using reduceRegion with grouped reduction. The output is a statistical summary of average NDVI values across different elevation thresholds within a buffered geometry.
task_name: Map maximum NDVI by elevation zones

task_description: The script classifies urban areas by applying spatially variable probability thresholds to a mosaic of infrastructure probability images from MapBiomas, using grid-specific thresholds. It clips the data per IBGE map sheets (cartas), applies a threshold to binarize the probability layer, and multiplies it with a previously classified urban map (SF1) to produce a refined urban classification (FS2). The output is a final binary urban/non-urban image for the specified year, combined across all map sheets, representing an improved urban extent map after thresholding and spatial filtering.
task_name: Classify urban areas using probability thresholds

task_description: The script computes mean annual greenup and dormancy dates from MODIS MCD12Q2 data for multiple five-year periods between 2001 and 2020, focusing on vegetation phenology dynamics across North America.

The script classifies land cover types using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data and multiple vegetation indices (NDVI, NDBI, NDWI, EVI, MSAVI2) within a specified region of interest. It trains a Random Forest classifier on training samples, validates the model using an independent validation dataset, evaluates accuracy through confusion matrices, and generates a classified land cover map with a visual legend.

The script analyzes vegetation dynamics in Córdoba, Argentina, by computing EVI, MSAVI, and MNDWI indices from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data across seven time periods between July 2020 and April 2021. It creates a multi-temporal mosaic to compare burned and unburned natural vegetation areas (from LULC 2017–2018) using fire-affected masks derived from historical fire data. The output includes masked composites for burned and unburned zones, enabling change detection and post-fire vegetation recovery assessment.

The script classifies the probability of urban infrastructure using Landsat 8 surface reflectance data, spectral indices, and machine learning applied to stratified sample points within specific grid cells (cartas) across Brazil for the year 2020. The output is a mosaic image asset named 'INFRAURBANA6-PROB-2020' representing urban probability.

The script calculates the total annual discharge in km³/year and mean runoff scaled by country area for a specific FAO GAUL country (code 37) using hydrological model output from the year 2000. It applies a country mask derived from a GeoTIFF to isolate discharge values and computes regional statistics via reduceRegion, while scaling runoff by the country's grid area.

The script classifies land cover types using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from June 15 to July 15, 2022, applying a cloud and shadow masking procedure, computing spectral indices (NDVI, NDBI, MNDWI, LSWI, EVI, BSI, REP), and training a Random Forest and SVM classifier on labeled ground control points. The output is a classified land cover map with accuracy assessment via confusion matrix and overall accuracy.

The script maps the distribution of Russian olive, an invasive woody species, in the Powder River Basin using NAIP imagery from 2017 and integrates topographic variables (elevation, mTPI, CHILI, landform diversity, physiographic diversity, and landforms) derived from USGS and CSP datasets to support habitat-level analysis.

The script identifies flooded areas by comparing Sentinel-1 VH backscatter before and after a flood event, applying focal median smoothing and thresholding on the difference to detect significant drops in radar signal associated with inundation.

The script classifies land cover types using surface reflectance and brightness temperature bands from Landsat 8 OLI/TIRS data, applying an SVM classifier trained on user-defined polygons to produce a land cover map for April 2022.

The script calculates the proportional area of each land cover class within user-defined points for each year from 2003 to 2019 using a land cover dataset. It outputs a flattened feature collection where each feature represents a point-year combination with proportions of 13 land cover classes.

The script classifies land cover into urban, wheat, and water classes using Sentinel-2 imagery and a support vector machine (SVM) classifier trained on user-defined regions of interest in Henan province between December 2018 and June 2019.

The script identifies flood inundation areas by comparing Sentinel-1 VV backscatter values before and after a flood event, applying a threshold (-11.00 dB) to classify water extent using median-filtered imagery.

The script performs land cover classification using a Random Forest classifier on satellite imagery, distinguishing between buildings, roads, trees, and fields. It trains the model using labeled polygon feature collections for each class, validates the results with independent point samples, and evaluates classification accuracy through error matrices, overall accuracy, kappa coefficient, and producer/consumer accuracy metrics. The output includes classified raster maps with visualizations and a legend for interpretation.

The script computes and analyzes multiple vegetation and water indices (NDVI, LSWI, MNDWI, NDWI, EVI, SAVI) from Landsat surface reflectance data between 2015 and 2022 over a defined area of interest. It generates median composites, extracts temporal statistics, identifies the least cloudy image, retrieves recent images, and enables interactive NDVI inspection at clicked locations.

The script classifies land cover types using a Random Forest classifier trained on spectral indices and Landsat bands, producing a classified map and calculating the area (in hectares) of each land cover class within a specified region. It also evaluates classification accuracy using a confusion matrix, overall accuracy, producer's and consumer's accuracy, and kappa coefficient.

The script identifies the least cloudy Landsat 8 TOA image from a collection filtered by WRS path 150, row 37, and date range January 1 to October 21, 2019. It outputs the full image collection, counts the number of images, computes the date range, calculates sun elevation statistics, retrieves the least cloudy image based on CLOUD_COVER, and lists the 10 most recent images sorted by acquisition date in descending order.

The script classifies land use and land cover (LULC) for the Chunati region in 2017 using a Landsat 8 surface reflectance mosaic. It trains a Random Forest classifier on labeled training samples (vegetation, agriculture, water, built area, bare land), performs classification, and evaluates accuracy using a confusion matrix and overall accuracy metric.

The script computes multiple spectral indices (MVI, EVI, MBI, NDBI, NDWI) and combines them with a DEM and Sentinel-like bands (B5, B6, B7) to perform image segmentation using the SNIC algorithm on a cloud-masked image. The output is a clustered image ('segments') representing spatially homogeneous regions based on multispectral and topographic properties.

The script compares median composites of Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery generated from three different cloud cover thresholds (10%, 20%, and 60%) over the same time period and region, applying two distinct cloud masking methods to assess data quality and clarity for land surface analysis.
task_name: Compare Sentinel-2 composites under varying cloud cover

task_description: The script analyzes Sentinel-1 GRD data to compute temporal VH backscatter statistics (5th and 95th percentiles) over Friendship County, China, between April and October 2021, generating a difference index (di) to monitor agricultural surface changes using radar remote sensing.

The script performs pan-sharpening on a Landsat 8 TOA reflectance image by fusing its visible bands (B4, B3, B2) with the panchromatic band (B8) using multiple algorithms (Brovey, Simple Mean, HPFA, IHS, PCA, Gram-Schmidt), then evaluates the quality of the Gram-Schmidt output against the original multispectral image using Q, RASE, and MSE metrics.

The script corrects temporal inconsistencies and small noisy patches (less than 1 ha) in MapBiomas Collection 3.1 land cover classifications by applying a spatiotemporal filtering algorithm that uses class transitions between consecutive years, focusing on aggregation of native vegetation and agriculture/pasture classes. The output is a corrected multi-temporal land cover dataset from 1985 to 2017, with reduced false transitions due to classification artifacts.

The script identifies the first day of year with no snow cover for each year from 2000 to 2022 using MODIS NDSI Snow Cover data, computes annual images of this phenological event, and analyzes temporal changes through differencing and regional mean trends within a user-defined area of interest.
task_name: Map first day of no snow cover

task_description: The script classifies land cover types including agriculture, forest, urban areas, wetlands, and water bodies using Sentinel-2 optical imagery and Sentinel-1 SAR data over a region in Iran. It trains an SVM classifier on multi-temporal optical and radar datasets and produces a classified map based on user-defined training samples.
task_name: Classify land cover using optical and SAR data

task_description: The script extracts cloud and shadow confidence bits from the Landsat 8 BQA band, identifies pixels with high confidence cloud or shadow, and creates a mask to remove them from the TOA reflectance image.

The script classifies land use types using Landsat 8 surface reflectance data from May 24 to June 24, 2020, applying an SVM (libsvm) classifier on labeled training samples for six classes: Agriculture, Baierland, Rangeland, Residential, Riverbed, and Waterbodies. It outputs a classified land use map and evaluates accuracy using a test dataset, printing the error matrix and overall accuracy.

The script performs gap-filling on a Landsat 7 image (with SLC-off artifacts) using regression-based neighborhood modeling with data from Landsat 5 and Landsat 8. It computes a percentile composite, applies radiometric normalization via linear regression and local statistics, and fills masked areas using spatially overlapping observations from different sensors. The final output is a mosaic of two filled versions (from Landsat 5 and Landsat 8) to improve coverage and quality.
task_name: Gap-fill missing pixels in Landsat 7 imagery

task_description: The script classifies land cover into six classes (Urban, Water, Bare, Cropland, Oil Palm, Rubber) using a Random Forest classifier trained on a multi-sensor composite of Landsat 8, Sentinel-1, and Sentinel-2 data from 2019. The output is a classified land cover map and accuracy assessment including confusion matrix, overall accuracy, producer's and user's accuracy, and area calculation per class within the AOI.

The script classifies land cover types using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from 2016, applying a CART classifier trained on user-defined regions of interest (Settlement, Water, Lake, Grassland, Forest, Farmland, Bareland) with specific spectral bands. The output is a classified raster map clipped to the ROI.

The script classifies land cover types including mangrove, oil palm, developed areas, aquaculture, tropical forest, barren land, cultivated crops, and water using Radarsat-2 HH and HV polarizations and derived indices (ratio and difference) within a defined study area in Sumatra. The output is a classified map and accuracy assessment based on training samples.
task_name: Classify mangrove and land cover types

task_description: The script identifies flood-affected water areas by comparing NDWI with NDVI and NDSI using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data, applying cloud masking and thresholding to isolate water bodies during a specific time period.

The script classifies land cover types using a CART classifier trained on sampled regions from a mean Landsat 5 TOA reflectance image, producing a classified map with 9 classes (e.g., forest, agriculture, water) and evaluating accuracy through an error matrix, kappa index, and user/producer accuracies. It also computes the area per class in hectares within the study region.

The script identifies urbanized areas by calculating the Normalized Difference Built-up Index (NDBI) from a cloud-free Landsat 8 image collected in March 2020 over a location at coordinates (68, 27), using SWIR and NIR bands.

The script analyzes vegetation dynamics using multiple spectral indices (NDVI, LSWI, MNDWI, NDWI, EVI, SAVI) derived from Landsat surface reflectance data between 1984 and 2021 over a defined study area. It generates a median composite image, identifies the least cloudy image, and enables interactive querying of mean NDVI values at clicked locations.

The script classifies land cover in Hinesburg, VT using NAIP imagery from 2014, computing NDVI and NDWI to enhance classification, and applies a Random Forest model trained on labeled regions, followed by shadow removal using focal filtering.

The script calculates the inverse barometer (IB) effect by masking ERA5 monthly mean sea level pressure data over water bodies, computing global mean pressure anomalies, and converting the deviations into millimeter-scale sea surface height changes using a physical scaling factor. The output includes two visualizations: one of raw sea-level pressure and another of the derived IB signal in mm.

The script calculates the median chlorophyll concentration from a JASMES SGLI ocean color image within a 2300-meter buffer around a point off the coast of Japan on August 13, 2019, and also computes the total masked pixel area in square meters to assess data coverage.

The script identifies flood inundation areas by comparing Sentinel-1 VV backscatter values before and after a flood event in May 2020, applying a threshold-based classification on median-filtered imagery to detect water extent changes.

The script computes a cloud score for Sentinel-2 images by analyzing reflectance in visible, near-infrared, and shortwave infrared bands, then creates a mosaic based on minimum cloudiness. It outputs two visualizations: one based on image acquisition date and another based on cloud score quality.

The script analyzes MODIS NDSI Snow Cover data from 2018 to identify days when snow was absent for at least 5-day intervals, generating a time-series of masked images indicating no-snow conditions per day-of-year, used to map ephemeral and constant snow cover patterns over the annual cycle.

The script detects and maps burned areas by computing the difference in Normalized Burn Ratio (dNBR) from Sentinel-2 imagery before and after a fire event, and compares the results with MODIS burned area products from NASA and ESA.

The script calculates spatial anomalies of methane column volume mixing ratio relative to the regional mean in August 2020, then converts these differences into a relative volumetric measure using methane and dry air density ratios at standard temperature (298K), focusing on the shellMart region.

The script classifies land cover types using a random forest classifier trained on spectral indices and surface reflectance bands derived from a median composite of Landsat 5, 7, and 8 imagery between 2017 and 2019. The classification is based on a set of 13 spectral variables including NDVI, NBR, SAVI, EVI, and others, with training data from labeled regions (mergedTable_total).

The script classifies land cover types using a Random Forest classifier trained on labeled sample points from Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery. The output is a classified image map where each pixel is assigned a land cover class based on spectral signatures.

The script calculates the mean precipitation for January using WorldClim monthly climate data, clips it to the provinces of Belgium, and performs a zonal statistics operation to compute the sum of precipitation values within each provincial boundary, resulting in a feature collection with precipitation sums per province.

The script detects changes in land surface conditions by analyzing temporal differences in VV polarization backscatter from Sentinel-1 SAR imagery before and after a specific date range, applying refined Lee filtering to reduce speckle noise and improve feature interpretation.

The script computes multiple vegetation and water indices (NDVI, LSWI, MNDWI, NDWI, EVI, SAVI) from Landsat surface reflectance data between 1984 and 2000 over a user-defined area. It generates a median composite, identifies the least cloudy image, extracts temporal statistics, and enables interactive NDVI inspection at clicked locations on the map.

The script classifies cropland into six categories using a Random Forest classifier trained on Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data and the Cropland Data Layer (CDL) 2016 as reference labels. It evaluates training and validation accuracy, and analyzes classifier performance across varying numbers of trees.

The script estimates surface soil moisture (SSM) using Sentinel-1 VV backscatter time series by computing dry and wet reference surfaces from percentile reductions, calculating sensitivity, and applying speckle filtering with the Refined Lee algorithm. It outputs a filtered ImageCollection of VV-polarized radar observations over the study area for the period March–October 2019, intended for SSM retrieval and monitoring.

The script extracts agricultural cropland areas within Pakistan by clipping the GFSAD1000 cropland dataset to the national boundary of Pakistan, using administrative boundaries and subnational boundaries for spatial filtering. The output is a clipped feature collection representing cropland extent in Pakistan.

The script retrieves GLAD deforestation alerts within a specific map grid (SC-24-V-D) in the Caatinga biome between January 1, 2018, and January 10, 2018, and also fetches Planet satellite imagery from January 1 to March 31, 2018, for visual validation or analysis. The primary output is a filtered collection of early warning deforestation detections and corresponding high-resolution imagery.

The script calculates the median NDVI value for the Batken administrative region in Kyrgyzstan during September 2019 using MODIS MOD13Q1 data, then prints the result as a dictionary from a reduceRegion operation. Only Batken is used in the analysis despite other regions being defined.

The script downloads all spectral bands (B1 to B12, including B8A, B9, B10, B11, B12) from Sentinel-2 Surface Reflectance data over a specified geometry for the year 2019, sorted by acquisition time, and generates direct download URLs for each image in the collection.

The script calculates NDVI anomalies for cropland areas by comparing MODIS MYD13A1 NDVI values from 2011–2015 against a baseline mean (2001–2005), then masks the summed anomaly with cropland areas using the USGS GFSAD1000 layer, resulting in a spatial map of cumulative NDVI deviation over agricultural regions.

The script classifies land cover into five classes—Water, Shrub, Forest, Agriculture, and Urban—using Sentinel-2 imagery and a Random Forest classifier. It generates a classified map, computes accuracy metrics (confusion matrix, overall accuracy, Kappa), and calculates area statistics per class in hectares and percentage within a region of interest.

The script classifies water and land areas using Radarsat-2 HH and HV polarization bands, along with derived ratio and difference indices, trained via a Random Forest classifier. It outputs a classified water mask, validation accuracy metrics, and computes the area per class within the study region.

The script generates a median composite of Sentinel-2 surface reflectance images from August 2020, masked for clouds and cirrus using the QA60 band, filtered by region and low cloud cover, and scaled by dividing by 10,000.

The script filters MODIS MOD13Q1 NDVI data for January 2019 using the DetailedQA bitmask to remove pixels affected by shadow, snow/ice, clouds, and non-low aerosol conditions, producing a quality-masked NDVI time series.

The script classifies land cover into three classes—water, crops, and forests—using spectral indices derived from Landsat 8 Surface Reflectance data between 2020 and 2021. It computes multiple vegetation and water indices (NDVI, GNDVI, NDSI, NDBaI, NDWI, SAVI, EVI, GLI), applies cloud masking, and generates a composite with percentile, mean, and standard deviation reductions for use in classification modeling.

The script classifies land cover types using Sentinel-2A satellite imagery by training a CART classifier on labeled regions (water, canopy, shrubs, bareland, agriculture). It generates a classified land use/land cover map and evaluates accuracy using a confusion matrix from a held-out test set.

The script calculates monthly MODIS NDVI anomalies by comparing each month's mean NDVI to the long-term monthly average, producing a time series of deviation images and plotting the anomaly values over time at a specific point.

The script performs unsupervised land cover classification using K-means clustering on Landsat 7 TOA reflectance data from 2013, compares single-band (NIR, blue) versus multispectral inputs, evaluates cluster stability under varying parameters, and attempts to align classified clusters with NLCD 2011 land cover labels for a region in Wisconsin.

The script creates a timelapse video of land surface changes using red, green, and blue bands from Landsat 5 and Landsat 7 surface reflectance data over a specific WRS path and row between 1991 and 2019, focusing on visual change detection in a defined region.

The script filters Sentinel-2 Level-1C imagery over Oslob between July and December 2017, masks clouds and cirrus using the QA60 band, removes images with more than 20% cloud cover, and returns a collection of surface reflectance values scaled by dividing by 10,000.

The script identifies surface water extent in the Kadapa region using Sentinel-2 imagery from early 2020 by computing NDWI (Normalized Difference Water Index) and applying a threshold (0.2) to classify water pixels, then calculates the total water area within the region of interest.

The script performs image segmentation using the SNIC (Simple Non-Iterative Clustering) algorithm on a principal components image of the Gran Chaco region, clipped to the WWF-defined boundary, to generate spatially contiguous clusters that represent homogeneous land cover units based on spectral characteristics.

The script generates a cloud-masked median top-of-atmosphere (TOA) reflectance composite from Landsat 8 imagery for Shandong Province, China, in 2019, using the BQA band for pixel quality filtering and clipping to a defined geometry. The output is a multispectral image suitable for visual interpretation or further land surface analysis.

The script classifies land cover into three classes—urban, vegetation, and water—using a median composite of Sentinel-2 imagery from 2016. It trains a Random Forest classifier on labeled sample regions, applies the model to classify the entire image, and evaluates accuracy using a validation dataset. The output is a classified land cover map and accuracy assessment.

The script detects changes in flood extent by comparing pre-flood and post-flood Sentinel-1 SAR imagery over Ernakulam district, using VH polarization and applying the Refined Lee speckle filter to improve image quality before and after the flood event.

The script identifies surface water extent using the Modified Normalized Difference Water Index (MNDWI) derived from the 30th percentile composite of Landsat 8 Top of Atmosphere (TOA) reflectance data over a specified area and time period. It compares results with and without cloud masking to assess the impact of cloud contamination on water detection accuracy.
task_name: Identify surface water extent with cloud masking

task_description: The script identifies water bodies by applying terrain-corrected slope correction and Perona-Malik diffusion filtering to Sentinel-1 GRD imagery, followed by Otsu thresholding on the VV band using edge-constrained histogram analysis.

The script classifies land cover into 3-class (Anthropogenic, Intensive, Shifting Agriculture) and 5-class (Anthropogenic, Logging, Oil Palm, Shifting Agriculture, Cocoa) systems using Sentinel-2 spectral indices, built-up areas from GHSL, and plantation data, with Random Forest classification (300 trees) trained on sampled points and validated using error matrices.

The script classifies land cover types using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data by training a CART classifier on labeled regions (Water, Urban, Forest, CropLand, ExposedSurface) and applying it to generate a classified land cover map for the region of interest.

The script filters the GEDI02_A dataset to retain only high-quality waveform observations from power beams, selecting valid shots based on quality and degradation flags, then extracts canopy height metrics such as rh98 for analysis.
task_name: Filter high-quality GEDI canopy height data

task_description: The script classifies land cover types using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data by training a Random Forest classifier on labeled sample points, then evaluates classification accuracy with a confusion matrix and kappa statistic.

The script classifies land cover types using a Random Forest classifier trained on Landsat 7 surface reflectance data. Training samples are derived from manually labeled feature collections for seven classes: mangrove, palm oil (labeled as 'developed' but contextually likely misnamed), developed areas, aquaculture, tropical forest, barren, and cultivated crops. The classification is applied to a median composite image from 2015, and the output includes a classified map and area calculations per class in square meters.

The script analyzes MODIS NDSI Snow Cover data to identify the first day of year without snow (FDWoS) and the first day of return snow (FDRS) annually, computes winter duration between consecutive years, and evaluates persistent snow cover dynamics in a specified region from 2011 to 2016.
task_name: Track first snow-free and snow-return days

task_description: The script classifies land use and land cover types using a supervised classification (CART) on a median composite of Landsat 5 TOA reflectance imagery. Training data includes classes such as Mangrove, water, homestead, agriculture, mudflat, sand, sp, and Extra. The output is a classified land cover map and its accuracy assessment via confusion matrix and validation accuracy.

The script processes TerraClimate data to extract and clip climate-related variables for the state of Wisconsin between 2002 and 2013, focusing on regional terrestrial hydrosphere and climate indicators.

The script identifies the largest cutblock (forest clearing) area that occurred after 2017 by filtering and sorting cutblocks based on 'lossyear' and 'Shape_Area', then retrieves the first image from Sentinel-2 collection before and after specific dates relative to the loss year for comparison.

The script classifies land cover types (urban, water, forest, farm) using Sentinel-2 imagery by training a CART classifier on median-composited bands and generating a classified map based on spectral signatures.
The script calculates the mean precipitation for the month of September from 2000 to 2019 using CHIRPS daily rainfall data, extracting regional averages over a user-defined area of interest (AOI).

The script combines MODIS LCCS land use and hydrology layers to prioritize cropland, herbaceous wetlands, and woody wetlands in the final land cover classification for the year 2019, producing a single combined land cover image.

The script classifies land cover into three or five anthropogenic classes (Anthropogenic, Intensive Agriculture, Shifting Agriculture, Oil Palm, Cocoa) using a Random Forest classifier trained on spectral indices and ancillary datasets from satellite imagery and GHSL layers. It evaluates classification accuracy and computes the area per class within a defined region.

The script classifies land cover types using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery over a specific region in Iran, applying a CART classifier trained on user-defined feature collections representing water, wetland vegetation (three classes), forest, agriculture, and urban areas. The output is a classified image map with distinct land cover categories.

The script calculates NDVI from NAIP imagery over the redwoods region, then computes the standard deviation of NDVI in a circular neighborhood to analyze textural variation in vegetation health and structure for the year 2012.

The script classifies land cover types using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data by computing vegetation indices (NDVI, RVI, DVI, EVI, SAVI), training a Random Forest classifier on labeled regions within an AOI, and applying the model to classify the entire area. It also validates the classification accuracy using a held-out test set and computes error metrics including kappa coefficient.

The script calculates the mean NDSI-based snow cover from MODIS Aqua data between January 1, 2019, and April 15, 2019, producing a single composite image representing average snow coverage over the period.

The script performs pan-sharpening on a Landsat 8 TOA reflectance image by fusing the high-resolution panchromatic band (B8) with the RGB bands (B4, B3, B2) through HSV transformation, resulting in a higher spatial resolution color image.
task_name: Sharpen multispectral image using panchromatic band

task_description: The script computes the median surface reflectance from Sentinel-2A SR data, masked for clouds and limited to less than 90% cloud coverage, over a specified boundary between October 2018 and December 2019.

The script performs a supervised land cover classification for the year 2010 using Landsat 7 surface reflectance data and a Random Forest classifier trained on manually labeled feature collections. The output is a classified raster map of 15 land cover classes, including water, forests, agricultural areas, urban zones, and bare soil, clipped to the study area (c1), with accuracy assessment metrics and visualizations.

The script computes and compares median NDVI and BSI vegetation and bare soil indices from Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8 surface reflectance data over a specified region and time period, applying cloud masking and generating visualizations for gap-filled composites. It outputs true-color and index-based layered maps for both sensors, enabling comparative analysis of vegetation and land surface conditions.
task_name: Analyze Sentinel and Landsat NDVI BSI

task_description: The script calculates NDVI and NDWI indices from Sentinel-2 imagery over San Francisco International Airport area to analyze vegetation health and surface water presence using near-infrared and shortwave infrared bands.

The script estimates Land Surface Temperature (LST) using top-of-atmosphere brightness temperature from Band 10 and emissivity derived from NDVI, applying a radiative transfer model with logarithmic correction for atmospheric effects. Outputs include NDVI, fractional vegetation cover (FV), emissivity (EMM), and LST layers.

The script creates a median composite image from Sentinel-2A/B Surface Reflectance data, masked for clouds and cirrus using the QA60 band, for clear-sky surface analysis over a specified region and time period.

The script calculates weekly mean Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD) at 0.47 µm from MODIS data over California between May 1 and December 31, 2000, samples the values within California's boundary, and outputs a feature collection with pixel-level AOD measurements tagged with year and day of year.

The script classifies land use and land cover (LULC) for the Chunati region and surrounding areas using a Landsat 7 surface reflectance mosaic from November 2012. It trains a Random Forest classifier on labeled training samples (vegetation, agriculture, water, built area, bare land), performs classification into five classes, and evaluates accuracy using a confusion matrix and overall accuracy metric derived from a 70-30 training-validation split.

The script calculates long-term monthly mean and standard deviation of NDVI, then computes mean-centered NDVI anomalies for each month and year. It outputs a time series of NDVI, monthly mean and standard deviation values over regions, and an image collection of NDVI anomaly maps by month and year.

The script classifies land cover into five classes—Water, Shrub, Forest, Agriculture, and Urban—using Sentinel-2 imagery from July 2021. It applies a Random Forest classifier trained on user-defined regions, performs cloud masking, and computes post-classification area statistics with accuracy assessment via confusion matrices. The output includes a classified map, legend, and a table showing area (ha) and percentage per class within the region of interest.

The script creates a cloud-filtered, true-color composite image from Sentinel-2 data by mosaicking and clipping images collected between December 15, 2021, and January 29, 2022, over a specified region, using the TCI_R, TCI_G, and TCI_B bands for visual interpretation.

The script classifies land cover types using supervised machine learning (CART and Random Forest) on Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data from January to May 2020 over Misiones, applying a cloud-masked composite and validating accuracy with ground truth samples. Final outputs include a classified land cover map, accuracy assessment metrics (confusion matrix, overall accuracy, kappa), and area estimation per class in hectares.

The script generates a time-series summary (timescan) of Sentinel-1 SAR data over Balochistan, focusing on the minimum and standard deviation of VH polarization to characterize surface structural properties and temporal variability, with terrain-flattened gamma0 calibration and spatial filtering applied.
task_name: Analyze VH backscatter minimum and variability

task_description: The script detects changes in surface water extent caused by flooding using pre- and post-event Sentinel-1 SAR imagery, generating mosaicked VV and VH polarization images for visual comparison before and after the flood event.

The script classifies land cover into four classes (agua, bosque, agricultura, descubierta) using a Random Forest classifier applied to median Sentinel-2 imagery from May to September 2017. It computes classification accuracy using validation samples and estimates the area (in km²) per class within a defined region.

The script processes Landsat 5 and Landsat 8 surface reflectance data from 1990 to 2021, applying a cloud masking function to improve data quality, and filters images by region and date. It prepares the collections for land cover analysis or change detection over time by organizing imagery into yearly composites through setting a 'year' property, enabling temporal comparison of land surface conditions.

The script calculates the area of Punjab province in Pakistan by counting pixels in a binary image clipped to the administrative boundary, using a specified scale and coordinate reference system, then converts the pixel count to square kilometers.

The script classifies land cover types such as permanent water, flooded vegetation, urban areas, and low vegetation by applying a CART classifier on Sentinel-1 VV and VH backscatter bands before and after a flood event, using filtered mosaic images for improved accuracy.
task_name: Classify land cover using SAR imagery

task_description: The script classifies forest degradation and deforestation in a specific grid (SH-21-Z-B) using spectral mixture analysis (SMA), NDFI, and decision tree rules applied to Landsat surface reflectance data from 2008 to 2015. Outputs include classified maps of forest, degradation, deforestation, water, and cloud-masked areas.

The script identifies and masks Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery to isolate pasture land cover in Goiás, Brazil, using MapBiomas Collection 7 land classification for 2021, producing a cloud-corrected composite focused on pasture regions.

The script identifies crop cultivation areas in Kerala, India, by analyzing seasonal NDVI patterns from Landsat 8 TOA data between 2013 and 2019. It computes monthly mean NDVI, classifies vegetation intensity between 0.3 and 0.7, and aggregates results into three seasonal periods (P1: Sep–Dec, P2: Jan–Apr, P3: May–Aug), combining them into a three-band composite (PFINAL) to map cropping intensity and seasonality. Additionally, it enables interactive NDVI and rainfall time series extraction at clicked locations using Sentinel-2 and CHIRPS data.

The script classifies land cover types using a supervised Random Forest classifier on Landsat 7 surface reflectance data from 2015, training on user-defined feature collections for mangrove, palm oil, developed areas, aquaculture, tropical forest, barren land, and cultivated crops within a study area in Sumatra, Indonesia, and outputs a classified map with accuracy assessment and area calculations per class.

The script classifies land cover in Balochistan for the year 2020 using a Random Forest classifier trained on NDVI, topographic (slope, DEM), SAR (Sentinel-1 VV/VH), NDBI, texture, and seasonal vegetation data. It outputs a classified land cover map with 18 classes, applies post-processing via focal mode filtering, and evaluates model accuracy through confusion matrix metrics and variable importance.
task_name: Classify land cover using Random Forest

task_description: The script classifies land cover types using Landsat 5 TOA reflectance data, applying a CART classifier on selected bands (B5, B4, B3), with training and validation samples from user-defined regions. It outputs a classified land cover map, accuracy assessments (confusion matrix, overall accuracy, kappa, user's and producer's accuracy), and computes the area (in hectares) per land cover class within a specified region.

The script identifies and maps surface water extent for April and May 2019 using Sentinel-1 VV backscatter data, applying a threshold of -18.5 dB to classify water pixels, computes the total water area in square kilometers, and compares flooding conditions between two dates in 2018 using masked imagery.

The script identifies sea ice and open water zones in the Arctic using Sentinel-1 HH/HV backscatter intensity, applying a threshold on smoothed HH band values (below -20 dB), then converts the resulting binary raster into vector polygons to compute lead (open water) area percentage within a region of interest.

The script fills missing pixels in a Landsat 7 image caused by SLC-off errors using a spatio-temporal regression gap-filling method based on a one-year pre- and post-median composite from the same sensor.
task_name: Fill Landsat 7 gaps with temporal composites

task_description: The script calculates NDVI using Landsat 8 surface reflectance data from January 2020 to January 2021, generating a median composite image of the first two scenes.

The script processes Landsat 8 and Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data to generate natural color composites, NDVI, and NDMI for the Riau region between 2015 and 2022, focusing on vegetation and land surface moisture analysis using the least cloudy scenes.
task_name: Analyze vegetation and moisture from satellite imagery

task_description: The script performs mathematical transformations on a list of integers from 0 to 9, first computing their squares, then filtering odd numbers by a custom modulus-based function, and finally recomputing the squares of the filtered odd numbers. It also demonstrates iterative Fibonacci sequence generation using Earth Engine's list iteration methods. Additionally, it splits a Landsat 8 image collection based on solar elevation, processes images below 40 degrees by multiplying by 2, and merges them back with unprocessed images above 40 degrees.

The script defines training polygons for land cover classes (vegetation types and water) within a specific region and processes Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery to support classification. It filters images by date and cloud cover, clips them to the study area, and prepares them for land cover analysis based on manually labeled features.

The script analyzes Sentinel-1 GRD SAR imagery to compute spectral statistics (HH, HV, incidence angle) and contrast ratios between target areas and surrounding buffer zones (100m, 200m, and background regions). It also integrates MODIS Aqua and Terra ocean color products (chlorophyll-a, particulate organic carbon, sea surface temperature, remote sensing reflectance) co-located in time and space with the SAR acquisition for multi-sensor marine environmental analysis.

The script identifies mangrove areas in Java, Indonesia for the year 2013 by applying a Modified Vegetation Index (MVI) thresholding technique on a Landsat 7 surface reflectance composite, masked by elevation and cloud-corrected data.

The script classifies land cover types using Sentinel-2 imagery and a Random Forest classifier trained on user-defined regions of interest, including water, forest, urban, grass, bare soil, river, and burned soil. It generates a classified land cover map clipped to the VdeA boundary.

The script detects and classifies cyanobacteria blooms in surface water using the Normalized Difference Chlorophyll Index (NDCI) derived from atmospherically corrected Sentinel-2 imagery. It applies a multi-step classification to identify bloom severity levels (0–3) and masks non-water pixels. The output is a daily composite image collection over the Patos Lagoon region, with bands including reflectance means, NDCI mean, and classified NDCI, used for mapping and monitoring algal bloom dynamics.
The script calculates the cumulative annual precipitation from CHIRPS daily data for the year 2018 and computes the mean value over a specified geometry, printing it to the console.

The script performs supervised land cover classification using a Random Forest classifier trained on manually labeled feature collections representing buildings, green spaces, roads, undeveloped areas, paths, dumps, and dirty roads. The output is a classified image map of urban land cover types (e.g., buildings, roads, green areas) derived from satellite imagery with validation accuracy assessment.

The script classifies anthropogenic land cover into 3 or 5 classes (Anthropogenic, Intensive, Shifting Agriculture, Oil Palm, Cocoa) using a Random Forest classifier trained on spectral indices (EVI, NDVI, BSI, NDMI, NDWI, MIR, SAVI) and auxiliary layers (GHSL built-up, urbanization, oil palm plantations) at 30m resolution. Outputs include classified maps, accuracy assessment via validation points, and area calculation in hectares per class.

The script classifies land cover types using Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data and a Random Forest and CART classifier. Training and testing samples are defined for seven classes (e.g., forest, agriculture, wetland, water, etc.), and the output includes classified land cover maps, accuracy assessments via confusion matrix, user/producer accuracy, and kappa index.

The script classifies land cover types using Sentinel-1 GRD SAR imagery with VH polarization, applying a Lee filter and Random Forest classification on filtered backscatter values. The output includes an original image, a Lee-filtered image, a classified land cover map, and an MNF-transformed image for feature enhancement.

The script calculates the area of forest loss within the home range of PH, classified by anthropogenic drivers (anthropogenic, subsistence agriculture, intensive agriculture) using a 3-class land cover classification map at 30m and 100m spatial resolutions. It outputs the total area in square meters and square kilometers for each class and the total affected area.

The script identifies surface water areas by comparing NDWI with NDVI and NDSI using Sentinel-2 data from October 2021, applying cloud masking and generating a masked composite where water is present based on spectral indices.

The script extracts a comprehensive set of surface reflectance values, vegetation indices, and auxiliary variables (e.g., built-up areas, plantations, urbanization) from Sentinel-2-like imagery at training points to support land cover classification modeling. Outputs are CSV files containing mean-reduced spectral and index values across four segmented band groups.
task_name: Extract spectral indices for land classification

task_description: The script calculates the mean Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) for Santa Clara County using Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data from March to May 2014, masks clouds using simple cloud scoring, and outputs the spatially averaged NDVI value over the county boundary.
task_name: Analyze spring NDVI in Santa Clara

task_description: The script calculates annual total precipitation from TerraClimate data (1990–2020) for the Chaco region, extracts mean values at point locations, and computes long-term average monthly mean temperature by deriving it from minimum and maximum temperatures. Outputs include a CSV file of precipitation values per point and temperature statistics, used for climate analysis in dryland ecosystems.
task_name: Extract annual precipitation and mean temperature

task_description: The script classifies land cover into forest formation, non-forest natural, water bodies, and other classes using spectral unmixing, NDFI, and a decision tree applied to Landsat 8 surface reflectance data from 2015. The output includes a classified image and a composite with derived indices and terrain layers.

The script identifies mangrove forests using a Modified Vegetation Index (MVI) derived from Landsat 8 surface reflectance data, applying thresholds and spatial clustering to classify and map mangrove extent in Banten, Indonesia for 2014.
The script creates a mosaic of NAIP aerial imagery for the year 2016 within a specified geographic region (pdx), resulting in a single composite image from multiple DOQQ images.

The script processes Sentinel-2 imagery from 2016 to 2019 over the Great Lakes region, filtered by a user-defined basin boundary, to analyze and map shoreline positions using a pre-existing shoreline classification and delineation feature collection. The output is likely a spatial representation of classified shorelines or changes in shoreline extent.

The script analyzes the impact of a hurricane on vegetation by comparing NDVI values from Sentinel-2 imagery before and after the event in 2016, 2017, and 2018. It computes median composites for pre- and post-hurricane periods, calculates NDVI, clips results to a region (PR), and extracts mean NDVI values for specific sub-regions (e.g., Southeast, North) at varying distances from the hurricane path. The outputs include visualizations of RGB and NDVI layers and a feature collection storing NDVI means and distances to the hurricane path for spatial comparison.
task_name: Assess vegetation impact before after hurricane

task_description: The script performs landscape segmentation by applying the LandTrendr algorithm on Landsat time series data from 1999 to 2021, using multiple spectral indices (NBR, B5, TCB, TCG, TCW) to detect change patterns. It standardizes fitted annual values, masks disturbance polygons, and applies SNIC (Simple Non-Iterative Clustering) superpixel segmentation to generate homogeneous landscape patches based on temporal spectral trajectories.
task_name: Segment landscape using LandTrendr time series

task_description: The script creates a greenest pixel composite by calculating NDVI from Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data and selecting the highest NDVI values over time, resulting in a cloud-minimized image representing peak vegetation greenness.

The script filters the Sentinel-2 surface reflectance image collection for images with less than 30% cloud cover, within a specific date range (2019-01-01 to 2020-01-01), and overlapping a point of interest near 103.655°E, 14.724°N. It outputs the count of images that meet these criteria.
The script selects the least cloudy Landsat 7 Top of Atmosphere (TOA) reflectance image from the year 2000 within the specified region (MTElgon), sorted by cloud cover in ascending order.

The script converts Sentinel-1 GRD backscatter from sigma0 to gamma0 using local incidence angle correction for two monthly composites (November 2015 and January 2016), enabling terrain-normalized analysis of surface reflectivity changes over time in a specified region.

The script identifies surface water extent using the 30th percentile composite of Landsat 8 OLI data and MNDWI thresholding, then masks water bodies located above a HAND threshold of 50 meters to exclude upland false positives, resulting in a refined surface water map for the area of interest.
task_name: Map surface water with HAND masking

task_description: The script calculates land cover transitions between 1985 and 2021 using MapBiomas Pampa Collection 2 classification data, computing area (in hectares) of change classes within seven regional territories. It outputs per-region feature collections with before/after land cover classes and corresponding areas.

The script processes Landsat 8 surface reflectance data from May to September 2021, masking clouds and cloud shadows, then computes multiple spectral vegetation and land surface indices (NDVI, NBR, NDMI, MNDWI, SR, EVI, MSAVI, GCVI, BI) to assess vegetation condition and land characteristics over a defined region in the eastern United States.

The script identifies active fire areas in Tunisia using thermal infrared data from the FIRMS dataset between August 1 and August 30, 2012. It calculates the total area (in km²) of active fires within the country boundary and overlays fire detections on buffered site locations to identify which sites are affected by fires.

The script identifies and classifies single-season crop areas by combining Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 data, using NDVI thresholding, temporal filtering based on a specific growth season (day of year 150–191), and a CART classifier trained on labeled regions. The output is a classified map showing crop vs. non-crop areas within the defined season.

The script identifies and maps the age of secondary forests in Brazil by analyzing annual land cover transitions from 1985 to 2021 using MapBiomas Collection 7 data, focusing on forest regeneration after anthropogenic disturbances while excluding water bodies.

The script classifies forest degradation and deforestation in the SH-21-Z-B grid using spectral mixture analysis (SMA), NDFI, and a decision tree applied to Landsat data from 2008 to 2015. Outputs include classified maps of forest, degradation, and deforestation, along with SMA fractions, NDFI, and reflectance mosaics for each year.

The script masks MODIS GPP (Npp) data for areas below 3000 meters elevation using SRTM digital elevation data, focusing on the year 2014. The output is a masked image of net primary productivity where only pixels with elevation less than 3000 meters are retained.

The script identifies permanent and temporary surface water bodies using MNDWI derived from Landsat percentile composites, applying cloud masking and HAND terrain filtering to improve accuracy over a specified time period.
task_name: Map permanent and temporary water bodies

task_description: The script identifies surface water extent in the AOI using Landsat 8 pixel quality bands and aerosol data to mask clouds and generate a median composite, then extracts water pixels using the pixel_qa band's water bit.

The script estimates above-ground biomass (AGB) in Diamir District, Pakistan, using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data and a Random Forest regression model trained on field AGB samples. The output is a classified AGB map validated against independent validation points with an R² score.

The script classifies land cover types using a Random Forest classifier trained on a percentile-composited Landsat 8 TOA reflectance image and validated against MODIS IGBP land cover data, producing a classified land cover map with accuracy assessment from training and validation samples.

The script selects the first (least cloudy) Landsat 8 image from a filtered collection based on spatial location (a point in California) and temporal range (June to October 2014), sorted by ascending cloud cover. The output is a single image representing the clearest observation during that period.

The script generates a median composite of true-color (B4-B3-B2) Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery for a specific administrative region in China (OBJECTID 16) during the first eight months of 2022, applying cloud masking and clipping to the boundary, for visual interpretation or baseline land surface analysis.

The script analyzes the impact of forest loss by computing temporal statistics (min, max, std, median, interquartile mean) of multiple vegetation and moisture indices (NDWI, NDVI, EVI, NDMI, BSI, MIR, SAVI, NBR) from a masked Landsat image collection, where non-forest and cloud-contaminated pixels are excluded. The output focuses on characterizing vegetation variability in areas that experienced forest cover loss after 2000 within a defined home range.
task_name: Analyze forest loss impact on vegetation indices

task_description: The script identifies grassland areas in Baringo and Nakuru counties, Kenya, using NDVI derived from surface reflectance bands of Landsat 8 OLI data collected in 2020. Grassland is classified based on NDVI values between 0.55 and 0.66.

The script classifies land cover types in the Corpus Christi district of Canindeyu, Paraguay, using supervised classification (CART) on median-composite Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data from 2020. Training polygons labeled as Forest, Agriculture, and Other are used to train the classifier, which is then applied to generate a classified land cover map.

The script detects land surface changes between January 2020 and March 2022 using Landsat 8 surface reflectance data by computing the Normalized Burn Ratio (NBR) difference (dNBR) with SWIR2 and NIR bands, then classifies significant loss, gain, and no-change areas based on thresholding.

The script generates a median composite from Landsat 5, 7, and 8 surface reflectance data, computes multiple vegetation and land cover indices (including NBR, NDVI, SAVI, EVI, BSI, NDWI, NDMI), and analyzes forest cover change using the Hansen Global Forest Change dataset. It specifically maps forest areas with greater than 50% tree cover in 2000 and calculates cumulative forest loss from 2001 to 2019, masking losses outside initial forested areas.
task_name: Map forest cover and cumulative loss

task_description: The script computes the Jeffries-Matusita (JM) distance for each spectral band in a Landsat 5 surface reflectance composite using labeled training points, to evaluate class separability between land cover types.
task_name: Compute JM distance for spectral bands

task_description: The script classifies land cover types by training a Random Forest model on Sentinel-1 VH and VV backscatter values sampled from a user-provided feature collection of labeled samples within the region of interest, then applies the classifier to a mosaic of Sentinel-1 imagery for the year 2018.

The script identifies areas below 817 meters elevation using a DEM, masks these low-lying regions, and calculates the total area submerged. It then clips 2015 population data to the study geometry, multiplies it by the underwater mask to estimate the population living in these low-elevation zones, and outputs both the underwater area in square kilometers and the affected population.

The script analyzes the temporal and metadata characteristics of Landsat 7 imagery over São Paulo, filtering images by cloud cover and date range (2019), extracting projection and resolution details, computing acquisition frequency, and evaluating data availability for time series analysis.

The script classifies land cover into four classes—forest, water, urban, and agropasture—using a Random Forest classifier applied to Landsat 5 surface reflectance bands and spectral indices (NDVI, NDWI, NDMI, EVI). It evaluates classification accuracy using a validation partition and applies a majority filter to improve spatial coherence of the output.

The script identifies permanent and temporary surface water bodies using MNDWI derived from Landsat 4, 5, 7, and 8 imagery for 2016, applying percentile reduction and cloud masking, then masks results using HAND data to exclude higher elevation areas.
task_name: Map permanent and temporary water bodies

task_description: The script extracts a specific urban boundary from a feature collection based on its 'system:index', centers the map on it, and clips a median Sentinel-2 image (RGB bands) to that urban geometry after filtering for low cloud cover and date range. The output is a true-color composite image of the selected urban area for visual analysis.

The script classifies land cover types using a time series of spectral indices (EVI, NDVI, NDMI, BSI, NDWI, MIR, NBR, SAVI) and surface reflectance bands from satellite imagery, applying Random Forest classifiers with varying tree counts (10–500). It evaluates classification accuracy using validation points and computes the area (in hectares) of each predicted land cover class within a defined region (homeRange_PH), achieving a maximum validation accuracy of 77%.

The script models high-resolution population density by aggregating census data ('INWONER') to a 100m grid, normalizing by area, masking with elevation data, and reprojecting to a local coordinate system (EPSG:28992). It outputs a continuous raster map of population per hectare (inh) and computes total population within and below sea level areas using a DEM mask.

The script calculates the Vegetation Condition Index (VCI) using MODIS MOD13Q1 NDVI data over a user-defined region between 2010 and 2020, normalizing NDVI values by pixel-wise min-max reduction within the region to assess vegetation health variability over time.

The script identifies persistent seasonal water surfaces by combining Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data with the JRC Global Surface Water dataset, applying cloud masking and a normalized difference index (B3-B8) threshold to derive a seasonality mask, which is then merged with permanent water bodies to produce a final water mask.

The script calculates monthly mean NDVI values for Nairobi by processing MODIS MOD09GA NDVI data from June 2021 to June 2022, then extracts regional statistics using reduceRegions over a predefined ROI, resulting in a feature collection with temporal NDVI metrics per region.

The script detects active fire areas by analyzing MODIS Terra and Aqua MOD14A1 and MYD14A1 Fire Mask data over a 15-day period starting from August 6, 2022, using a threshold (FireMask >= 7), and aggregates the results into frequency and thermal intensity (MaxFRP) maps.

The script calculates NDVI from a single Landsat 8 TOA image using near-infrared and red bands, then classifies and masks pixels with NDVI values greater than 0 and less than 0.5, representing low vegetation cover.

The script analyzes mangrove vegetation health and structure in North Sumatra using WorldView-3 multispectral and panchromatic imagery, applying shadow correction and pan-sharpening techniques to compute NDVI and NDI45 indices for detailed spectral analysis.

The script classifies land cover types using Landsat 7 surface reflectance data from January 2001 to January 2003, applying a Random Forest classifier trained on labeled samples of water, agricultural land, built-up areas, bare land, and forest within a study area. The output is a classified land cover map and accuracy assessments including confusion matrix, overall accuracy, and kappa coefficient for both training and validation datasets.

The script identifies agricultural and related land cover types (shrub/scrub, grassland, pasture/hay, cultivated crops) within specific HUC10 and HUC08 watersheds in Minnesota using NLCD 2011 land cover data, masking non-agricultural areas and applying a buffer exclusion around TD permit locations.

The script classifies land cover types using Dynamic World v1 data for the year 2021, applying temporal aggregation and rule-based post-processing (crop, snow, built-up) on median and mean surface reflectance probabilities. It outputs labeled images where each pixel is assigned a land cover class based on phenological patterns and thresholds.

The script creates a median cloud-masked, pansharpened true-color composite from Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data for the year 2016, enhancing spatial detail by fusing the panchromatic band with visible bands (B2, B3, B4) using HSV transformation.
The script filters Sentinel-2 surface reflectance images over Henan region from 2022 to 2023 with less than 10% cloud cover and prints the resulting image collection for further analysis.

The script classifies land cover into four categories—Forest, Settlement, Bareland, and Agriculture—using tree cover, loss, gain, and loss year variables derived from Landsat data. It trains a CART classifier on labeled regions and applies it to classify the kapchemutwa region, producing a thematic map of land cover classes.

The script detects and classifies cyanobacteria blooms in inland waters using the Normalized Difference Chlorophyll Index (NDCI) derived from atmospherically corrected Sentinel-2 imagery. It processes daily mosaics, applies a classification to identify bloom severity levels (0–3), and outputs time-series images with bands for reflectance, NDCIn, and classified NDCI for each day within the specified range.

The script classifies land cover types using a Random Forest classifier trained on Landsat 8 surface reflectance bands within a study area, producing a classified land cover map and evaluating model accuracy with training and validation datasets.

The script enhances the spatial resolution of a natural color Landsat 8 image by fusing panchromatic band (B8) with multispectral bands through HSV pan-sharpening, producing a visually improved RGB output for detailed land observation.

The script identifies and maps forest loss within legally protected areas, peatlands, and forest estates in Indonesia between 2013 and 2017 using Hansen global forest change data and land use designations, with output focused on district-level loss statistics.
task_name: Map forest loss in protected areas

task_description: The script analyzes the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) from MODIS MOD13Q1 data for the state of Pernambuco, Brazil, in 2019, applying quality masking to remove low-quality and cloudy pixels, and generates median composites for both masked and unmasked conditions.

The script filters GEDI Level 2A data for high-quality, non-degraded observations over Rio between June 2019 and July 2022, then computes the mean of rh98 (98th percentile of relative height) across beams to map vertical vegetation structure, specifically canopy height, using a color gradient from red to dark green.

The script identifies surface water bodies by calculating NDWI from Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data and applying Otsu's method for automatic thresholding on both individual images and the median composite. Outputs include water masks, NDWI layers, and associated Otsu thresholds for a specified AOI and time range.
task_name: Identify surface water extent using NDWI and Otsu thresholding

task_description: The script detects flood extent changes by comparing median-filtered VV polarization SAR images from Sentinel-1 before and after a flood event, identifying areas where the backscatter difference exceeds a threshold, indicating potential inundation.

The script identifies the medioid image from a Sentinel-2 image collection by selecting the image with the smallest spectral distance in NDVI to the median NDVI composite, effectively finding the most spectrally representative image for a region.

The script identifies forest loss by masking Hansen forest cover loss data and computes the distance from mining activities within a 1000-meter radius, highlighting areas of potential habitat fragmentation due to proximity to mining.
task_name: Identify forest loss near mining areas

task_description: The script calculates NDVI from cloud-masked Landsat 8 surface reflectance data to estimate vegetation greenness over a specified region and time period, producing a median composite image representing typical vegetation conditions.

The script classifies land cover into three classes—Anthropogenic, Cocoa (as part of intensive or shifting agriculture), and Shifting Agriculture (including Oil Palm and Logging)—using a Random Forest classifier applied to multispectral indices and surface reflectance bands from satellite imagery. It evaluates classifier performance with varying numbers of trees (10–500) and selects the 300-tree model based on validation accuracy (~74%). The output includes classified raster maps and area estimates in hectares per class within a specified region (homeRange_PH).

The script performs supervised land cover classification using Landsat 8 surface reflectance data, training an SVM classifier on user-defined regions of water, urban, vegetation, and soil, then classifying and validating the output with accuracy assessment and a visual legend.

The script retrieves Sentinel-2 surface reflectance images with less than 10% cloud cover, selects the red, green, and blue bands (B4, B3, B2), clips them to a user-defined geometry (table), and generates a cloud-cleared, visually interpretable image collection for early 2020.

The script interpolates sea surface temperature (SST) values from sampled points using kriging with an exponential model, generating a continuous SST surface map from NOAA AVHRR Pathfinder data for a specific date and region in the western Atlantic Ocean.

The script classifies land cover into urban, water, and forest categories using a CART classifier trained on Landsat 8 surface reflectance bands. It outputs a classified image map with distinct color coding for each land cover type.

The script identifies glacier extents over time using the ratio of Landsat bands B4 and B5 (near-infrared to shortwave infrared) in monthly composites from 1999 to 2023. It applies Otsu's method on histograms to compute dynamic thresholds for each image, segments glaciers using a binary mask, filters small noise with connected pixel count, computes the area and perimeter of detected glaciers, and generates vector polygons representing glacier boundaries.
task_name: Identify glacier extent from ratio threshold

task_description: The script analyzes Sentinel-1 GRD imagery over Oriente, identifying IW and EW instrument modes, filtering by polarization (VV, VH, HH, HV), orbit direction (ascending/descending), and time period (2016-01-01 to 2016-03-01). It creates multi-temporal composites combining mean backscatter from different orbits and polarizations for structural and directional surface analysis.
task_name: Analyze Sentinel-1 SAR modes and polarizations

task_description: The script classifies land cover into two classes (fire and nofire) using a Random Forest classifier applied to a median Landsat 5 TOA reflectance composite from August to October 2011, training on sample regions and producing a classified raster map clipped to the region of interest.
task_name: Classify land cover using random forest

task_description: The script calculates the mean tree canopy percentage from a tree percent cover dataset within different land use and land cover classes (e.g., roads, open spaces, residential, informal settlements) defined in an urban land use map for subcity-level administrative boundaries in Addis Ababa. It outputs a feature collection with mean tree cover values per class per subcity.
task_name: Estimate tree cover by land use type

task_description: The script extracts forest areas by identifying pixels where the Land_Use band equals 3 in the USFS GTAC LCMS v2021-7 mosaic, generating a binary mask (1 for forest, 0 otherwise).

The script identifies pixels showing a declining trend in fitted spectral index values (e.g., NDVI, NBR, TCG) from 2018 to 2020 using LandTrendr-fitted time series data, then extracts and analyzes the change patterns within insect disturbance regions (beetle and defoliator outbreaks) by generating histograms of fitted and original spectral values.

The script calculates the total annual precipitation by summing monthly precipitation data from the WORLDCLIM dataset for the year 1970, producing a single composite image representing yearly accumulated precipitation.

The script classifies cropland types by training a Random Forest classifier on a Sentinel-2 composite from seasonal medians (quarterly) of 2016, using USDA NASS CDL 2016 as training labels. It evaluates classification accuracy through stratified sampling and error matrix analysis across varying numbers of trees in the forest.
task_name: Classify crop types using satellite imagery

task_description: The script models marine environmental conditions by computing median chlorophyll-a and sea surface temperature from MODIS-Aqua data, reclassifying them into ordinal classes based on ecological thresholds, and combining them into a composite index representing water quality or habitat suitability for a specific marine application.

The script identifies mangrove areas in Thailand by applying a threshold on the Mangrove Vegetation Index (MVI) derived from a Landsat 8 surface reflectance composite, masked by elevation and NDWI, for the year 2019.

The script models the spatiotemporal probability of fly movement and persistence by combining temperature (day/night LST) and vegetation (NDVI) suitability thresholds, integrating over time with a 16-day movement kernel, and masking unsuitable land cover. The output is a probability map indicating areas where environmental conditions support sustained fly activity between 2010 and 2019.
task_name: Model habitat suitability for fly movement

task_description: The script computes a modified vegetation index (MVI) using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data, applying cloud masking, elevation filtering below 30m, and land mask from the Hansen forest change dataset, to analyze low-elevation vegetated areas within a specific region for the year 2022.

The script classifies land cover types such as dense forest, open forest, natural non-forest, agriculture/pasture, and bare soil using spectral mixture analysis (SMA), NDFI, NDVI, SAVI, EVI2, and decision tree modeling on Landsat imagery from 2000 to 2016 for grid SH-21-Z-B.

The script filters a Landsat 8 TOA reflectance image collection for a specific geographic point and date range, then selects the blue, green, and red spectral bands (B2, B3, B4) for further visual or analytical use, such as true-color compositing or urban/vegetation monitoring.

The script identifies cloud-covered areas in Landsat 8 TOA imagery over a user-defined region (poly_10) between January and July 2014 using a cloud scoring algorithm based on spectral and thermal thresholds, then applies pan-sharpening to improve spatial resolution and evaluates image quality.

The script calculates NDVI from Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data between March 2014 and May 2016, applies cloud masking, computes a mean composite image, and extracts the mean NDVI value within Santa Clara County boundary.
task_name: Analyze NDVI in Santa Clara County

task_description: The script classifies land cover types using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data and training samples from six classes: forest formation, non-forest natural formation, agricultural area, non-vegetated area, water body, and not observed. It applies a Random Forest classifier to produce a land cover map.

The script estimates surface soil moisture (SSM) using Sentinel-1 C-band SAR data in VV polarization. It imports and processes a time series of S1 images over a user-defined AOI, applies temporal speckle filtering and Refined Lee speckle filtering, computes the driest and wettest backscatter conditions using percentiles, derives sensitivity, and normalizes a multitemporal median image to produce a soil moisture map scaled from 0 to 100% for October 2019.
task_name: Estimate surface soil moisture from Sentinel-1 VV

task_description: The script maps land cover transitions between 2001 and 2018 in the Pampa region using MapBiomas Pampa Collection 1 classification data, calculating transition areas within administrative boundaries of Soriano and tri-national sub-regions (Argentina, Brazil, Uruguay).

The script identifies urban built-up areas by combining and comparing multiple global urban datasets (WRI Urban Land Use, GHSL, Tsinghua GAIA, CGLS-LC100, and WSF) to analyze agreement levels across products, producing a composite map showing where different datasets agree on urban extent.

The script identifies submerged aquatic vegetation, particularly seagrass habitats, using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data by applying NDWI-based water masking and glint correction to enhance underwater feature detection in the Lombok region.

The script extracts a time series of evapotranspiration (ET), potential evapotranspiration (PET), latent heat flux (LE), and potential latent heat (PLE) from MODIS MOD16A2 data over a defined region of interest in the northwestern USA between October 1, 2006, and September 30, 2020. The output is a CSV file containing mean values of these variables per image date, derived using zonal statistics over the ROI.
task_name: Extract ET and PET time series

task_description: The script classifies land cover into water, non-forest, and forest categories using Sentinel-2 imagery by computing the Normalized Difference Built-up Index (NDBI) and applying thresholding. It also remaps classified values to new categorical codes for further analysis.

The script corrects the red band reflectance from MODIS MYD09GQ (250m) using ratio-based scaling derived from coincident MYD09GA (500m) observations on the same date, then fuses blue and green bands from MYD09GA onto the 250m grid by downscaling via reflectance ratios, producing a higher-resolution RGB composite with improved spatial detail.

The script applies a topographic correction using the SCSc method to Landsat 7 Surface Reflectance data over path 4, row 56 for the year 2019, producing a median-composite image with improved radiometric accuracy in mountainous terrain by modeling illumination conditions based on solar and terrain geometry.
task_name: Correct surface reflectance for terrain illumination

task_description: The script calculates the time difference in days between the current date and the most recent acquisition dates of Landsat 7, 8, and 9 images available in the Google Earth Engine catalog, providing a measure of data latency for each satellite.

The script creates a median true-color surface reflectance composite for Los Angeles using Landsat Collection 2 data from January to April 2022, applying cloud and shadow masking along with digital number to surface reflectance conversion.
task_name: Generate true color surface reflectance composite

task_description: The script performs supervised classification of urban land cover types (buildings, roads, green spaces, and undeveloped areas) using a support vector machine (SVM) classifier trained on manually labeled feature collections. The output is a classified raster map where each pixel is assigned one of four classes based on spectral characteristics derived from satellite imagery.

The script analyzes changes in forest vegetation over time using LandTrendr-based time series of spectral indices derived from Landsat surface reflectance data, with a focus on areas having more than 20% tree cover in the year 2000. Outputs include annual composites and transformed collections for multiple spectral indices (e.g., NDVI, NBR, TCG) used to detect land cover and vegetation dynamics between 1997 and 2020.

The script performs land cover classification by training Random Forest classifiers on Sentinel-1 SAR (VV/VH) and Landsat 8 optical (surface reflectance with NDVI) data, comparing classification accuracy from SAR-only, optical-only, and fused SAR-optical datasets over a specified region and time period.
task_name: Classify land cover using SAR and optical data

task_description: The script performs temporal gap-filling on a time-series of land cover classification images by propagating earlier classifications forward and backward through time to fill missing values, producing a temporally continuous land cover dataset for a specific area.

The script identifies burned areas by computing the difference in Normalized Burn Ratio (dNBR) between pre-fire and post-fire Landsat image composites, using median and mosaic reductions respectively, and applying a cloud and shadow mask based on pixel QA bits.

The script analyzes digital elevation model data to identify areas where elevation exceeds specific thresholds (0.0 and 0.08), representing potential changes between 1970 and 2018, and computes the mean value over the current map view extent.

The script performs image sharpening on a Landsat 8 multispectral image (B4, B3, B2) using panchromatic band (B8) and the PCA method via the geeSharp library, producing a high-resolution color image for visual analysis.

The script maps stable vegetation classes in the PAMPA biome for the year 2017 by analyzing a MapBiomas classification image collection, filtering for persistent land cover types such as forest, savanna, mangroves, wetlands, grasslands, non-forest vegetation, and water, then generating a masked composite of these stable areas.

The script calculates NDVI using Sentinel-2 bands B8 and B4 to assess vegetation health in the Nioro region, generating two NDVI layers (ndvi2 and ndvi3) from mean surface reflectance values after filtering and compositing imagery from June to November 2017.

The script monitors algal blooms in reservoirs across Latin America using Sentinel-2 data and the NDCI index to estimate chlorophyll-a concentration, detect bloom presence, classify trophic state (TSI), and generate temporal statistics and visualizations for user-selected water bodies.

The script estimates Land Surface Temperature (LST) using top-of-atmosphere brightness temperature from Band 10 and emissivity derived from NDVI-based fractional vegetation cover, applying a radiative transfer model expression. Outputs include NDVI, fractional vegetation (FV), emissivity (EMM), and LST layers.

The script retrieves a cloud-minimized Landsat 8 image from 2021, selects visible bands (B4, B3, B2) and the panchromatic band (B8), then applies multiple pan-sharpening techniques (GS, HPFA, IHS, PCA, SFIM, brovey, simpleMean) to enhance spatial resolution of the RGB bands using the higher-resolution panchromatic band. The output includes visualizations of both unsharpened and sharpened images for comparison.
task_name: Sharpen multispectral imagery using panchromatic band

task_description: The script classifies land cover types at a specific point location using the first available Sentinel-2 image with less than 30% cloud cover between 2021-01-01 and 2022-01-01, then applies the Dynamic World model to generate a labeled land cover map with nine classes: water, trees, grass, flooded vegetation, crops, shrub and scrub, built, bare, and snow and ice.
