task_name: Classify land cover with Dynamic World

task_description: The script analyzes land surface conditions in the Pampa biome using median composites of Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery before and after a specific period in 2018, applying cloud masking to generate clear visualizations of pre- and post-season conditions.

The script classifies land cover types with a focus on human settlements using Sentinel-2 imagery from 2016 and 2020, trains a Random Forest classifier on sampled training data, and generates classified maps for both years. It also computes the difference between the two classifications to detect changes in settlement patterns over time.

The script identifies areas of vegetation loss in Dominica caused by a hurricane by comparing NDVI values from Sentinel-2 imagery before (2016) and after (2017) the event, computing the difference, and classifying regions with significant NDVI decline as impacted. It outputs a binary map of loss/no loss and calculates the percentage of land area that experienced NDVI loss.

The script estimates green leaf area index (LAIg) using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data by first computing the SeLI index (Sentinel-2 Leaf Index) from B8A and B5 bands, then applying a linear transformation. It also compares the result with MODIS Fpar (Fraction of Absorbed Photosynthetically Active Radiation) product as a reference. Outputs include a SeLI layer, a derived LAIg layer, and the MODIS Fpar layer for the same period and area.

The script assesses urban flood vulnerability by combining population density, elevation data, and built-up intensity. It calculates a flood vulnerability index using the expression 'POP * (1 / (AVE - LocalMin))', where population is weighted inversely by adjusted elevation above a city-specific minimum. The output includes mapped layers for surface water change, forest loss, and multitemporal built-up areas, with visualizations tailored to selected cities (Cape Town, Kigali, or Addis Ababa).

The script classifies land cover types in the Mata Atlântica biome for the year 2017 using a pre-trained Random Forest model (version 3) applied to mosaic imagery. It evaluates classification accuracy through an error matrix derived from stratified sampling within a specific region (reg_01), producing a confusion matrix table for user-defined classes: forest, savana, campo, veg.ñflo, agro, aflo, and agua.

The script classifies eucalyptus and non-eucalyptus areas using a CART classifier trained on Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery from 2017, producing a land cover classification map clipped to the study area.

The script performs supervised classification to identify and map land cover types (vegetation, water, mining, deforestation, clouds) using Sentinel-2 imagery from July 2017. It trains a CART classifier on user-defined sample regions and applies it to a specific Sentinel-2 image, producing a classified land cover map masked to retain only valid classes.

The script identifies glacier areas by calculating the Normalized Difference Snow Index (NDSI) from Landsat 8 surface reflectance data, applying thresholds on NDSI and spectral bands (SR_B4, SR_B2), and generating a binary mask that is vectorized to produce glacier boundary polygons for the year 2016.

The script classifies land cover types using a Random Forest classifier trained on a feature collection with spectral and vegetation indices from a multi-temporal image stack. The output is a classified map showing different land cover classes such as forest, agriculture, water, and bare soil, along with accuracy assessment metrics including overall accuracy, kappa coefficient, and user/producer accuracies derived from a confusion matrix.

The script analyzes MODIS NDSI Snow Cover data to identify the first and last days of snow cover and snow-free periods, computing continuous durations of snow presence and absence over a year for specific regions. Outputs include FDWS (First Day With Snow), LDWS (Last Day With Snow), FDWoS (First Day Without Snow), LDWoS (Last Day Without Snow), MaskedCounter, and NrDaysSnow.

The script classifies land cover types using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data, computing NDVI, NDBI, and NDWI indices, applying a Random Forest classifier trained on labeled samples, and validating the results with an error matrix and kappa statistic.
The script calculates the mean NDVI from Sentinel-2 imagery over the Lindi region for the year 2020, producing a single composite image representing average vegetation greenness.

The script calculates brightness temperature from ASTER band 13 (thermal infrared) data by converting digital numbers to spectral radiance and applying a thermal conversion using K1 and K2 calibration constants, resulting in a surface temperature map between 295K and 310K for the specified region and time period.

The script classifies water and land areas using Radarsat-2 HH and HV polarization bands, along with derived ratio and difference indices, through a Random Forest classifier. It trains on labeled feature collections within a study area in Sumatra, Indonesia, validates the classification accuracy using a held-out test set, and computes the area of classified land and water regions.

The script performs supervised classification of land cover types using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data and training samples from user-defined regions of interest. It trains a CART classifier on 70% of the labeled samples, classifies the image mosaic, and evaluates accuracy using a confusion matrix, overall accuracy, and kappa coefficient on the remaining 30% test samples. The output includes a classified land cover map and accuracy assessment metrics.

The script processes Sentinel-1 GRD data before and after a flood event to generate median VV, VH, incidence angle, and VV/VH ratio composites for both time periods, merging them into a multi-temporal dataset to analyze changes in surface scattering properties, likely related to flood extent or land cover change.

The script filters classification maps from 2019 and 2021 to remove small patches of a target class (class 3) using a spatial connectivity and minimum area threshold, then identifies deforestation by detecting pixels that changed from class 1 (e.g., forest) in 2019 to class 3 (e.g., non-forest) in 2021, producing a final map with an added deforestation class (4).

The script creates a pan-sharpened false color composite image by fusing the high-resolution panchromatic band (B8) of Landsat-8 with the hue and saturation components derived from the visible and near-infrared bands (B5, B4, B2), enhancing spatial detail while preserving spectral characteristics for visual interpretation.

The script classifies land use and land cover (LULC) for the year 2018 by training a Random Forest classifier on a mosaic of Landsat 8 surface reflectance images clipped to the chunati region. It uses ground truth samples from three classes (aail, other, agriculture) to train and validate the model, outputs a classified LULC map with a custom color palette, and evaluates classification accuracy using a confusion matrix and overall accuracy metric.

The script classifies land cover types using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data and a CART classifier, trained on sample regions for classes including road, water, crop, qiaomu, guanmu, building, weizaocheng, and weiliyong. It outputs a classified land cover map, confusion matrix, overall accuracy, and kappa coefficient based on 70% training and 30% testing samples.

The script identifies areas of forest decline in the SPB region by combining a binary forest mask from LANDFIRE vegetation type data with regions of decline derived from NBR, TCW, and TCG time series analysis between 2019 and 2020, then excludes pixels within 30 meters of roads and 90 meters of surface water, as well as those overlapping with post-2016 fire perimeters, resulting in a refined mask of persistent forest decline.
task_name: Identify forest decline areas excluding roads water and recent fires

task_description: The script classifies land cover types using Landsat 7 TOA reflectance data that has been pansharpened, trained with labeled feature collections for mangrove, palm oil, developed areas, aquaculture, tropical forest, barren land, and cultivated crops. It produces a classified image map and computes classification accuracy and area statistics per class for the year 2015 in Sumatra, Indonesia.

The script identifies surface hotspots by detecting pixels in a temperature image (in Kelvin) that exceed 303 K, performs connected components analysis to group adjacent hotspot pixels, and calculates the area of each connected hotspot region. The output includes a binary mask of hotspots, an image labeling individual hotspot objects, and an estimation of the total area for each hotspot based on pixel count and pixel area.

The script classifies coastal habitat types (mangrove, seagrass, coral reef, estuary, soft sediment) in Brazil and the Amazon ecoregion using a Random Forest classifier applied to Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data, spectral indices (NDVI, NDBI, MNDWI, BSI), and elevation masking from bathymetry data. The output is a classified land cover map for 2020 with accuracy assessment via confusion matrix and overall test accuracy.
task_name: Classify coastal habitats using spectral indices

task_description: The script identifies bare land areas by calculating NDVI and NDWI from a single Landsat 8 image, applying thresholds (NDVI < 0.2 and NDWI < 0), and masking the result to highlight regions with minimal vegetation and moisture.
The script calculates NDVI from Sentinel-2 imagery at a specific point in Southeast Asia, then classifies vegetation into non-forest and forest areas using a threshold of 0.5 on the NDVI values.

The script computes the maximum NDVI from Landsat 8 surface reflectance data over a user-defined geometry for the year 2016, groups it by elevation zones derived from SRTM topography, and calculates mean NDVI per elevation zone within a buffered region.
The script calculates the Bare Soil Index (BSI) using a custom spectral expression on a median composite of Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data, highlighting areas of exposed soil within the study region.

The script classifies land cover into two classes using Random Forest and SVM classifiers on median-composited Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data from June to September 2016, with accuracy assessment via confusion matrix, overall accuracy, and kappa coefficient based on a stratified sample dataset.
task_name: Classify land cover using RF and SVM

task_description: The script classifies land cover into two classes (fire and no-fire) using a Random Forest classifier trained on Landsat 5 TOA reflectance bands, producing a classified raster map of the region.
task_name: Classify land cover using random forest

task_description: The script calculates the annual actual evapotranspiration (AET) for the HUC-8 watershed '10070002' using TerraClimate data for the year 2018, applying a scaling factor and spatial clipping, then outputs the result as a single reduced image.

The script calculates the mean column number density of multiple atmospheric gases (CH4, NO2, CO, SO2, HCHO, O3) globally for the year 2019 using Sentinel-5P OFFL L3 data, and outputs the annual average O3 column density value.

The script identifies areas around Kamchatka's volcanoes by creating 3.5 km buffers and retrieves cloud-filtered Sentinel-2 imagery from summer 2020 to generate a median composite image, which is then clipped to the buffered zones for visual analysis of potential volcanic activity or surface changes.

The script analyzes seasonal vegetation dynamics in the Naracoorte region by computing NDVI from Landsat surface reflectance data between 1999 and 2013, with gap-filled composites for later years using temporal regression against prior and future imagery to mitigate cloud cover effects.

The script calculates hourly 10-meter wind speed in kilometers per hour from ERA5-Land reanalysis data for the time period between 2021-07-01 and 2022-12-31 at 14:00 UTC, clipped to a user-defined boundary (wi_co_bnds), using u and v wind components.

The script identifies and maps the age of secondary forests in Brazil by analyzing annual land cover changes from 1985 to 2021 using MapBiomas Collection 7 data, masking for anthropogenic areas and permanent water bodies, and tracking forest regeneration over time.

The script performs supervised land cover classification using RapidEye imagery, distinguishing vegetation, water, mining, deforestation, and clouds. It trains a CART classifier on user-defined sample regions and applies it to classify the image into thematic classes, then remaps and masks the output to highlight specific land cover changes.

The script calculates the mean monthly daytime and nighttime land surface temperature (LST) from MODIS MOD11A1 data, converts it from Kelvin to Celsius, and extracts January composites for analysis. The output is a time series of monthly LST images with temperature in degrees Celsius, specifically isolating January observations for long-term comparison.

The script calculates land cover transition areas between 1985 and 2021 using MapBiomas Pampa Collection 2 classification data, focusing on the Soriano region and its sub-regions in Argentina, Brazil, and Uruguay. It computes transitions by combining classified images from two time points into a single transition code, then derives area (in hectares) per transition class within specified geographic boundaries.

The script models the seasonal pattern of EVI (Enhanced Vegetation Index) using harmonic regression on scaled PROBAV S1 TOC surface reflectance data over a single point in Beijing, China, fitting a time series to capture temporal dynamics between 2015 and 2016.
task_name: Model EVI seasonality with harmonic regression

task_description: The script identifies inconsistencies in deforestation classification by comparing a user-provided land cover image with a reference dataset from MapBiomas, specifically detecting areas where certain class values (216, 219, 220, 221, 316, 319, 320, 321) occur in the combined reference layer derived from time-series deforestation data.

The script processes Sentinel-1 GRD data to generate a filtered, terrain-corrected, and wind-masked Normalized Polarization Ratio (NPOL = VH/VV) image, along with mean VV backscatter and its standard deviation over a specific region and time period. It applies incidence angle correction, speckle filtering using a refined Lee filter, and masks pixels affected by high wind speeds (>12 km/h) to improve water detection accuracy. The outputs include NPOL, VV mean, and VV standard deviation mosaics clipped to the study area, intended for surface water mapping under reduced wind contamination.
task_name: Map surface water and wind-affected areas

task_description: The script creates a median true-color composite image from Sentinel-2 data over the PolSGG region, using bands B4 (red), B3 (green), and B2 (blue), to visually analyze land surface features with minimal cloud interference.
task_name: Extract true color composite for vegetation analysis

task_description: The script quantifies the sources of cropland gain and loss between 2000 and 2020 by analyzing land cover transitions, specifically identifying how much cropland expansion originated from forests, wetlands, primary forests, IFLs, water, snow, bare areas, short vegetation, and built-up areas, using high-resolution global land cover datasets and forest extent layers.

The script classifies land cover types with a focus on human settlements, built-up areas, agriculture, and water bodies using Sentinel-2 imagery from 2016 and 2020. It trains a Random Forest classifier on labeled training data to produce classified maps for both years, then computes the difference between them to detect changes in settlement patterns over time.

The script calculates hourly air temperature at 2 meters, dew point temperature, wind speed, solar radiation, surface pressure, and derived variables such as vapor pressure, relative humidity, and wind speed adjusted to 2m height for Santa Helena, Paraná, Brazil, using ERA5-Land reanalysis data from January 2022.
task_name: Calculate air temperature and dew point in Santa Helena

task_description: The script analyzes changes in land surface characteristics by comparing Sentinel-1 SAR imagery before and after a specific time period, using VV and VH polarizations over Ernakulam district, clipped to the administrative boundary.

The script estimates Land Surface Temperature (LST) in the El Bagre municipality using Landsat 8 Collection 1 Tier 1 Surface Reflectance data. It computes NDVI, derives fractional vegetation cover (FV), calculates emissivity (EMM), and applies a radiative transfer-based expression to derive LST, which is then clipped to the municipal boundary for localized analysis.

The script classifies land cover types in the Cordillera region of Peru using spectral mixture analysis (SMA), NDFI, and a decision tree applied to Landsat 5 and 7 surface reflectance data from 2012. It generates a classified mosaic with bands including vegetation fractions (gv, npv, soil), indices (ndvi, ndfi), terrain attributes (slope, elevation), and a final land classification map.

The script identifies forested areas located at elevations above 700 meters by combining MODIS land cover type classification (LC_Type1) with SRTM elevation data. It outputs a binary map where pixels classified as forest (classes 1 to 4) in the MODIS product and above 700 meters in elevation are assigned value 1, others are masked out.
The script calculates the difference in NDVI between 2000 and 2010, focusing on large parks within 2000 meters of subway lines, and computes the average NDVI change for each of these parks.

The script generates 100 random sample points within a defined polygon, extracts mean elevation values from the ALOS World 3D digital surface model (DSM), and performs kriging interpolation to create a continuous elevation surface based on these sampled points.

The script identifies and classifies burned areas by computing spectral differences between pre-fire and post-fire Sentinel-2 images, using indices such as NDVI, SAVI, BAIS2, BAI, and NBR, and applies a Random Forest classifier to detect fire-affected regions.

The script creates a normalized Landsat 8 surface reflectance composite for April–June 2016, computes spectral indices (NDVI, MNDWI, BSI), and masks non-urban areas using the WSF2015 urban settlement layer to isolate built-up regions within the MainProject boundary.

The script applies a multitemporal despeckling filter to Sentinel-1 GRD imagery using a spatio-temporal neighborhood and entropy-based masking, producing smoothed VV and VH backscatter images for improved visual and analytical interpretation.

The script detects changes in surface water extent by comparing two Sentinel-1 SAR images acquired before and after a potential flood event, using VV polarization to identify flooded areas, with non-water areas masked out using a global water dataset.

The script identifies residential structures potentially affected by oil/gas wellpad operations by buffering wellpad centroids at multiple distances (152.4m, 213.36m, and 609.6m) and filtering building footprints within the largest buffer zone. Outputs include buffered zones around wellpad locations and the subset of structures intersecting these zones.

The script identifies sugarcane cultivation areas by filtering polygon features with predicted class 1, computes mean NDVI from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery between March and October 2022 over tile 42RWS, clips the NDVI to a region 'p2p', and performs mean value reduction of NDVI over sugarcane polygons.
task_name: Identify sugarcane cultivation area using NDVI

task_description: The script classifies land cover into four classes—vegetation, water, built-up (construction), and other—using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from 2019. It computes NDVI, trains a Random Forest classifier using labeled training samples, applies the classifier to produce a land cover map, and validates the result using ground truth points with an error matrix to compute overall accuracy, user's accuracy, and producer's accuracy.

The script identifies potential cyanobacteria blooms in surface water using Sentinel-2 data by computing NDCI and applying a multi-threshold classification on NDVI and spectral reflectance conditions. Outputs include classified images indicating cyanobacteria presence (NDCI_class), NDCI values, NDVI, and cloud-masked, atmospherically corrected surface reflectance imagery clipped to a region of interest.

The script classifies land cover types including agriculture, forest, urban, wetlands, and water bodies using Sentinel-2 optical imagery and Sentinel-1 SAR data. It trains a CART classifier on fused VV and VH bands from Sentinel-1 and applies it to generate a classified land cover map, with accuracy assessed via confusion matrix.
task_name: Classify land cover using SAR and optical data

task_description: The script performs stratified sampling of GPS point data based on class labels (ID), splitting the dataset into training and accuracy assessment subsets using a 70/30 ratio. It outputs histograms of class distribution, sample counts, and two stratified feature collections for model training and accuracy evaluation.
task_name: Stratify GPS point samples by class

task_description: The script identifies forest disturbances caused by beetle infestations and defoliator outbreaks using LandTrendr-fitted spectral trajectories from Landsat data, focusing on declining trends in B4 (NIR) and other vegetation indices between 2018 and 2020.

The script identifies areas of vegetation, water, built-up surfaces, and barren land in Rawalpindi District using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from August to October 2020. It computes NDVI, NDWI, NDBI, and a derived Barren Land index, applies thresholds to classify land cover types, and calculates the area (in acres) of each class within the Punjab region.
task_name: Identify vegetation and barren land areas

task_description: The script performs pansharpening on Landsat 7 ETM+ multispectral bands using its panchromatic band with multiple algorithms (GS, PCA, Simple Mean, Brovey, HPFA), then evaluates the quality of each method by comparing the sharpened output to the original multispectral image using quantitative metrics such as Q, ERGAS, MSE, PSNR, RASE, RMSE, BIAS, and DIV.

The script detects and analyzes vegetation disturbance patterns using LandTrendr-based time-series segmentation of Landsat spectral indices (NBR, B5, TCB, TCG, TCW) from 1999 to 2021, focusing on standardized fitted values for 2010, 2014, 2017, 2018, and 2019, with post-disturbance masking based on high-magnitude change polygons. It generates a segmented image composite using SNIC superpixels to identify spatially coherent change regions.

The script classifies land cover types in 2005 using Landsat 5 imagery and a Random Forest classifier trained on user-defined regions of interest, including water bodies, built-up areas, forest, crop, and scrub lands. The output includes a classified land cover map and an accuracy assessment with confusion matrix, overall accuracy, and Kappa coefficient.

The script calculates Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) from cloud-masked Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery over the state of Pernambuco, Brazil, in 2019, producing a time series of NDVI images to assess vegetation greenness.

The script identifies areas below a certain elevation threshold (817 meters) using a DEM, masks them within a watershed boundary, calculates the total underwater area in square kilometers, and estimates the population living in these low-lying zones by intersecting with 2015 population data.
task_name: Identify underwater area and estimate population exposure

task_description: The script analyzes the distribution of MODIS-derived land cover types (LC_Type1) over a set of farm locations in Indonesia by extracting mean pixel values from scaled land cover classifications, resulting in a flattened feature collection with statistical summaries per farm.
task_name: Analyze land cover distribution on farms

task_description: The script retrieves 2-meter above ground temperature, relative humidity, and 10-meter wind component forecasts from the NOAA GFS 0.25-degree global model for a specific date (October 28, 2020) and generates interpolated raster surfaces of temperature using inverse distance weighting from sampled points across South America over a 9-step forecast horizon (24 to 216 hours).

The script identifies water bodies by calculating the Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI) from Sentinel-2 imagery and applying Otsu's thresholding method to automatically classify water pixels within a region of interest.

The script corrects land cover classifications over time by filtering noise in transition pixels (smaller than 1 ha) between consecutive years using a temporal smoothing algorithm, focusing on the Cerrado biome. It outputs corrected annual land cover maps and evaluates noise reduction by comparing original and corrected transition data.

The script creates a median composite of Sentinel-1 GRD imagery over the specified AOI and time period, selecting VV and VH polarization bands. The output is a calibrated, scaled, and quantized image asset representing backscatter intensity, suitable for land cover analysis, agriculture monitoring, or change detection in humid tropical regions.

The script calculates and compares surface albedo from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data between two time periods, identifying areas where albedo has increased by at least 0.1, indicating potential land surface changes such as vegetation loss or urbanization.

The script classifies land cover types including dense mangrove, sparse mangrove, waterbodies/aquaculture, built-up areas, and barren land using a Random Forest classifier trained on Landsat 7 surface reflectance data from 2015 and applied to data from 2011–2012.

The script analyzes the presence and concentration of cyanobacteria in inland water bodies using Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-3 satellite data, applying atmospheric correction, computing NDCI (Normalized Difference Chlorophyll Index), estimating chlorophyll-a levels via Mishra's model, and classifying bloom intensity. Outputs include daily mosaics of NDCI, chlorophyll-a, and classification layers over regions of interest in southern Brazil, with time series analysis and spatial comparison using random sampling points.

The script analyzes crop types in 2016 using USDA NASS Cropland Data Layer and integrates environmental variables including precipitation (bio12), evapotranspiration (ET), gross primary productivity (GPP), and NDVI from multiple satellite sources, focusing on summer months (July–September 2016) within a specified geometry. Outputs include clipped and processed raster layers for precipitation, crop type, ET, GPP, and NDVI for regional agricultural-environmental assessment.
task_name: Analyze crop type and environmental variables

task_description: The script generates a cloud- and shadow-corrected annual medoid composite of surface reflectance from Landsat 5, 7, and 8 data for the year 2011 over Peru, using TDOM for shadow masking, haze removal, and sensor harmonization (Roy et al. method) to ensure consistency across sensors.

The script models cumulative cost of movement from a randomly sampled point within pasture areas, using a remapped land cover cost surface derived from classified land use data, to analyze spatial accessibility or connectivity across the landscape.
task_name: Model pasture accessibility via cost surface

task_description: The script remaps a land cover classification image from 1985 to identify pasture areas by reclassifying specific classes into pasture (1) and non-pasture (0), then calculates the total pasture area within a 9km radius around each pixel using a circular neighborhood sum of pixel areas.
task_name: Map pasture area from land cover

task_description: The script identifies perennial surface water bodies by filtering the JRC Global Surface Water dataset for pixels with seasonality equal to 12 (indicating year-round water presence) and clipping the result to a specific basin geometry derived from user-defined basins. The output is a binary mask of permanent water within the region of interest.

The script analyzes surface reflectance in permanent water bodies using atmospherically corrected Sentinel-2 imagery, applying CDI-based cloud and glint masking to generate spectral profiles over time within a region of interest.
task_name: Analyze surface reflectance in water bodies

task_description: The script defines multiple feature collections representing different land cover classes (e.g., vegetation, water, urban, agriculture) with labeled polygons and points, then creates a classification image by painting these features into a raster layer based on the 'LC' class label. It outputs this classified raster and computes a histogram of class frequencies within a specified region.

The script analyzes the elevation characteristics of the Sirinhaém River Basin using SRTM 30m and 90m digital elevation models, computing minimum, maximum, mean, median, and first quartile values, applying masks to isolate areas below the first quartile elevation, and generating histograms and visualizations for comparative analysis.

The script fills elevation gaps in the AHN2_05M_INT (interpolated) LiDAR-derived digital elevation model using morphological filtering and neighborhood-based max/median reduction with a circular kernel, followed by Gaussian smoothing to produce a continuous terrain surface for land areas.
task_name: Fill elevation gaps in AHN data

task_description: The script analyzes annual land cover data from MapBiomas Collection 7 to identify persistent forests, detect forest loss events, and compute forest age (duration of continuous forest cover) between 1985 and 2020 in a specified region of Brazil. It outputs time-series images representing forest extent, cumulative forest persistence, forest loss, and forest age for each year.
task_name: Map forest persistence and loss over time

task_description: The script detects flooded areas by computing the log ratio of pre- and post-event Sentinel-1 SAR images, applying a Gaussian kernel and thresholding on the VH polarization band, then masking non-water and low-lying areas using a forest/water mask and digital surface model. Outputs are binary flood extent maps for different pre-flood acquisition dates and orbits.

The script classifies land cover into urban and agricultural categories using a CART decision tree classifier trained on median composite Landsat imagery from 2017 to 2019. The output is a classified raster map derived from spectral bands (blue, green, red, NIR, SWIR) with cloud-masked pixels, where urban areas are labeled as 0 and agricultural areas as 1.

The script calculates daily minimum and maximum temperatures, converts them to Fahrenheit, computes mean temperature, derives growing degree days (GDD) with a base of 50°F, sets negative GDD values to zero, and sums the non-negative GDD over the date range for a specified region. The final output is a single image representing the cumulative growing degree days.

The script performs a supervised classification of land cover types using a Random Forest classifier trained on manually defined training samples. It classifies an input image (img_selected) into multiple land cover classes including exposed soil, water, pasture, wetlands, non-woody vegetation, and forest types, producing two separate classifications with different sample sets and evaluating their accuracy using confusion matrices.

The script identifies soybean cultivation areas in 2010 and 2020 using MapBiomas land cover data and classifies Landsat imagery with Random Forest to map soybean expansion. It computes the gain in soybean area between 2010 and 2020 and estimates the total expansion area in hectares.

The script analyzes tropospheric NO2 column number density over Pakistan for February, March, and April of 2019 and 2020 using Sentinel-5P data, producing monthly mean images to compare air quality changes year-over-year, particularly focusing on potential impacts from human activity reductions. Outputs include mapped visualizations of NO2 concentrations with a color bar legend and printed image metadata.

The script identifies water bodies by computing NDVI, NDWI, and MNDWI from Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data for the year 2015, then applies a threshold-based classification to detect water using the condition: NDVI < 0, NDWI > 0, and MNDWI > 0.5.
task_name: Identify water bodies using spectral indices

task_description: The script classifies land cover types using Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data from January to May 2020 over the Misiones region. It applies a CART classifier trained on user-defined training samples (e.g., forest, agriculture, water) and evaluates accuracy using an error matrix. The output includes a classified land cover map, accuracy metrics (overall accuracy, kappa, user’s and producer’s accuracy), and area estimates per class in hectares.

The script segments land cover regions in Fujian using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data processed to remove clouds and scaled, then applies SNIC superpixel segmentation on a masked and unmasked composite image to generate homogeneous regions based on spectral and spatial characteristics.

The script creates annual and semi-annual cloud-masked median composites of Landsat 8 surface reflectance data for a specific watershed region (C6C5) in 2019, using band ratios and pixel quality masking to enhance land surface analysis, particularly for vegetation and land cover monitoring.

The script classifies land cover types using a Random Forest classifier trained on spectral, vegetation, and texture features derived from monthly mosaic images. It generates classified subgrid outputs for specific time periods, remapping input classes to a standardized output scheme based on MapBiomas Collection 3 reference data.

The script performs histogram matching of a WorldView-2 multispectral image to a Sentinel-2 surface reflectance image over a specific AOI, using the first available cloud-cleared Sentinel-2 image from September 2022 as reference. The output is a pan-sharpened WorldView-2 image spectrally adjusted to match Sentinel-2's radiometric characteristics for visual and analytical consistency.

The script estimates Land Surface Temperature (LST) using brightness temperature from Landsat 8's Band 10 and emissivity derived from NDVI-based Fractional Vegetation Cover (FVC), applying a radiative transfer model with logarithmic correction for atmospheric effects.

The script corrects land cover classification time series by smoothing temporal inconsistencies using multi-year neighborhood filtering and frequency-based validation, producing a refined annual land cover map from 1985 to 2020.

The script calculates the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) using near-infrared (B5) and red (B4) bands from a single Landsat 8 TOA image, producing a continuous index map of vegetation greenness.

The script analyzes future coastal and riverine flooding impacts under climate change scenarios and overlays them with built-up areas from ESA WorldCover to assess urban flood exposure. It calculates the percentage of built-up land exposed to flooding in selected cities for start (1980) and end (2050) years, producing mapped layers and tabular statistics.

The script analyzes seasonal vegetation dynamics in 2020 by computing NDVI from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data, filtering for low cloud cover and applying cloud masking, then generating median composites for winter, spring, and summer seasons over Durbuy. Outputs include visualizations of true-color imagery and NDVI maps for each season.

The script classifies land cover into water and tundra classes using NDVI and Sentinel-2 spectral bands within a defined polygon boundary, producing a classified map based on training data derived from user-defined geometries.

The script calculates the area of high carbon stock (HCS) land cover classes within the Kota Jayapura administrative boundary in Indonesia, specifically focusing on the Papua province. It clips an HCS dataset to the Kota Jayapura region and computes the total area per class using pixel counting at 10m resolution.

The script processes Sentinel-1 GRD data over Fuyi City to compute terrain-corrected and speckle-filtered VH polarization images, normalizes the values, and derives a composite image representing minimum (5th percentile), maximum (95th percentile), and difference index (DI) of VH backscatter over key growing periods in 2021. The output is a three-band image (min, max, di) used for analyzing agricultural surface changes or crop phenology using SAR intensity time series.

The script performs supervised classification of urban land cover using a Random Forest classifier on Sentinel-2-like multispectral imagery, distinguishing four classes: trees, roads, non-developed areas, and buildings. Training samples are manually defined as polygons for each class, and the resulting classified map is validated using an independent validation dataset with accuracy assessment including error matrix and overall accuracy.

The script extracts Sentinel-1 GRD imagery over Nenjiang City (Nehe) between 2019 and 2020, filters for VH and VV bands, masks pixels where VH > VV, clips to region of interest, and computes mean backscatter values within soybean, corn, and rice fields. It also constructs a constant image from the mean values per band and defines a function to compute mean-reduced images across an image collection for a given ROI.
task_name: Extract mean SAR backscatter for crops

task_description: The script analyzes seasonal vegetation dynamics in the Lake Chad and Borno regions using Landsat 8 surface reflectance data from 2000 to 2017. It computes NDVI for different agricultural seasons (preparation, lean, harvest), applies cloud masking, and generates composite images using qualityMosaic('ndvi') and median reduction. The script also calculates the percentage of high-NDVI areas (above 0.7 threshold) within the Borno region for each season to assess vegetation productivity changes over time.

The script identifies surface water areas by comparing NDWI with NDVI and NDSI using Sentinel-2 data from September 2019, applying cloud masking and generating a masked NDVI layer where water is present based on spectral index thresholds.

The script generates time series of multiple vegetation and land surface indices (NDVI, NDWI, EVI, NDMI, BSI, MIR, SAVI, NBR) from Landsat surface reflectance data between 2000 and 2019, extracting pixel values at specific point locations to monitor land cover changes associated with anthropogenic activities such as logging, oil palm expansion, cocoa farming, and shifting agriculture.

The script calculates Fraction of Absorbed Photosynthetically Active Radiation (FAPAR) values from 16-day composite MODIS NDVI data (MOD13A1) using land cover classification from MODIS MCD12Q1. It generates FAPAR maps for a selected month and year over Estonia and produces seasonal FAPAR time series graphs based on user-defined land cover types and map clicks.
task_name: Calculate FAPAR from NDVI by land cover type

task_description: The script classifies land use types (built-up, vegetation, water, bare) in 2018 using Landsat 8 surface reflectance data and a Random Forest classifier trained on user-defined regions of interest. The output is a classified land use map and an accuracy assessment via confusion matrix and overall accuracy.
task_name: Classify land use with random forest

task_description: The script creates a median composite of Landsat 8 TOA reflectance for 2016, masks it using the UMD Hansen global forest change data to retain only land areas (excluding water), identifies water bodies from the mask, and generates a custom mosaic where the median image is overlaid with blue-colored water regions.

The script estimates Land Surface Temperature (LST) using top-of-atmosphere radiance, brightness temperature from Band 10, and emissivity correction derived from NDVI and vegetation proportion over a Landsat 8 pixel at 68.59, 27.62.

The script classifies land cover into three categories—urban, vegetation, and water—using a random forest classifier trained on Landsat 8 TOA reflectance bands. The output is a classified image map with urban in red, vegetation in green, and water in blue.

The script estimates surface soil moisture by combining time-series Sentinel-1 VV backscatter with Landsat 8 NDVI. It computes the difference between individual VV observations and a dry reference (minimum VV), normalizes this delta using NDVI-dependent scaling, and produces a final soil moisture map for November–December 2020.
task_name: Estimate soil moisture from SAR and NDVI

task_description: The script filters Landsat 8 TOA reflectance images from 2017 to 2018, applies a mask using the BQA (Band Quality Assessment) band where pixel values equal 2720—typically indicating high-confidence clear pixels—and computes the median composite of the masked image collection.

The script calculates the day of year with the highest pentadal precipitation for each year from 2015 to 2016 using CHIRPS data, and also computes the long-term average (LTA) timing of peak and minimum precipitation. It outputs images representing the day of year when maximum and minimum precipitation occurs based on quality-mosaic compositing over time.

The script analyzes ALOS PALSAR backscatter intensity (sigma0) in dB, filtered using coincident MODIS EVI from Landsat 7, to study vegetation characteristics over a specific region of interest between 2010-04-01 and 2010-06-29. It applies a refined Lee speckle filter to improve sigma0 data quality and computes median composites before and after filtering for comparison.

The script filters a 3-class land cover classification (Anthropogenic, Intensive, Shifting Agriculture) by removing small patches below 560 pixels (~50 hectares) using connected pixel count and replaces them with values derived from a 10-pixel radius focal mode filter, resulting in a smoothed land cover map.
task_name: Filter land cover patches by size and majority mode

task_description: The script calculates the beginning and ending days of the rainy season based on pentad CHIRPS precipitation data, identifies the length of the growing season, and computes long-term trends and coefficients of variation (CV) for these phenological metrics over South Asia between 1982 and 2019.
task_name: Estimate onset and cessation of rainy season

task_description: The script performs superpixel segmentation using the SNIC algorithm on a median composite image of South Sumatra, Indonesia, to generate homogeneous regions (clusters) and computes morphological properties including area, perimeter, width, height, and spectral standard deviation for each cluster.

The script processes Landsat 8 Surface Reflectance data to mask clouds and cloud shadows, filters images by date (2020), cloud cover (<20%), and sorts by cloudiness to identify the clearest image. It computes a median composite before and after cloud masking and extracts thermal band (B10) for surface temperature analysis.

The script identifies cloud-free pasture areas in Goiás, Brazil using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from January to March 2021, masked by MapBiomas land cover classification and filtered for low cloud coverage.

The script extracts MODIS NDVI data for the year 2019, filtering images within a specific date range and calendar month bounds derived from the dataset's metadata. It isolates the NDVI band and creates a filtered image collection for analysis, focusing on temporal segments within or overlapping 2019.

The script quantifies forest area lost to different anthropogenic drivers—specifically settlements, subsistence agriculture, and intensive agriculture—within the home range of a species (PH) across multiple West African countries (Ivory Coast, Liberia, Sierra Leone, Guinea) using classified land cover change data. It calculates areas in square meters and converts them to square kilometers, both for the full region and within designated protected areas. Additionally, it assesses original forest cover in 2000 at 1% and 50% canopy thresholds.

The script identifies surface water areas by summing JRC (Joint Research Centre) global surface water data from 2013 to 2015, applying a threshold mask (>40), and converting the resulting raster into vector polygons. It then extracts points from these vectors to represent water locations, producing a binary water mask, vectorized water bodies, and point representations of water features within the specified region.

The script identifies surface water areas by computing NDWI from Sentinel-2 imagery, applying Otsu thresholding to delineate water bodies, and calculating the total water-covered area in square kilometers within a specified polygon for November 2019.

The script classifies rice cultivation areas in the Sanjiang region for 2021 using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data and a support vector machine (SVM) classifier trained on labeled samples. It computes NDVI, generates a max-NDVI composite, and produces a classified rice map output masked to the region of interest.

The script classifies land cover into three classes (likely mangrove, water, and other) using Landsat-8 surface reflectance data and a Random Forest classifier trained on labeled sample points. It outputs a classified map, validation accuracy metrics (overall accuracy, kappa, error matrix), and area statistics per class in square kilometers.

The script identifies flooded agricultural areas by comparing pre- and post-flood Sentinel-1 SAR imagery, applying a median filter and thresholding on the difference to detect significant backscatter drops, and masking results with MODIS land cover data to isolate croplands (LC_Type1 = 12).

The script prepares a collection of Sentinel-2 surface reflectance images with less than 20% cloud cover within a specified study area and time range (2019), and loads a preprocessed NALCMS land cover dataset clipped to the same area. It does not perform classification or generate new land cover maps but sets up data for land cover analysis using Sentinel-2 and NALCMS.
task_name: Map land cover in study area

task_description: The script calculates daily accumulated precipitation by aggregating NASA GPM IMERG data over a specified region and time period using the 'precipitationCal' band, grouping images by their daily date attribute.

The script classifies land cover into urban, bare, water, and vegetation categories using a Random Forest classifier trained on Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from July 2020, producing a classified land cover map clipped to the input region.

The script classifies land cover types using optical satellite imagery and a Random Forest classifier trained on stratified samples. It outputs a classified land cover map with distinct categories including vegetation, water, urban areas, agriculture, bare land, and wetlands.

The script models the relationship between daytime land surface temperature (LST) and precipitation in Delaware from 2000 to 2020 using MODIS and GPM data, performing linear regression to estimate coefficients and residuals. The output includes mean LST and precipitation images, and a regional regression analysis.

The script identifies fire-affected areas by computing the difference in spectral indices (NDVI, SAVI, BAIS2, BAI, NBR) and reflectance bands between pre-fire and post-fire Sentinel-2 images, then classifies burned vs unburned regions using a Random Forest classifier trained on labeled samples. Three classification outputs are generated: one based on multispectral bands and vegetation indices, another on post-fire image only, and a third using burn-sensitive indices (BAIS2, BAI, NBR).
task_name: Identify fire-affected areas using spectral indices

task_description: The script identifies built-up (urban/constructed) areas in Surakarta, Indonesia, using NDBI (Normalized Difference Built-up Index) derived from atmospherically corrected Landsat 8 surface reflectance data from 2020. It classifies pixels with NDBI > 0 as built-up, converts the result into vector polygons, labels them as 'Bangunan' (Building) or 'Non Bangunan', and calculates the total built-up area in square kilometers.

The script maps the age of secondary forests in Brazil from 1986 to 2020 using annual land cover classifications from MapBiomas Collection 6, identifying forest regeneration after deforestation by analyzing temporal transitions and applying anthropogenic and water masks.

The script calculates the Normalized Difference Built-up Index (NDBI) using Landsat 8's shortwave infrared and near-infrared bands over a user-defined region, identifying built-up or urbanized surfaces based on spectral reflectance differences.

The script identifies wheat and rice cultivation areas in Uttar Pradesh using land cover classification from the GFSAD dataset, then generates stratified random sample points within those areas. It analyzes NDVI time series from Sentinel-2 data at one of the sample points to monitor vegetation dynamics over 2019.

The script classifies land cover types using a Random Forest classifier trained on spectral indices and surface reflectance bands from satellite imagery. It evaluates classification accuracy across different numbers of trees (10 to 500) and selects the 200-tree model based on validation performance, achieving up to 74% overall accuracy. The output includes classified land cover maps and area estimates (in hectares) per class within a defined region.

The script classifies land cover types using a Random Forest classifier trained on spectral indices and surface reflectance bands from satellite imagery, with training and validation points derived from 'mergedTable_total'. It produces a classified land cover map, evaluates accuracy using confusion and error matrices, and calculates the area (in hectares) of each land cover class within the 'homeRange_PH' region.
The script calculates monthly mean temperature by averaging minimum and maximum temperature from TerraClimate data, scaled by 0.1, for each month between 1990 and 2020.

The script classifies land cover types with a focus on human settlements, built-up areas, agriculture, and water bodies using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from 2016 and 2020. It applies supervised classification (Random Forest for 2016 and SVM for 2020) on training samples to generate thematic maps of settlement patterns over time.

The script trains a random forest classifier using a 70% training subset of labeled samples to classify land cover, then validates the model with a 30% validation subset, producing a confusion matrix and overall accuracy estimate.

The script identifies corn and soybean cultivation areas in Steele County, Iowa, by fitting a harmonic model to Sentinel-2 time series data (NDVI/EVI), computing first-order derivatives of the fitted signal, and generating spectral indices from peak and growth phase composites to distinguish crop types.
task_name: Identify corn and soybean areas using harmonic analysis

task_description: The script classifies land cover types in Aceh, Indonesia for the year 2019 using a Random Forest classifier trained on spectral, terrain, radar, and distance-based features derived from Landsat 8, elevation, and Sentinel-1 data. The output is a classified land cover map with 25 distinct classes including forest types, agroforestry systems, plantations, crops, settlements, and water bodies, validated using GPS sample points.

The script identifies wetland areas by calculating NDVI from Landsat 7 surface reflectance data for July–September 2002 and applying a threshold (t=0.36) to classify pixels as wetland where NDVI is greater than or equal to this value, resulting in a binary wetland extent map clipped to the AOI.

The script calculates annual forest cover, loss, and gain areas from 2001 to 2014 within protected areas in Guyana and Suriname using the Hansen Global Forest Change dataset, aggregating pixel-based area statistics per region.
task_name: Analyze forest loss and gain area

task_description: The script extracts land cover classification from the CORINE dataset for the year 2012, clips it to a user-defined region of interest (roi), and calculates the total area (in square meters) for each land cover class within that region using Earth Engine's reduceRegion with grouped sum. The output is a dictionary mapping each landcover class to its corresponding area, which is then set as a property of the dataset image.

The script detects changes in surface water extent by computing the NDWBI (Normalized Difference Water Body Index) from MSI imagery on two dates in June 2020, applying a threshold to identify water bodies, and calculating the difference between the binary water masks to highlight areas of change.

The script classifies double-cropped, single-cropped, and non-rice agricultural areas using VH-polarized Sentinel-1 SAR time series data from March to October 2022, applying a Random Forest classifier on backscatter intensity features. The output is a classified raster map of rice cultivation types and an area statistic within the study region.

The script classifies the statistical significance and direction of vegetation trends using p-values and trend slopes, producing a categorized map of six change types: extremely significant improvement, significant improvement, non-significant improvement, non-significant degradation, significant degradation, and extremely significant degradation.

The script creates a median composite of atmospherically corrected Landsat 8 TOA reflectance images from January to September 2019, applies cloud masking using the BQA band, and enhances spatial resolution through HSV-based pan-sharpening by fusing the 30-meter multispectral bands (B4, B3, B2) with the 15-meter panchromatic band (B8), resulting in a high-resolution natural color image for visual interpretation.

The script performs pan-sharpening on WorldView-3 multispectral imagery using the HPFA method, fusing high-resolution panchromatic bands with lower-resolution multispectral bands to produce higher spatial resolution color imagery. The output includes the sharpened image, a comparison of original and sharpened imagery, and RMSE-based quality assessment between resampled multispectral and sharpened outputs.

The script extracts the surface water extent for the year 2017 from the JRC Global Surface Water dataset, masks non-water areas (water class 2: 'Seasonal water'), clips to a region of interest (roi), and calculates the total area (in square meters) of seasonal water within that region.

The script calculates the volume of methane in the atmosphere by integrating methane column density from Sentinel-5P with elevation data from SRTM, likely to estimate dry air volume mixing ratios relative to topographic height. The function 'volumeCalc' is intended to process elevation and methane data over a given geometry, though it remains unimplemented.

The script classifies land use types using Landsat 8 surface reflectance data from 2020 to 2021, training a Random Forest classifier on labeled regions (Agricultural, Baierland, Rangeland, Residential, Riverbed, Waterbodies) and validating accuracy with independent test samples. The output is a classified land use map and its accuracy assessment including an error matrix and overall accuracy.

The script analyzes minimum temperature from GRIDMET and mean snow water equivalent (SWE) from TerraClimate within the Red HUC04 watershed boundary. It clips the temperature data to this region, computes long-term mean SWE, and performs zonal statistics to extract mean SWE values for U.S. counties intersecting the area. The output includes a clipped image of minimum temperature and a FeatureCollection of counties with mean SWE values.
task_name: Analyze minimum temperature and snow water equivalent in Red HUC04 region

task_description: The script estimates aboveground biomass (AGB) in Diamir District, Pakistan, using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data and a Random Forest regression model trained on field-measured AGB samples. It generates an AGB map, evaluates model performance with validation samples, and outputs variable importance, R², and RMSE metrics.

The script identifies persistent seasonal water bodies by combining Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data with the JRC Global Surface Water seasonality layer, masking for clouds and applying a normalized difference index (B3-B8) to refine surface water detection within the Piauí region.

The script identifies areas of forest decline in the SPB region by combining a binary forest mask from the SPB forest dataset with vegetation type classification to isolate forested areas, then excludes regions within 30 meters of roads and 90 meters of surface water, and further removes areas affected by fires after 2016, resulting in a refined mask of persistent forest decline regions not influenced by infrastructure, hydrology, or recent fire activity.
task_name: Identify forest decline areas excluding roads water and recent fires

task_description: The script estimates the optimal elevation of the snow line using the RSLE algorithm applied to NDSI snow cover data, evaluating elevation bands where snow presence and absence are minimized above and below a threshold. It outputs a time series of optimal snow line elevations and associated costs, along with a final classified annual snow analysis image.

The script analyzes surface reflectance statistics from Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8 imagery over a specified region and time period, generating median, mean, 20th percentile, and standard deviation composites for selected optical bands. It processes both Sentinel-2 Surface Reflectance (SR) and Top of Atmosphere (TOA) data, applies cloud masking, and computes multi-temporal summary statistics. Outputs include reduced image composites representing long-term spectral characteristics, primarily for land surface analysis such as vegetation, soil, and agricultural monitoring.

The script calculates the total annual precipitation for the year 2017 by summing daily precipitation values from the GRIDMET dataset, resulting in a single raster layer representing accumulated precipitation over the period.

The script creates a median composite of Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery from 2019, focusing on visible and near-infrared bands to represent land surface conditions around a specified point location.
task_name: Generate median composite for land observation

task_description: The script performs supervised land cover classification using Sentinel-2 imagery and a Random Forest classifier. It trains on labeled sample regions (vegetation, bare soil, buildings, water) to classify each pixel into one of these categories, then evaluates model accuracy using a confusion matrix, overall accuracy, and Kappa coefficient on a held-out test set.

The script classifies land cover types (urban, bare, water, vegetation) within a selected urban area using a median composite of Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from 2019 and a Random Forest classifier trained on ground control points.

The script generates a surface reflectance composite from Landsat Surface Reflectance data for Vermont in 2019, applies multiple preprocessing steps including cloud and shadow masking using Fmask, TDOM, and cloud scoring, and computes spectral indices (NDVI, carbonate index, rock outcrop index, clay index, ferrous index) and Tasseled Cap components (brightness, greenness, wetness) to create a multi-band predictor layer stack for mineral and vegetation analysis.
task_name: Extract mineral and vegetation indices from Landsat composite

task_description: The script estimates the long-term linear trend in sea surface height (SSH) over time using a time series regression analysis, modeling SSH changes in millimeters per year based on temporal and harmonic variables.

The script maps annual maximum tree canopy cover for 2015 using the NASA MEASURES GFCC TC v3 dataset, compositing images with qualityMosaic based on the 'tree_canopy_cover' band and clipping to a user-defined region of interest. The output is a single image representing maximum observed tree canopy cover in percent (0–100%) over the ROI.

The script classifies land cover into urban, bare, water, and vegetation categories using a Random Forest classifier trained on Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from 2019 over Bangalore. The output is a classified land cover map for the region.

The script detects areas affected by fire using the Normalized Burn Ratio (NBR) derived from Sentinel-2 imagery, comparing pre-fire and post-fire conditions between February 2019 and identifying burned regions based on a threshold of 0.3 difference in NBR.
The script processes monthly maximum temperature data from the TerraClimate dataset by scaling the values by a factor of 0.1 and preserving the timestamp property for each image in the collection.

The script retrieves the least cloudy Landsat 8 images from 2013 and 2022 over a specified point, creates true-color RGB composites, and applies panchromatic sharpening using the near-infrared band (B8) via HSV transformation to enhance spatial detail. The outputs are two pan-sharpened visualizations for 2013 and 2022, enabling visual comparison of land surface changes, particularly in urban or vegetated areas, with enhanced edge clarity.

The script classifies urban development intensity using nighttime lights from the DMSP-OLS sensor, applying a ternary expression to categorize areas into low, medium, and high development based on stable_lights values: pixels above 50 are set to 63, below 25 to 0, and others retain their original value.

The script analyzes the Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI) time series from Landsat 8 surface reflectance data over a specific biome boundary region, extracting mean EVI values within conservation units between 2012 and 2020. The output is a CSV file containing dates and corresponding EVI values for each feature in the region.

The script calculates the mean Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) for Brazil using Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data from 2019, applying cloud masking and spatial filtering, then outputs the average NDVI value over the country's geometry.

The script identifies water bodies by calculating the Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI) from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data, masking pixels with NDWI values above 0.4, and visually overlaying the result on a true-color image mosaic for a region around -70.48, 43.3631 in 2019.

The script computes and combines multiple vegetation and water-related spectral indices (NDVI, NDWI, EVI, SAVI, RGVI) from a median composite of Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data between May 31, 2015, and October 10, 2015, then calculates the mean pixel values within a specified geometry.

The script classifies land cover in the Zanjan region using median-composited Landsat 8 surface reflectance and thermal data from 2018, enhanced with NDVI and NDWI indices, trained on MODIS Land Cover Type 2 data via a random forest classifier, producing a classified land cover map.

The script calculates the mean UV aerosol layer height and methane-related aerosol data from Sentinel-5P observations between January 1, 2020, and January 30, 2020, then computes the standard deviation of aerosol height within the Mojave Desert region. Outputs are printed values of the standard deviation for UV and CH4 aerosol height.

The script analyzes vegetation health using NDVI, soil-adjusted vegetation index (SAVI), and water content using NDWI from Landsat 8 surface reflectance data over Chimborazo, Ecuador, in 2020. It generates three visualizations: natural color composite, NDVI, NDWI, and SAVI layers for ecological assessment.

The script classifies land cover into forest, pasture, and mining areas using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from June to August 2020. It trains a Random Forest classifier on spectral indices and fractions, applies post-classification filtering to remove noise, and evaluates accuracy with a confusion matrix and Kappa coefficient.

The script calculates the mean surface air temperature for the month of September over the years 2000 to 2019 within a specified area of interest, using NCEP/NCAR Reanalysis data. It outputs the mean temperature values for each year via reduceRegion.

The script creates a buffered representation of residential roads from OpenStreetMap data, converts it into a continuous area layer, reprojects it to a 5-meter resolution, and clips it to the administrative boundary containing the specified point. The output is a binary image indicating the spatial extent of residential roads within the AOI.

The script classifies urban land cover types using Sentinel-2 imagery by training a Random Forest classifier on manually defined feature collections representing different land cover classes (e.g., residential, industrial, vegetation, water). It computes EVI2 and NDBI indices, clips and masks images for clouds and borders, and evaluates classification accuracy using stratified sampling for training and testing. The final output is a classified land cover map with an associated error matrix and accuracy assessment.

The script filters Sentinel-2 surface reflectance images by cloud percentage and date range, then selects images intersecting a specified geometry. It is likely used to analyze vegetation or land cover using spectral indices, given the use of cloud-filtered optical data over a growing season.

The script detects land cover changes between 2015 and 2019 using spectral indices (NDVI, NDMI, NDWI, SAVI, NBR) derived from segmented satellite imagery. It computes a Change Magnitude (CM) index, normalizes it (NCM), and evaluates its effectiveness in distinguishing changed versus unchanged areas using GPS sample points with a ROC analysis to determine an optimal threshold for change classification.

The script analyzes vegetation, water, bare soil, snow, and burned areas in Stockholm and surrounding regions using Landsat 8 spectral indices including NDVI, EVI, NDWI, NDWBI, NDBI, BAI, NBRT, and NDSI derived from specific date-filtered imagery.
task_name: Analyze urban vegetation and land cover

task_description: The script filters a forest/non-forest dataset for the period from 2014 to 2015, computes the maximum value across time to derive persistent forest presence, and then identifies non-forest areas by applying a threshold (values less than 2), resulting in a binary layer where non-forest pixels are highlighted.

The script identifies vegetation-covered areas in Henan by computing NDVI from Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data between June and October 2016, then composites the highest-quality pixels based on NDVI values and clips the result to the Henan region.

The script calculates the area of tree cover in the year 2000 and annual forest loss from 2001 to 2015 for Guyana and Suriname, using pixel-based area computation in hectares. It filters protected areas by country (GUY, SUR) and excludes marine regions, then computes tree cover extent and forest loss area by multiplying binary masks with pixel area.
task_name: Map tree cover and loss area

task_description: The script models the probability of species habitat presence using Maxent classification on Landsat 8 surface reflectance bands, trained with presence/absence point data, and outputs a classified probability map.

The script calculates total biological production (TBP) by scaling NPP values, adjusting them by dekadal duration, and aggregating into yearly sums. The final output is the mean of yearly TBP images, representing long-term average dry matter productivity in kg/ha.

The script calculates the mean cloud fraction over North America for July 2010, masks pixels with cloud fraction below a threshold, and estimates the number of days with low cloud cover by scaling the count of such images to a 30-day period.

The script detects and maps forest disturbances caused by specific biotic agents (e.g., insect infestations, diseases) using LandTrendr-based time-series analysis of Landsat spectral indices (NBR, TCB, TCG, TCW) and overlays with ADS (Aerial Detection Survey) data to identify spatial patterns of defoliation and mortality. Outputs include annual dNBR change images, segmented disturbance zones, and visualizations of agent-specific impact layers.

The script generates a median composite of Sentinel-2A Surface Reflectance images from January 2020 to December 2021, masked for clouds and cirrus using the QA60 band, filtered by less than 20% cloud coverage, and normalized by dividing by 10,000, resulting in a cloud-free surface reflectance image over the specified area.
The script computes NDVI, MNDWI, and SAVI indices from Sentinel-2 imagery over Geneva to analyze vegetation health and surface water extent, using median composite of cloud-filtered images from 2019.

The script normalizes a stack of 37 biophysical, socioeconomical, and institutional environmental variables to a 0–1 scale using min-max scaling within the Gran Chaco region, producing a standardized dataset for spatial modeling and analysis. Outputs include a raw stacked image (set_datos), a normalized version (set_datos_escal_0_1), and a CSV point sample dataset extracted from the raster stack.

The script computes a median composite of Sentinel-2A/B surface reflectance data, masked for cloud coverage and clipped to a region of interest (Subae), scaled by 0.0001 to convert to reflectance units, intended for land surface analysis such as vegetation or crop monitoring.
task_name: Analyze surface reflectance in agricultural areas

task_description: The script classifies land cover types, specifically forest, water, crop, urban, and plantations, using Sentinel-2 imagery from 2017 and a Random Forest classifier trained on reference data. It outputs a classified land cover map and evaluates classification accuracy with a confusion matrix, overall accuracy, producer's accuracy, consumer's accuracy, and kappa coefficient.
The script identifies vegetation and surface water areas in Tainan using MNDWI, NDBI, and NDVI indices derived from a cloud-filtered Landsat 8 surface reflectance mosaic from 2013.
The script selects the least cloudy Sentinel-2 satellite image within a specified date range and spatial region in China, sorted by cloud coverage, and prints the resulting image metadata.

The script classifies land cover types in the Gayo region using a Random Forest classifier trained on a stacked composite of Landsat 8-derived brightness, wetness, greenness indices, topographic variables (elevation, slope, aspect), and land surface temperature from three seasonal periods (normal, rainy, dry seasons) in 2018.

The script analyzes the median NDVI values across California from May to September for each year between 2000 and 2019, generating a composite image representing long-term vegetation greenness patterns in the region.

The script classifies land cover types in the Arkavathy basin using a Random Forest classifier trained on Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from 2019 to 2020, with ground control points split into training and validation sets; it outputs a classified land cover map and evaluates accuracy using a confusion matrix and overall accuracy metric.

The script classifies land cover into four classes—Closed Forest, Open Forest, Shrubs, and Bareland—using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance and Sentinel-1 VH backscatter data across four seasonal periods in 2019–2020. It trains a Random Forest classifier using labeled field data and evaluates accuracy with confusion matrices, producing a classified map and accuracy metrics including overall accuracy, producer's/consumer's accuracy, and kappa coefficient.

The script generates a sequence of dates from January 1981 to December 2022 by mapping over years and months, and performs various list manipulation operations including mathematical transformations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division) on numeric lists using Earth Engine's functional programming model. It also demonstrates the use of dictionaries within mapped functions to return multiple computed values per element.
task_name: Apply list operations and date generation

task_description: The script identifies areas of forest recovery in regions defined by a feature collection (df) after 2017, using MapBiomas Collection 5.0 land cover classification for 2019, specifically detecting pixels classified as class 3 (forest) and calculating the total area (in km²) of forest recovery per region ID.

The script calculates monthly NDWI (Normalized Difference Water Index) from Sentinel-2 imagery in 2018 for the Narmada Basin (BASIN_ID: 258706), applies a water threshold (0.05) to detect surface water, and generates a composite water occurrence intensity map showing how frequently water is detected across the year.

The script maps land surface vegetation using surface reflectance data from Landsat 8, applying cloud and shadow masking to produce a median composite for the year 2016, clipped to the Shushufindi area of interest.
The script calculates mean elevation values from SRTM data within selected provinces of Indonesia, specifically those containing 'Jawa' in their name, and outputs regional statistics.

The script calculates the normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) using the median composite of Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery from August 15 to September 15, 2021, over a specified area of interest (AOI), then extracts the minimum NDVI value within that region.

The script identifies permanent and temporary surface water bodies using percentile-based MNDWI analysis from Landsat data between 2016-01-01 and 2016-12-31, applying cloud masking, HAND terrain filtering, and NDVI vegetation masking to improve accuracy.
task_name: Map permanent and temporary water bodies

task_description: The script classifies land cover types using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data by applying a rule-based classification (PINO1/PINO2) to identify features such as water, clouds, snow, dense evergreen forests, deciduous vegetation, shrubs, grasslands, and bare soil across a defined region of interest. The output is a classified raster map (image) labeled with distinct land cover classes based on spectral thresholds and indices.

The script analyzes changes in vegetation between 2000 and 2020 using EVI derived from Landsat 7 and Landsat 8 surface reflectance data, identifying areas of significant vegetation loss (EVI decrease > 0.2) and gain (EVI increase > 0.2).

The script estimates surface soil moisture (SSM) using Sentinel-1 VV polarization backscatter time series. It computes a sensitivity index based on the 5th and 95th percentiles of the backscatter distribution, then derives SSM for October 2019 by normalizing a median image between dry and wet references, scaling to a 0–100% range. Outputs include despeckled VV images, sensitivity layers, and SSM maps.
task_name: Estimate soil moisture from Sentinel-1 VV

task_description: The script generates 1000 random points within a defined polygon, extracts mean DSM (Digital Surface Model) values from the ALOS AW3D30 dataset at these points, computes the mean and standard deviation of the sampled elevation values, and performs inverse distance weighted interpolation to create a continuous interpolated elevation surface from the sample points.

The script maps monthly surface water extent by applying a probabilistic water classification model using annual and monthly composites, thresholds, and environmental constants. It generates a final water product based on scene probability, temporal filtering, and gap-filling logic, comparing results with a reference water layer from MapBiomas AGUA.

The script estimates Land Surface Temperature (LST) from Landsat 8 thermal bands (B10, B11) using atmospheric water vapor correction from NCEP Reanalysis data, emissivity modeling based on NDVI-derived vegetation cover, and a split-window algorithm. The output is a time series of LST values in Kelvin at the specified point.

The script calculates an Ecosystem Service Value (ESV) map by reclassifying MODIS Land Use/Land Cover (LC_Type1) data into corresponding ESV coefficients for Sumatera, Indonesia, using a predefined lookup table. The output is a continuous raster representing estimated economic value per land cover type.
task_name: Reclassify land cover to ESV values

task_description: The script creates a cloud-free Landsat 8 surface reflectance mosaic by masking both clouds and cloud shadows using the pixel_qa band from the Landsat Collection 1 Tier 1 Surface Reflectance dataset over a specified region between 2013 and 2018.

The script classifies land cover in Bangalore into four categories (likely built-up, bare soil, water, and vegetation) using a pre-computed classified image from 2019 and calculates the area of one class (gray cover, likely built-up areas) within the city boundary.

The script calculates NDVI using the near-infrared (B5) and red (B4) bands from Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data collected between December 2021 and March 2022, filtered by cloud cover and region of interest, to assess vegetation greenness.

The script retrieves Sentinel-2 surface reflectance image collections for a specific point location during summer months of 2019 and 2021, then merges them for comparative analysis of surface conditions across the two time periods.

The script computes a cloud score for Landsat 5 TOA images between July and September 2000, then generates a cloud-free mosaic by selecting pixels with the lowest cloud score (highest quality) and clips the result to a user-defined area of interest.

The script evaluates the accuracy of land cover classification for the PAMPA biome in 2017 by comparing classified map data from MapBiomas Collection 3.1 with stratified validation samples across seven regions. It computes error matrices and generates accuracy assessment tables per region, focusing on specific classes such as forest, wetlands, grasslands, agriculture, non-vegetated areas, rocky outcrops, and water.

The script calculates NDVI, EVI, EVI2, and SAVI vegetation indices from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data and adds them as bands to each image in the collection for the period between 2016 and 2019 over a region in Brazil.

The script extracts MODIS Land Surface Temperature (LST) data for Delaware between 2000 and 2020, converts Kelvin values to Celsius, clips to the state boundary, and prepares the collection with time and constant bands for further analysis such as trend modeling.

The script analyzes the impact of a fire event on vegetation by comparing NDVI values from pre-fire, during-fire, and post-fire Landsat 8 images over a specific location in Oregon, using both radiometrically corrected (RT) and surface reflectance (SR) data to assess burn severity and vegetation recovery.

The script classifies land cover types using a CART classifier trained on Landsat 8 surface reflectance data from 2016, with training labels from a user-provided feature collection, and evaluates the classification accuracy using a confusion matrix derived from test samples.
