The script performs a supervised classification of land cover types (Water, Forest, Agriculture, Pastizal, Pasture) using median-composite Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery from September to December 2019 over a user-defined region (ID=3). It computes NDVI, trains a Random Forest classifier on labeled samples, applies the model to classify the study area, validates accuracy with an error matrix, and estimates the area (in hectares) for each class.

The script creates a multi-temporal SAR composite from Sentinel-1 data, combining mean VH and VV backscatter from ascending passes during two distinct periods (2014–2016 and 2018–2020) over a small polygon in southern hemisphere, likely for monitoring surface structural and moisture changes.
task_name: Generate SAR composite for surface analysis

task_description: The script identifies areas with high vegetation cover using NDVI derived from Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data collected in 2017, applying a threshold (NDVI > 0.7) to isolate dense vegetation, and computes the total area of such regions within a specified ROI.

The script performs supervised land cover classification using a Random Forest classifier on an input image, training with 70% of labeled sample points and validating with the remaining 30%. It outputs a classified land cover map, confusion matrix, overall accuracy, and kappa coefficient to evaluate classification performance.

The script identifies areas of high vegetation cover by computing the maximum NDVI from Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data over a one-year period and applying a threshold (NDVI > 0.6) to isolate densely vegetated regions within a buffered region of interest.

The script identifies wet snow areas by computing the difference between two Sentinel-1 SAR images (July and January 2019) over a region in Chile, applying focal median filtering to reduce noise, and thresholding the VV backscatter difference (values < -3 dB) to detect wet snow presence.

The script calculates the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery over a specific area of interest between October 2018 and October 2019, producing a time series of NDVI-enhanced images for vegetation monitoring.

The script classifies forested areas using time-series Sentinel-1 SAR imagery from March 2020 to February 2021, applying a Random Forest classifier trained on labeled samples, and evaluates accuracy with validation data. The output is a classified land cover map with forest detection and variable importance analysis.

The script filters a Sentinel-1 GRD image collection over a specified AOI and time range, applying speckle edge masking to remove low-backscatter pixels (likely noise or water edges), and outputs the masked VV/VH polarized radar imagery for flood-related surface analysis.
task_name: Filter SAR imagery for flood monitoring

task_description: The script detects water bodies and extracts coastlines using Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-1 data over a specified geometry, applying AWEI-based thresholding and morphological filtering to identify seasonal water extent and shoreline changes. It also computes water area and performs accuracy assessment using reference binary masks.

The script classifies land cover types using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery and a CART decision tree classifier, trained on ESA WorldCover 2020 reference data within a region of interest in California. It evaluates model performance with stratified training and validation samples and outputs a classified land cover map along with accuracy assessments.

The script calculates the yearly occurrence of burned areas by summing MODIS MCD64A1 BurnDate images from 2001 to 2019, converting each year's burn detection into a binary layer (burned/not burned), and then counts how many times each pixel was classified as burned across the time series. The output is an image collection of annual burned area masks and a frequency map showing the number of burning events per pixel over 19 years.

The script analyzes land cover change from pasture to annual crops between 2006 and 2016 using classified land cover maps. It computes the area of conversion, identifies unchanged annual crops, and calculates the extent of annual crop areas in both years.
task_name: Analyze Pasture to Annual Crop Change

task_description: The script analyzes annual greenness and fitted residual trends using a boolean change detection approach over the Xilinhot region from 1987 to 2017, identifying areas of persistent vegetation change. It outputs CSV files containing mean boolean change values, median fitted residuals with percentiles, and median greenness with percentiles within a specified change window (e.g., 2017), along with pixel area statistics for the change period.

The script calculates the difference in Normalized Burn Ratio (dNBR) between two Landsat 8 images from March and August 2015 to analyze changes in vegetation condition, likely related to fire impact or seasonal vegetation dynamics.

The script identifies connected components in an image, calculates their area using pixel count and pixel area, and masks out objects smaller than 5000 square meters. It outputs a labeled map of objects that meet the minimum mapping unit (MMU) threshold.

The script identifies areas with persistent shade and low green vegetation/soil cover across multiple years using MapBiomas mosaic data, combining annual conditions to compute frequency of occurrence, then aggregates results into vector objects clipped to grid cells, calculating mean frequency per object and assigning hydrographic basin identifiers (levels 1–3) based on point sampling within each object.

The script identifies water bodies using the AWEI index from a Landsat 8 surface reflectance composite between May and October 2015, applies Otsu thresholding to delineate water, fills small gaps in land and water features, and extracts the coastline as both a raster and vector output clipped to the specified geometry.

The script computes NDWI from Landsat 8 surface reflectance data to generate a median composite and a quality mosaic (maximum NDWI) representing typical and maximum water extent, respectively, over a region near latitude 38.45 and longitude -8.8 between 2016 and 2018.
task_name: Map surface water extent using NDWI

task_description: The script classifies burned areas (fire scars) by training a Random Forest classifier on spectral indices (NDVI, NDWBI, NDSI, NDWI, NBR) and Landsat 8 surface reflectance bands. It outputs a classified raster map labeled as 'Cicatrices de fuego' (burn scars), distinguishing between two classes—likely burned vs unburned land—based on manually defined training points (cicatrices and no_cicatrices).
task_name: Classify fire scars using Landsat indices

task_description: The script computes a mean image from a filtered image collection over a specific time period and region, applies a threshold (>=0.5) to create a binary layer, then converts the resulting binary regions into vector polygons labeled as 'CropType1'. The final output is a histogram of the 'CropType1' classes, indicating the distribution of crop types derived from the classified cultivated areas.

The script computes NDVI from Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data between February and September 2015, then creates a composite image representing the greenest (highest NDVI) pixels over that period using qualityMosaic. It calculates the mean NDVI value within a specified geometry.

The script calculates hourly wind speed and wind direction at 10 meters above ground level from ERA5-Land reanalysis data for a specific region and time period (2020-09-04 to 2020-09-06 at 12:00 UTC), using u and v components of wind, then clips the results to a user-defined geometry and prints the wind direction collection.

The script calculates the Normalized Difference Chlorophyll Index (NDCI) from Landsat 5 and 7 surface reflectance data, applies cloud and water masking using pixel QA and NDWI, and computes the standard deviation of NDCI across the combined time series to assess temporal variability of chlorophyll-related water quality in water bodies within the region of interest.
task_name: Analyze NDCI variability in water bodies

task_description: The script computes monthly mean synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images from Sentinel-1 GRD data, combining VV, VH polarizations and their squared difference (VH-VV)² over a defined area of interest, to analyze temporal changes in surface scattering characteristics likely related to land cover dynamics.

The script identifies non-forest areas in the Amazon biome by analyzing a time series of land classification data and applying spectral mixture analysis (SMA) and Normalized Difference Fraction Index (NDFI) on Sentinel-2 imagery. It first masks out classified forest (class 3) from historical classifications, then computes NDFI from unmixed fractions (green vegetation, non-photosynthetic vegetation, soil) to detect persistent non-forest surfaces based on a threshold (NDFI ≤ 175). The final output is a binary mask of non-forest regions derived from median NDFI values before a target date.

The script detects harmful algal blooms (HABs) in a water body using Landsat 8 Surface Reflectance data by computing the AFAI (Algae Fractional Abundance Index) and MNDWI (Modified Normalized Difference Water Index). It calculates the area (in km²) of detected algal blooms within a specified vector boundary for each image in the date range, applying cloud masking and thresholding (AFAI > threshold and MNDWI >= 0). The output includes the HABs area per image and prints it.

The script creates a median composite image from a satellite image collection filtered by region, date (2018–2019), and minimal cloud cover (<1%), intended for clear-surface analysis of land features.

The script calculates the total area of forest loss per year within the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) using the Hansen Global Forest Change dataset. It outputs a grouped reduction result showing the sum of forest loss area for each loss year.

The script classifies land cover into five classes (natural water, anthropogenic water, hydrography, bare soil/mining, and false positive objects) using a Random Forest classifier trained on labeled feature collections for a specific Brazilian biome and year. The output is a classified raster image where each pixel is assigned a class based on spectral, morphological, and temporal features.

The script creates a multi-temporal composite of Sentinel-1 GRD HH backscatter imagery from five consecutive years (2016–2020) during the March–October growing season, computing annual mean images and combining them into an RGB composite where each color channel represents the average HH backscatter intensity of a different year. This enables visual interpretation of long-term surface changes, particularly in land cover dynamics such as agriculture, deforestation, or urban expansion.

The script classifies land cover into four classes—open water, bare fields, vegetation, and forest—using Sentinel-1 SAR (VV/VH) and Landsat 8 surface reflectance data from August 2019. It trains Random Forest classifiers on fused optical and radar features and produces three classification maps: SAR-only, optical-only, and combined optical/SAR, evaluating accuracy via confusion matrices.
task_name: Classify land cover types using SAR and optical data

task_description: The script processes a time series of Sentinel-1 GRD VV polarization images to generate a three-layer stack representing mean backscatter over three distinct periods in 2016. It applies the Refined Lee speckle filter to reduce noise and compares the results with boxcar-filtered outputs, enabling improved interpretation of land surface changes using radar imagery.

The script trains a Random Forest classifier using terrain, vegetation, moisture, and precipitation variables to model landslide susceptibility. It generates three outputs: a susceptibility map from training data (SIfit), a validation map using spatial cross-validation (SIValid), and a prediction map on an independent grid (SIpred). It evaluates model performance via confusion matrix, ROC curve, AUC, and binary classification (true/false positives) against known landslide occurrences.

The script identifies forested areas affected by fires using thermal anomalies from FIRMS data and land cover classification from CORINE, then extracts post-fire vegetation boundaries using Landsat imagery.

The script classifies land cover types in the Asahan Toba watershed using median surface reflectance from Landsat 8 SR data between 2018 and 2020, applying a Random Forest classifier trained on user-defined regions of interest for various land cover classes.

The script applies a threshold on the Near-Infrared band (B4) of a Landsat 5 TOA reflectance image to create a water mask, then masks out pixels below the threshold (assumed water) from the original image, resulting in a water-excluded visual composite.
task_name: Mask water bodies using NIR threshold

task_description: The script evaluates the accuracy of water classification by comparing three different water masks (mask1_clip, mask2_clip, mask3_clip) against a reference water layer (mask_RIF) using confusion matrix components: true positives (tp), true negatives (tn), false positives (fp), and false negatives (fn). It calculates pixel counts for each category to assess classification performance.

The script calculates the minimum and maximum values of shortwave black-sky albedo (Albedo_WSA_shortwave) from MODIS MCD43B3 data for the year 2016, outputting the reduced pixel-wise min and max as printed values.
task_name: Extract annual albedo minimum and maximum

task_description: The script generates a time series of Sentinel-2 images, computes vegetation and moisture indices (EVI, REP, LSWI), applies temporal smoothing, and extracts spectral features at sample points to create a training dataset for crop yield estimation. The final output is a CSV file containing smoothed vegetation index values linked to yield measurements at field locations.
task_name: Estimate crop yield from vegetation indices

task_description: The script applies radiometric terrain correction to Sentinel-1 GRD imagery by modeling local incidence angle, correcting for volumetric scattering effects, and identifying layover and shadow areas using SRTM-derived slope and aspect. Outputs include terrain-corrected gamma nought (γ⁰) in dB for VV and VH polarizations, their ratio, and ancillary layers for topographic corrections.
task_name: Correct SAR backscatter for terrain effects

task_description: The script classifies land cover types using a Random Forest classifier trained on Landsat 8 surface reflectance data and topographic variables, producing classified maps for multiple years (2014–2018) over a user-defined area. Training and validation are performed using labeled point samples, and classification accuracy is assessed via confusion matrices.

The script classifies land cover types using Landsat 8 surface reflectance data from 2019, computing NDVI and EVI vegetation indices, training a Random Forest classifier on labeled samples, and producing a classified land cover map which is then filtered with a focal mode operation. The output includes the classified image, accuracy assessment via confusion matrix, and area calculation per class in hectares.

The script analyzes temporal changes in SAR backscatter from Sentinel-1 data over a wetland area in Alberta, Canada, by computing multi-temporal despeckled VV and VH Gamma0-corrected imagery for summer and fall seasons, then deriving delta (difference) images between them to detect surface moisture or structural changes. Outputs are mean summer VV, VH, their despeckled versions, and the difference (delta) between summer and fall despeckled backscatter for wetland monitoring.

The script classifies land cover into forest, urban, and agriculture categories using a random forest classifier trained on Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data within a specified region of interest in Japan for the year 2019.

The script identifies landslide-affected areas by comparing pre- and post-event Sentinel-1 SAR (VV) and Sentinel-2 optical imagery over Glacier Bay, applying Refined Lee filtering to SAR data, computing backscatter and reflectance differences, and extracting change zones through thresholding and vectorization. Outputs include mapped landslide polygons from both S1 and S2 data with area calculations.
task_name: Identify landslide areas using SAR and optical imagery

task_description: The script classifies rice cultivation areas in Kurigram district using a Random Forest classifier trained on Landsat 8 surface reflectance bands and FABDEM elevation data, generating a probability-based classification map for the winter season of 2020.

The script identifies vegetation areas by thresholding the near-infrared band (N) of a NAIP image after scaling, then applies morphological operations (median, mode, min, max, opening, and closing) to refine the binary vegetation mask. The output includes visualizations of the original image, median-filtered image, and multiple binary vegetation layers processed with neighborhood reducers.

The script calculates the standard deviation of monthly surface water area across the Paraguay River basin subbasins from 1985 to 2019, using annual feature collections that contain monthly water area properties, producing a spatial map of temporal water extent variability.

The script computes a weighted spectral index from MSS bands (B1–B4), normalizes it using percentile-based scaling, then calculates GLCM texture metrics (contrast and correlation) at two different neighborhood sizes (4 and 1). The outputs are 8-bit integer texture layers for visual analysis and further processing, specifically focusing on spatial patterns of surface roughness and pixel coherence in historical MSS imagery.
task_name: Analyze MSS-derived texture contrast and correlation

task_description: The script classifies land cover changes in Colombia between 2016 and 2018 using CCDC-derived harmonic coefficients and ancillary topographic data, producing a stratification map that identifies forest loss, forest gain, herbaceous persistence, and conversion areas based on time-series Landsat analysis.

The script classifies land cover types using Landsat 5 surface reflectance data from 2007 to 2009, applying a CART classifier trained on sample regions representing different land cover classes within the ABT_30HILLS area.

The script generates a time series of flood inundation maps for Jamalpur District, Bangladesh, using Sentinel-1 SAR imagery. It computes total flooded area (in m²) and fractional flooded area relative to the district's geometry by applying a flood detection algorithm between specified baseline dates and each image's acquisition date.

The script maps annual burned areas in Peru from 2009 to 2018 using MODIS MCD64A1 Burn Date data, applying a quality mask to retain only valid burn detections, clipping results to the Peruvian boundary, and calculating the pixel count of burned areas per year.

The script estimates a continuous variable 'y' (likely a biophysical or agricultural parameter such as crop yield or biomass) by training a random forest regression model on Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data with custom spectral indices (a=f(B4/B3), b=B5/B3, c=B3-B4, d=B3/B4, e=B3/B5, f=B3/B1) over a specified region. The output is a classified (predicted) continuous surface derived from the trained model applied to median composite imagery.
task_name: Estimate crop yield using spectral indices

task_description: The script identifies areas of vegetation loss by analyzing temporal differences in VH-polarized Sentinel-1 SAR backscatter between filtered mosaics from three time periods (2017–2018 and 2018–2019), applying thresholds to difference images, masking results, and computing loss area statistics within a region of interest.

The script detects burned areas by computing the difference in Normalized Burn Ratio (dNBR) between pre- and post-fire periods using Landsat 8 and 9 TOA reflectance data, applying cloud masking and focal filtering to improve accuracy.

The script detects vegetation disturbance events using the LandTrendr algorithm on a time series of satellite imagery, analyzing changes in the NBR (Normalized Burn Ratio) index between 1993 and 2021. It generates two primary outputs: a 'Year of Detection' (yod) layer identifying when the change occurred, and a 'Magnitude of Change' (mag) layer showing the severity of the disturbance. The output is masked to exclude clouds, shadows, snow, and water, and filtered based on statistical significance, recovery patterns, and minimum observation requirements.

The script analyzes land cover transitions over time by comparing classified land cover images from two different periods (1984–1989 and 2009–2014), computing a transition matrix that quantifies changes between classes using sampled points.

The script identifies surface water extent and calculates the frequency of water occurrence over time by applying Otsu's thresholding method to MNDWI (Modified Normalized Difference Water Index) derived from Landsat 5/7/8 surface reflectance data between 2018 and 2020, producing a cumulative water frequency map for the region of interest.

The script calculates the Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI) from Landsat 7 Surface Reflectance data over a specific county in 2018, applying cloud and shadow masking, and adds a time variable for trend analysis. Outputs include a time series of EVI images and associated metadata.

The script performs a supervised land cover classification using Sentinel-2 TOA data and Random Forest algorithm to distinguish between forest and non-forest areas within a user-defined region of interest. It outputs a classified raster, accuracy assessments (confusion matrix, overall accuracy, producer/user accuracy), and vectorized polygons from the classification result.

The script generates a thematic map of surface moisture for Peru between August and September 2020 using Sentinel-2 data, calculating the Normalized Difference Moisture Index (NDMI) to highlight areas with high moisture content such as lakes, wetlands, snowfields, and vegetated regions through evapotranspiration.

The script identifies areas where forest cover was lost between 2001 and 2020 and subsequently converted to agricultural land by combining a forest loss layer with an agricultural land use map, producing a spatial output highlighting these transformation zones in yellow.
task_name: Identify forest loss converted to agriculture

task_description: The script evaluates the accuracy of a land cover classification image by comparing classified pixels against reference points, computing an error matrix, and generating a confusion table with relative proportions for specific classes: forest, other vegetation, farming, bare soil, and water.

The script processes Sentinel-1 GRD data to compute the mean VV-polarized radar backscatter over a specified region and time period, focusing on descending IW mode acquisitions. The output is a single mean image representing average VV intensity, which can be used for monitoring surface structure and moisture under all-weather conditions.

The script calculates the Perpendicular Drought Index (PDI) using red and near-infrared bands from a Sentinel-2 surface reflectance composite, with top-of-atmosphere scaling corrected by dividing by 10000. The output is a PDI band added to the image.

The script analyzes the expansion of impervious surfaces between 2000 and 2018, specifically within areas affected by satellite-observed flooding, and computes the total area of increased imperviousness in U.S. states, highlighting regions where urban development has encroached on floodplains.
task_name: Identify impervious surface change in flood-prone areas

task_description: The script identifies transitions between land and water in the Amazon region using MapBiomas land cover classification data from 1985 to 2017, specifically detecting gain and loss of water by comparing classified images across user-selected years.

The script detects coastal water bodies and extracts coastlines using Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 optical imagery from 2018 to 2019. It applies Otsu thresholding on AWEI for water detection, performs morphological filtering to refine land-water masks, computes coastline vectors, and evaluates classification accuracy against a reference binary mask. Outputs include monthly water masks, coastline layers, area calculations in km², and confusion matrix components (tp, tn, fp, fn) for validation.

The script classifies land cover into vegetation and buildings using Random Forest classification on Landsat surface reflectance data from 1988, 1998, 2008, and 2018. It computes mean NDVI for vegetation areas and counts of building pixels over time to analyze changes in vegetation health and urban expansion.

The script identifies water bodies in the Progo River Basin by combining NDWI analysis with reflectance thresholds from Landsat 8 surface reflectance bands, specifically using B7 and B5 for additional water masking.
task_name: Identify water bodies using NDWI and reflectance

task_description: The script creates median composites and mosaics of Sentinel-2 imagery for Delhi, India, for 2019 and 2020, filtered by cloud cover and date, to produce cloud-reduced visualizations of surface reflectance.

The script calculates soil abundance in a region by applying spectral mixture analysis (SMA) to Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data, using unmixed fractions of endmembers (green vegetation, non-photographic vegetation, soil, cloud), and generates a binary layer identifying areas with soil fraction greater than or equal to 25%.
task_name: Identify soil abundance from spectral unmixing

task_description: The script detects vegetation change in Botswana (BWA) using the LandTrendr algorithm applied to NBR time series from 2000 to 2020, generating a change map with year of detection and magnitude, focusing on significant changes exceeding a threshold of 900 in magnitude.

The script identifies small water bodies (ponds) in Bangladesh using Sentinel-2 imagery from 2018 by combining multiple water indices (NDWI, MNDWI, AWEI), applying Otsu thresholding, and filtering based on spatial morphological features and area thresholds.

The script analyzes a single Sentinel-2 scene from August 2019 to generate true-color and false-color composites, compute NDVI for vegetation assessment, and calculate NDWI with masking to identify surface water features. Outputs include visualizations of the true-color image, false-color composite, NDVI map with a color palette indicating vegetation density, and a masked NDWI layer highlighting water bodies.

The script computes the mean VV polarization backscatter from Sentinel-1 GRD imagery over a specific point location, producing a single composite image representing average radar reflectivity under ascending IW mode passes.

The script classifies land cover types for the year 1999 using Landsat 5 surface reflectance data, training a Random Forest classifier on labeled sample points representing different land cover classes (Agriculture, Plantation, Native vegetation, Harvested areas, Sand, Urban, Water, Other), and evaluates classification accuracy with confusion matrices for both training and testing partitions.

The script classifies water and land areas in Zhejiang using Landsat 5 surface reflectance data from 1989 to 1991, trained with labeled sample points and a Random Forest classifier, producing a water-land classification map.

The script assesses the impact of a wildfire event near Pignola, Italy, in August 2017 by computing pre- and post-fire spectral indices (NDVI, NBR, GRVI) from Sentinel-2 imagery. It calculates dNBR and dGRVI to quantify burn severity and derives rGRVI (relative GRVI) as a normalized measure of vegetation change. The final output is a CSV file containing mean rGRVI values per region from feature collection 'table7', representing spatially aggregated fire impact metrics.

The script analyzes vegetation changes over time by computing the Normalized Burn Ratio (NBR) and its difference (dNBR) from Landsat 5, 7, and 8 surface reflectance data, prioritizing images by sensor type and acquisition month to select optimal seasonal composites per year.

The script analyzes land cover transitions in tropical moist forests between 2005 and 2015 using annual land cover change data from the JRC TMF dataset, identifying specific pathways such as undisturbed forest to degraded forest, deforestation, and regrowth, with distinct visualizations for each transition type.
task_name: Detect forest degradation and deforestation transitions

task_description: The script analyzes time-series Sentinel-1 SAR backscatter (VV and VH) from monthly composites over forested areas (>50% tree cover in 2000, excluding loss areas) to compute mode and standard deviation within grid cells for each month of 2017, outputting a feature collection with per-grid temporal statistics.

The script identifies fishponds by classifying water bodies based on morphological and spatial features (area, perimeter, IPQ, SOLI, PFD, CONV, SQP) derived from Sentinel-2 imagery and validated using a CART classifier trained on labeled fishpond and non-fishpond polygons. The output includes classified fishponds, validation accuracy metrics, and filtered results based on area thresholds.

The script calculates the Burn Area Index (BAI) from a Sentinel-2 image to detect burned regions, applies a water mask derived from NDWI, and uses morphological operations on NDVI to refine vegetation coverage. The output includes visualizations of the original image, unmasked BAI, and water-masked BAI for analysis.

The script calculates and compares NDVI values from Landsat 5 (2010) and Landsat 8 (2020) imagery over the same geographic area, computing the difference in vegetation index to assess changes in vegetation health or cover over a decade.

The script classifies land cover types in the Rocha region for 2018 using Sentinel-2 imagery and a Random Forest classifier trained on user-defined regions of interest, producing a classified map with six classes: Agriculture, Native Forest, Water Bodies, Pasture, Urban Area, and Forestry.

The script calculates the area (in hectares) of each land cover class within a specified region of interest (roi) using a classified land cover image (afolu_2010). It groups pixel counts by class code and outputs the total area per class.
task_name: Calculate land cover area by class

task_description: The script identifies forested areas and water bodies in a region of the Amazon using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from June to August 2022. It computes NDVI to detect dense vegetation (forests) with a threshold (>0.8), MNDWI to highlight water bodies, and creates a classified map distinguishing forests, non-forests, and water. The outputs include true-color imagery, NDVI layers (manually computed and via normalizedDifference), MNDWI, binary forest masks, and a reclassified land cover layer combining water, non-forest, and forest classes.
task_name: Identify forest and water areas using NDVI and MNDWI

task_description: The script classifies land cover into three categories (water, vegetation, others) using Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data from 2017 by training a Random Forest classifier on sampled regions, then applies the model to produce a classified map, evaluates accuracy with an error matrix, and computes area per class within the AOI.

The script detects surface water extent and coastline dynamics using Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 satellite imagery over a dam area (Alaco Dam) from 2019, applying Otsu thresholding on AWEI and HSV-based classification for optical data, speckle filtering and thresholding for SAR data, and computes water area and confusion matrix metrics (tp, fp, tn, fn) for accuracy assessment across three different water detection approaches.
task_name: Detect water bodies and coastline changes

task_description: The script detects vegetation loss by analyzing changes in VV and VH backscatter from Sentinel-1 GRD data over three time periods (2016, 2018, 2019), applying temporal differencing and thresholding on filtered images, and estimating affected areas within a defined region of interest.

The script identifies the best cloud-minimized Sentinel-2 image per MGRS tile within a region of interest, removes overlapping pixels by masking to the nominal 100km x 100km tile extent, and divides this tile into 10,000 m² (10km x 10km) sub-tiles. It then creates a raster layer assigning each sub-tile a unique ID, enabling spatial partitioning for downstream processing such as classification or sampling.

The script identifies areas in Peru with elevations between 4000 and 6000 meters using SRTM digital elevation data, masks those elevations, and calculates the total area (in square kilometers) of such high-elevation regions within the country boundary.

The script validates a land cover classification image by comparing classified reference points with remapped classification results, generating an error matrix and accuracy assessment tables for specific land cover classes: forest, other vegetation, farming, bare soil, and water.

The script identifies soil line characteristics by analyzing the relationship between red (B4) and near-infrared (B8) reflectance in Sentinel-2 L2A images, using sub-tile stratification and minimum NIR values within red reflectance intervals to extract soil line pixels. Output is a CSV of point samples representing soil line features per tile and date.
task_name: Extract soil line features from Sentinel-2 imagery

task_description: The script analyzes temporal variability of Sentinel-1 C-band VH polarization backscatter over the Manyara Basin from 2016 to 2017, computing statistical summaries (mean, median, min, max, stdDev, percentile) and deriving a mask based on high range (>10), low minimum (<-25), and high standard deviation (>2), likely targeting areas with strong surface scattering dynamics such as flood-prone or irrigated agricultural zones.

The script classifies land cover into urban, bare, water, and vegetation categories using a random forest classifier trained on Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from 2020, producing a classified map clipped to the ULB boundary.

The script calculates NDVI from minimum composite Landsat 8 and Landsat 7 surface reflectance images to analyze changes in vegetation over time, specifically comparing April 2015 (Landsat 8) with April–December 2000 (Landsat 7) at a specific point in Colombia (-75, 11). It also computes the spectral difference between the two composites to highlight land surface changes.

The script identifies flood extent by calculating z-scores from Sentinel-1 SAR imagery during a target date (2017-08-16) relative to a baseline period (2016), applying thresholds on VV and VH polarizations, power, and pixel intensity to detect inundated areas, and outputs a flood map and boolean map indicating flooded regions. It also compares detected floods with JRC water occurrence data and computes zonal statistics over administrative divisions.

The script analyzes Sentinel-2 surface reflectance images to generate two composite mosaics: one showing areas under direct sunlight and another showing topographic shadows, using hillshade modeling based on solar angles and a Copernicus DEM. The outputs are masked composites representing sunlit and shadowed regions within the ROI.
task_name: Map solar illuminated and shadowed terrain

task_description: The script performs pansharpening on both Landsat 8 and SkySat multispectral imagery by fusing high-resolution panchromatic bands with lower-resolution RGB bands using the HSV color space transformation method, producing higher spatial resolution color images for visual analysis.

The script calculates and analyzes NDVI values from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data over a specific region (table) for multiple years (2015–2018), focusing on the months of June, July, and August. It computes monthly maximum and minimum NDVI composites after applying cloud masking using the QA60 band, aiming to assess vegetation dynamics during summer months across consecutive years.

The script calculates land surface temperature (LST) in Celsius from Landsat 8 Thermal Infrared Band (B10) radiance values using calibration constants and a thermal conversion formula, then computes the mean LST for 2016 over a specified region.

The script classifies land cover into seven categories (Agriculture, Plantation, Harvested, Native vegetation, Sand, Urban, Water) using a Random Forest classifier trained on Landsat 8 surface reflectance data and topographic variables. It generates classified maps for multiple years (2014–2018) and evaluates classification accuracy using a confusion matrix from training and testing partitions.

The script filters a Sentinel-2 image collection over Madagascar for the period from January 1, 2019, to April 20, 2019, sorts images by cloud coverage, and selects the first (least cloudy) image. It outputs the size of the filtered collection, the collection itself, its object type, and the selected single image.

The script calculates annual rainfall erosivity (R-factor) using daily precipitation data from CHIRPS. It computes the exponent β based on mean precipitation intensity and wet-day frequency, then applies a power-law model to half-monthly precipitation sums to derive erosivity for each year from 2010 to 2020 over Yulin region.

The script identifies areas of deforestation by combining detection alerts from Sentinel-2, Landsat 8, and Sentinel-1 satellite data, then compares them with PRODES 2017 forest loss data to compute hyper-areas and alert densities within predefined grid cells. Outputs include a feature collection of cells flagged for significant deforestation activity and their associated areas in square meters.

The script classifies land cover into four classes (Bosque, Urbano, Mar, AAbiertas) using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from 2020, applying a Random Forest classifier on spectral bands and derived indices (NDVI, NDWI, SAVI), with accuracy assessment via validation points.

The script detects vegetation disturbance events using LandTrendr algorithm on a time series of Landsat imagery, analyzing the NBR index between 1985 and 2020 to identify changes in magnitude and year of detection, with specific thresholds for change characteristics such as duration, magnitude, and pre-event vegetation condition.

The script quantifies long-term deposition and erosion dynamics at river deltas by analyzing water occurrence changes from JRC Global Surface Water and AquaMonitor datasets within buffered delta shorelines, excluding urban areas, and computes net surface change in square kilometers.

The script maps the spatial extent of cropland areas in Canada using reclassified ESA CCI Land Cover data for 2017, converting classified pixels into a binary crop/non-crop raster, computing pixel area in hectares, and aggregating total crop area per country through zonal statistics.
task_name: Map crop extent from land cover data

task_description: The script performs land cover classification to distinguish between deciduous and coniferous forests using a Random Forest classifier trained on Sentinel-1 SAR data. It evaluates model performance with an error matrix, overall accuracy, and Kappa statistic using a 70/30 train-test split.

The script computes and normalizes four environmental indicators—NDVI, NDBSI, LST, and Wetness—for the Yulin region from 2010 to 2020, then performs Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to derive dominant spatial patterns of surface ecological conditions. The output is a set of principal component images representing transformed spectral indices, with variance percentages reported for each component.

The script processes a feature collection of schools in São Paulo, filters for public institutions (excluding private), and categorizes them based on administrative class and type (e.g., CEI, CEMEI, CEU, EMEF). It cleans school names by removing institutional prefixes to standardize naming, distinguishes CEU-type centers, and merges corrected features into a unified dataset for spatial analysis of public educational infrastructure.

The script identifies areas with high vegetation density by computing the maximum NDVI from Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data over a specified geometry, applying a threshold (NDVI > 0.6), and analyzing the spatial distribution of this vegetation in relation to elevation zones derived from SRTM data within a buffered region.

The script identifies surface water bodies by applying an Otsu threshold on the NDWI (Normalized Difference Water Index) derived from a normalized image (guiyi) over a feature collection (DTshp). It computes an optimal threshold from the NDWI histogram, classifies pixels into water (1) and non-water (4), masks and clips results, then evaluates classification accuracy using manually defined water and non-water samples (water, nowater) through a confusion matrix, reporting overall accuracy, kappa, and producer/consumer accuracies.
task_name: Identify surface water extent using NDWI and Otsu thresholding

task_description: The script performs continuous change detection and classification (CCDC) on Landsat time series data from 1986 to 2022 over a user-defined study area, identifying land cover changes using spectral bands and the NDMI index. It outputs change parameters including magnitude (MAG), break date (tBreak), and number of breaks (numTbreak), along with synthetic imagery and coefficient images for a specified date.

The script identifies areas of glacier retreat by comparing the median VH polarization backscatter from Sentinel-1 SAR data between 2015 and 2021, detecting significant negative changes (less than -8 dB) indicative of ice loss.

The script calculates the maximum annual NDVI from Landsat 7 surface reflectance data in the year prior to wildfire occurrence (2011–2015) for specific fire polygons, then extracts mean NDVI values within each polygon to assess pre-fire vegetation conditions across 2013–2016 fires.
task_name: Estimate pre-fire NDVI for burned areas

task_description: The script performs Principal Component Analysis (PCA) on surface reflectance imagery from 2011 and 2016 over a selected region in Peru to detect land cover changes, focusing on PC1 and PC3 components. It generates PC masks within specified thresholds to highlight areas of potential change, particularly analyzing spectral differences in SWIR, NIR, and red bands.
task_name: Identify land cover change using PCA

task_description: The script classifies land cover into water, vegetation, bare soil, and mixed classes (EFV, WBS, DV, OW1, GV1, BS1) using spectral unmixing and threshold-based rules on a median-composited Landsat image. It outputs a classified image collection per grid cell with fractional abundances and a final class map.

The script trains a Random Forest classifier using spectral and texture indices (S_mean, S_std, NDVI_mean, NDVI_std, NDWI_mean, NDWI_std, HCv_mean, HCv_std, VCv_mean, VCv_std) to predict 'area'—a property representing water extent—from a feature collection of grid cells. The output is a trained classifier model for estimating water area based on remote sensing features.
task_name: Predict water area from spectral indices

task_description: The script calculates multiple spectral indices including NDVI (using B2 and B11) and six custom band ratios from Sentinel-2 data to analyze land surface characteristics, with a focus on vegetation and land cover properties. It generates a composite image representing normalized differences and transformed band combinations for two time periods, clipped to a specific region.
task_name: Analyze vegetation and land cover indices

task_description: The script identifies soil line characteristics by analyzing red (B4) and NIR (B8) reflectance relationships in Sentinel-2 images, masking for optimal pixels within sub-tiles, and extracting georeferenced points with associated SOC values, spatial metadata, and image acquisition details for further modeling.
task_name: Extract soil line features from Sentinel-2 imagery

task_description: The script identifies surface water extent in multiple administrative districts of Bangladesh by computing MNDWI, NDWI, and AWEInsh indices from Sentinel-2 imagery and applying Otsu's thresholding method on time-series composites to generate binary water masks for the year 2018.
task_name: Identify surface water extent using Otsu thresholding

task_description: The script calculates the Normalized Radar Polarization Burned index (NRPB) using VV and VH polarization bands from Sentinel-1 GRD imagery over a specific region of interest (CENTROINIA) for January 2020. It filters and processes an ImageCollection to mask out extreme low backscatter values before computing NRPB as a new band added to each image.
task_name: Compute NRPB from Sentinel-1 VV and VH

task_description: The script creates a median composite of Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery from November to December 2021, masked by a regional boundary, to support land cover analysis within the defined AreaReg region, with visual overlays of watershed units (Cubetas) and the regional boundary.
task_name: Map land cover in regional area

task_description: The script analyzes long-term and short-term vegetation trends using time series data, masks results by significant Hansen statistics and land cover types from MODIS, and classifies trend significance into positive, negative, and stationary categories within a region of interest. It also identifies cropland areas based on greenness thresholds in the final year of analysis.

The script processes a PlanetScope image collection to compute and smooth the GNDVI and NDVI vegetation indices over a specific agricultural or vegetated site (RIP) using a Savitzky-Golay-like filtering approach. It masks images based on UDM quality, filters by spatial coverage and minimum GNDVI threshold, coregisters images to a template, resamples to a coarser scale, and prepares a time series for smoothing analysis. The output is a ready-to-process ImageCollection with added spectral indices and temporal metadata, intended for time-series smoothing of GNDVI dynamics.

The script identifies and extracts seasonal coastlines by detecting water bodies using the AWEI index from Sentinel-2 imagery, applying Otsu thresholding, filling small islands and water bodies, and vectorizing the resulting raster boundaries for winter, spring, summer, and autumn composites between December 2020 and September 2021.

The script generates a land cover classification map distinguishing intact forest, degraded forest, and deforested areas using temporal metrics derived from Landsat surface reflectance data. It computes spectral indices (NDVI, NDWI, SAVI) and statistical, trend, and seasonal change metrics over two time periods (2015–2018 for training and 2015–2020 for classification), trains a Random Forest classifier using labeled sample points, and classifies the study area with validation accuracy assessment.

The script retrieves the least cloudy Landsat image within a specified date range and geographic point, sorting by 'CLOUD_COVER' and selecting the first (least cloudy) image for that year and location.

The script analyzes temporal NDVI patterns over Bhutan using Landsat 8 surface reflectance data from 2015 to 2020, comparing raw and cloud-masked image collections to assess vegetation dynamics while reducing atmospheric interference.

The script applies terrain slope correction to Sentinel-1 GRD imagery using a volume or surface scattering model, correcting radar backscatter (VV and VH) for topographic effects such as layover and shadow, and outputs corrected mosaics with ratio bands (VV-VH) for visual and analytical comparison.

The script classifies land cover types (Forest, Urban, Grass) using a Sentinel-2 surface reflectance composite from March 2019 to June 2020, applying a CART classifier on bands B2–B7, and outputs a classified map clipped to a buffered polygon around Cerveteri, Italy.

The script retrieves the least cloudy satellite image within a specified date range and region of interest, then calculates the mean pixel value of all bands in the image over that region using a 30-meter scale.
task_name: Extract mean value from least cloudy image

task_description: The script calculates mean and standard deviation of NAIP imagery in shadow and non-shadow regions, then applies a linear transformation to restore surface reflectance values for red, green, and blue bands within a specified geometry. The output includes statistical summaries and a restored RGB image layer clipped to the region of interest.

The script identifies areas where agriculture has expanded into locations of prior forest loss by combining a forest loss layer with an agriculture land cover layer, then detecting overlapping pixels with a value sum of 2, indicating both forest loss and agricultural presence.
task_name: Identify agriculture expansion into forest loss areas

task_description: The script classifies fishponds in Barisal and surrounding districts of Bangladesh by training a CART classifier on spatial shape metrics (e.g., ipq, soli, pfd) derived from water body vectors. It uses Sentinel-2 imagery and multiple water indices (AWEI, MNDWI, NDWI) to generate water masks, then extracts morphological features for classification. The output includes classified fishpond maps, training/validation datasets, and accuracy assessments via confusion matrices.

The script classifies land cover types (e.g., forest, urban, pasture/agriculture, water) using harmonic coefficients derived from CCDC (Continuous Change Detection and Classification) model outputs on Landsat surface reflectance data. It trains a Random Forest classifier using labeled sample points and applies the model to classify up to six temporal segments of land cover within the study area, producing a multi-band image where each segment contains classified land cover, start time, and end time.

The script identifies changes in urban development by analyzing the median nighttime light intensity from VIIRS DNB data, comparing the earliest and latest periods between January 2018 and March 2022, and highlighting significant increases or decreases in radiance.
task_name: Detect urban change using nighttime lights

task_description: The script applies multiple speckle filtering algorithms (Focal Median, Lee Sigma, Frost, Gamma Map) to Sentinel-1 GRD SAR imagery to reduce noise in the VV polarization band over the Black Sea region, producing filtered versions of the VV band for visual and analytical comparison.

The script identifies snow-covered areas by calculating the Normalized Difference Snow Index (NDSI) from a specific Landsat 8 surface reflectance image, using Green (B2) and Shortwave Infrared (B5) bands, and applying a threshold of 0.5 to classify snow. The output includes a binary map of snow presence and visualizations of true and false color composites.

The script identifies vegetation-covered areas in Portugal using NDVI derived from median-composited Landsat surface reflectance imagery (2016–2018), applying Otsu's thresholding method on NDVI histogram data within a coastal buffer zone near Setúbal to produce a binary classification (vegetated vs. non-vegetated) mapped as 'class A'.

The script calculates the Vegetation Condition Index (VCI) for each month from January to July 2022 by using Sentinel-2 NDVI data, comparing monthly maximum NDVI values against historical monthly min/max from 2018–2022, and outputs masked and clipped VCI images per month.

The script classifies land cover into five categories—vegetation, water bodies, urbanization, exposed soil, and rock—using a Random Forest classifier trained on Landsat 5 TOA reflectance bands. It outputs a classified land cover map and evaluates training accuracy via a confusion matrix, along with generating random points within the study area for potential validation.

The script loads Argentina's administrative divisions (departments) at level 2 from a custom GEE asset, computes the area of each department in square kilometers, generates bounding boxes for each, filters departments that intersect with the Chaco dry/humid region, further selects large departments (>2500 km²), and isolates departments within Salta and Jujuy provinces. Outputs include area statistics, filtered feature collections, and mapped layers of departments, bounding boxes, and selected regions.

The script identifies water bodies and extracts their coastlines using Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-1 data over a specified time period. It computes AWEI for water detection, applies Otsu thresholding to delineate water, performs connected component analysis to refine land-water boundaries, and generates vectorized coastlines. Outputs include binary water masks, coastline rasters, area calculations in km², and confusion matrix components (tp, tn, fp, fn) for validation against a reference geometry.

The script identifies water bodies by applying Otsu's thresholding method on NDVI values derived from a normalized image (guiyi), then evaluates classification accuracy using a confusion matrix based on reference samples (water and nowater). The output includes a classified map (tm1), masked results (result1, pre_img), and accuracy metrics such as overall accuracy, kappa coefficient, and user/producer accuracies.

The script classifies rice cultivation areas using a Random Forest classifier trained on MODIS surface reflectance bands and FABDEM elevation data. It evaluates classification accuracy using a confusion matrix and outputs accuracy metrics including overall accuracy, consumer's and producer's accuracy, kappa, and F-score.

The script creates a median cloud-free composite of Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery for June 2020 over a specific AOI, filtering images by cloud cover and nodata percentage, then applying a QA60-based cloud mask before reduction.

The script analyzes agricultural vegetation conditions by combining Sentinel-1 SAR (VV, VH, VV/VH) and Sentinel-2 (B2, B3, B4, NDVI, NDWI, MNDWI) data over a specific area and time period, producing a fused multispectral image for detailed land surface analysis.

The script identifies dry land areas by applying a mode-reduced water index mask (from AWEI, MNDWI, and NDWI) to Sentinel-1 or Sentinel-2 imagery, converting the resulting raster into vector polygons, and computing morphological attributes such as area, perimeter, shape indices, and convexity metrics for each detected feature within specific administrative districts in Bangladesh.

The script quantifies long-term deposition and erosion dynamics at global delta shorelines by analyzing water occurrence change data from JRC Global Surface Water and AquaMonitor, masking urban areas using GlobCover land cover, and computing net surface area changes within buffered delta geometries. Outputs include a feature collection of deltas with attributes for deposition, erosion, and net change, as well as a raster image of mean change intensity.

The script classifies water and land areas in Zhejiang using Landsat 5 surface reflectance data from 1984–1986, trained with labeled points and a Random Forest classifier, producing a binary water-land map based on JRC Global Surface Water occurrence thresholds.

The script calculates the average elevation within a boundary (ulb) using a DSM, identifies areas where elevation is below 1000 meters, masks those areas, and computes the total area in hectares of terrain below this elevation threshold.

The script integrates supervised classification results from multiple land cover classes (urban, water, herbaceous, and woody vegetation) using NDVI and multispectral data from 2014–2015 to produce a final Level 2 land cover map. It combines classifications for herbaceous crops, natural pastures, plantations, native forests, and agricultural areas, masking them with urban and water layers to generate a unified land cover product.

The script identifies areas of deforestation in Laos between 2016 and 2020 by filtering an annual disturbance dataset for 'dis_type' equal to 7 (indicating deforestation), creating a binary map of cumulative deforestation, and sampling reference points from ground truth data within the same time period. The output includes a summed deforestation occurrence map and sampled feature collection linked to reference deforestation years.

The script analyzes Sentinel-1 VV and VH backscatter and Landsat 8 surface reflectance data from August 2019 to generate a composite image with NDVI, applying speckle filtering to SAR data for improved land surface analysis in the region of interest.
task_name: Analyze SAR and optical vegetation characteristics

task_description: The script detects flooded areas by computing the log ratio of VH-polarized Sentinel-1 SAR imagery before and after a flood event, applying a Gaussian filter and thresholding at -2 dB, then masking non-water areas using a global water mask. The output is a binary flood extent map.

The script identifies water bodies in a lake region by applying Otsu's thresholding method on the VV polarization band of Sentinel-1 SAR imagery from January 2020, producing a binary water mask and analyzing the histogram distribution of backscatter values.
task_name: Identify water bodies using VV backscatter

task_description: The script classifies surface water extent in Zhejiang province using NDWI and MNDWI indices derived from Landsat 8 surface reflectance data for the year 2022, applies thresholds to identify water bodies, and evaluates classification accuracy using validation points with error matrix metrics including overall accuracy, kappa, and producer's/consumer's accuracy.

The script analyzes time-series Sentinel-1 GRD data to detect deforestation in the Amazon by comparing backscatter changes (VV and VH polarizations) between a reference period and subsequent months, using predefined land cover geometries for forest, recent deforestation, secondary forest, agriculture, and water.

The script calculates the rate of change in NDVI between two Sentinel-2 images taken on 2021-01-28 and 2021-02-01, applying cloud and shadow masking to improve accuracy. It outputs a classified rate-of-change layer (tasa_res) binned into discrete intervals and computes the area (in hectares) covered by each class within a given region (lote).

The script identifies flooded areas by analyzing changes in VH polarization backscatter from Sentinel-1 SAR imagery before and after a flood event, applying a Refined Lee speckle filter and thresholding the ratio of post-event to pre-event VH values above 1.35, masking with forest cover data from Hansen global forest change dataset.

The script identifies flooded areas by analyzing changes in VV-polarized backscatter from Sentinel-1 SAR imagery before and after a flood event, applying focal median smoothing and thresholding to detect significant decreases in radar signal indicative of surface water inundation.

The script classifies high-resolution aerial imagery into distinct benthic substrate types (sand, seagrass, rock, algae) in a shallow coastal environment using a trained CART classifier. The output is a classified raster map of seabed composition derived from RGB imagery collected by drones or aircraft.

The script calculates the normalized difference in near-infrared (NIR) reflectance (band b8) between two PlanetScope images from July 31 and August 1 to detect changes in surface water. It classifies areas into dry, wet, or water based on thresholding the difference image: values less than -0.12 are classified as water (blue), greater than -0.10 as dry (grey), and in between as wet (green).
task_name: Detect water change using NIR difference

task_description: The script calculates short-term average NDVI from Sentinel-2 data (2019–2022, June months) over a region, computes NDVI median for June 2021, and derives absolute, relative, and standardized anomalies to assess vegetation deviation during that period.

The script computes the mean surface reflectance and brightness temperature from Landsat 8 Collection 1 Tier 1 SR data over Mt. Kenya between 2014 and 2022, applies pixel and radiometric saturation masking, and generates a composite image and NDVI layer to assess vegetation health and distribution in the region.

The script detects changes in surface water extent caused by flooding using pre- and post-event Sentinel-1 SAR imagery, applying focal mean filtering to reduce speckle noise and enhance flood signal detection.

The script identifies changes in vegetation between two time periods using NDVI composites derived from Sentinel-2 imagery, comparing pre- and post-date cloud-filtered image collections over a specified AOI.

The script identifies areas of high vegetation using maximum NDVI and 90th percentile NDVI from Sentinel-2 imagery between December 2019 and February 2020, applying cloud masking and generating a color-coded map with a legend for NDVI values above 0.70.

The script classifies water and land areas in Zhejiang province using Landsat 5 surface reflectance data from 1994 to 1996. It applies a Random Forest classifier trained on labeled points, with input features from SR_B1 to SR_B7 bands, to generate a water-land classification map based on historical water occurrence data from the JRC Global Surface Water dataset.

The script retrieves the first available image from a filtered and sorted image collection at the map center, clips it to a region of interest (ROI), selects band B8, and analyzes pixel area statistics using different reducers (sum, mean, first, count) on both ee.Image.pixelArea() and a reprojected constant image, printing the results. It also prints the total area of the ROI.

The script classifies land cover into two categories (likely water and non-water or vegetation and non-vegetation) using a median composite of Sentinel-2 imagery from 2015 to 2019, applying Random Forest and SVM classifiers trained on spectral indices (NDVI, EVI2, NBR, NDMI, NDSI, NDWI) and reflectance bands. The output includes classified raster maps for both classifiers over the area of interest.

The script classifies land cover types using Landsat 5 surface reflectance data from 2003, applying Random Forest classification on spectral bands, NDVI, and NDWI percentiles derived from a cloud-filtered image collection. Training and validation are performed using labeled sample points, with outputs including a classified land cover map, variable importance scores, and accuracy assessment metrics (confusion matrix, overall accuracy, kappa coefficient, producer's and user's accuracy).

The script calculates the ratio of VH to VV polarization from Sentinel-1 GRD data, then computes the minimum value over a six-day period in March 2020, outputting a clipped image of the minimum VH/VV ratio and the minimum backscatter values for the region of interest.

The script identifies forest, non-forest, and agricultural land cover classes in the Amazon region for the year 2009 using MapBiomas Amazonia collection data, reclassifies them based on a custom legend, and compares with an independent forest dataset to detect discrepancies in forest classification.

The script identifies and extracts the minimum NIR reflectance values corresponding to specific red reflectance intervals from a Sentinel-2 image to derive soil line anchor points, which are used in soil reflectance modeling and normalization.

The script predicts the fraction of flooded areas using MODIS surface reflectance data and a Random Forest regression model trained on labeled flood data, generating both spatial maps and time series outputs for Mozambique's Southwest region.

The script identifies irrigated agricultural areas by analyzing the maximum NDVI values from surface reflectance data of Landsat 8 collected between August and October 2021, applying cloud masking and enhancing vegetation and water indices for improved detection.

The script calculates the difference between the 90th and 10th percentiles of VH polarization backscatter from Sentinel-1 descending passes in 2016, then creates a binary mask identifying areas where this difference exceeds 7.5 dB, highlighting regions with high radar amplitude variability.
The script maps daily snow cover extent in Lebanon using MODIS Aqua MYD10A1 data, specifically analyzing the NDSI_Snow_Cover band, clipped to a defined geographic boundary for performance.

The script classifies land cover into vegetation, water, and built-up areas using a CART classifier trained on Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data. The output is a classified image map labeled according to these three land cover classes.

The script detects forest clearing by analyzing multi-temporal Landsat composites from 2007 to 2010 using NDVI differencing and supervised classification with a CART classifier trained on labeled sample points. Outputs are classified change maps for the periods 2007–2008, 2008–2009, and 2009–2010, identifying areas of vegetation loss.

The script analyzes long-term and short-term vegetation greenness trends using a time series of greenest pixel values, identifies statistically significant trends using t-statistics, detects breakpoints using the Hansen statistic, and classifies pixels into four categories: negative/positive stationary trends and negative/positive breakpoints. It also masks cropland and non-trending pixels based on the last year's greenness value, producing a classified map of vegetation change dynamics.
task_name: Classify long-term vegetation trends with breakpoints

task_description: The script identifies aquaculture fishponds by classifying water bodies based on morphological and spatial features (ipq, soli, pfd, conv, sqp) derived from Sentinel-2 imagery, using a CART classifier trained on ground truth pond data. It outputs classified fishponds, accuracy assessments, and filtered results by area thresholds.

The script identifies flooded areas by comparing pre-flood and post-flood Sentinel-1 VV backscatter imagery, computing the difference in focal median-smoothed images, and thresholding to detect significant drops in backscatter indicative of flooding.

The script classifies land cover types using Landsat 8 surface reflectance data from 2019 to 2020 by computing spectral indices (MNDWI, NDBI, NDVI) and applying an SVM classifier trained on labeled sample regions. The output is a classified land cover map and accuracy assessment including confusion matrix, overall accuracy, and kappa coefficient.
The script calculates the mean precipitation for each month of 1997 within the Manyara Basin using TRMM 3B42 data, outputting a dictionary of mean values per month.

The script detects flood extent by analyzing VV-polarized Sentinel-1 GRD SAR imagery across three temporal periods, applying a refined Lee speckle filter to backscatter data, converting to decibels, and compositing the results into a three-band RGB image (Red: period1, Green: period2, Blue: period3) for visual flood change analysis over the AOI.

The script identifies flooded areas in Bangladesh by calculating z-scores from Sentinel-1 GRD time series data, comparing target date backscatter values (2017-08-16) against a baseline period (2015-11-01 to 2016-03-01), and applying thresholds on VV, VH polarizations and power to detect flood signals. It outputs a flood map and a boolean mask of flood extent, then calculates flooded area per administrative union.
task_name: Map flood extent using radar imagery

task_description: The script calculates the Normalized Swir Index (NSI) using Landsat 8 SWIR and NIR bands to analyze land surface properties, specifically highlighting areas with potential moisture or vegetation stress. It generates a single NSI image and creates a time-lapse video of NSI visualizations from 2017 to 2018 over a specified point location.
The script extracts a time series of VV polarization SAR backscatter values from Sentinel-1 GRD data filtered for ascending IW mode acquisitions between 2014 and 2020.

The script calculates the total annual precipitation from CHIRPS pentad data for Central American countries and the Dominican Republic in 2018, computes mean rainfall per country using reduceRegion, and generates histograms of precipitation distribution within each country's geometry.

The script detects surface water extent for a specific month and year by combining monthly, annual, and inter-annual water probability metrics from MapBiomas Coleção de Água, applying thresholds to identify persistent and seasonal water bodies, while masking out static false positives and agriculture areas. The output is a binary classification (water/no water) image asset clipped to a Brazilian biome boundary.

The script reprojects a high-resolution SRTM DEM to match the coarser projection and resolution of a MODIS image, specifically using the first image from the MODIS/MOD13A1 collection, for potential integration with vegetation or land surface analysis.
task_name: Reproject elevation data to MODIS resolution

task_description: The script applies a Refined Lee speckle filter to Sentinel-1 GRD imagery to reduce noise in the VV polarization band, converting the data from decibel to natural units before filtering and back to decibel afterward, producing a smoothed radar backscatter image for improved interpretation of land surface structure.

The script classifies land cover by combining time-series Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery with ALOS PALSAR SAR data. It computes NDVI from seven temporal composites of Sentinel-2, creates a stacked image of these composites along with SAR HV backscatter, and samples training data from labeled regions (campo) for potential classification. The output is a multiband stack intended for supervised classification, where each band represents spectral, vegetation, and radar characteristics across multiple dates.
task_name: Classify land cover using SAR and multispectral imagery

task_description: The script extracts median NDVI values over agricultural farms using annual Landsat 8 NDVI composites from 2012 to 2020, generating a time series of NDVI per farm with image identifiers, formatted as a table where each row corresponds to a farm and columns represent NDVI values for each annual image.

The script analyzes land cover and vegetation greenness changes over time in the Naiman Banner region using MODIS, ESA WorldCover, and a custom Greenness dataset. It computes residuals between greenness and precipitation to remove climate variability effects, then applies the LandTrendr algorithm to detect breakpoints and trends in vegetation dynamics from 1985 to 2019, identifying potential land cover conversions or degradation in rangelands.
task_name: Detect land cover change in rangelands

task_description: The script calculates multiple bare soil indices (S1, S2, S3, S4, S5) from Landsat 8 surface reflectance data for the year 2016, applying cloud masking and excluding non-target areas such as glassland, urban, valley, and non-land regions. The outputs are spatial layers of NSI-based soil indices styled with a defined color scale for visual interpretation.
task_name: Analyze bare soil index using Landsat

task_description: The script classifies historical land cover types for the year 1974 using a pre-processed MSS image and a labeled feature collection, applying a Naive Bayes classifier trained on manually defined land use classes. The output is a classified raster map grouped into 9 aggregated land cover categories (e.g., native forest, plantation, agriculture) with accuracy validation via confusion matrix and overall accuracy assessment.

The script identifies surface water extent by applying an Otsu thresholding method on VV polarization of Sentinel-1 GRD imagery, followed by spatial smoothing, and computes the mean annual water occurrence in the region of interest for 2020.

The script identifies snow-covered areas by calculating the Normalized Difference Snow Index (NDSI) from a specific Landsat 8 surface reflectance image, using green (B2) and shortwave infrared (B5) bands, and applies a threshold (NDSI >= 0.5) to classify snow pixels.

The script evaluates the accuracy of a land cover classification for Haiti by computing an F1-score based on a comparison between an obtained classification result and a validation dataset, both converted to binary rasters within a region of interest.

The script processes MODIS MYD11A1 Collection 6 data to extract and mask nighttime Land Surface Temperature (LST) using quality assurance bits, converts the digital values to Celsius, and computes the minimum LST over a specific date range. The output is a single image representing the lowest observed nighttime temperature during the period.
task_name: Extract minimum night land surface temperature

task_description: The script identifies high-quality, cloud-free, and non-shadow pixels in a Landsat 8 surface reflectance image by applying band-specific threshold filters and spectral indices (NDVI, NBR, NBR2, EVI), then masks out cloudy and shadowed areas for improved land surface analysis.

The script calculates NDVI from Sentinel-2 imagery acquired between October 1 and October 7, 2021, to assess vegetation health, with lower values indicating sparse or stressed vegetation and higher values indicating dense green vegetation. The output includes a composite RGB image and a false-colored NDVI map.
The script calculates NDVI using near-infrared (SR_B5) and red (SR_B4) surface reflectance bands from a single Landsat 8 image acquired on August 18, 2017, to assess vegetation health or presence.

The script identifies green vegetation, non-photogenic vegetation, soil, and cloud fractions using spectral mixture analysis (SMA) on Landsat 8 imagery, then applies the Shade Water Soil Cloud (SWSC) model to detect water pixels based on shade, vegetation, and soil conditions.
task_name: Identify green vegetation and shade fractions

task_description: The script identifies snow-covered areas in a Landsat 5 image from March 31, 2002, over a location near -73.15, -48.92 by calculating the Normalized Difference Snow Index (NDSI) using Green and SWIR bands and applying a threshold of 0.5 to classify snow.

The script determines the dominant class among nine input images by comparing pixel values across all images and assigning a class label (1–9) where each image has the highest value. It then validates the classification accuracy using a feature collection of reference points, generating an error matrix to compute overall accuracy, user's accuracy, producer's accuracy, and kappa coefficient.

The script identifies glacier-covered areas by calculating the Normalized Difference Snow Index (NDSI) from Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data over a specific region, applying a threshold (NDSI > 0.4), and counting the number of glacier pixels within a polygon boundary.

The script classifies land cover into four classes (likely paddy, agriculture, forest, and urban or similar) using Sentinel-2 spectral bands and vegetation indices (EVI, NDVI, SAVI) over Hongliu region. It trains a Random Forest classifier with labeled samples, validates accuracy using a confusion matrix, and computes paddy field area per county.

The script classifies land cover changes in Guatemala between 2009 and 2012 using Landsat 7 surface reflectance data, training a Random Forest classifier on labeled sample points to produce a classified change map with four land cover classes.

The script performs gap-filling of Landsat 7 SLC-off imagery over a district using temporal composites from Landsat 5, applying a neighborhood regression-based method to restore missing pixels in the 30th percentile composite.

The script computes a median composite of Sentinel-2 TOA reflectance data from 2016 to 2021 over a specific floristic region (ID=2), applies cloud masking, and calculates multiple vegetation-related spectral indices including NDVI, TVI, REP, MTCI, IRECI, CRE, MCARI2, and others. The output is a clipped, multi-band image asset containing 26 selected bands and derived indices, used for detailed vegetation analysis.
task_name: Analyze vegetation indices in floristic region

task_description: The script calculates the mean VV and VH polarization backscatter values from Sentinel-1 GRD data over a specific region between September 1, 2020, and October 1, 2020, likely to analyze surface moisture or flood-related changes.
task_name: Compute VV and VH backscatter mean

task_description: The script classifies land cover by training a model on spectral and vegetation index data (NDVI, NDWI, EVI) derived from Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery over multiple bi-monthly periods in 2020. It combines labeled training samples from two land cover datasets (lc_EG and LC_Ethop) to generate a combined training set for supervised classification.
task_name: Classify land cover using spectral indices

task_description: The script calculates NDVI time series from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data, masks clouds and shadows, removes tile overlap, and extracts mean, standard deviation, percentiles, and count statistics for subdivided test areas. The output is a CSV file of these per-polygon temporal statistics.
task_name: Extract NDVI time series for test areas

task_description: The script detects and maps the frequency of surface water occurrence from 1985 to 2017 using a time series of mosaicked images, identifying persistent and seasonal water bodies within the Amazon region. It also evaluates data quality by detecting shaded, low-vegetation, and cloudy pixels to mask unreliable observations in 2017.

The script classifies land cover into mangrove, non-mangrove, bare soil, and water classes using Sentinel-2 imagery from 2019 and a Random Forest classifier trained on manually labeled polygons. It evaluates classification accuracy using validation samples and computes NDVI as a vegetation index for analysis.

The script identifies surface water presence and frequency of occurrence across years (1985–2017) by analyzing spectral fractions (shade, green vegetation, soil, cloud) from MapBiomas mosaics and applying a multi-year threshold-based detection model, with spatial filtering based on consistency. Outputs include annual water detection layers, frequency maps before and after gap-filling, and integration with MapBiomas water classification for comparison.

The script detects vegetation loss by analyzing temporal differences in Sentinel-1 VH polarization backscatter between filtered VV and VH bands from descending IW mode images, applying thresholding on the difference to identify significant changes indicative of vegetation loss, and quantifying the affected areas through regional statistics.

The script identifies forested areas within a defined region by calculating NDVI from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data and applying a threshold (NDVI > 0.8) to distinguish forests from non-forests. It also computes MNDWI for water body detection and reclassifies land cover into water, non-forest, and forest classes with remapped values. Outputs include true-color imagery, NDVI maps, binary forest masks, and reclassified land cover layers.

The script analyzes soil moisture conditions using temporal stacks of Sentinel-1 VV and VH backscatter from both ascending and descending orbits over a specific field site between July 1–16, 2019.
