The final output is a binary map of oilseed rape presence (youdao) and a county-level CSV table summarizing cultivated area (in km²) per administrative unit.

The script analyzes seasonal vegetation dynamics in the Lake Chad and Borno regions using Landsat 8 surface reflectance data from 2000 to 2017. It computes NDVI, applies cloud masking, and generates composite images (qualityMosaic and median) for four phenological periods: harvest (Sep–Jan), lean (Jul–Oct), preparation (Feb–May), and a broader July–Sep window over Lake Chad. The script calculates the percentage of high-NDVI areas (above 0.7 threshold) within Borno region for each composite, compares harvest vs. lean season differences, and outputs layered visualizations and numerical area proportions for seasonal vegetation change assessment.

The script classifies land cover types using Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data from 2018. It computes spectral indices (MNDWI, NDBI, NDVI), applies cloud masking, and trains a CART classifier on labeled sample regions (built, water, cultivated, forest, glass) to generate a land cover classification map. The output includes a classified raster with a color palette for five classes, along with accuracy assessment metrics: confusion matrix, overall accuracy, and kappa coefficient derived from 30% testing samples.

The script processes the ERA5-Land hourly meteorological dataset to generate daily maximum composites for multiple variables including 2m temperature, dewpoint temperature, wind components, precipitation, evaporation fluxes, radiation terms, and soil/skin temperatures. It first aggregates hourly data into daily maximums, then further computes monthly maximums from these daily values, and finally applies bicubic resampling and reprojection to a 1km MODIS-compatible projection. The output is a filtered ImageCollection containing resampled monthly maximum images from October 2003 to December 2019, specifically extracted for months October, November, and December each year.

The script extracts and compiles a multi-source environmental dataset for ecological analysis by combining bioclimatic variables, evapotranspiration (ET and PET), vegetation greenness (NDVI), and topography (elevation) into a single composite image. It processes monthly WorldClim, MODIS ET/PET (MOD16A2), MODIS NDVI (MOD13A1), and SRTM data, renames bands to shift index-based month labeling (e.g., from 0_ to 1_), and samples pixel values at specified point locations. The output is a feature collection containing extracted values at each point, suitable for species distribution modeling or ecological regression analysis.
task_name: Extract environmental variables for ecological modeling

task_description: The script processes Sentinel-1 GRD imagery over a user-defined study area to generate terrain-corrected radar backscatter. It applies radiometric terrain correction using SRTM-derived slope and aspect to compute gamma nought (γ⁰) and corrects for volumetric scattering, layover, and shadow effects. The output includes a mosaic of VV/VH polarized bands with added layers for corrected backscatter (in dB), ratios, local incidence angle, slope, layover/shadow masks, and uncorrected sigma nought, intended for land cover analysis in mountainous or topographically complex regions.
task_name: Correct SAR backscatter for terrain effects

task_description: The script detects vegetation loss in a region of interest by analyzing time-series Sentinel-1 C-band SAR imagery. It processes VV and VH polarizations from descending IW mode, filters images for specific dates (2016, 2018, 2019), applies focal mean filtering for speckle reduction, computes temporal differences in backscatter, and thresholds the difference to identify significant changes indicative of vegetation loss. Outputs include filtered SAR mosaics, difference layers, thresholded binary maps showing vegetation loss areas, histograms, regional statistics (mean and standard deviation), and area calculations masked to a specified geometry.

The script computes Principal Component Analysis (PCA) on a hyperspectral image from the NEON dataset over a small polygonal region. It first clips the image to the region, centers the data by subtracting band means, calculates the covariance matrix, extracts eigenvalues and eigenvectors, and projects the data to derive principal components. The output is a transformed image where each band represents a scaled principal component, useful for dimensionality reduction and feature extraction in spectral analysis.
task_name: Compute principal components of hyperspectral image

task_description: The script classifies forest and non-forest areas using Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery from 2020 to 2021, applying a Random Forest classifier trained on user-provided forest and non-forest points. It then performs a second classification for crop types using Cropland Data Layer (CDL) as a mask and stratified sampling over Kansas, generating two classified raster maps: one for forest/non-forest and another for crop types, along with accuracy assessment via error matrix and training/validation point analysis.

The script maps maize cultivation areas in Kenya and Tanzania by combining classified cropland masks with a maize-specific classification layer derived from Sentinel-2 imagery. It applies masking and mosaicking operations to generate a unified regional maize map, then computes the GCVI vegetation index to support yield modeling. The core output is a fused land cover classification raster that distinguishes maize within croplands, intended for integration with climate and vegetation data in crop yield prediction models.

The script analyzes forest cover, loss, and gain from the year 2000 using the Hansen Global Forest Change dataset. It calculates tree cover area, annual forest loss and gain areas by year (from 2001 to 2014), and aggregates these metrics within a user-defined feature collection (embalse). The output includes a FeatureCollection with summed cover, loss, and gain areas per region, extended with yearly loss and gain attributes for each year from 2001 to 2014, enabling temporal analysis of forest dynamics at regional scale.
task_name: Analyze forest cover change over time

task_description: The script retrieves a Landsat 8 TOA reflectance image collection for a specific WRS path and row over a one-year period, filters images by date, and performs metadata-level analysis including counting images, extracting temporal range, sorting by cloud cover and acquisition time, and computing sun elevation statistics. It outputs metadata summaries such as image count, date range, sun elevation statistics, the least cloudy scene, and recent acquisitions without performing pixel-based processing or classification.

The script computes Principal Component Analysis (PCA) on atmospherically corrected Landsat 8 TOA reflectance imagery over a point location for mid-2021. It first reduces the image collection by calculating mean pixel values within each image's geometry, centers the data by subtracting band means, then derives principal components using eigen-decomposition of the covariance matrix. The resulting PC bands are normalized by standard deviation and appended to the original images. Output is a transformed ImageCollection with added 'pc1' to 'pc6' bands alongside original spectral bands for further analysis.

The script computes Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) over the Hengduan Mountains using Landsat 5, 7, and 8 surface reflectance imagery from 2020 to 2021. It applies cloud masking using pixel quality bands (QA_PIXEL) and merges collections across sensors. The workflow includes band selection, cloud and shadow filtering, NDVI calculation via spectral band math, and outputs a processed ImageCollection of NDVI values for temporal analysis.

The script detects burn scars by computing the difference between pre- and post-event NBR-like indices (using SWIR and NIR bands) derived from median-reduced Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8 surface reflectance composites. It calculates NRQ indices (normalized ratio using B5 and B12) for pre- and post-fire periods, computes their difference, applies a threshold (>=0.66) to identify burned areas, and outputs a binary burn scar map. Additional outputs include mosaicked imagery, median composites, NDVI layers, and FIRMS active fire detections for validation.
task_name: Detect burn scars using spectral index difference

task_description: The script analyzes spatial texture patterns of NDVI derived from high-resolution NAIP imagery over a 10-meter resolution grid. It computes NDVI from near-infrared and red bands, then calculates neighborhood statistics (standard deviation, mean, median, maximum) at 1-, 2-, and 3-meter radii using square kernels. These texture metrics are aggregated to 10 meters via reduceResolution and reprojection for consistent scaling. The output includes layered visualizations of the original NAIP image, NDVI at 10m, and downsampled texture layers for comparison, supporting fine-scale vegetation structure analysis.
task_name: Analyze NDVI texture at multiple scales

task_description: The script classifies land cover types in the Arequipa region using Sentinel-2 imagery. It trains a Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier on manually labeled training samples representing five classes: water, bare soil, and three vegetation types. The classification is performed using spectral bands B2, B3, B4, B5, B6, B8, B9, and Bnir, resulting in a land cover map. Accuracy is assessed using an independent validation dataset, producing a confusion matrix and overall accuracy metric.

The script generates a median composite of Landsat 8 Operational Land Imager (OLI) surface reflectance imagery over Peru for 2019, applying cloud and cloud shadow masking using the pixel_qa band. It compares the masked composite with the original unmasked composite through visual layers in the map interface, enabling improved land surface analysis by reducing atmospheric contamination.

The script classifies land cover types using Sentinel-2 imagery from January to November 2017. It selects the least cloudy image, trains multiple classifiers (CART, SVM, Random Forest, Naive Bayes, Minimum Distance, Perceptron) on labeled sample regions (cultivo, bosque, nubes, urbano), and evaluates their performance using validation samples by computing kappa statistics from error matrices. The output is a list of kappa values for each classifier, indicating their accuracy in land cover classification.

The script analyzes MODIS Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD) data from 2010 to 2021 over Lebanon, applying a bit-based QA mask to filter low-quality observations. It computes two mean composites—one with quality masking and one without—and compares them visually on the map. Additionally, it extracts mean AOD values within the Lebanon boundary using reduceRegions, generating a FeatureCollection with dates attached for time-series analysis.

The script analyzes Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery over railway corridors in the UK to compute weekly NDVI composites from 2018 to 2020. It calculates NDVI using bands B8 and B4, applies cloud masking via the MSK_CLDPRB band, and generates a time series of bi-weekly composites. Then, it computes pairwise differences between consecutive NDVI images to detect temporal gaps in vegetation greenness. Finally, it identifies the timing (week) of the maximum negative NDVI change across the time series using a quality mosaic and masks results to tree cover areas, outputting a single raster map indicating when the largest drop in NDVI occurred within tree-covered regions near railways.

The script extracts nighttime light coverage (cf_cvg) from the VIIRS Day/Night Band data for a specific month across 2017–2020, clips it to Jordan and Lebanon, and creates binary masks where coverage values are below a threshold. It outputs masked images for each country and year, representing areas with low nighttime light detection, likely indicating limited human activity or infrastructure.

The script identifies surface water extent in August–September 2007 using NDWI derived from Landsat imagery. It processes a cloud-filtered image collection, computes median composite, applies NDWI with green and NIR bands, thresholds the result at 0.3 to classify water, and calculates the total water area in square meters using pixel area multiplication and reduction, outputting a binary water map and area statistic.

The script detects vegetation loss in a region of Colombia using Sentinel-1 C-band SAR imagery (VV and VH polarizations) from 2016 to 2019. It computes temporal differences between filtered VV and VH backscatter mosaics for the periods 2017–2018 and 2018–2019, applies thresholding based on standard deviation analysis over a refined ROI, and identifies significant decreases in backscatter as potential vegetation loss. The outputs include difference maps, thresholded binary loss layers, histograms, regional statistics (mean and standard deviation), and estimated loss area within a specific zone, validated against the Hansen Global Forest Change dataset for forest loss during 2016–2018.

The script classifies land cover types using Landsat 8 TOA reflectance imagery from May to June 2016 over the Riverline area. It selects the least cloudy image, uses six spectral bands (B2–B7), and trains a Classification and Regression Tree (CART) classifier on labeled training samples from four classes: Riverline, Bareland, Grassland, and Water. The output is a trained classifier model based on sample regions with land cover labels, intended for land cover classification mapping.

The script computes four spectral indices—MSAVI, TGSI, WETNESS, and ALBEDO—from MODIS MOD09A1 surface reflectance data over a specified region between November 2000 and April 2001. It normalizes each index using min-max scaling derived from the median composite's regional statistics, then applies Principal Component Analysis (PCA) on the normalized indices to generate the first three principal components. The output includes a composite image of normalized indices, PCA-transformed bands with explained variance, and visualizations clipped to two sub-regions (Norte and Sur). Results are printed and mapped for analysis.

The script analyzes changes in surface water extent by computing the Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI) using Sentinel-2 Surface Reflectance imagery. It defines pre- and post-event images over a reservoir (embalse), then processes an ImageCollection filtered by date, location, and cloud cover (<10%). NDWI is calculated using B8 (NIR) and B12 (SWIR) bands through spectral expression, and the resulting NDWI layers are mapped. The workflow focuses on water body detection and change assessment, outputting NDWI raster visualizations for the study area.

The script extracts cloud and cirrus pixel information from Sentinel-2 Level-1C imagery over a specified region by decoding the QA60 quality band. It applies bit masking to identify pixels flagged as cloudy (bit 10) or cirrus-contaminated (bit 11), creates binary mask bands named 'nuvol' (cloud), 'cirrus', and 'SenseNuvol' (cloud-free), and returns a collection of images with these added mask bands. The output is a filtered and sorted image collection containing only the derived mask layers for visual inspection or further filtering.

The script computes the median NDVI over a specified region and time period using Sentinel-2 imagery. It applies cloud masking using the QA60 band to filter out cloudy pixels, calculates NDVI from the near-infrared (B8) and red (B4) bands, and generates a median-reduced NDVI composite image. The output is a single NDVI raster representing temporal median vegetation greenness, suitable for land cover and vegetation condition analysis.

The script classifies land cover in Anand district using Sentinel-2 imagery from November 2020. It selects a cloud-filtered image mosaic, clips it to the administrative boundary, and trains an SVM classifier using labeled polygons representing classes such as water, crops, plantation, fallow, and urban areas. The classification is performed using 10 spectral bands (B2–B12 excluding B9/B10), and the output includes a classified raster map, training polygon overlay, confusion matrix, and overall accuracy assessment for model evaluation.

The script identifies potential oilseed (likely rapeseed) cultivation areas in Fujian (FJ), Jiangxi (JC), and Jiujiang (JJ) regions using dual-polarization SAR (VH) and red-edge vegetation index (CIre) time series from Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2. It applies threshold-based masking on T2_VH_diffneg_sum_2021 (multiplied by 0.0001, masked at <-7.5, -6.5, -3.5 dB) and T3_CIre_diff_sum_2021 (multiplied by 0.0001, masked at <-0.2, <0.1, <0.15) to detect winter crop growth patterns. The cropland mask is derived from a land cover map (classes 10,11,12,20), then binarized. Final detection (youdao) is generated by combining region-specific detections, unmasking and summing, then reapplying binary mask. Elevation zones (from DEM) are used to compute cultivated area per elevation band (0–400+ m) via reduceRegion with grouping. Outputs include a classified raster map of oilseed extent and a CSV table of area (km²) per elevation zone for the entire study region.

The script calculates the total area of Arequipa Province, Peru, using a binary mask derived from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery. It first creates a mosaic of cloud-filtered images from August to December 2020, clips it to the Arequipa administrative boundary, and generates a binary layer (1s and 0s) based on valid pixel presence in band B2 (blue). The actual area is computed by summing pixel areas where values are greater than 0, while a second estimate counts all pixels and multiplies by pixel size (100 m²). Both results are reported in km², along with their difference, providing an accuracy assessment of pixel-based area calculation within the region.
task_name: Estimate Arequipa's surface area using Sentinel-2 pixels

task_description: The script evaluates cloud contamination in Sentinel-2 imagery over a specific region for June 2017 using two masking approaches: a custom 'sentinelCloudScore' function that computes a cloud probability score based on spectral indices and band ratios, and the built-in QA60 bitmask. It generates three visualizations: the original image before masking, the computed cloud score layer, and two masked versions—one using the cloud score threshold (10), and another using the QA60 pixel quality band. Outputs include a cloud-scored image, a threshold-masked reflectance image, and a QA-based masked image for comparative cloud filtering analysis.

The script identifies salinized cropland areas in Fujian (FJ) and Jiangxi (JC) provinces using multi-threshold masking on remote sensing indicators derived from Sentinel-1 and optical data. It applies thresholds to T1_VV70sub30 (backscatter difference), T3_CIre_diff_sum (vegetation index difference), and T4_ARI_EVI2_coupling (stress coupling index) to generate binary masks, combines them with a cropland mask derived from land cover classification, and produces a final salinization map. Outputs include a classified raster of salinized cropland and a CSV table summarizing the area of salinization per administrative unit.

The script processes Sentinel-2 imagery over a defined geometry for the year 2017, applying multiple cloud and cloud shadow masking techniques. It retrieves the collection using custom modules for band renaming and mask generation, then applies four distinct masks: cloud flag, simple cloud score, cloud shadow flag, and TDOM-based cloud shadow detection. The output includes visualizations of the original image and each masked version (removing pixels identified as cloud or shadow by each method), enabling comparison of masking effectiveness. The final outputs are masked image collections with specific cloud/shadow pixels excluded, intended for cleaner downstream analysis.
task_name: Mask clouds and shadows in Sentinel-2 imagery

task_description: The script analyzes changes in surface reflectance and vegetation health between July 2014 and July 2015 using Landsat 8 Surface Reflectance data over a specific region. It applies cloud masking via the pixel_qa band, computes median composites for both years, and calculates the difference in spectral bands (B7, B6, B5) and NDVI (from B5/B4). The outputs include visualizations of RGB composites for both years, a difference layer in mid-infrared and shortwave infrared bands, a dNDVI map showing vegetation change, and a MODIS burned area product from May to June 2015 to assess potential fire impact. The analysis supports detection of environmental disturbances such as deforestation, agricultural shifts, or burn scars.

The script calculates geometric properties (area in km², perimeter in km, geometry type, coordinates, and geodesic status) of a merged feature collection from two user-defined geometries. It also retrieves the least cloudy Landsat 8 TOA image within a specified date range and point location for potential visual analysis, though no image processing or classification is performed. Outputs include printed metadata and statistics about the polygons and the selected image.

The script classifies land cover types using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery from January to March 2020. It processes the images by masking clouds, computing NDVI and MVI indices, and applying SNIC superpixel segmentation to generate homogeneous regions. Training vectors are recoded with class IDs and combined with user-drawn features for classification input. The output includes a median composite image, percentile-reduced image collection, segmented image layer, and map visualizations of the classified surface and segments.

The script analyzes land cover change and fire-affected areas in Venezuela for 2019 and 2020 using MapBiomas land cover classifications and MODIS burned area data. It extracts annual land cover maps (2019 and 2020), isolates specific vegetation and land use classes (e.g., forest, savanna, wetlands, urban, mining), and overlays MODIS-derived fire patches to identify the dominant land cover types affected by fires. Using reduceRegions with mode reducer, it determines the primary land cover within each fire patch and computes total burned area statistics per land cover class for both years, outputting aggregated area statistics for comparison.

The script identifies cloud cover in MOD09GA imagery for a single day (2013-06-01 to 2013-06-02) using the state_1km QA band. It extracts bit 10 (internal cloud algorithm flag) via bitwise operations, creates a binary cloud mask, and maps this over the collection. For each image, it computes a grouped count of pixels by cloud status (cloudy vs. clear) within the HARV geometry using reduceRegion, outputting a feature collection with these statistics for further analysis.

The script analyzes MOD09GA surface reflectance data to detect cloud presence using the state_1km QA band. It extracts bit 10 (internal cloud algorithm flag) to identify cloudy pixels, maps this flag across the image collection for a specific time period, and computes grouped region reductions over HARV geometry to summarize cloud coverage statistics. The output is a feature collection containing count summaries of cloudy and non-cloudy pixels per image.

The script computes Principal Component Analysis (PCA) on a mosaic of Earth observation images over a region of interest. It first composites multiple user-uploaded images into a single image stack, then centers the data by subtracting band means, calculates the covariance matrix, and derives principal components normalized by standard deviation. The output is a set of principal component bands representing orthogonal transformations of the original spectral data, intended for dimensionality reduction or feature extraction in land cover analysis.
task_name: Extract principal components from image stack

task_description: The script identifies salinized cropland areas in Fujian (FJ) and Jiangxi (JC) provinces using multi-threshold masking on Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 derived indices. It applies thresholds to T1_VV70sub30 (backscatter), T3_CIre_diff_sum (vegetation index difference), and T4_ARI_EVI2_coupling (stress coupling index) to generate binary masks, combines them with a cropland mask derived from land cover classification, clips to provincial boundaries, and merges results. Outputs include a final salinized cropland raster map and a CSV table summarizing the area of affected and non-affected cropland per administrative unit.

The script interpolates NDVI values for cloud-contaminated pixels in a Sentinel-2 image over a specific point by using temporal nearest neighbor composites from previous and next cloud-cleared time periods. It computes NDVI, applies cloud masking using QA60 band, estimates missing NDVI values through linear interpolation in time based on 'time' metadata, and fills the holes caused by clouds, resulting in a spatially continuous NDVI layer. Outputs include the original image, NDVI layers, cloud mask, and the final interpolated NDVI image.

The script calculates NDVI and SAVI vegetation indices from a single Sentinel-2 surface reflectance image. It uses band math operations: NDVI is computed as (B8 - B4) / (B8 + B4), while SAVI is calculated using an expression with a soil brightness correction factor (L=0.5). Outputs include two raster layers—NDVI and SAVI—added to the map, with SAVI initially turned off in the layer manager.
task_name: Compute NDVI and SAVI vegetation indices

task_description: The script analyzes forest loss and land cover change in the Pan-Amazon region between 2010 and 2020 using MapBiomas RIOS, TMF, and GFW datasets. It generates binary masks for forest loss (from TMF and GFW) during specific time periods, identifies areas of agricultural expansion by comparing MapBiomas land cover classifications in 2010 and 2020, and computes regional statistics using reduceRegions over country-per-biome units. Outputs include classified rasters for forest loss and agricultural expansion, visual layers on the map, and tabular summaries of affected areas.
task_name: Identify agricultural expansion from forest loss

task_description: The script identifies peanut cultivation areas in Heilongjiang Province (HLJ) in 2019 using multiple vegetation and crop condition indices derived from satellite imagery. It applies threshold-based masking on PA (Photochemical Reflectance Index-based Absorption), CCCI (Canopy Chlorophyll Content Index), and CARI (Chlorophyll Absorption Ratio Index) to isolate potential peanut pixels, followed by masking with cropland and rice maps. The final output is a binary classified raster map indicating peanut presence and a CSV table summarizing the area of peanut and non-peanut land per administrative unit.

The script classifies land cover in a region using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery from December 2019 to February 2020. It applies cloud masking via the QA60 band, computes a median composite, and trains a CART classifier using labeled feature points (renost, agri_inactive, agri_active, water, urban) with bands B2, B3, B4, and B8. The resulting classification map is validated using an error matrix on a test partition, and outputs include the classified raster, validation dataset, accuracy metrics, and visualizations of false-color and classified images.

The script estimates chlorophyll-a concentration in inland water bodies using Sentinel-2 imagery from 2015 to 2021. It applies cloud and atmospheric correction (via SIAC), computes the NDCI index using B4 and B5 bands, and derives chlorophyll-a through a power-law relationship (Lobo model). It also classifies water quality into five levels based on NDCI thresholds. Outputs include a time-series corrected Sentinel-2 image collection with added NDCI, chla_NDCI, and NDCI_class bands, as well as a monthly median composite collection for temporal analysis.

The script calculates the median of 2-meter air temperature over a specific region (NECA) and time period (2018-12-20 to 2019-01-01) using daily mean temperature data. It filters the dataset by date and spatial bounds, computes the median across the time series, then extracts the mean value within a defined geometry (Maine) using reduceRegion. The output is a dictionary containing the mean temperature value for the region.

The script selects a specific Sentinel-2 surface reflectance image over a region of interest and computes the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) using bands B8 (NIR) and B4 (red). It does not apply cloud masking or temporal compositing but directly calculates NDVI from a single image, resulting in a continuous index raster representing vegetation greenness. The output is an NDVI image layer for visual inspection or further analysis.

The script detects changes caused by a landslide at Cengalo using Sentinel-1 GRD SAR imagery. It compares pre- and post-event VV-polarized radar backscatter, applying a refined Lee filter to reduce speckle noise and computing the logarithmic difference in backscatter (in dB) between two dates. A thresholded difference image highlights significant changes, likely associated with surface disturbance from the landslide. The output includes visualizations of pre- and post-event SAR images, their difference, and corresponding optical Sentinel-2 imagery for context, enabling qualitative assessment of landslide extent and impact.

The script extracts the list of 'system:index' properties from a filtered Landsat 8 TOA image collection over a user-defined polygon. It applies cloud masking using the simpleCloudScore algorithm, retains images with cloud scores ≤ 20, and outputs a list of image IDs (system:index) for further reference or processing. No spectral analysis, classification, or derived index computation is performed.

The script analyzes forest cover, loss, and gain from 2000 to 2014 using the Hansen Global Forest Change dataset. It calculates pixel-area-weighted tree cover, deforestation, and reforestation in hectares, then aggregates these metrics by administrative districts. For each district, it computes annual forest loss and gain per year (2001–2014) by masking the lossyear band and reducing regions, ultimately producing a feature collection with yearly breakdowns of forest area change.

The script identifies burned areas in California using MODIS MCD64A1 Burn Date data from July 1 to September 10, 2021. It generates a binary burn mask, extracts stratified training samples within the burned zone, and creates random points inside and outside burned regions using vectorized masks. The outputs include a burn mask, training sample points, and random point datasets for fire-affected and non-affected areas, intended for use in classification or validation workflows.
task_name: Identify burned areas and generate fire/no-fire training points

task_description: The script selects Landsat 8 Level-2 surface reflectance imagery over Lake Erie for the summer of 2015, specifically filtering for the least cloudy image within the date range '2015-07-01' to '2015-09-01'. It does not perform analysis such as algal bloom detection but prepares and outputs a single candidate image likely intended for subsequent water quality or algal assessment. The output is a printed selected image with the label '2015_Algae_Imagery_Selected'.

The script calculates the total area of the Arequipa region in Peru using a administrative boundary dataset. It loads the level-1 administrative boundary (ADM1) for Arequipa from FAO GAUL 2015, computes pixel area in square meters using ee.Image.pixelArea(), converts it to square kilometers, and performs a reduceRegion operation to sum the area over the geometry. The output is a dictionary containing the total area in km², which is printed to the console.

The script classifies land cover types in the Jiangjun region using Sentinel-2 imagery from the first half of 2019. It applies cloud filtering and computes median pixel values across the image collection, then uses a Random Forest classifier trained on labeled samples (water, agriculture, building, road) to generate a classified land cover map. Accuracy assessment is performed using a separate test set, producing a confusion matrix, overall accuracy, user's and producer's accuracies, and kappa coefficient for validation.

The script calculates NDVI from Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data over a specified ROI between January and June 2018. It computes mean NDVI values for the region per image, then iterates through the collection to compute the difference in NDVI between consecutive images. The output is an image collection where each image is annotated with the NDVI difference from the prior image, enabling change detection analysis over time.

The script analyzes surface reflectance properties of a specific location using Landsat 8 Collection 2 Level-2 imagery from 2021 to 2022. It applies atmospheric and thermal scaling, computes spectral indices (NDWI, NDVI, BSI), performs cloud masking using the QA_PIXEL band, and generates composite statistics including median, mean, 20th percentile, and standard deviation for optical bands. Outputs include individual masked images, multi-band statistical composites, and their visualizations for true color, mean, median, percentile, and standard deviation layers.
task_name: Analyze surface reflectance vegetation and soil indices

task_description: The script processes Landsat 8 Surface Reflectance (SR) imagery from 2017 over a defined geometry to generate multiple cloud and cloud shadow masks using both pixel QA flags and spectral methods (Simple Cloud Score and TDOM). It applies four different masking approaches—cloudFlagMask, cloudScoreMask, cloudShadowFlagMask, and cloudShadowTdomMask—each removing specific atmospheric obstructions. The output includes visualizations of the original image and masked images with individual cloud/shadow layers removed, enabling comparative assessment of mask effectiveness on surface reflectance data.
task_name: Mask clouds and shadows in Landsat imagery

task_description: The script analyzes snow cover in a high-elevation region using NDSI derived from Landsat 8 imagery for the years 2013, 2014, and 2015. It computes median composites for each year, masks areas below 2800 meters using a DEM, calculates NDSI with green (B3) and SWIR (B6) bands, applies a threshold (NDSI ≥ 0.4) to classify snow-covered pixels, and computes mean NDSI and fractional snow cover within a geometry. Outputs include NDSI maps, binary snow threshold layers, and printed regional statistics for comparison across years.

The script calculates multiple radiometric vegetation and water indices (RVI, NDVI, SAVI, NDWI) from a single Sentinel-2 image acquired in winter. It uses spectral band math operations including ratio and normalized difference methods on red, near-infrared (NIR), and shortwave infrared (SWIR) bands. The outputs include false-color visualizations of the original image and layered maps of each index with specific color palettes for interpretation, all focused on assessing land surface conditions during winter.

The script identifies salinized cropland areas in Fujian (FJ) and Jiangxi (JC) provinces using multi-threshold masking on Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 derived indices. It processes VV backscatter (T1_VV70sub30), chlorophyll index red-edge difference (T3_CIre_diff_sum), and ARI-EVI2 coupling index (T4_ARI_EVI2_coupling) to generate binary masks, combines them with a cropland mask derived from land cover classification, clips to provincial boundaries, and merges results. Outputs include a final salinized cropland raster map and a CSV table summarizing the area of detected salinization per administrative unit.

The script compiles a multi-temporal, multi-sensor Landsat surface reflectance collection (Landsat 5, 7, and 8) over a specified region of interest. It applies consistent filtering for cloud cover, geometric quality, and image quality, then maps preprocessing functions to standardize band names and add multiple spectral indices including NDWI, MNDWI, AWEI (water), DBSI, NDBI, BSI, MBI (bare soil and built-up), and NDVI, GNDVI, CMRI (vegetation). The output is a merged ImageCollection containing consistently processed images with 13 selected bands and derived indices, enabling long-term land surface monitoring and change analysis across sensors.

The script identifies areas with high near-infrared (NIR) reflectance in a Landsat 8 surface reflectance image from July 2016 over a region in Spain. It applies cloud masking using the pixel_qa band, computes a threshold on the NIR band (B5 > 3000), performs morphological opening (focal_min followed by focal_max) to remove noise, and outputs a binary thresholded map, the raw NIR band, and the opened result. Visualizations include false-color composites (B4-B3-B2) for context.

The script generates a median composite from Sentinel-2 imagery over a specified geometry for the year 2016, applies cloud masking using QA60 band to exclude cloudy and cirrus-affected pixels, and computes a spectral composite. It then performs superpixel segmentation using the SNIC (Simple Non-Iterative Clustering) algorithm with a seed grid of 5 meters and segment size of 10, producing mean reflectance values per cluster for Sentinel-2 bands B2–B12. The output includes a classified raster of segmented clusters with random colors and a layer showing mean band values, intended for land cover homogenization and regional pattern analysis.

The script analyzes changes in vegetation condition over two time periods using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data. It processes two image collections (2018 and 2020) by masking clouds, computing NDVI and MVI vegetation indices, calculating median composites, and deriving the difference in NDVI between the periods. The output includes median S2 images, percentile reductions, NDVI difference maps, and visualizations for both time points, with results masked to areas of significant vegetation (NDVI > 0.20).

The script analyzes vegetation dynamics over a defined agricultural field using Sentinel-2 imagery from 2016 to 2020. It computes NDVI and SAVI indices after applying cloud masking based on the S2_CLOUD_PROBABILITY dataset and CDI/Cirrus band thresholds. The workflow includes joining Sentinel-2 surface reflectance with cloud probability, masking clouds, filtering images by maximum cloud cover and number of cloudy pixels, removing specific dates, and computing temporal composites (max, median, sum) of NDVI for 2020 and multi-year periods, as well as SAVI sum over selected winter seasons. Outputs include composite raster maps of NDVI max/median/sum, three-year NDVI sum, and SAVI sum, all clipped to the field boundary, along with true-color images for each date in the 2020 collection added to the map for visual inspection.
task_name: Analyze vegetation dynamics using NDVI and SAVI

task_description: The script filters a Landsat 8 TOA reflectance image collection using multiple criteria: temporal range (2014-01-01 to 2014-04-01 or shorter intervals), WRS path/row coordinates (44,34), spatial bounds defined by a user-specified polygon over Beijing, and specific image IDs. It does not perform analysis or modeling but demonstrates data selection workflows for a target region and time period, outputting filtered image collections for inspection in the console.
task_name: Filter Landsat images by region and date

task_description: The script classifies land cover in A Coruña, Spain using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery from July 2020. It computes multiple spectral indices (NDWI, NDBI, MNDWI, AWEI, NDVI) to enhance discrimination between land cover classes, applies cloud masking via QA60 band filtering, and trains a Random Forest classifier using labeled training samples (VT_tierra, VT_agua, RF_tierra, RF_agua). The classification is performed on the composite dataset of indices, and feature importance is printed for model interpretation. Outputs include a classified land cover map and relative importance scores for each spectral index used.

The script generates a multi-temporal composite of surface reflectance imagery from Landsat 7 and 8 over three seasonal periods (Jan-Apr, May-Aug, Sep-Dec) between 2014 and 2016. It applies atmospheric correction, cloud masking, band harmonization (ETM+ to OLI), spectral index calculation (NDVI, EVI, GCVI, NBR, NDWI, mNDWI, NDBI, NDSI, MSAVI2, SATVI, BSI, BR), percentile-based outlier filtering (99th percentile), gap-filling using median composites, and finally computes temporal standard deviation across the full period. The output is a stacked image combining three gap-filled seasonal median composites and one standard deviation layer, all masked to remove extreme pixel values, intended for land surface monitoring and change analysis.

The script performs terrain correction on Sentinel-1 GRD imagery to mitigate topographic distortions such as layover and shadow in mountainous areas. It calculates gamma nought (γ⁰) backscatter using radiometric terrain normalization, applies a volume scattering model to correct for slope effects, computes local incidence angle, and derives terrain-corrected VV and VH bands along with auxiliary layers including layover, shadow, slope, aspect, and backscatter ratios. The output is a terrain-corrected SAR image with enhanced radiometric accuracy for use in land cover analysis over rugged terrain.

The script classifies land cover types using Sentinel-2 imagery and a set of labeled training regions. It loads a single image from the Sentinel-2 collection, trains a CART (Classification and Regression Trees) classifier using sample points from six classes (calles, pasto, arbustos, Ciudad, suelo_desnudo, nubes), applies the classifier to the image for pixel-wise classification, and generates a classified raster where each class is renamed to a descriptive label (e.g., 'calles', 'pasto'). The output includes the classified map and intermediate assets such as training samples and the raw classification result for analysis.

The script analyzes temporal changes in land surface temperature (LST) around Hyderabad using Landsat imagery from 1984 to 2020. It constructs an annual and monthly time series of LST by selecting the least cloudy images for April–May each year, computes long-term mean and standard deviation, identifies extreme early and late periods (first and last 5 years), and calculates normalized deviations from the mean. The outputs include mean LST maps for early and late periods, normalized deviation composites, histograms comparing LST and standardized anomalies, and regional statistics (min, max, mean) over the AOI for change analysis.

The script calculates the frequency of daily precipitation events exceeding 12 mm/day over Yunnan in 2020 using NASA's GPM IMERG data. It processes each day's precipitation image by applying a threshold (>=12 mm) to identify significant rainfall days, then counts how many days meet this criterion (ERA_bigger), and separately counts total days with any measurable rain (<12 mm unmasked as 1) to compute the ratio P_d12 = sum(bigger12) / sum(counter). Outputs include intermediate ImageCollections (ERA_bigger, ERA_counter), the final ratio raster (P_d12), and visualizations added to the map.

The script analyzes the mean monthly change in nighttime light intensity in Jordan between 2019 and 2020 using VIIRS-derived data. It applies coverage and low-radiance masks to ensure data quality, computes mean nightlight change per administrative division via reduceRegions, classifies the results into four intensity categories based on thresholding, and outputs a categorized raster map of nightlight change intensity along with a feature collection containing mean statistics for each region.

The script maps mining areas in two time periods (2013 and 2020) using Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery. It applies cloud masking based on pixel QA bits, computes median composites for each year, and trains an AMNH Maxent classifier using known mining locations and random background points. The classification is applied to the 2013 composite for both years' analyses (with training from respective median images), generating probability rasters of mining presence. Outputs include median-composite false-color visualizations and Maxent-derived probability layers for 2013 and 2020, enabling change analysis in mining extent.

The script extracts the 'pixel_qa' band from a Landsat image and applies bitwise operations to identify cloudy and shadowed pixels. It evaluates specific bit flags in the pixel quality assessment band corresponding to cloud confidence, cloud shadow, snow, and cirrus conditions, combining them into a single binary mask where 1 indicates cloud or shadow contamination. The output is a cloud/shadow mask raster for use in masking out poor-quality pixels in downstream analyses.

The script analyzes vegetation patterns in a 3000-meter buffered region around a point in Idaho using NAIP imagery from 2014. It computes NDVI at 1m and 10m resolutions and derives texture metrics (standard deviation of NDVI) using square kernels of 1, 2, and 3 meters, then resamples them to 10m. The output includes layered visualizations of NAIP imagery, NDVI at two scales, and three texture layers representing spatial variability of vegetation, intended for fine-scale land cover or agricultural structure analysis.
task_name: Analyze NDVI and texture at multiple scales

task_description: The script analyzes fire occurrence in a specified region using the ESA CCI FireCCI/5_1 dataset from 2001 to 2018. It filters fire images by confidence level (>50), computes annual count of distinct burn days (indicating burned area extent) and the modal day of year (indicating peak burning time) per year, clips results to a user-defined geometry, and outputs two image collections: one for annual burned area (fireCNT) and one for dominant burn timing (fireDOY), both with year properties set for time-series analysis.
task_name: Map annual burned area and timing

task_description: The script compares seasonal surface water variations in 2019 by computing NDWI from Sentinel-2 imagery for summer and winter periods. It applies cloud masking using the QA60 band, calculates median composites for each season, computes NDWI using bands B3 and B8, and generates NDWI and RGB visualizations for both seasons. The difference between summer and winter NDWI is also computed to highlight changes in surface water extent, supporting analysis of seasonal hydrological dynamics.

The script analyzes surface water extent at Theewaterskloof, South Africa, using Landsat 8 TOA and Surface Reflectance (SR) data from May to August 2019. It computes median composites for both collections, then derives NDVI and NDWI indices to compare vegetation and water presence. A binary water mask is generated by comparing NDWI > NDVI, highlighting pixels where water signals dominate over vegetation. Outputs include RGB visualizations, NDVI and NDWI maps with custom color palettes, and two water masks—one from TOA and one from SR data—for comparative analysis of atmospheric correction impacts on water detection.
task_name: Identify water bodies using NDWI and NDVI

task_description: The script predicts bathymetric depth in a coastal or inland water body using Sentinel-2 imagery. It applies cloud and cirrus masking via QA60 band, filters pixels using B9 (aerosol/Water Vapor) and B3 (green) reflectance thresholds, performs morphological closing with focal_min, then computes NDWI (Green/SWIR: B3/B7) to mask non-water areas. A linear regression model is trained from sampled points with known depths to relate NDWI values to observed depths, deriving slope and intercept. The final output is a predicted depth raster map derived from the NDWI-regression model, validated using RMSE, and summarized with min/max predicted depth over the study area.

The script analyzes vegetation patterns in the Lake Chad region using NDVI derived from Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery between July and September from 2000 to 2017. It applies cloud masking to improve data quality, computes NDVI using near-infrared and red bands, renames spectral bands for clarity, and generates two composite images: one using a quality mosaic based on maximum NDVI and another using median reduction. The outputs include false-color visualizations of a sample image, NDVI-enhanced composites, and mosaicked results for vegetation assessment over time.

The script computes monthly mean NDVI and NDVI anomalies for Spain using MODIS MOD13Q1 data from 2000 to 2020. It calculates long-term monthly averages, then compares a selected year (2005) to this baseline to derive per-pixel NDVI anomalies. The output includes 12 monthly mean NDVI images, 12 corresponding anomaly maps, and a visual legend panel added to the map for interpretation of anomaly values.

The script processes Landsat 8 TOA reflectance imagery over a study area to generate a median composite for the year 2015. It filters images by date and geographic bounds, applies cloud masking using the simpleCloudScore algorithm with a threshold of 40, and computes the median pixel value across the time series. The output includes visualizations of individual scenes, the median composite before and after cloud masking, and metadata such as image count, sun elevation statistics, and least cloudy image. The final product is a cloud-corrected median composite image suitable for land surface analysis.
task_name: Generate median composite of cloud-masked Landsat imagery

task_description: The script computes the Vegetation Condition Index (VCI) using NDVI derived from Landsat 5 and 8 TOA reflectance data over a defined bounding box between 1998 and 2000. It first filters both collections by date and spatial bounds, applies cloud masking using simpleCloudScore, merges the collections, calculates NDVI, and then normalizes NDVI values per image using min-max scaling over the region to derive VCI. The output is a mean VCI image layer and a printed ImageCollection of VCI images for temporal analysis.

The script processes Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery from 2017 to 2020 over three regions (mextro, nicoya, guayaq) to compute a set of spectral indices including NDVI, MNDWI, AWEI, NDBI, BSI, and others. It applies cloud filtering and image quality screening, then calculates median, 10th, 25th, 75th, and 90th percentiles across the time series. An IQR band is derived and combined with median and percentile bands into a mosaic. Spectral signatures are extracted at labeled point samples within each region using sampleRegions, producing feature collections with class-labeled spectral data for input to land cover classification models.
task_name: Extract spectral indices for land cover classification

task_description: The script extracts Fraction of Photosynthetically Active Radiation (FPAR) values from MODIS MCD15A3H data over a specified region and time period (2002–2018). It applies quality filtering using the QA and QA2 bands by masking out poor-quality pixels based on specific bit flags in the DetailedQA layers, then scales the FPAR values by multiplying by 0.01. The output is a masked and scaled ImageCollection of FPAR suitable for time-series vegetation analysis.

The script classifies land cover types in a user-defined region using Landsat 8 TOA reflectance imagery from 2018. It computes spectral indices (MNDWI, NDBI, NDVI), applies cloud masking via simpleCloudScore, and trains a Random Forest classifier using labeled sample regions (built, water, cultivated, forest, glass). The output includes a classified raster map with five land cover classes and an error matrix for accuracy assessment using a 70-30 train-test split.

The script processes Sentinel-3 OLCI Level-1B radiance data from October 20–21, 2019, to generate a median RGB composite using Oa08, Oa06, and Oa04 radiance bands. It extracts the quality_flags band and applies bit-level decoding to identify cloud presence by checking bit 27 (indicative of cloud flag in Sentinel-3), creating a binary cloud mask. This mask is then applied in two ways: first by masking pixels (setting them to null) and second by multiplying pixel values with the mask (zeroing out cloudy pixels). The outputs include the original RGB composite, the raw cloud mask, the masked image collection, and the multiplied image collection for visual comparison and further analysis.

The script extracts surface reflectance and snow albedo data over cropland areas using MODIS MCD43A4 and MCD43A2 products for July 2018. It first masks the land cover to include only cropland (LC_Type1 = 10) using MCD12Q1, then combines nadir reflectance bands (b1–b7) from MCD43A4 with snow quality assurance (SNOWQA) from MCD43A2. A filtering mask is applied to exclude saturated pixels (values ≥32767) and scenes with non-zero snow QA flags. The output is a masked and filtered ImageCollection containing surface reflectance and snow-free conditions over cropland within the region of interest.

The script computes a cloud-masked median composite from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery over a user-defined region of interest (roi) for mid-year 2020. It applies cloud, shadow, and cirrus masking using the MSK_CLDPRB, MSK_SNWPRB, and SCL bands, then calculates spectral indices including NDVI (vegetation), NDBI (built-up areas), MNDWI (surface water), and BSI (bare soil index) to analyze land cover characteristics. The output is a multi-band image with added spectral indices, clipped to the roi, for detailed land surface analysis.
task_name: Analyze vegetation and land cover indices

task_description: The script identifies surface water extent in reservoirs using NDWI derived from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery collected between 2022-10-20 and 2022-12-09. It computes NDWI using green (B3) and NIR (B8) bands, applies Otsu's thresholding on NDWI histograms to dynamically binarize water pixels, masks non-water areas, and calculates the water-covered area per image within reservoir boundaries. Outputs include a feature collection with area measurements for each reservoir and date, enabling temporal water extent analysis.

The script analyzes carbon monoxide (CO) column number density from Sentinel-5P satellite observations over a user-defined region across multiple years. It filters the S5P OFFL/L3_CO dataset for specific date ranges in March–July of 2019, 2020, and 2021, selects the 'CO_column_number_density' band, and maps each image to extract the acquisition month. The resulting collection is grouped by distinct months for potential monthly compositing or time series analysis, and outputs a mapped layer of the input table geometry on the interactive viewer.

The script models the Drought Severity Index (DSI) by combining vapor pressure deficit (vpd) and elevation-derived snow water equivalent proxy (swe) from GRIDMET and NASADEM, respectively. It transforms monthly PDSI data into daily resolution and computes a GAM regression model using vpd, swe, dsi, and pdsi as predictors to predict pdsi. The output is a trained GAM model with selected hyperparameters based on AICc, printed for evaluation.

The script extracts stable nighttime lights from the DMSP-OLS sensor for the year 1993. It filters the NOAA/DMSP-OLS/NIGHTTIME_LIGHTS ImageCollection to the year 1993, selects the 'stable_lights' band using both direct and chained filtering methods, and prints the resulting image collections. The output consists of filtered ImageCollections containing only the 'stable_lights' band for 1993, intended for analysis of human settlement patterns or urbanization via nighttime light intensity.

The script analyzes surface and root-zone soil moisture from the SM dataset over a specific time period. It filters images from two different years (2017 and 2000), selects the first available image for each year, computes the difference between top-layer (0–10 cm) and deeper-layer (40–100 cm) soil moisture in 2017, and also computes the temporal difference of top-layer moisture between 2017 and 2000. The outputs include mapped layers of initial soil moisture states, their vertical difference in 2017, and the inter-annual change from 2000 to 2017 for comparative analysis.

The script identifies surface water extent in a reservoir using Sentinel-1 VV backscatter data from October 2–11, 2021. It applies speckle filtering via focal median, followed by unsupervised k-means clustering (2 clusters) on sampled pixels within the reservoir to classify water vs. non-water. The dominant cluster is inverted to generate a binary water mask, which is then mapped across the image collection. Outputs include individual water mask layers labeled by date and a printed image collection of the resulting water extent rasters.

The script computes annual mean and standard deviation of the Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI) from MODIS MOD13Q1 data over a 16-year period (2001–2016). It calculates yearly composites using temporal reduction (mean and stdDev), then derives interannual mean of annual means and interannual mean of annual standard deviations. The outputs include a multi-band image combining these two interannual metrics, individual annual SD layers added to the map, and printed image collections for further analysis.

The script computes and compares NDVI values over a shared boundary area using a single Landsat 8 TOA image and a single Sentinel-2 SR image acquired in early April 2021. It calculates NDVI using red and near-infrared bands from each sensor, clips both images to a common geometry (excluding rivers), and generates NDVI maps, min/max statistics over the region, and histograms for visual comparison of vegetation index distributions between the two satellite sensors.
task_name: Compare NDVI from Landsat and Sentinel

task_description: The script analyzes forest and surface structural characteristics using ALOS PALSAR L-band SAR backscatter data over Novo Progresso, Brazil, and compares it with Sentinel-1 C-band SAR observations over Tribune, Kansas. It converts PALSAR HH and HV digital numbers to calibrated logarithmic backscatter (dB) through a custom expression, stacks time-series images into multi-band composites, and generates median VV and VH intensity maps from Sentinel-1 GRD data for seasonal analysis. Outputs include calibrated backscatter layers (HH_log, HV_log), stacked time-series bands (HH_stack, HV_stack), and seasonal VV composites for visual and further analytical use.

The script classifies land cover types in a user-defined study area using Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery from July 2019 to June 2020. It computes NDVI, generates median and standard deviation composites, and applies a Random Forest classifier trained on buffered sample points to produce a classified land cover map. The classification is refined using a focal mode filter, and accuracy is assessed via an error matrix using a test dataset, with results including overall accuracy, user's accuracy, and producer's accuracy.

The script identifies oilseed (likely rapeseed) cultivation areas in Fujian (FJ, SJDM='35') and Jiangxi (JC, SJDM='36') provinces using dual-polarization SAR and spectral indices from Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 imagery in 2018. It applies threshold-based masking on T2_VH_diffneg_sum (VH backscatter difference) and T3_CIre_diff_sum (red-edge chlorophyll index difference), combines the masks, and intersects them with cropland derived from a land cover map. The output is a binary raster map of oilseed cultivation (youdao) and a county-level CSV table summarizing cultivated area (in km²) for each administrative unit.

The script prepares Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery over Yilan for land cover classification. It filters images by date (2022-06-01 to 2022-10-31), location (Yilan), and cloud cover (<20%), then composites the median pixel values across the time period. The resulting composite is used to extract training samples from three predefined classes—water, vegetation, and built-up areas—based on user-defined geometries. Outputs include a median composite image in surface reflectance bands and a training dataset for supervised classification, which can be used to train a classifier for land cover mapping.

The script identifies salt-affected cropland in Fujian (FJ) and Jiangxi (JC) provinces using multi-source remote sensing indicators from 2018. It processes SAR backscatter (VV), crop index difference (CIre_diff_sum), and ARI-EVI2 coupling data, applying threshold-based masking to derive binary indicators for salinity stress. These masks are combined with a cropland map derived from land cover classification, and the final yandao (salt-affected farmland) map is generated by merging results from both regions. Outputs include a classified raster of salt-affected cropland and a CSV table summarizing the area per administrative unit at county level.

The script calculates an optimal threshold for Sentinel-1 VV polarization backscatter values using Otsu's method applied to a histogram derived from a median-reduced SAR image over a region of interest. It first filters Sentinel-1 GRD imagery by date, polarization (VV), and instrument mode (IW), computes the median composite, extracts a histogram of VV values within the ROI, and applies the custom OTSU function to determine the threshold that maximizes inter-class variance. The output is a single threshold value printed as 'threshold_S2', which can be used for binary classification (e.g., water/non-water or urban/vegetation).

The script identifies peanut cultivation areas in Liaoning Province (focusing on Fuxin City) for the year 2020 using two vegetation indices: CCCI and CARI. It first processes CCCI to mask low values (<0.08) and CARI to mask high values (>0.60), both scaled appropriately, then combines them with a cropland mask (LN_cropland) and excludes rice areas (WS_RICE_LN_2020). The final peanut cultivation mask is generated by intersecting these conditions: CCCI near zero, CARI indicating red-edge vegetation signal, and non-rice cropland. Outputs include a classified raster map of peanut areas and a CSV table summarizing the area (in km²) of peanut and non-peanut classes within Fuxin City.

The script calculates the area of illuminated pixels (greater than 0 in B2) within Arequipa's administrative boundaries using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data. It generates a binary mask of active pixels, computes total area via pixel summation and pixel counting methods, and outputs the difference between both area estimates for validation purposes.

The script retrieves a collection of Landsat 8 Top-of-Atmosphere (TOA) reflectance images over a specific point location, filters them by date from 2000 to 2019, and selects the image with the lowest cloud cover over land. It outputs the full ImageCollection for inspection and then prints the least cloudy image based on the 'CLOUD_COVER_LAND' metadata property.

The script maps maize cultivation areas in Kenya and Tanzania by combining classified cropland masks with a maize-specific classification layer derived from Sentinel-2 imagery. It applies masking and mosaicking operations to generate a unified maize extent map for East Africa, using GCVI as a vegetation index input for modeling. The output is a raster map representing cropland and refined maize-covered areas.

The script identifies burned areas in California using MODIS MCD64A1 Burn Date data from July 1 to September 10, 2021. It generates a binary mask distinguishing burned and unburned regions, converts these into vector polygons, and creates 200 random points within both fire-affected and no-fire regions. Outputs include vector layers for fire and no-fire regions, random point samples, and visualizations on the map for spatial analysis.
task_name: Identify burned areas and generate fire/no-fire random points

task_description: The script computes annual summer median NDVI values from Landsat surface reflectance imagery (L5, L7, L8) over a circular area of 5 km radius centered at a point in Mongolia. It extracts NDVI using the normalized difference of NIR and red bands, filters images for June through September each year from 1994 to 2016, calculates median composites per summer period, and retrieves mean NDVI within the AOI. The output is a dictionary mapping each summer start date to the mean NDVI value over the region, used for trend analysis.

The script computes multiple vegetation and land surface indices from Sentinel-2 imagery over a specified region between July 7, 2022, and August 21, 2022. It processes cloud-filtered images (with less than 15% cloud cover), clips them to a user-defined ROI, and calculates 16 spectral indices including NDVI, SAVI, MSAVI, GNDVI, GLI, ARVI, AVI, EVI, VARI, LAI, NDRE, RECI, NDMI, MSI, GCI, NBRI, and BSI. These indices are mapped across the image collection and reduced using the last observation to produce a single composite image representing peak vegetation conditions. The output is a multi-band raster with all computed indices for further biophysical analysis.

The script performs land cover classification using a Random Forest classifier trained on spectral and index-based features. It splits sample points into training and testing sets using a random column with a fixed seed, trains the classifier using bands and indices (blue, green, red, nir, swir1, swir2, NDVI, NDWI), evaluates training accuracy via confusion matrix, and validates the model on an independent test set to compute validation accuracy. Outputs include the trained classifier's confusion matrices for both training and testing data, overall accuracy metrics, and a classified feature collection with predictions.

The script calculates the median of 2-meter air temperature over a specified region (NECA) and time range (1999-12-20 to 2000-01-01) using daily mean temperature data. It filters the temperature dataset by date and spatial bounds, then applies a median reduction across the image collection to produce a single composite image representing median air temperature, and prints the resulting image and a dictionary (likely containing metadata or reduced values).

The script performs Principal Component Analysis (PCA) on a mosaicked image collection (INDEX2000_01) over a defined region (ZONA). It centers the image data by subtracting mean values derived from the region, computes covariance and eigenvalues/vectors to derive principal components, normalizes them by standard deviation, and selects the first three components (pc1, pc2, pc3). It then calculates min/max pixel values per PC band across the region, adds these as bands, and applies a normalization expression '(I-IMIN)/(IMAX-IMIN)' on 'cp1' (likely a typo for 'pc1') to generate a normalized index band 'cp1_N'. The output is a processed raster with PCA bands, min/max statistics, and a normalized component band, centered on the study area.
task_name: Extract principal components from image collection

task_description: The script identifies vegetation areas in the Olaroz-Cauchari basin using a Tasseled Cap transformation (greenness component) derived from Sentinel-2 imagery. It computes NDVI and applies a spectral condition (blue < SWIR1) to mask non-vegetation pixels. Training and validation samples for shrublands and meadows are collected, and the greenness index is used to generate threshold-based classification models evaluated for producer accuracy. The output includes mean greenness values for vegetation and soil classes, a series of binary vegetation masks at different thresholds, and their validation results.
task_name: Identify vegetation areas using greenness index

task_description: The script identifies water body clusters within a specified region using a precomputed 'cluster' image (likely derived from NDWI or similar water index). It extracts the pixel value at a specific point to isolate a target cluster, creates a binary mask for that cluster, converts it to vector polygons, applies buffering and union operations to merge adjacent features, computes centroids of resulting polygons, and excludes those overlapping with urban and industrial areas. Outputs include a binary water mask, vectorized water bodies, buffered polygons, merged geometry, and filtered centroids representing potential water bodies away from human settlements.
task_name: Identify water body clusters and extract centroids

task_description: The script analyzes vegetation conditions in Cundinamarca, Colombia using Sentinel-2 imagery. It filters cloud-free images (less than 20% cloud cover), mosaics and clips them to the department boundary, computes median composites, and derives NDVI and EVI vegetation indices. Key outputs include a false-color composite image, NDVI and EVI maps with custom color palettes, a histogram of DN values for visible and NIR bands, and printed metadata including image count, date range, and cloud statistics.
task_name: Analyze NDVI and EVI vegetation indices

task_description: The script calculates the extent of surface water within a reservoir (embalse) using a threshold-based NDWI (Normalized Difference Water Index) approach. It generates a binary water mask where pixels with NDWI >= 0 are classified as water, computes the pixel area for each water pixel, masks the area image to retain only water-covered pixels, and performs a zonal sum reduction over the reservoir geometry to estimate total water surface area in square meters. Outputs include the water mask layer, masked pixel area, and the final surface area value printed to the console.

The script processes Landsat 7 Surface Reflectance data over a user-defined region (chuandian3) to extract vegetation-related information. It filters imagery by date and spatial bounds, selects red and near-infrared bands (SR_B3, SR_B4), applies cloud masking using QA_PIXEL and an external landcover mask, clips to the region of interest, and maps a cloud-removed function across the collection. The output is a cleaned ImageCollection ready for vegetation index computation (e.g., NDVI), intended for vegetation monitoring or land cover analysis.

The script identifies abandoned cropland areas in Fujian (FJ) and Jiangxi (JC) provinces, China, using multi-threshold masking on radar (VV) and optical vegetation indices (CIre, ARI/EVI2 coupling) derived from Sentinel-1 and likely Sentinel-2 data. It applies pixel-wise thresholds to T1_VV70sub30, T3_CIre_diff_sum, and T4_ARI_EVI2_coupling to generate binary masks, combines them with a cropland mask derived from land cover classification (classes 10,11,12,20), clips to provincial boundaries, merges results, and computes the total area of abandoned cropland per elevation band using SRTM DEM. Outputs include classified raster layers for visual inspection and a CSV table summarizing abandoned cropland area (in km²) across elevation zones.

The script analyzes Aqua satellite imagery from July 2016 to identify regions with negative remote sensing reflectance at 678 nm (Rrs_678) within a 10 km buffer around a point location. It creates a binary mask of negative Rrs_678 values, computes the median pixel value in the region from the first image, and calculates the total area (in square meters) where Rrs_678 is negative using pixel area summation. Outputs include a dictionary of median reflectance values and a dictionary of total masked area.

The script analyzes Sentinel-1 GRD imagery to examine VV polarization backscatter characteristics over the 'yan' region during July 2020. It filters for IW mode, ascending orbit, and spatial bounds, then computes metadata statistics including temporal range, sun elevation, and cloud cover. The script identifies the least cloudy image based on CLOUD_COVER metadata, retrieves the 15 most recent images sorted by acquisition time, and prepares a feature collection from the recent image set. Outputs include metadata summaries, image counts, date ranges, solar and cloud statistics, and selected image subsets for further analysis.

The script computes the Modified Normalized Difference Built-up Index (MNDBI) from Landsat surface reflectance imagery (Landsat 4, 5, 7, and 8) over a defined region from 1985 to 2020. It applies sensor-specific cloud and shadow masking using pixel_qa bands, merges collections across sensors, calculates annual median MNDBI composites, and extracts median MNDBI values per administrative unit (or region) via reduceRegions. The output is a time-series CSV table of median MNDBI values by year and geographic unit (identified by 'NUM2') for monitoring urban expansion trends.

The script identifies urban green spaces in a city using FROM-GLC 2015 land cover data. It reclassifies vegetation-related land cover classes into a binary green space mask, clips it to a city boundary derived from a global urban boundary dataset, and converts the raster to vector polygons. It then filters small green space patches (≤1,000,000 m²), computes their areas, and analyzes land surface temperature (LST) within buffered annular zones (30m to 1530m) around these green spaces using LSTmean data. Outputs include the green space vector layer, filtered feature collection, and mean LST values at increasing buffer distances for thermal influence assessment.

The script prepares paired observations of surface reflectance from Landsat 8 and Sentinel-2 over a specified region and time period. It preprocesses both collections by applying cloud masking, clipping to the ROI, reprojecting Sentinel-2 data to match Landsat's resolution and projection, and aligns them temporally. The input features are Landsat 8 bands (B1–B7, solar angles), and the output properties are Sentinel 2 bands (B2, B3, B4, B5, B6, B7, B8A, B8, B11, B12), suggesting a regression or band translation model from L8 to S2. No explicit modeling is performed in this script, but the structure indicates preparation for such a task. Outputs include filtered and processed image collections ready for feature-label pairing.

The script identifies built-up areas in a specified region using the Building Area Extraction Index (BAEI) derived from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery acquired on February 25, 2021. It computes BAEI using red, green, and SWIR1 bands, applies thresholding (BAEI > 0.02 and BAEI < 0.3) to extract built-up surfaces, and outputs a binary raster map of built-up areas along with min/max BAEI values over the study area via reduceRegion.

The script identifies abandoned cropland areas in Fujian (FJ) and Jiangxi (JC) provinces, China, using multi-threshold masking on radar and vegetation index time series derived from Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 data for 2021. It applies threshold-based filters to T1_VV70sub30 (backscatter), T3_CIre_diff_sum (vegetation greenness change), and T4_ARI_EVI2_coupling (stress index) to generate binary masks, combines them with a cropland mask derived from land cover classification (classes 10,11,12,20), clips to provincial boundaries, and merges results. The output includes classified raster maps of abandoned cropland and an area statistics table aggregated by administrative units.

The script analyzes burned areas in the Manacacias region from 2010 to 2019 using FireCCI 5.1 BurnDate data. It filters fire observations by month, clips them to the study area, and computes the minimum burn date per pixel for each month. Then, it counts the number of burned pixels per month within the region using reduceRegion with a count reducer. The results are combined into a dictionary of monthly burned pixel counts, converted to an array, and used to compute percentile statistics (25, 50, 75, 80, 90, 95, 99) and maximum pixel count across months. Outputs include a map of monthly burn layers and printed tables of monthly pixel counts, fire season percentiles, and peak burning intensity.
task_name: Map monthly burn dates and count pixels

task_description: The script identifies the least cloudy Sentinel-2 image over a specified region of interest between 2019 and 2020. It filters the Copernicus S2-HARMONIZED collection by location, date, and cloud cover (less than 50%), then selects the first image with the lowest CLOUDY_PIXEL_PERCENTAGE. The output includes metadata such as image ID, cloud percentage, and acquisition time, along with visualizations of the full collection and the selected image using false-color composites (B4, B8, B2).

The script classifies land cover types using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery from 2021 to 2022. It applies cloud masking based on the QA60 band, computes NDBI as an additional spectral index, and trains an SVM classifier using labeled sample regions (qita and fadianzhan) with 70% of the data for training and 30% for validation. The output includes a classified land cover map, a confusion matrix, overall accuracy, kappa coefficient, and vector polygons derived from the classification, supporting accuracy assessment and spatial analysis.

The script estimates bathymetric depth in the Babitonga estuary using Sentinel-2 satellite imagery from 2018. It applies cloud and water masking using QA60 and SCL bands, filters images by date and geometry, and enhances water pixels using NDWI. Two genetic algorithm-derived models (aGenesColab and aGenesLocal) are used to compute quality bands (QAC and QAL), which incorporate blue, green, and NIR bands to estimate water clarity and depth. A median composite and quality mosaics (based on QAC and QAL) are generated. The output includes RGB visualizations of raw, masked, and quality-mosaic images, with potential use for shallow water bathymetry mapping.
task_name: Estimate bathymetric depth using satellite imagery

task_description: The script generates a multi-temporal composite of Landsat surface reflectance imagery over a specified region from 2014 to 2016, divided into three seasonal periods (Jan-Apr, May-Aug, Sep-Dec). It applies cloud masking, band harmonization between Landsat 7 and 8, conversion of digital numbers to reflectance, and computes 13 spectral indices including NDVI, EVI, GCVI, NBR, NDWI, mNDWI, NDBI, NDSI, MSAVI2, SATVI, BSI, BR, and an indexMax layer. Percentile-based outlier filtering (99th percentile) is applied before computing per-period median composites and a long-term (2014–2016) standard deviation map. The outputs include three median composites for seasonal analysis, a standard deviation map for change detection, and intermediate filtered/indexed image collections for land surface monitoring.
task_name: Extract seasonal vegetation and water indices

task_description: The script classifies land cover in a specific WRS path and row using a Random Forest model trained on labeled data. It uses Landsat 8 TOA reflectance in specified bands ('B1' to 'B5') and applies the classifier to an image collection filtered by date, cloud cover, and spatial location. If doRMSE is true, it splits the training data into train and test sets to evaluate model performance. The output is a classified image collection where each image has a predicted land cover map based on the trained model.
task_name: Classify land cover using Random Forest

task_description: The script calculates mean annual precipitation for 2019 by processing the CHIRPS daily rainfall dataset over a user-defined AOI. It extracts precipitation values at sample points, computes summary statistics (mean and standard deviation), and applies Inverse Distance Weighting (IDW) interpolation to generate a continuous precipitation surface. The output includes an interpolated raster map of precipitation, sample point features with precipitation values, and statistical summaries printed to the console.
