A libsvm classifier is trained on labeled sample regions, applied to produce a classified land cover map, and evaluated using accuracy and kappa metrics on training and validation datasets, resulting in a thematic raster output and classification performance statistics.

The script analyzes changes in vegetation over three time periods (2002, 2010, and 2018) using Landsat 7 surface reflectance imagery. It applies a cloud and shadow mask using the pixel_qa band, clips to a region of interest, computes NDVI using bands B4 (red) and B5 (NIR), calculates median composites for each year, and computes pairwise NDVI differences (2002–2010 and 2010–2018) to assess temporal vegetation change. The output is a set of median NDVI composite images and NDVI difference rasters for change analysis.

The script calculates the mean total water storage in the root zone and underlying soil layers by summing mean soil moisture from four depth intervals (0–10 cm, 10–40 cm, 40–100 cm, 100–200 cm), plus mean snow water equivalent and canopy interception from the GLDAS dataset over a 21-year period. It processes each layer separately using time-averaged images clipped to a user-defined geometry, then combines them into a single composite image representing average integrated terrestrial water storage in the unsaturated and surface-intercepted zones, and outputs the resulting summed raster for analysis.

The script classifies land cover types in the Eden district using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery from September to November 2020. It applies cloud masking, computes a comprehensive set of 45 spectral indices (e.g., NDVI, EVI, SAVI, NDMI), and integrates ALOS landforms and SRTM DEM data. A libsvm classifier is trained on labeled samples to produce a detailed land cover map with 77 classes, validated using accuracy metrics including overall accuracy, kappa, and producer’s/consumer’s accuracy. The output includes classified raster maps, training/validation datasets, and error matrices for both training and validation sets.

The script classifies land cover types in the Eden region using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery from September to November 2020. It applies cloud masking, computes a comprehensive set of spectral indices (e.g., NDVI, EVI, SAVI, NDMI), and integrates terrain features (elevation, slope) and landforms from ALOS AW3D30 and SRTM. A libsvm classifier is trained on labeled sample points to produce a land cover map. The output includes the classified raster, training/validation datasets, and accuracy assessments (overall accuracy and kappa) for both training and validation sets.

The script classifies land cover types in the UH_Tajzara region using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery from 2019 to 2020. It computes NDVI by applying normalizedDifference on bands B8 and B4, adds this as a new band to the median composite, and samples training data from labeled regions (table2) with class labels (CID). A Random Forest classifier is trained using selected bands including B2, B3, B4, B8, B11, and NDVI, then applied to classify the entire image. The output includes a classified land cover map, along with accuracy assessment metrics: confusion matrix, overall accuracy (kappa_precision), and Kappa coefficient, printed for validation.
task_name: Classify land cover using Random Forest

task_description: The script identifies urban areas within grid cells using a combination of Sentinel-2 derived bare soil fraction (Bare_Soil from SCL band), water-masked NDWI, and population density thresholds. It integrates WorldPop population data and JRC GHSL population count to define inhabited areas, applies cloud-masking to Landsat 8 and Sentinel-2 imagery, computes thermal anomalies (focal mean of B10), and generates layered visualizations of urban extent, water frequency, and thermal variation. Outputs include classified urban masks, thermal anomaly rasters, water occurrence maps, and regional statistics for each grid cell.
task_name: Identify urban areas using spectral and population data

task_description: The script analyzes forest extent, tree cover, and forest loss/gain dynamics within three defined Conservation Forest Initiative (CFI) zones—active, potential, and combined—using the UMD Hansen Global Forest Change dataset. It calculates total forest area, tree cover in 2000, and spatially explicit forest loss and gain areas by clipping the forest change rasters to each CFI feature collection and computing pixel-area-weighted sums via reduceRegion. Outputs include printed statistics for each zone reporting area (m²), tree cover (m²), lost area (m²), and gained area (m²), along with map visualizations of the CFI boundaries.
task_name: Analyze forest area and change in CFI zones

task_description: The script classifies land cover types in the Chi basin using Landsat 7 surface reflectance imagery from 2015. It trains a Random Forest classifier with labeled regions (urban, agriculture, forest, bare soil, water) from two time points (urban1/agri1/etc. and urban2/agri2/etc.), applies the classifier to generate a land cover map with five classes, validates accuracy using an error matrix, and computes the area of bare soil in square kilometers. Outputs include a classified raster map, validation accuracy metrics, and bare soil area statistics.

The script classifies land cover into urban, vegetation, and water classes using Landsat 8 TOA reflectance imagery from 2015 over a user-defined region of interest (roi). It trains a CART classifier (ee.Classifier.smileCart) using sample points collected from labeled feature collections (urban, vegetation, water), applies the classifier to produce a land cover map, computes area per class using pixel counting with ee.Image.pixelArea(), and evaluates classification accuracy via an error matrix on a validation set. Outputs include the classified raster map, area statistics per class, validation error matrix, overall accuracy, and a styled legend added to the map.

The script analyzes vegetation conditions in Mexico for the year 2013 using Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery. It computes three spectral indices—NDII1 (similar to NDWI), NDII2 (similar to NBR), and EVI—from atmospherically corrected images after masking clouds and shadows. Median and standard deviation composites are generated for both original bands and derived indices, along with an image count layer indicating data availability per pixel. The output includes median and variability rasters of spectral bands and vegetation indices, as well as a count map of observations, supporting long-term vegetation monitoring and drought or fuel moisture assessment.

The script identifies flood extent before and after a flooding event using Sentinel-1 GRD SAR imagery over a region of interest. It applies speckle filtering via focal mean with a 50-meter radius, then performs land cover classification using a CART classifier trained on manually defined training regions (e.g., permanent water, flooded areas, urban, vegetation). The classification is based on VV polarization and outputs a classified raster map showing different land cover types including flooded areas. Additionally, population density and road infrastructure layers are overlaid for impact assessment.

The script combines median composites of cloud-masked Sentinel-2 Surface Reflectance and Landsat 8 TOA reflectance imagery over a shared geometry. It selects specific optical and SWIR bands from both sensors, normalizes their time stamps, and merges them into a single multi-sensor image collection using 'combine'. The output is a fused image with bands from both platforms, intended for joint analysis or classification, without further processing such as classification or index computation.

The script estimates precipitation (PR) by training a Random Forest regression model using backscatter from Sentinel-1 (VV), MODIS NDVI, and MODIS land surface temperature (LST) as predictors. It samples pixel values at specified point locations to train the model, then applies the trained classifier to a merged image stack to generate a continuous precipitation estimation map. The output is a classified raster layer representing spatially distributed precipitation estimates based on multi-sensor satellite data.
task_name: Estimate precipitation using SAR and MODIS data

task_description: The script classifies land cover types using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery from September to November 2020 over a user-defined region. It computes a comprehensive set of 43 spectral indices and combines them with elevation, slope, SRTM DEM, and ALOS landform data as input features. A libsvm classifier is trained on labeled sample points to produce a classified land cover map. The output includes the classified raster, training accuracy (from confusion matrix), and validation accuracy (from error matrix) metrics.

The script classifies land cover types in a specified region using Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery from September to October 2020. It trains a Random Forest classifier on labeled samples of 'Indigeneous_Forest' and 'Sugarcane' classes, evaluates classification accuracy via a confusion matrix using a stratified 70/30 train-test split, and generates a classified raster map clipped to the study area. Additionally, it computes the area (in square meters) of each classified land cover class within the region using pixel counting and outputs both the classification map and area statistics for further analysis.

The script classifies land cover types in the Chi basin using Landsat 7 surface reflectance imagery from 2015. It trains a Random Forest classifier with labeled regions (urban, agriculture, forest, bare soil, water) from two different datasets (Turban/Tagri/Tforest/Tbaresoil/Twater and Vurban/Vagri/Vforest/Vbaresoil/Vwater), applies the model to generate a classified land cover map, and validates the result using an error matrix and overall accuracy assessment. Outputs include the classified raster map, training/validation datasets, and accuracy metrics.

The script computes a mean composite from merged Landsat 5 and Landsat 8 surface reflectance collections after preprocessing (including cloud/shadow masking and band renaming via prepL57 and prepL8 functions). It first reduces resolution using a mode reducer, reprojects to EPSG:4326 at 500m scale, then merges the two collections and calculates their pixel-wise mean. This mean image is then further reprojected using reduceResolution with a mean reducer at 30m default projection and resampled to a specified scale, resulting in a smoothed, spatially consistent landsatMean layer added to the map. The output is a continuous raster representing average spectral reflectance properties across time and sensors.

The script classifies land cover types using a multi-temporal Sentinel-2 or Landsat-like surface reflectance dataset with spectral and derived indices (NDVI, NDBI, NDWI) across four time periods. It trains a Random Forest classifier on labeled samples for five classes (wheat, maize, tree, vegetable, other), validates the model using a held-out sample set, and outputs a classified land cover map along with accuracy metrics including confusion matrix, overall accuracy, producer's and user's accuracy, and Kappa coefficient.

The script estimates water clarity depth (Secchi depth) in inland waters using atmospherically corrected Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data. It applies a series of radiative transfer and bio-optical algorithms to derive remote sensing reflectance (Rrs), backscattering, absorption, diffuse attenuation (Kd), and Weber contrast, ultimately computing Secchi depth (z) based on optical water properties. The output is a median composite map of estimated Secchi depth over the study period.

The script identifies vegetated areas in a specific region using NDVI derived from Landsat 8 TOA imagery from 2016. It computes median composites from cloud-filtered images, calculates NDVI for two regions (one general and one cropped), applies a threshold (0.5–0.79) to isolate vegetation, masks non-vegetation pixels, and clips the result to the study area. Outputs include RGB mosaics, NDVI maps, a binary vegetation mask, mean NDVI values for both regions, and total area statistics for classified vegetation in square kilometers.

The script classifies land cover types in the Eden region using Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-1 satellite imagery combined with ALOS PALSAR, SRTM, and ALOS World 3D topographic data. It computes a comprehensive set of spectral, radar, and terrain indices, then applies an SVM (libsvm) classifier trained on labeled regions to produce a land cover map. The output includes the classified raster, training/validation sample splits, and accuracy assessment via confusion and error matrices for model validation.

The script retrieves two cloud-filtered Sentinel-2 surface reflectance image collections over a specific area for two different time periods in 2015 and 2020. It selects blue, green, red, and near-infrared bands (B2, B3, B4, B8) and applies a cloud coverage threshold of less than 25%. The outputs are two printed image collections (composite1 and composite6), which can be used for visual comparison or further analysis of surface changes over time, such as vegetation or land cover change detection.

The script estimates vegetation fractional cover (VFC) in Wuhan using Landsat 8 Surface Reflectance data from June to September 2020. It calculates NDVI, samples vegetation and non-vegetation training points based on land cover types, computes mean NDVI values for these classes, and applies a linear spectral unmixing model (NDVI-based VFC) with fixed soil and vegetation endmembers. The output is a normalized vegetation fraction map (clamped between 0 and 1) representing the proportion of vegetated area per pixel.

The script calculates the area (in hectares) of several predefined regions (L142, l142, b1, L12F, L143, L8, Lote8, resto, lote11) and prints their sizes. It also queries Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery from two time periods: August 2023 for recent conditions and September 2022 to March 2023 to identify potential burn events. The script filters images by cloud cover and spatial bounds, then inspects image collections for visual analysis of burned areas. Outputs include printed area values and two image collections for pre- and post-burn assessment, with a focus on mapping or identifying burned land extent using temporal Sentinel-2 data.

The script analyzes time-series Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from 2016 to 2020 over a defined geometry to derive smoothed EVI, NDVI, SNDBI, and SNDWI using cloud masking and Savitzky-Golay filtering. It computes annual land surface phenology (LSP) metrics including SOS (start of season), EOS (end of season), LOS (length of season), maxIntegral, base vegetation level, peak value, and midtime by fitting seasonal trajectories and detecting key phenological transition points via midpoint thresholding on the smoothed EVI trajectory. The output is a mean multi-band image representing long-term average phenological metrics across years.

The script retrieves the first available REMA (Reference Elevation Model of Antarctica) 8m resolution image from the specified date range and location, filtered by minimal cloud cover. It selects the highest-quality image (least cloudy) within the temporal and spatial constraints around a point in Antarctica, and outputs the resulting image metadata for inspection. No raster processing or analysis is performed beyond filtering and selection.

The script processes Landsat 8 TOA reflectance imagery over a defined AOI to generate multiple composites: median, maximum value, and mosaic images. It filters the collection by spatial bounds and time range (2015–2016), selects the least cloudy scene and ten most recent scenes for inspection, and creates visualizations using bands B4, B5, and B6 (visible to NIR). Outputs include layered composites on the map and metadata prints of image counts and properties, focusing on temporal-spectral aggregation rather than classification or change detection.
task_name: Generate median and max composite from Landsat

task_description: The script analyzes temporal changes in radar backscatter (VV and VH polarizations) from Sentinel-1 over different land cover types—water, dryland, wetland, and irrigated agriculture—within the high divide region. It computes mean VV and VH intensity for July–September across 2016–2019, clips them to predefined polygons, concatenates annual images into time-series stacks, and generates histograms of backscatter values per land cover type to compare their microwave reflectance characteristics over time.

The script classifies land cover types in the ZJ region using Sentinel-2-like multispectral imagery from four different dates (May 2 to August 15). It computes multiple spectral indices (NDBI, NDWI, NDVI) and uses reflectance bands (B2, B3, B4, B5, B6, B8_savg, B8A, B11, B12) as features. A Random Forest classifier is trained on labeled sample points (maize, rice, citrus, maize-citrus, bare land, other) with a 50/50 split for training and validation. The output includes a classified land cover map with six classes and an accuracy assessment via confusion matrix, reporting overall accuracy, producer's accuracy, user's accuracy, and Kappa coefficient.

The script calculates the area of tree cover loss in the year 2001 that meets minimum canopy cover and forest area thresholds. It multiplies a binary loss image (minLoss) by the pixel area to compute area in hectares, then aggregates the total using reduceRegion over a user-defined geometry. The output is a printed dictionary entry with the total area of tree loss in hectares for 2001.

The script estimates chlorophyll-a concentration in a water body using Landsat 8 surface reflectance data from 2018. It applies cloud masking (filtering images with less than 10% cloud cover) and temporal averaging, then computes a band ratio algorithm based on red, NIR, and green bands (B3, B4, B5). A data mask ensures valid pixel regions (non-zero B4), and the final output is a single-band raster representing chlorophyll-a levels, which is mapped over the study area.

The script analyzes MODIS NDVI time series to extract land surface phenology (LSP) metrics for Namibia, focusing on austral summer vegetation cycles. It applies Savitzky-Golay filtering to smooth the MOD13A2 NDVI data, then computes annual phenological indicators including start of season (SOS), end of season (EOS), length of season (LOS), integral of NDVI, base and maximum winter season (MaxWS) values, mean dry season (MeanDS) NDVI, and dry season integral (DSINT). The workflow identifies SOS and EOS using midpoint thresholds derived from min and max NDVI, and outputs a multi-band image collection where each image represents yearly LSP metrics mapped spatially.

The script filters a feature collection of sheds in the Diamer region by the administrative boundary of Diamir District, Pakistan. It processes the 'Live_Bio_1' attribute by parsing it as a number, then selects sheds with 'Live_Bio_1' values less than 5. The output includes the count of sheds after spatial filtering and after attribute-based filtering, although there is a bug where 'largeSheds' is used instead of 'table'.

The script extracts MODIS-derived surface reflectance (Es) values over farm boundaries, scales them by 0.0001 to obtain NDVI-like vegetation index values, and generates a time series of mean index values per farm. It maps the reduced regions to form a flattened feature collection of triplets (farm_id, imageId, Es), then formats it into a structured table where each row represents a farm and columns represent formatted NDVI values indexed by image acquisition date. The final output is a dictionary-formatted feature collection suitable for time series analysis of vegetation dynamics at the farm level.

The script analyzes global surface and subsurface soil moisture data from the NUSM_SMAP dataset between 2010 and 2018. It selects specific soil moisture bands (ssm, susm, smp, ssma, susma), filters them into annual (and partial final year) image collections, mosaics each year's images, and computes the minimum and maximum pixel values over a global land extent using reduceRegion with minMax reducer. Outputs are printed metadata objects containing min and max values for each time segment for analysis.
task_name: Extract soil moisture min max values

task_description: The script applies radiometric terrain correction to Sentinel-1 GRD imagery over a specified geometry for October 2020. It calculates gamma nought (γ⁰) backscatter using SRTM-derived slope and aspect, models volume scattering effects, identifies layover and shadow areas, and computes backscatter ratios (VV/VH). The output includes terrain-corrected VV and VH bands in dB, incidence angle, local incidence angle, alpha_r, phi_s, layover/shadow masks, and pre- and post-correction ratios, added as new bands to the original image collection.
task_name: Apply terrain correction to SAR imagery

task_description: The script estimates Land Surface Temperature (LST) in Chiang Mai using Landsat 8 Collection 1 Tier 1 Surface Reflectance data from 2013. It applies cloud masking using pixel_qa, computes NDVI, derives fractional vegetation cover (FV), estimates emissivity (EM), and calculates LST using a radiative transfer-based expression involving brightness temperature (B10) and emissivity. Outputs include NDVI, FV, EM, thermal band, and LST layers, with min/max statistics computed over the region for scaling visualizations.

The script analyzes vegetation health and moisture conditions using Sentinel-2-derived NDVI and NDMI indices over a specific region, combined with terrain slope classification derived from ALOS World 3D elevation data. It computes spectral indices using custom formulas, applies cloud filtering, clips to a geometry, and generates smoothed slope classes. Additionally, it estimates soil moisture from Sentinel-1 VV backscatter using a mathematical inversion model. Outputs include layered visualizations of RGB composite, NDVI, NDMI, classified slope, and soil moisture maps for integrated environmental assessment.

The script calculates monthly actual evapotranspiration (ET) over a user-defined region using the MODIS MOD16A2 ET product for May–July 2020. It adjusts for partial 8-day composites at month boundaries by applying a day-weighted correction using linear interpolation between consecutive images based on their acquisition day. The final output is a monthly summed ET image collection with a 0.1 scaling factor applied, representing total ET per month in millimeters, and includes time-start metadata formatted as 'YYYY-MM'.

The script estimates urban heat intensity (UHII) for Miami by aggregating UHII values from an ImageCollection to TIGER/2010 Census Tracts. It filters the UHII dataset to the region of interest defined by census tracts, computes mean UHII per tract using reduceRegions with a mean reducer at 30m scale, and selects specific properties (fuel1, capacitymw), renaming them (Fuel_1, Capacity_MW). The output is a FeatureCollection of census tracts with mean UHII and renamed properties, printed for inspection.
task_name: Estimate urban heat intensity by census tract

task_description: The script classifies land cover types in an agricultural region using multispectral and texture features from Sentinel-2 or Landsat imagery across three dates (June, July, August). It computes spectral indices (NDVI, NDBI, NDWI) and Gray-Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) texture metrics (B8_corr, B8_contrast, B8_diss), then trains a Random Forest classifier on labeled samples. The classification is applied to generate a thematic map, and accuracy is assessed using a confusion matrix with producers' accuracy, consumers' accuracy, overall accuracy, and Kappa coefficient outputs.

The script corrects Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery for bidirectional reflectance distribution function (BRDF) and topographic effects using solar and view angles derived from image geometry and DEM. It applies a k-volumetric kernel-based BRDF correction followed by SCS+c topographic normalization, producing BRDF- and topographically-corrected reflectance images for both sensors, with outputs including corrected rasters for blue, green, red, nir, swir1, and swir2 bands.
task_name: Correct surface reflectance for BRDF and topography

task_description: The script extracts environmental variable values at Calomys rodent presence points from a dataset (HS12) using sampleRegions. It uses a merged feature collection of presence records from 2012, clips to specific polygon geometries in Argentina, and samples raster data at these points. The output is a feature collection with sampled pixel values attached to each presence point, printed as 'estad pts', intended for ecological modeling or habitat analysis.
task_name: Extract environmental variables for Calomys presence

task_description: The script calculates the total area, tree cover in 2000, forest loss, forest gain, and annual forest loss from 2000 to 2017 within a floodplain region (RM_floodplain) using the Hansen Global Forest Change dataset. It computes pixel-area-weighted sums via reduceRegion, multiplying binary or fractional images by pixel area, and outputs area statistics in square meters for each metric.
task_name: Quantify forest cover and loss over time

task_description: The script identifies recently harvested agricultural areas near Marcos Juárez, Argentina, using Sentinel-2 imagery from March 12–16, 2023. It computes NDVI from bands B8 and B4, applies a threshold (NDVI > 0.16) to detect low vegetation cover indicative of post-harvest conditions, masks pixels above the threshold over time, and generates a binary map of harvested areas. The total harvested area within a specified polygon is calculated in square meters using pixel area summation and reduction over the region, outputting both a visual layer and quantitative area estimate.

The script analyzes Sentinel-1 SAR imagery before and after a flood event to detect changes in surface water extent. It applies terrain correction using SRTM DEM and speckle filtering (refined Lee filter) to improve image quality. The workflow computes gamma0 backscatter in dB for VH and VV polarizations, corrects for topographic effects, and generates three visualizations: uncorrected mean backscatter, terrain-corrected mean backscatter, and Perona-Malik filtered terrain-corrected backscatter for both pre-flood and post-flood periods. Outputs include mapped layers and metadata on image count and temporal coverage for comparison.

The script extracts a time series of Landsat surface reflectance images (Landsat 5, 7, and 8) over a given geometry with cloud cover filtering, selects red, NIR, green, and blue bands, and computes multiple spectral indices including ratios (e.g., NIR/Red, Red/NIR) and normalized combinations (e.g., (NIR+Red)/2, NIR/(Red+Green)). It outputs a multiband image collection where each image contains these derived indices per time step, intended for vegetation or land surface analysis.

The script segments high-resolution NAIP imagery from 2019 into homogeneous regions using the SNIC (Superpixel Neighbors Clustering) algorithm. It computes NDVI and NDWI as part of spectral preprocessing, selects visible and near-infrared bands (R, G, B, N), normalizes pixel values, generates superpixels via seeded grid clustering, and converts resulting clusters into vector polygons clipped to a buffer zone (goat_buff). The output includes a visual overlay of segmented boundaries on true-color imagery and the derived segmentation map for land cover analysis.

The script computes NDVI using Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery over a specified geometry, filtering images by cloud cover (less than 5%) and date range from 2018 to 2019. It maps an NDVI calculation function across the image collection using bands B4 (red) and B5 (near-infrared), returning a new image collection where each image contains a single 'NDVI' band. The output is printed to the console for inspection.

The script calculates monthly mean Gross Primary Productivity (GPP) from the UMT/NTSG/v2/LANDSAT/GPP dataset over the period 1986–2021. It filters the GPP image collection to select only the 'GPP' band, then applies a temporal compositing function that aggregates the data into monthly means using a sequence of 420 one-month intervals starting from January 1986. The output is a new ImageCollection where each image represents the average GPP for a specific month, with time start and end metadata set accordingly for temporal analysis.

The script computes annual Climate-Enhanced Fraction (CEF) maps for green vegetation (gv), non-photosynthetic vegetation (npv), shade, and soil components over a defined AOI using monthly fraction images derived from Landsat time series. It aggregates monthly gv, npv, shade, and soil fractions by year, normalizes them by the count of valid observations (using GPmask), applies land cover masking to retain only vegetated areas (LC classes 1,2,4,5,6,7), and outputs four multi-band image assets representing yearly CEF values from 1987 to 2020 at 30m resolution.
task_name: Compute annual CEF from Landsat fractions

task_description: The script analyzes forest cover, loss, and gain within the Ream National Park and a specific polygon layer (Elc_no_evidence_of_adjustment_layer_polygon.89) using the UMD Hansen Global Forest Change dataset. It calculates tree cover extent in 2000, forest loss, and total valid data area by clipping the imagery to the region of interest, masking pixels, and computing pixel-area-weighted sums via reduceRegion. Outputs include printed area statistics in square meters for tree cover and forest loss within the defined geometries, along with map visualizations of forest cover and loss layers.
task_name: Analyze forest cover and loss in protected area

task_description: The script calculates monthly average surface soil moisture over a specified region using NASA USDA HSL SMAP 10km soil moisture data from October 2020 to January 2021. It processes the image collection by aggregating daily values into monthly composites using the mean function, clips to a user-defined geometry, and computes the median across time. Finally, it extracts the regional mean value of this median-reduced time series at 10 km scale and prints the result.

The script analyzes temporal changes in Sentinel-1 VV and VH backscatter values from 2016 to 2019 over four land cover types: water, dryland, wetland, and irrigated agriculture. It computes mean backscatter for each year and region, then combines them into multi-band images per land cover type. Histograms of backscatter values are generated for each region and polarization (VV/VH) to compare radar response across years and land types, revealing seasonal and interannual patterns in surface moisture and vegetation structure.
task_name: Analyze VV and VH backscatter over water, dryland, wetland, and irrigated areas

task_description: The script computes NDVI and NDWI vegetation and water indices over a specified point location using Landsat 8, Sentinel-2, Landsat 7, and MODIS satellite data within a given date range. It processes each sensor's imagery by selecting relevant bands, calculating normalized difference indices (NDVI and NDWI), and generating maximum value composites for each index. The outputs include layered visualizations of NDWI and NDVI maps from all four sensors on the map interface for comparative analysis.
task_name: Compute NDVI and NDWI for multiple sensors

task_description: The script creates a multi-temporal Sentinel-1 SAR composite using VV and VH polarization from both ascending and descending orbits over a three-month period in early 2018. It computes the mean backscatter intensity for VH band from ascending passes, mean of merged VV bands from both orbit directions, and VH from descending passes, then combines them into an RGB composite with focal median filtering applied to reduce noise. The output is a spatially smoothed three-band image intended for visual interpretation or classification of surface structure and moisture patterns, particularly useful for land cover and vegetation monitoring.
task_name: Generate SAR composite for land cover analysis

task_description: The script classifies vegetation and non-vegetation areas within a study site using a Landsat 5 TOA reflectance image with the least cloud cover. It trains a Random Forest classifier (100 trees) using labeled training points (Veg_train and Nonveg_train), applies the model to classify the input image into a binary vegetation map, and validates the result using an error matrix and overall accuracy derived from the same training data. Outputs include the classified raster map and classification accuracy metrics.

The script analyzes land cover within the 'page' region by isolating non-irrigated areas through geometric differencing between two feature collections (page and pageIrr). It generates a stratified random sampling grid (30m and 5m) over the non-irrigated area for potential image sampling or analysis. Additionally, it computes the total area of NWI wetlands within the study region using feature area aggregation and attaches this as a property to images in an NAIP time series. Outputs include mapped layers of NAIP imagery (2009, 2019), non-irrigated land, sampling grids, and aggregated wetland area values.

The script computes median NDVI values from MODIS MOD13Q1 imagery across ten consecutive austral summer periods (2009–2019) over Argentina. It processes each time window independently by filtering the image collection to a specific date range, selecting the NDVI band, and reducing it with a median reducer. The output consists of ten median NDVI composite images representing seasonal vegetation conditions over time, enabling temporal comparison of vegetation dynamics across Argentina.

The script classifies land cover types using multi-temporal Sentinel-2 or Landsat-like imagery over a defined region. It computes spectral indices (NDVI, NDBI, NDWI) and includes a Savitzky-Golay smoothed band (B8_savg) across several dates. Training and validation samples are created from labeled polygons (wheat, maize, trees, vegetables, other), and a Random Forest classifier is trained and applied to generate a classified land cover map. Accuracy assessment is performed using a confusion matrix, with outputs including producers' accuracy, consumers' accuracy, overall accuracy, and Kappa coefficient.

The script classifies land cover types in a region defined by the 'xunyi' feature collection using a Random Forest classifier applied to multi-temporal imagery (IMG_05 and IMG_08). It trains the model using labeled sample points (XY_0BC to XY_5DP) split into training (50%) and validation (50%) sets, generates a classified land cover map with a specified color palette, and evaluates classification accuracy using a confusion matrix, producing metrics including producers' accuracy, consumers' accuracy, overall accuracy, and Kappa coefficient.

The script calculates the mean surface reflectance value in the red band (B4) of Landsat 8 OLI sensor over Chad for May 2019. It selects the B4 band from the Landsat 8 Surface Reflectance dataset, filters images by date and location within Chad's geometry, computes the median composite, and then extracts the average pixel value across the country using reduceRegion with a mean reducer. The output is a dictionary containing the mean reflectance value printed to the console.

The script analyzes vegetation conditions in a region of interest using Landsat 8 imagery from April to September 2018. It calculates NDVI and applies an unsupervised clustering method (Weka Cobweb) to segment the landscape. A weighted NDVI (windvi) is computed by multiplying NDVI with cluster labels, followed by summing across the time series. Finally, a normalized enhanced NDVI (rendvi) is derived by dividing the summed windvi by the summed cluster values, producing a composite index map that integrates spectral-temporal patterns and land cover heterogeneity for vegetation assessment.
task_name: Estimate vegetation condition using cluster-weighted NDVI

task_description: The script computes Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI) from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data over a specified geometry, applies a Savitzky-Golay filter to smooth the time series, and extracts key land surface phenology (LSP) metrics including start of season (SOS), end of season (EOS), length of season (LOS), maximum EVI, base EVI, integral of EVI, small integral above base, timing of mid-season, and values at SOS and EOS. These metrics are derived annually by fitting a smoothed seasonal profile and detecting inflection points relative to a midpoint threshold. The final output is a multi-band image representing the long-term mean of each phenological metric across 2016–2020.
task_name: Extract phenological metrics from EVI time series

task_description: The script computes and compares mean summer daytime land surface temperature (LST) for 2019 versus the long-term summer average from 2000 to 2018 using MODIS imagery. It calculates 8-day composite LST during June–August, derives mean temperature maps for both periods, clips them to country boundaries, and computes a difference map. The outputs include three visual layers: mean LST (2000–2018), mean LST (2019), and their difference, enabling spatial analysis of anomalous temperatures in 2019.

The script computes multiple vegetation-related spectral indices (2BDA, 3BDA, NDCI from Sentinel-2; SABI from Landsat 8) over a specific region using surface reflectance data from 2019. It generates individual index images, renames them with descriptive band names, and prints metadata to the console. The outputs are continuous raster layers representing biophysical vegetation properties, intended for detailed vegetation condition or crop health analysis.
task_name: Compute vegetation indices from Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8

task_description: The script identifies surface water areas using Landsat 8 and Landsat 7 surface reflectance imagery from March to November 2020. It computes multiple water indices (NDWI, MNDWI, AWEInsh, AWEIsh) and applies k-means clustering on NDVI-based image segmentation to classify water bodies. For each image, it calculates the total water surface area in square kilometers by masking low-NDVI clusters and summing pixel areas, outputting a time-series collection of images with associated water area estimates.

The script calculates a weighted sum of clay content at three soil depth intervals (0–5 cm, 5–15 cm, and 15–30 cm) using mean clay fraction data from SoilGrids. It extracts the first three bands from the 'clay_mean' dataset, applies depth-specific weights (0.17, 0.33, 0.5), and combines them into a multi-band image stack (Arcilla_stk) representing stratified clay distribution. The output is a printed info summary and a composite raster with weighted clay values per depth layer for further soil analysis.

The script estimates vegetation cover fraction in Shanghai using Sentinel-2 imagery from June to September 2020. It computes NDVI after applying cloud masking (using QA60 band) and filters images by cloud cover. Vegetation and non-vegetation training samples are extracted based on land cover types, and mean NDVI values from these samples are used in a linear spectral unmixing model to compute vegetation fractional cover (VFC). The output is a VFC raster map where values are capped between 0 and 1, representing the proportion of vegetation cover per pixel.

The script generates a segmentation-based clustering of ecological units in the Gran Chaco region by integrating 31 standardized environmental, social, and land-use variables. It first builds a multiband image stack from diverse raster datasets (e.g., elevation, climate, soil, fragmentation, accessibility), normalizes each band using min-max scaling within the study region, and applies the SNIC (Superpixel Neighborhood Iterative Clustering) algorithm to segment the landscape into spectrally homogeneous regions. The output includes a clustered image, vectorized cluster boundaries, and visualizations of seeds and cluster lines, aimed at supporting regional conservation and land management planning.
task_name: Identify ecological clusters using multisource variables

task_description: The script processes a Landsat 8 TOA reflectance image collection by splitting it based on solar elevation: images with SUN_ELEVATION less than 40 degrees are multiplied by 4 (likely simulating a radiometric adjustment), while those with SUN_ELEVATION greater than or equal to 40 are left unchanged. The two subsets are then merged into a single collection. The script outputs the size of the original and processed collections, demonstrating conditional processing of satellite imagery based on metadata. Additionally, it includes list manipulation examples (squaring numbers, filtering odd values) that serve as auxiliary demonstrations but are not part of the main geospatial analysis.
task_name: Process Landsat imagery by sun elevation

task_description: The script classifies land cover in the Chi basin using Landsat 5 SR imagery from 2009. It applies a cloud masking function to surface reflectance data, computes a median composite, and trains a Random Forest classifier using labeled regions (urban, crop, forest, water). The output includes a classified raster map with four land cover classes (forest, crop, water, urban), accuracy assessment via validation points, and area calculations (in sq.km) for each class within the study region.

The script classifies land cover types using a combination of optical bands and spectral indices (e.g., NDBBI, NDWI, BSI, MNDWI) along with principal components (pc1_savg, pc2_savg, pc2_corr) derived from Sentinel-2 or similar multispectral imagery. It trains a Random Forest classifier on labeled sample points (BC, NC, PFM, VC) representing different land cover classes, applies the model to classify the entire region of interest, and validates the results using a held-aside validation set. The output includes a classified land cover map, a confusion matrix for accuracy assessment, and computation of F1 score by combining user's and producer's accuracy metrics.

The script identifies surface water bodies in the Zhangduhu region using NDWI derived from Sentinel-2 imagery from February to December 2020. It applies cloud masking, computes NDWI (B3/B8), normalizes the index, and uses Otsu's method on a histogram to determine an optimal threshold for binary water classification. The output is a water mask and the total water area (in km²) calculated via pixel area summation and printed as a feature property.

The script compares statistical summaries (mean, count, standard deviation) of two modeled datasets (model01 and model16c) grouped by land cover classes across Mexico. It combines each model with a landcover band, then computes regional statistics using reduceRegion with grouping by the 'code' field (land cover class), outputting grouped mean, count, and standard deviation values for each class within the study area.

The script generates a merged shoreline feature collection from multiple Beaufort and Chukchi coastal segments, buffers each shoreline by 1000 meters to create a polygon zone, then extracts random sample points within this buffered zone. It samples a composite Landsat-derived NDWI image collection at these points to obtain pixel values for further analysis. The output is a FeatureCollection of sampled points with NDWI and other index values, intended for use in coastline change or land cover analysis.

The script analyzes cropland phenology in Heilongjiang Province by generating monthly composites of surface reflectance from Landsat and Sentinel-2 imagery for the year 1992. It applies sensor-specific cloud masking to Landsat 5, 7, 8, and Sentinel-2 collections, merges them into a unified time series, and creates monthly mean images over a grid-based region. The output includes visualizations of flood (May–June) and growth (July–September) period composites, individual monthly layers, and a 10x10 grid system over the study area for spatial stratification, supporting regional agricultural monitoring.
task_name: Analyze cropland phenology using multi-sensor imagery

task_description: The script analyzes Sentinel-1 GRD SAR imagery over a specific region using the VV polarization from descending orbit 37. It selects three monthly images from April, May, and June 2015, applies a refined Lee speckle filter to reduce noise while preserving edges, converts the data between natural and decibel units, and generates a three-band RGB composite stack (original and filtered). The output includes visualizations of the original VV stack, the refined Lee filtered stack, and a boxcar 3x3 filtered stack for comparison, enabling qualitative assessment of filtering performance on radar backscatter.

The script classifies land cover types using Landsat 8 Surface Reflectance imagery from July and August 2019. It creates a stratified sample of training points based on an existing classification (aug_class), applies zonal statistics to extract spectral values from image collections for these points, and generates buffered geometries for analysis. Outputs include a point feature collection with spectral and metadata attributes, suitable for classification model training or accuracy assessment.

The script analyzes the relationship between maximum NDVI derived from Landsat 8 TOA reflectance and elevation zones defined by SRTM. It computes NDVI using near-infrared (B5) and red (B4) bands, identifies the maximum NDVI value per pixel over a one-year period, classifies elevation into discrete thresholds (300, 400, 500, 750, 1000 m), masks invalid elevations, clips to a 20km buffer around a point, and calculates mean NDVI grouped by elevation zone using reduceRegion. Outputs include a grouped statistics object showing average NDVI per elevation band for regional vegetation-elevation analysis.

The script generates a cloud-masked, multi-temporal composite from Sentinel-2 imagery over a specific region, calculating NDVI and BSI for each image. It computes median reflectance across spectral bands, along with maximum, mean, and standard deviation for NDVI and BSI. The final output is a clipped, multi-band asset combining spectral bands and statistical vegetation/soil indices, intended for land surface analysis such as monitoring vegetation health and soil exposure.
task_name: Generate vegetation and soil indices composite

task_description: The script classifies land cover types in the Eden district using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance, Sentinel-1 SAR, ALOS World 3D, SRTM DEM, and ALOS landforms data. It computes multiple spectral indices, combines optical, radar, and topographic features, and applies an SVM classifier to generate a land cover map with 77 classes. Accuracy metrics including overall accuracy, kappa, and producer's/consumer's accuracies are computed using training and validation datasets.

The script analyzes forest loss over time within specific patches in the Chiquitania region using the Hansen Global Forest Change dataset. It extracts the 'lossyear' band to compute a histogram of forest loss per year for each patch in the GB_patches feature collection. The output includes a frequency count of forest loss by year, identifies the smallest non-zero area of annual forest loss, and determines the index of that minimum value in the time series, enabling detection of years with minimal deforestation activity.

The script classifies mangrove and non-mangrove areas using Landsat 7 Surface Reflectance imagery from 2007. It applies cloud masking, computes spectral indices (NDVI, NDMI, MNDWI, SR, R54, R35, GCVI), and uses a Random Forest classifier trained on labeled sample regions. The output includes a classified raster map, validation error matrix, overall accuracy, and training/testing sample counts for assessing classification performance.

The script selects the first available cloud-minimized top-of-atmosphere (TOA) reflectance image from Landsat 8 within a one-year period over a region in Kilimanjaro. It filters the Landsat 8 image collection by date and spatial intersection with an unspecified point, then retrieves the least cloudy image, which is cast as a single image output for visual or further analysis.

The script computes and compares the median NDVI values over two distinct regions (crop area and total area) using Landsat 8 TOA imagery from 2015. It processes two image collections filtered by date and cloud cover, calculates median composites, clips them to respective geometries (table2 and table3), derives NDVI using bands B5 and B4, and computes mean NDVI values within each region via reduceRegion. The outputs include printed mean NDVI values for both areas, along with map visualizations of the NDVI rasters for crop and total land cover.

The script identifies surface water bodies by computing the Modified Normalized Difference Water Index (MNDWI) on Sentinel-2 imagery after pan-sharpening and atmospheric correction. It applies a rescaling function to reflectance values, renames bands for clarity, enhances spatial resolution via IHS pan-sharpening, and calculates MNDWI using green and SWIR1 bands. The output includes a time-series of MNDWI-enhanced images and visualizations of SWIR bands for analysis.

The script analyzes a pre-classified land cover image of Bangalore from 2019 to extract green cover (vegetation) within the city boundary. It computes the total vegetation area in square kilometers by masking pixels classified as vegetation (class value 3), multiplying by pixel area, and aggregating via reduceRegion over the Bangalore boundary. Outputs include a classified land cover map, a binary green cover layer, and printed area statistics for the city and its vegetation.

The script compiles a merged ImageCollection from multiple Landsat 4, 5, and 7 surface reflectance datasets (Landsat Collection 1 Tier 2) for specific WRS paths and rows. It filters images by predefined LANDSAT_PRODUCT_IDs, selects visible bands (B3, B2, B1), merges all filtered image collections into a single collection, converts it to a list, extracts the image IDs, and prints both the ID list and total count of images. The output is a consolidated list of image identifiers and the size of the collection for quality control or further processing.

The script analyzes monthly surface soil moisture (susm) and NDVI over the United States from 2010 to 2017. It processes two user-hosted ImageCollections (NUSMCMP for soil moisture and NDVI_8days), applies masking to remove invalid values, reprojects and rescales both datasets to a common projection and resolution, aggregates them into monthly composites, and filters them spatially and temporally. The output includes filtered and processed ImageCollections of monthly mean soil moisture and NDVI, intended for time-series analysis of land surface conditions.
task_name: Analyze soil moisture and vegetation trends

task_description: The script calculates the area of land cover types classified as forest (IGBP class 1–5) from MODIS MCD12Q1 LC_Type1 data between 2001 and 2019. It computes pixel area in square kilometers for pixels with IGBP class ≤ 5, clips elevation data from ALOS AW3D30 DSM to lake geometries, applies a mask based on elevation relative to lake level, converts the masked area to vectors, and extracts annual land cover sums within those zones. The output is a CSV table containing yearly forested area values (in million m²) for each lake feature, including properties such as Hylak_id, LakeEleve, and HYBAS_ID.

The script estimates inherent optical properties (IOPs) of coastal and inland waters using Landsat 8 surface reflectance data. It applies atmospheric correction by rescaling surface reflectance bands, computes remote sensing reflectance (Rrs), derives absorption and backscattering coefficients through semi-analytical modeling, and calculates total absorption and backscattering across multiple wavelengths. The output includes mapped layers of absorption (abstot) and backscattering (backtot) coefficients, which are key indicators of water constituents such as suspended sediments and colored dissolved organic matter.

The script detects vegetation loss over multiple years using Sentinel-1 C-band SAR imagery. It processes VH and VV polarizations from descending IW mode, applies temporal filtering and threshold-based change detection on the difference images (e.g., 2017–2018, 2018–2019), masks water bodies using a VH backscatter threshold, and identifies areas of significant decrease in VH intensity indicative of vegetation loss. Outputs include filtered mosaics, binary change layers, vectorized water masks, and statistical summaries of change magnitude and affected area.

The script analyzes forest loss in the Congo Republic using the Global Forest Change (GFC) dataset from 2014. It isolates forest loss events that occurred specifically in 2012 by evaluating the 'lossyear' band, creates a binary mask of pixels lost in that year, and calculates both the pixel count and total area (in square meters) of forest loss within a specified region (table). Outputs include the count of lost pixels and the total area affected, printed to the console for the defined geometry.

The script classifies land use and land cover (LULC) for sugarcane and other crops in KwaZulu-Natal using Landsat 8 OLI/TIRS imagery from November 2019 to March 2020. It mosaics four cloud-minimized images filtered by region, trains a Random Forest classifier using labeled regions, evaluates accuracy via confusion matrix with a 70-30 train-test split, and computes classified area in square meters. Outputs include a classified LULC map, accuracy assessment, and area statistics.

The script identifies bare land areas in Gomishan using Dynamic World surface classification imagery from 2018-09-23 to 2019-09-23. It filters the Dynamic World ImageCollection by date and region, clips to the Gomishan city boundary, extracts the 'bare' probability band, creates a mosaic, applies a threshold (>0.6) to identify high-probability bare land, and generates a masked raster of crop classification (label 7) for area calculation. The output includes a classified raster map of bare land, a probability layer, and the total area of crops within Tehran administrative boundary calculated in hectares.

The script analyzes urban vegetation and surface water conditions in Dhaka city using median Sentinel-2 imagery from 2020. It applies cloud masking and atmospheric correction to generate a composite image, then computes NDVI, MNDWI, and SAVI indices to assess vegetation health, surface water extent, and soil-adjusted vegetation patterns. Outputs include false-color visualizations and index maps for urban environmental assessment.

The script analyzes multi-temporal Landsat 8 surface reflectance and temperature data over a defined region from 2017 to 2020. It applies scaling factors to optical and thermal bands, computes spectral indices (NDVI, NDWI, BSI), masks clouds using a custom function, and generates composite statistics (median, mean, 20th percentile, standard deviation) across the image collection. Outputs include layered visualizations of true color composites, index medians/means, and variability maps (e.g., NDVI_mean, BSI_stdDev) for assessing land surface dynamics such as vegetation health, water presence, and soil exposure.

The script calculates the Air Quality Index (AQI) for Ahmadabad district based on Sentinel-5P satellite observations of NO2 column density from July 7 to July 16, 2018. It computes the mean NO2 concentration over this period, applies a threshold-based lookup to determine the corresponding AQI category, and uses linear interpolation within that category's range to derive a continuous AQI value. The output includes a mapped AQI layer, the average AQI over the district via reduceRegion, and visualizations of both NO2 and AQI layers clipped to the administrative boundary.

The script classifies land cover into forest, grass, barren, and water using MODIS surface reflectance data. It trains a Random Forest classifier on labeled polygons for each class, applies the model to annual peak vegetation period composites from 2000 to 2019, and outputs yearly pixel counts for each class within a defined geometry. The classification is based on Nadir reflectance bands, and temporal compositing uses day-of-year filters to capture peak vegetation.

The script analyzes changes in vegetation condition by computing median NDVI from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery before (2020-06-22 to 2020-09-22) and after (2022-07-22 to 2022-08-22) a specific period. It applies cloud masking using QA60 band, calculates NDVI using B8 and B4 bands, computes median composites for both time periods, and outputs the difference as a change map. The results include three visualizations: 'NDVI Before', 'NDVI After', and 'NDVI Change' layers on the map.
task_name: Analyze NDVI change before and after

task_description: The script identifies surface water extent using a Dynamic Surface Water Extent (DSWE) classification applied to Landsat 7 Surface Reflectance imagery from May 8, 2015. It computes initial surface water frequency (SWF) by thresholding DSWE values ≥1, then samples pixel values within buffered stratified sample points. Covariates including spectral bands and indices (MNDWI, Tasseled Cap components) are extracted and aggregated over buffered samples using mean reduction. The output includes a histogram of initial SWF values across samples and a mapped layer of buffered sampling points for accuracy assessment or model training.

The script classifies land cover types using Sentinel-2-like multispectral imagery (10m resolution) and a suite of spectral indices including NDBI, NDWI, SAVI, and texture measures from principal components. It trains a Random Forest classifier on labeled sample points (BC, NC, PFM, VC, WC, SC) representing different land cover classes, applies the model to classify the full image, and evaluates accuracy using a validation set. Outputs include a classified land cover map with a six-class color palette, confusion matrix, producers' and consumers' accuracy, overall accuracy, and Kappa coefficient for model assessment.

The script identifies surface water extent in a HUC10 watershed in Madagascar using Landsat 8 Surface Reflectance data from 2013 onward. It applies cloud masking and computes spectral indices (EVI, NDVI, MNDWI) to implement two water detection methods: Deng et al.'s threshold-based approach combining EVI and MNDWI, and Lefebvre et al.'s method using NIR and SWIR2 reflectance thresholds. The output includes a quality-mosaic composite image based on the Deng index, binary water maps (Deng and Lefebvre), and vectorized water polygons derived from the Deng classification for spatial analysis.

The script identifies vegetated areas within a region of interest using Landsat 7 Surface Reflectance data from 1996. It computes multiple spectral indices including NDVI, NDMI, MNDWI, SR, R54, R35, and GCVI, applies cloud masking, then filters the composite by NDVI > 0.25 and elevation < 65 meters. The output is a masked median composite image clipped to the ROI, intended for vegetation analysis under specific topographic and spectral conditions.
task_name: Identify vegetation areas with NDVI and elevation constraints

task_description: The script computes annual mean NDVI values over Côte d'Ivoire using Landsat 7 Surface Reflectance data from 1999 to 2021. It applies cloud masking using the pixel_qa band, calculates NDVI from bands B4 and B3, aggregates images yearly via mean reduction, and outputs a time-series-ready ImageCollection where each image represents the mean NDVI of one year, annotated with 'system:time_start' for temporal analysis.
task_name: Generate annual NDVI for Côte d'Ivoire

task_description: The script identifies surface water presence by integrating multiple global water datasets (MODIS, GLCF, JRC GSWD, MERIT Hydro) and terrain-based proxies (valley, mountain, landform features from SRTM) within a defined region of interest. It combines binary water masks using logical addition, applies focal mean smoothing to reduce noise, and generates a final water mask through thresholding. The output includes layered visualizations of individual and combined water layers, a smoothed water layer, and a final binary water mask, along with the study area boundary for spatial context.

The script classifies land cover into four classes—water, barren, grass, and forest—using MODIS surface reflectance data from August–September 2000. It trains a Random Forest classifier using manually defined training regions (MultiPolygons) for each class, applies the model to a median-composited image, and outputs a classified raster map clipped to a specified geometry. The script also computes forest pixel counts by masking out non-forest classes and performing a zonal sum over the study area.

The script computes mean monthly VV polarization backscatter values from Sentinel-1 GRD imagery over a three-year period (2016–2018). It filters the Sentinel-1 SAR data for IW mode, ascending orbit, and VV polarization, then calculates monthly mean images using .mean() on time-filtered subsets. Each monthly image is stored as a separate variable (im1 to im36), forming a dense time series of 36 monthly composite images. The output consists of individual monthly radar backscatter layers in VV polarization at 10m scale, reprojected to their native projection, intended for time series analysis of surface dynamics such as land cover change, vegetation growth, or soil moisture variation.

The script classifies land cover types using Sentinel-2, Sentinel-1, ALOS, and SRTM data over a specific region. It computes multiple spectral indices from Sentinel-2, extracts SAR backscatter features from ascending and descending orbits of Sentinel-1, incorporates elevation and slope from ALOS AW3D30, and adds terrain and landform layers from SRTM and ERGo datasets. After computing 49 spectral and radar-derived indices, it trains an SVM classifier using labeled training data to produce a classified land cover map. Accuracy is assessed via confusion matrices on training and validation samples, with reported overall accuracy and kappa statistics for both sets.

The script estimates total aboveground carbon stocks in broadleaf and coniferous forests within a defined region using two global carbon datasets: ESA CCI Biomass (ESAU18_c) and JRC Forest Carbon Density (JRCU18_c). It first computes total carbon for the entire forest area without clipping, then filters the forest vector layer (Forest_V) by 'forest_type' (1 = broadleaf, 2 = conifer) to calculate pixel counts (area) and sum carbon values separately for each forest type. The outputs include printed dictionaries of pixel counts and summed carbon content for both forest types and both datasets at 100m scale, enabling comparison of carbon storage across forest types and data sources.
task_name: Estimate forest carbon content by type

task_description: The script maps daily surface water extent in a district using Sentinel-1 VV backscatter data. It applies Otsu's thresholding method on mosaicked daily images to classify water pixels, leveraging edge masking and JRC Global Surface Water for static water masking. Outputs include a time-series table of water occurrence metrics (thresholds, wet pixel counts) and individual GeoTIFFs of daily water classification maps clipped to the region of interest.
task_name: Map surface water extent using SAR

task_description: The script computes and compares NDVI from Landsat 5 SR and MODIS MOD09Q1 data over a specified time period and region. It applies cloud masking using pixel QA bits for both sensors, calculates NDVI using red and near-infrared bands, resamples MODIS NDVI to finer resolution, and prepares the two NDVI time series for temporal joining within an 8-day window. The output is a paired NDVI dataset enabling cross-sensor comparison, with properties preserved for temporal alignment analysis.

The script calculates median land surface temperature from Landsat 8 Collection 1 Tier 1 Surface Reflectance data for a single day (2017-12-31 to 2018-01-01), using thermal band B10. It applies scaling (multiply by 0.1) after clipping to a user-defined geometry (table), preserves timestamp properties, and computes the median value across the collection, resulting in a single median temperature raster for the area of interest.

The script classifies land cover types in a specified area using Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery from 2019. It filters images by cloud cover, date, and spatial bounds, then creates a median composite. Training and validation data are generated from labeled ground control points (builtup, water, vegetation, baresoil, wetland), and a Random Forest classifier is trained to classify the mosaic into five land cover classes. The classified map is clipped to the study area, and accuracy is assessed using a confusion matrix and overall accuracy. Outputs include the classified land cover map, visualizations in true and false color, and classification accuracy metrics.

The script analyzes multi-temporal SAR imagery (JERS-1 and ALOS PALSAR) from 1996 to 2016 to detect vegetation loss and gain, particularly in mangrove ecosystems. It converts backscatter values to decibels, applies spatial smoothing, computes temporal ratios, and uses threshold-based classification to identify areas of significant change. The outputs include mapped layers of vegetation loss and gain over multiple time intervals (1996–2007, 2007–2010, etc.), along with regional statistics (mean and standard deviation) extracted from defined land cover change polygons.

The script analyzes sugarcane growth stages in a specific region using Sentinel-2 imagery from 2019 to 2020. It selects images corresponding to key phenological phases (stem elongation, sugar accumulation, and maturation), applies cloud masking via the QA60 band, computes NDVI, and generates a composite image summarizing median reflectance, maximum NDVI, mean NDVI, and NDVI standard deviation. The output is a multi-band asset containing spectral bands and vegetation indices clipped to the ROI, intended for monitoring crop development and spatial variability.

The script calculates the area of vegetation cover based on a threshold applied to the B4 band (red reflectance) from a mosaic image. It creates a binary mask where pixels with B4 reflectance greater than or equal to 0.3 are retained, representing vegetated areas. The resulting masked image is added to the map, and the total area in square kilometers is computed using ee.Image.pixelArea() and printed to the console.

The script classifies land cover types in the Cape Town region using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance, Sentinel-1 SAR, and ALOS World 3D terrain data from September to November 2020. It computes a comprehensive set of spectral, radar, and topographic indices, then applies an SVM classifier trained on labeled samples to generate a land cover map. The output includes the classified raster, training accuracy (from confusion matrix), and validation accuracy (from error matrix) for model evaluation.

The script analyzes changes in surface backscatter from Sentinel-1 SAR imagery before and after a potential flood event in the Wouri region. It filters IW-mode, dual-polarization (VV, VH) GRD data acquired during descending passes, mosaics images within pre- and post-event time windows, clips them to the Wouri administrative boundary, and outputs the clipped mosaicked images for visual and analytical comparison. The primary outputs are two radar intensity rasters representing the area before (2020-07-26 to 2020-08-21) and after (2020-08-21 to 2020-09-02), enabling detection of flood-induced changes in surface conditions.

The script extracts MODIS MOD13Q1 NDVI images for the specific Julian day 353 (December 19 in non-leap years) within the year 2015, filtered by a user-defined geometry. It maps over the ImageCollection to add a 'diaJuliano' band representing the day of year and retains only images where this value equals 353. The output is a filtered ImageCollection containing one or more NDVI images from that specific day, along with metadata validation using a conditional test confirming the correct day was selected.

The script classifies land cover types using Sentinel-2 or similar multispectral imagery over a user-defined region of interest (roi). It selects specific spectral and derived indices (B2, B3, B4, B11, B12, NDBBI, NDWI, BSI, NDBI, MNDWI) to form a feature stack. Training and validation samples are created by splitting labeled point data (BC, NC, PFM, VC) randomly into 60% training and 40% validation sets. A Random Forest classifier with 500 trees is trained on the training set and applied to classify the entire image. Accuracy assessment is performed using a confusion matrix and F1 score calculation based on validation points. Outputs include a classified land cover map, validation results, and classification accuracy metrics.

The script compiles and filters Landsat 8, Landsat 9, and Sentinel-2 surface reflectance image collections over a specific WRS path/row and MGRS tile for the year 2022. It manually constructs time-specific image collections by selecting individual scenes based on known acquisition dates, enabling comparative analysis across sensors. The output consists of multiple filtered image collections and explicitly defined image composites for further processing, such as change detection or spectral index computation, but does not perform classification or generate maps directly.
task_name: Extract multi-sensor imagery for regional analysis

task_description: The script classifies land cover types in the Voronezh region using a Random Forest classifier trained on Sentinel-2 surface reflectance composite and ground control points (GCPs). It first converts GCPs into a raster layer, then extracts stratified training samples (8000 points) and validation samples (500 points) from the image. A Random Forest model with 50 trees is trained, applied to classify the full image, and post-processed with a focal median filter. The output includes a classified land cover map clipped to the administrative boundary, along with accuracy assessments: confusion matrix, overall accuracy, kappa, and F1-score from both training and validation data.

The script analyzes spatial patterns of vegetation health and environmental conditions in a defined study area using MODIS-derived NDVI, ET, and CHIRPS precipitation data for 2015. It computes mean NDVI, standard deviation, and coefficient of variation (CV) from high-quality MODIS MOD13Q1 images after masking poor-quality pixels using SummaryQA. It integrates surface water extent from JRC Global Surface Water, evapotranspiration from MOD16A2, and annual precipitation from CHIRPS pentad data. These variables are combined into a multiband stack and used to extract zonal statistics for buffered landscape units and natural areas. The outputs include a composite image (mean NDVI, CV, water class, ET, PPT), and two feature collections with mean values per landscape and natural area unit, intended for ecological or land-use analysis.
task_name: Analyze vegetation variability and environmental conditions

task_description: The script analyzes Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery over the Caytepe region from May 15 to July 20, 2020, filtering images by cloud cover (≤40%) and selecting specific optical and shortwave infrared bands. It generates a time series of composite RGB visualizations (using B4, B3, B2) for 19 specific two-day intervals, allowing visual assessment of surface changes—particularly vegetation dynamics—during the growing season. Outputs include multiple mosaicked layers added to the map viewer for comparison, along with a boundary outline of the study area, supporting temporal monitoring of agricultural or land surface conditions.

The script extracts a time series of Sentinel-2 imagery within a buffer around a reservoir over the period from August 1, 2021, to December 31, 2021. It filters images based on cloud cover (≤90%) and spatial bounds, generating a filtered collection of S2 images. The output is a printed image collection for visual inspection or further processing, with no classification or index computation performed.

The script detects burned areas in 2020 by analyzing Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data. It computes the Modified Index for Burned Areas (MIRBI) from B11 and B12 bands, applies cloud masking using the Scene Classification Layer (SCL), and derives temporal MIRBI percentiles (5th to 100th). A delta layer is created as the difference between the 95th and 25th percentile MIRBI values, and a threshold of 0.7 is applied to identify burned regions. The result is masked using the Hansen water mask and compared visually with MODIS MCD64A1 burned area product. Outputs include a delta MIRBI layer, a binary burned area map from Sentinel-2, and the MODIS burned area for comparison.

The script assesses forest cover in Lam Dong province using MODIS-derived NDVI from April 2013 and April 2014. It computes NDVI from surface reflectance bands, applies a threshold-based reclassification (NDVI >= 0.68 for forest, < 0.68 for non-forest), clips results to the Lam Dong boundary, and calculates the total area (in m²) of forested and non-forested land for each year using pixel count aggregation via reduceRegion. Outputs include classified NDVI maps and printed area summaries grouped by reclassified values (0: non-forest, 1: forest).

The script detects flood inundation in Buzi District by analyzing Sentinel-1 SAR imagery before and after a flood event. It applies speckle filtering using the Refined Lee algorithm to VH-polarized C-band data, computes the ratio of post-flood to pre-flood backscatter, and identifies flooded areas where the ratio exceeds a threshold of 1.25. Outputs include filtered radar mosaics, a flood difference layer, and a binary water mask indicating inundated areas.

The script calculates monthly mean NDVI values for district boundaries in Pakistan from 2017 to 2023 using MODIS MOD13Q1 data. It first computes a time-series of mean NDVI images per month and year, converts them into a multi-band image, clips to district boundaries, and extracts zonal statistics (sum) before and after masking with a land cover classification image (wt). The outputs are two CSV tables containing NDVI values for each district: one covering the full district area and another masked to only include areas classified as value 4 in the wt image, likely representing cropland or a specific crop type.

The script classifies land cover types using Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery from April 1, 2016 to March 19, 2020. It selects the least cloudy image in the time range over a region of interest, trains a CART classifier using labeled sample regions (urban, water, forest, mountains, light agricultural, dark agricultural), and applies the classifier to generate a land cover map. The classification output is validated using an error matrix and overall accuracy assessment, producing both a classified raster layer and accuracy metrics.

The script calculates NDVI from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery over a specified region during April 2021, masks clouds using the QA60 band, clips to user-defined geometries (parcels), and computes mean NDVI values per parcel. It outputs a median NDVI map, a merged parcel ID raster, and a dictionary of parcel-wise area statistics derived from NDVI aggregation, intended for agricultural monitoring and land productivity analysis.

The script identifies the greenest pixels in a Landsat 8 image collection over a specified area and time range using EVI and NDVI as quality metrics. It computes multiple vegetation and water indices (EVI, NDVI, NDVIG, NDWI), applies quality mosaicking based on 'greenness', and generates a composite of the greenest pixel values. The output includes a greenest-pixel mosaic based on NDVI, its standard deviation layer, and masked composites using terrain (SRTM), temperature (MODIS LST), and vegetation thresholds, intended for refined vegetation analysis.

The script processes a Landsat time series from 1990 to 2020 over a user-defined geometry, filtering by WRS path and row (7,58 and 7,59), and prepares the collection for CCDC-based change detection. It adds day-of-year (DOY) and time metadata to each image, converts the collection to an array, removes consecutive duplicate observations based on DOY to ensure temporal uniqueness, and reconstructs individual images from the deduplicated array. The output is a cleaned, chronologically sorted image collection suitable for land surface monitoring and change analysis, with intermediate layers added to the map for quality checking.

The script computes multiple vegetation and land surface indices (NDVI, EVI, IRECI, GCVI, LSWI, SAVI, RGVI, NDWI, NWI, NDBI) from a median composite of Sentinel-2 imagery over a specified region. It applies cloud masking using the QA60 band, filters images by date and cloud cover, clips to a user-defined geometry, and adds the calculated spectral indices as new bands to the image. The output is a multispectral raster with enhanced vegetation and land condition information for analysis.

The script detects levee structures using a digital elevation model (Levee) by applying threshold-based masking and edge detection. It first masks areas below specific elevation thresholds (10.0, 20.0, 28.0), then applies the Canny Edge Detector to identify edges in the masked levee image. A water mask derived from the JRC Global Surface Water dataset is used to exclude water bodies. The detected edges are filtered by connected pixel count (≥60 pixels long), morphologically opened and closed to remove noise, and finally masked again using higher elevation thresholds. Outputs include layered visualizations of the original levee, edge detection results, and processed binary masks for analysis.
task_name: Detect levee edges from elevation data

task_description: The script analyzes the temporal dynamics of NDVI within valley bottoms using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery from May 2018 to October 2020. It computes monthly mean NDVI values by aggregating cloud-filtered images, handles missing data with a sentinel value (-999), and extracts regional statistics using reduceRegions over a user-defined feature collection. The output is a flattened feature collection containing monthly NDVI means, image counts, and timestamps for each geometry, filtered to exclude invalid records.

The script detects land surface changes before and after a specific incident date (2021-06-30) using Sentinel-2 imagery. It computes spectral distance and spectral angle between median composites of pre- and post-event periods through cloud-masked image collections. Key methods include cloud masking using QA60 band, temporal filtering for before (one year prior) and after (one month following) the event, median reduction to create composite images, and calculation of Euclidean spectral distance and angular difference in reflectance space. Outputs include true-color visualizations of before and after states, a spectral distance map highlighting magnitude of change, and a spectral angle map indicating directional change in multispectral signatures, all centered on a user-defined region.
