The script classifies land cover types in a user-defined area using Landsat 8 TOA reflectance imagery from January to October 2019. It applies BQA-based cloud masking, computes a median composite, and uses a CART classifier trained on 70% of labeled sample points from a user-provided feature collection to generate a classified land cover map with 7 classes. The output includes the classified raster map, a confusion matrix, and training accuracy assessment.

The script classifies land cover types in Kerala, India for the year 2018 using MODIS MCD12Q1 data. It extracts the LC_Type1 band to map 17 IGBP land cover classes, clips the data to administrative boundaries, computes built-up (urban) area extent, and calculates per-class land cover areas by district. Outputs include a classified land cover map, a binary built-up surface layer, total urban area in square kilometers, and a CSV table summarizing land cover areas for each district.

The script classifies land cover into three categories—vegetation, non-vegetation, and water—using Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery from May 2020 to June 2021. It selects the least cloudy image, trains a CART classifier on user-defined training regions (vegetasi, nonvegetasi, water), uses bands B2–B7 for classification, and outputs a classified raster map with color-coded land cover classes: red for vegetation, white for non-vegetation, and blue for water.

The script classifies land cover into two classes—'hijau222' (forest) and 'penuhkehidupan' (built-up)—using Sentinel-2 and Landsat-8 surface reflectance data from 2018 to 2019. It merges training samples from both classes, extracts spectral features from a composite image, trains a Random Forest classifier, and applies it to an AOI. The output includes a classified raster map, confusion matrix, overall accuracy, producer's accuracy, and user's accuracy for validation.

The script classifies paddy rice cultivation intensity in Ningxia, China using a threshold-based approach on a remapped cluster image (remapped_cluster1). It first generates a binary mask for potential paddy areas where pixel values are between 0 and 305, then applies multi-level thresholds to categorize rice intensity into four classes (1–4) based on pixel value ranges. The output includes a binary classification map and a multi-class intensity map, both masked to the study region, alongside visualizations of reference datasets including Monsoon Rice 2020, WorldCover crop areas, and administrative boundaries for China.

The script detects land surface change between two dates using Landsat 7 TOA reflectance imagery over a specific AOI. It computes change magnitude from red and NIR band differences (B3 and B4), classifies change direction into four quadrants based on the sign of red and NIR differences, and applies a threshold to distinguish changed from unchanged pixels. The output includes a composite image with three bands: 'Magnitude' (change intensity), 'Codes' (sector codes indicating direction of change), and 'Change' (binary change detection), along with histograms of magnitude and sector codes, and visualizations of both temporal images and change layers.

The script generates a median composite of Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery over a specified region between September 30, 2018, and May 30, 2019. It applies cloud and cirrus masking using the QA60 band, filters images by cloud cover (<20%), and scales the reflectance values by dividing by 10000. The output includes a full composite image, a clipped version to a vector boundary (table), and visualizations in true color (B4, B3, B2). The final outputs are a median RGB composite map and a spatially clipped version for focused analysis.

The script computes three spectral indices—NDVI (from B5 and B4), NBR (from B5 and B7), and NDSI (from B3 and B6)—using a single cloud-masked Landsat 8 image. It applies pixel-wise normalized difference calculations, derives brightness from visible bands (B2–B4), and outputs layered visualizations of the indices along with exportable rasters for NDVI and the study area boundary as a shapefile.

The script computes NDVI from Sentinel-2A Surface Reflectance imagery over a specific region (roi1) for multiple dates between May 2020 and February 2021, with cloud cover less than 10%. It calculates NDVI using bands B8 and B4 for each selected image, clips to the region of interest, and extracts mean and standard deviation statistics within the geometry (roi) using reduceRegion at 10m scale. The outputs include individual NDVI images, their descriptive statistics (mean and std dev), and visualizations added to the map for select dates. No classification or change detection is performed—only per-image spectral index computation and regional summary statistics.

The script estimates Land Surface Temperature (LST) from Landsat 8 TOA reflectance and thermal data over a region using NDVI-based emissivity modeling. It computes NDVI, masks clouds, derives fractional vegetation (FV), calculates surface emissivity (EM), and applies a radiative transfer-based expression to derive LST. Outputs include NDVI, FV, EM, thermal brightness temperature, and final LST layers for visual analysis and quantitative assessment.

The script estimates cropping intensity in agricultural regions by analyzing harmonized Landsat and Sentinel-2 NDVI time series fused with MODIS data. It uses MODIS phenology to define crop seasons, applies Chastain-based sensor harmonization across Landsat 7, Landsat 8, and Sentinel-2, performs gap-filling using MODIS NDVI regression, and identifies single vs. double cropping patterns based on seasonal NDVI thresholds. The output is a classified raster map of cropping intensity (0 = bare/no crop, 1 = single crop, 2 = double crop) and accuracy assessment via error matrix against reference data.
task_name: Map cropping intensity using NDVI time series

task_description: The script detects changes in land surface backscatter using Sentinel-1 SAR imagery before and after a specific period. It computes the difference between filtered VH polarization images from descending passes, applies a threshold to identify significant increases in backscatter, and generates a binary change map. The analysis includes spatial smoothing with a 50-meter radius focal mean to reduce noise, and outputs include the filtered before/after images, the difference raster, and a binary change detection layer for identifying altered areas such as potential flooding or deforestation.

The script estimates Land Surface Temperature (LST) using Landsat 8 Collection 1 Tier 1 Surface Reflectance data. It mosaics two adjacent scenes, clips to a user-defined geometry, and computes brightness temperature from band B10. A threshold mask based on physical temperature bounds (288–312 K) is applied. Emissivity is derived using NDVI-based classification with OLI bands B4 and B5. Finally, LST is calculated using a radiative transfer equation combining brightness temperature and emissivity. Outputs include false-color composite, brightness temperature, emissivity, and LST layers, along with min/max statistics for brightness temperature and LST within the study area.

The script assesses flood risk by combining 100-year flood depth rasters from two JBA datasets (fluvial and surface water) into a single mosaic. It samples flood depths at predefined locations from a feature collection 'table', then filters those locations where FirstStreet's 100-year flood risk exceeds a threshold of 1. The outputs include the merged JBA flood depth layer, sampled points with JBA flood depths, and filtered high-risk locations based on FirstStreet data. Visualizations compare FEMA flood zones, FirstStreet 100-year flood depths, JBA 100-year flood depths, and sample points.

The script calculates a rainfall erosivity index using monthly precipitation data from the PERSIANN-CDR dataset for the years 2017–2021. It computes mean precipitation for each two-month period across five years, sums them to create an annual cumulative precipitation image, then derives individual IMF (Modified Fournier Index) components by squaring monthly means and dividing by the total sum. The IMFs are summed and transformed into an erosivity estimate using a power-law equation (Erosivity = 2.56 × SumIMF^1.065). Outputs include intermediate monthly IMF layers, the final erosivity raster, and clipped visualizations added to the map.

The script classifies saltmarsh areas by combining Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery, PALSAR forest/non-forest data, and a reference saltmarsh dataset from Mcowen. It applies cloud masking on Sentinel-2 images, computes a median composite for 2018, and uses Random Forest classification trained on sampled pixels to generate a classified raster. Accuracy is assessed via resubstitution and validation error matrices, with outputs including classified maps, training accuracy, and validation accuracy.

The script computes the maximum NDVI value from Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery over the San Francisco Bay area for the year 2018, stratifies the region into elevation zones using SRTM DEM data, and calculates mean NDVI grouped by these elevation zones. It outputs a max NDVI raster, elevation zone map, region boundary, and a grouped reduction result showing mean NDVI per elevation class.
task_name: Map maximum NDVI by elevation zone

task_description: The script performs land cover classification using a Random Forest classifier trained on labeled training data (table2) and applied to test data (table3). It constructs band names dynamically from the property names of the input table, excluding two properties, and trains the classifier to predict a 'class' label. The output includes a confusion matrix, overall accuracy, producer's and consumer's accuracy, and Kappa statistic for model evaluation, based on the classification of test samples.

The script calculates monthly accumulated precipitation from CHIRPS pentad data over the period 2000–2020. It first filters and processes the CHIRPS ImageCollection by extracting year and month metadata, then aggregates pentad data into monthly sums for specific years (2000, 2005, 2010, 2015, 2020). These monthly composites are used to compute mean precipitation values over regions defined in a feature collection (likely watersheds or administrative units), using reduceRegions with a mean reducer at 1000m scale. The output is a flattened FeatureCollection containing mean precipitation per region per month, each feature annotated with date, month, and year, printed as a table limited to 1000 entries.

The script classifies land cover in the Dak Nong province using a pre-existing classified image. It extracts the administrative boundary of Dak Nong from the GAUL dataset, overlays the classified raster map with 11 classes, and computes the area (in square meters) for each land cover class within the region using pixel counting at 10m scale. Outputs include a visual classification map and a grouped area summary table by class.
task_name: Classify land cover in Dak Nong

task_description: The script computes long-term mean values of maximum temperature, minimum temperature, precipitation, and water deficit from the TerraClimate dataset (1958–2020), and also extracts multi-year banded precipitation data. It prepares climatic baseline data by aggregating monthly imagery into annual composites for specific years (2001–2019) and imports a WorldClim biovars image for comparison. Outputs include a renamed multi-band mean climate image (with bands: maxTemp, minTemp, RAINFALL, waterDef) and a time-composited precipitation image where each band represents a month/year combination, intended for temporal climate analysis.

The script classifies land cover types in a defined study area using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery from July to November 2021. It applies cloud masking via the QA60 band, computes mean spectral values across the time period, and uses a Covariate stack (B2, B3, B4, B8) to train a CART classifier on labeled training points representing impervious and pervious land covers (e.g., buildings, trees, irrigated areas, water). The resulting classification model is applied to generate a land cover map with six classes, validated using an independent validation dataset, and accuracy metrics (confusion matrix, overall accuracy) are computed for both training and test sets. Additionally, the script supports area calculation per class in acres.

The script analyzes vegetation health using NDVI derived from Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery over Staten Island for the year 2019, combined with a digital elevation model (DEM). It computes median pixel values after filtering and clipping to the study area, then generates an NDVI layer. Elevation data is classified into discrete altitude zones (20m intervals up to 140m) using thresholding. The NDVI values are aggregated by these elevation zones via a grouped mean reduction over the region, producing statistics that relate vegetation greenness to elevation bands.

The script generates 10-day median composites of Sentinel-2 surface reflectance and spectral indices over a user-defined region and year, then applies linear interpolation to fill gaps in the time series using neighboring valid observations. It outputs a daily interpolated ImageCollection from day of year 9 to 30 (likely representing early spring) with key vegetation and moisture indices including NDVI, EVI, LSWI, NDSVI, NDTI, RENDVI, and REP, masked and clipped to the region, enabling phenological or condition monitoring under varying cloud cover.

The script calculates river channel width by analyzing the JRC Global Surface Water dataset's 'occurrence' layer. It first derives a maximum water extent mask (waterMax) from the occurrence data, then uses a custom function `ExtractChannel` to isolate river channels based on hydrographic network geometry (grwl_test). A series of quantile-based water presence thresholds (0–100 by 10) are applied to generate binary water masks, which are combined into a multi-band quantile image. This image is masked with the river channel and used in `reduceRegions` to compute mean water presence along river segments. The result is a feature collection with statistical metrics per segment, enabling analysis of variable river width over time. Additionally, cross-section endpoints are generated perpendicular to river centerlines for potential width sampling.
task_name: Extract river width from water occurrence

task_description: The script classifies land cover in Samarinda using Landsat surface reflectance imagery from four time periods (1995–1996, 2006–2007, 2015–2016, 2018–2019). It applies cloud masking specific to Landsat 4/5/7 and Landsat 8, computes median composites for each period, and performs supervised classification using Support Vector Machine (SVM) with training regions defined for water, vegetation, settlement, and bare land. The output includes classified raster maps for each time period, accuracy assessments (confusion matrix, overall, producer’s, and user’s accuracy), and area calculations per class within the study region.

The script computes multiple vegetation and land surface indices (NDVI, GDNVI, EVI, NDMI, NSI, MSAVI, GCI, GLI, SIPI) from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data over the Busia region. It applies cloud masking, filters images by date and cloud cover, aggregates them into 10-day composites, and calculates spectral indices using band math expressions. The output is a multi-band image collection with each index mapped over time, suitable for monitoring vegetation dynamics and land surface conditions.

The script computes Fractional Vegetation Cover (FVC) from the maximum NDVI composite of MODIS MOD13A2 imagery over the region of interest for the year 2020. It first derives NDVI soil and vegetation endmembers using the 0.5th and 99.5th percentiles from the reduced region, then applies a linear spectral mixing model to calculate FVC as (NDVI - NDVI_soil) / (NDVI_veg - NDVI_soil). The output is a single-band FVC image representing vegetation coverage fraction, renamed as 'FVC', clipped to the study area.

The script classifies paddy rice growth stages in Malaysia using Sentinel-2 NDVI time-series data. It trains a Random Forest classifier on labeled point data with spectral bands (B1–B5) and evaluates model performance through training and validation accuracy, confusion matrices, overall accuracy, and kappa statistics. Outputs include a trained classifier, accuracy assessments, and classified validation points for stage mapping.

The script analyzes future land development patterns and farmland protection scenarios in the contiguous United States by combining projected urban development (UHD, LDR), solar installations, flood zones, and existing protected lands. It uses precomputed rasters for business-as-usual (BAU), best-case conservation (BBC), and resilience scenario (RS) models, along with farmland protection layers (existing and projected), to generate composite land change maps. The output includes layered visualizations of development types, protected areas, land cover classes, and flooded zones, using custom color palettes for thematic representation on the map.
task_name: Map future land development and farmland protection

task_description: The script extracts daytime land surface temperature (LST) from MODIS Terra data over a specified region of interest for the period 2016–2017. It applies scaling to convert digital numbers to physical values, clips the imagery to the ROI, renames bands by image ID, stacks the time series into a multi-band image, and computes mean LST values per feature using reduceRegions. The output is a CSV file containing mean LST values for each polygon in the input feature collection.

The script evaluates future crop and corn suitability under RCP 2.6 and RCP 8.5 climate scenarios by comparing baseline (2015–2016) land use with projected suitability in 2040. It uses remapped land cover classifications (corn, winter wheat, cropland) derived from LUC data and applies threshold-based shifting functions to assess changes in suitability. The output includes hillshade visualizations of suitability for corn and general cropland in 2040 under different emission pathways and baseline conditions, masked to land areas, enabling spatial analysis of agricultural resilience and climate impacts.
task_name: Map crop suitability under climate scenarios

task_description: The script filters a Landsat 8 TOA reflectance image collection for a specific WRS path and row over a summer period in 2014, then extracts and formats the acquisition dates of all images. It computes summary statistics including image count, date range, sun elevation metrics, identifies the least cloudy scene, and retrieves the 10 most recent images. The outputs are metadata-based: lists of formatted dates, descriptive statistics, and sorted image subsets for temporal analysis of satellite coverage.

The script identifies crop intensity (single vs. double cropping) in agricultural areas using time-series NDVI data from Landsat, Sentinel-2, and MODIS. It harmonizes multisensor imagery using Chastain regression, fills gaps with MODIS-based linear regression, and applies phenology-driven seasonal windows to detect vegetation cycles. Based on thresholding of NDVI during sowing, growing, and harvest periods derived from MODIS phenology, it classifies pixels into no-crop, single-crop, or double-crop categories, producing two annual crop intensity maps (CI1 for 2018 and CI2 for 2019) and validating results against ground truth points.

The script corrects Sentinel-1 GRD SAR imagery for terrain-induced distortions using SRTM elevation data. It applies either a volume or surface scattering model to normalize radar backscatter (VV, VH) by local incidence angle and topography, computes a layover-shadow mask with optional buffering, and outputs slope-corrected gamma nought images in dB. The result includes both corrected backscatter bands and a no-data mask for terrain-affected areas, enabling improved analysis of surface reflectivity in mountainous regions.
task_name: Correct SAR backscatter for terrain slope

task_description: The script detects vegetation disturbance events using annual NDVI time series derived from Landsat surface reflectance data (1984–2020). It harmonizes and masks Landsat 5, 7, and 8 imagery, computes annual median composites, applies the LandTrendr algorithm to identify spectral breaks, and extracts the most significant disturbance event per pixel based on magnitude, duration, and pre-disturbance conditions. Outputs include a filtered image of disturbance attributes: year of detection, magnitude, duration, and pre-disturbance NDVI value.

The script identifies vegetation presence in the Podunajska region using NDVI derived from Sentinel-2A/B SR (Surface Reflectance) imagery from March 2021. It applies cloud and shadow masking using SCL, MSK_CLDPRB, and MSK_SNWPRB bands, computes NDVI from B8 and B4, and generates a median composite and pixel count image. Outputs include a count raster of B4 band observations and a clipped median reflectance mosaic for vegetation analysis.

The script computes NDVI time series from Landsat 4, 5, 7, and 8 surface reflectance data over the Hunan province region. It applies consistent cloud masking and radiometric normalization across sensors, calculates NDVI using red and near-infrared bands, merges collections, and outputs a combined ImageCollection of mean NDVI values. The analysis focuses on temporal aggregation but contains errors in month-year mapping logic and undefined variables (e.g., 'col', 'cloudMaskL89', 'ndv_LANDSAT_8'), resulting in incomplete execution.

The script retrieves Sentinel-1 Ground Range Detected (GRD) Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery over a user-defined region and time period, filtering for VH polarization, IW acquisition mode, and ascending orbit direction. It sorts the resulting image collection by acquisition time in descending order and prints the collection to the console for inspection, but does not perform further processing or generate maps or statistics.

The script classifies land cover in the Gulbarga region using Sentinel-1 SAR imagery from 2019 to 2020. It computes a VV/VH backscatter ratio (BSI) and normalizes the median composite before applying a Random Forest classifier trained on manually defined ground control points (GCPs) for five classes: water, urban, agriculture, forest, and bare soil. The output includes a classified land cover map, accuracy assessment via confusion matrix (with producer's, user's, overall accuracy and kappa), and estimation of water area in square kilometers.

The script estimates Land Surface Temperature (LST) over the Gresik region using Landsat 8 Collection 1 Tier 1 Surface Reflectance data. It begins by masking clouds and cloud shadows using the pixel_qa band, then calculates NDVI to derive fractional vegetation (FV) and emissivity (EMM). Using the emissivity and brightness temperature from Band 10, it computes LST through a radiative transfer-based expression. The output includes masked reflectance imagery, NDVI, emissivity, and LST layers, with min/max statistics for NDVI and LST extracted over the study area.

The script creates cloud-free median composites for Landsat 8 and Sentinel-2 imagery over a user-defined region during 2018. It applies bit-based cloud masking using the BQA band for Landsat and QA60 for Sentinel, filters images by cloud cover percentage, and composites the remaining pixels using median reduction. Outputs are two RGB visualizations: one for Landsat (B7, B5, B2) and one for Sentinel (B4, B3, B2), labeled 'LandsatCloudless' and 'SentinelCloudless', respectively.

The script computes a median composite of Sentinel-2A Surface Reflectance (SR) imagery over a specific study area named 'grape_study' for March 2021, filtering images with less than 0.5% cloud coverage. It outputs a single median-reduced image representing surface conditions during that period, likely used for land cover or vegetation analysis related to grape cultivation.
task_name: Map surface reflectance in grape region

task_description: The script retrieves the first (least cloudy) Landsat 8 surface reflectance image from January to December 2020 that intersects a specific point in New Jersey. It filters the Landsat 8 Collection 1 Tier 1 surface reflectance dataset by location and date, sorts by cloud cover in ascending order, and outputs the metadata of the top-scoring image along with the total count of images in the filtered collection.

The script computes the mean surface reflectance of a user-defined polygon using Landsat 5 Tier 1 Level 2 surface reflectance and surface temperature data from January 15, 2011, to January 27, 2012. It applies scaling factors to optical and thermal bands, composites the image collection into a median image, clips it implicitly to the region, and calculates the mean pixel values within the polygon using reduceRegion. Outputs include the median composite image, the mean dictionary of band values, and a constant image representation of those means for further analysis.

The script estimates Land Surface Temperature (LST) over a specified area using Landsat 8 OLI/TIRS imagery from 2021. It first computes NDVI to derive fractional vegetation cover (FV), which is then used to estimate emissivity (EM). Using the thermal band (B10) and emissivity, LST is calculated via a radiative transfer equation. The output includes an LST raster map clipped to the study area, histogram of LST values, and printed statistics including minimum, maximum, mean, and standard deviation of LST.

The script processes a Landsat 5 Surface Reflectance image collection from 2002, applying a cloud masking function using pixel_qa bit flags to identify and remove clouds and shadows. It also preserves the original mask by reducing it with a minimum reducer, then applies both masks to the images. The output is a filtered ImageCollection after cloud masking, printed along with its size, intended for land surface analysis over a specific region.

The script analyzes daily snow cover from MODIS MOD10A1 data for a specific two-day period, creating binary masks where snow-covered pixels are identified (values 200 or 25 in the 'Snow_Cover_Daily_Tile' band). It defines three buffer zones (10km, 30km, and 50km radius) around a central point in Chile to spatially constrain the analysis. The output includes filtered image collections, printed to the console for inspection, focusing on valid snow cover observations within these regions.

The script detects land surface changes between two Landsat 7 TOA images from March and July 2011 using the NIR band (B4). It computes a difference image, analyzes its statistical properties (mean, standard deviation, min, max), and classifies change into three categories: negative change (below lower threshold), no significant change (within ±1 std dev), and positive change (above upper threshold). The classification is smoothed using a focal median filter with an 11-pixel radius. Outputs include a histogram of the difference image, printed statistics (upper/lower thresholds, min/max values), and layered visualizations of the before/after images, difference image, raw classification, and smoothed classification on the map.

The script classifies land cover types in the Terai region using a Random Forest classifier applied to a fused Landsat 8 and Sentinel-2 surface reflectance composite. It trains the model using labeled sample points, performs connected pixel filtering to remove small patches, clips the result to the study area and forest cover, and validates classification accuracy using an independent validation dataset. Outputs include a classified raster map with four classes, accuracy assessment metrics (overall accuracy, kappa, producer's and consumer's accuracy), and error matrix.

The script extracts and processes CHIRPS daily precipitation data from 2000 to 2019 over Niger, creates 16-day temporal composites starting from '2019-01-01' for 23 intervals, clips the data to the Niger region, stacks the composite images into a multi-band image, and computes mean precipitation values per administrative region. It outputs a CSV file containing the time-series mean precipitation values for each region in Niger for further analysis.

The script analyzes MODIS MCD64A1 Burn Date data to map the median annual burn scar date and cumulative fire frequency over Punjab and Haryana, India, from a specified start to end year. It processes yearly burn date images for a post-monsoon period (defined by input months and days), computes the minimum burn date per year, masks non-burned areas, and aggregates results into a median burn date image and total fire frequency layer. Outputs include mapped visualizations of burn date (273–336 day range) and frequency (1–16 years burned), each with associated legends added to the interactive map.
task_name: Map burn scar date and frequency

task_description: The script analyzes multi-temporal Landsat surface reflectance imagery from 1990 to 2020 to detect land cover changes using spectral temporal segmentation via the LandTrendr algorithm. It harmonizes sensors (TM, ETM+, OLI) to a common scale using regression coefficients, applies consistent cloud masking, composites annual images, computes NBR, and fits breakpoints in time series to identify change magnitude, duration, and rate. Outputs include annual composite mosaics, NBR time series, and LandTrendr-derived segments characterizing disturbance, recovery, and trends.
task_name: Detect land cover change over time

task_description: The script retrieves a specific dam feature from a feature collection (damLocs) using its system:index, extracts the 'Height_M' property of that dam, and stores it in a JavaScript list via a mapped function. The primary output is the populated JavaScript list 'emptyList' containing the height value(s), demonstrating an attribute extraction workflow rather than spatial or temporal analysis.

The script calculates NDVI using three different methods—manual formula, built-in normalizedDifference function, and image expression—on a 5-year composite of Landsat 7 TOA reflectance data (1999–2003). It outputs three NDVI layers to the map for visual comparison, enabling assessment of method equivalence in vegetation index computation.

The script analyzes tropospheric nitrogen dioxide (NO2) column number density over a region in Asia from June to September 2022 using Sentinel-5P NRTI L3 NO2 data. It applies spatial clipping to a defined polygon, then implements a custom filtering workflow involving Gaussian smoothing and high-pass convolution to enhance local contrasts in NO2 concentrations. The output includes two layered visualizations on the map: the mean original NO2 levels and the mean filtered NO2 levels, both using the same color palette for comparison.

The script analyzes vegetation health and seasonal variation in Fort Morgan, CO using Landsat 8 surface reflectance data from 2018. It computes NDVI for winter and summer scenes, identifies the least cloudy images per season, and generates a maximum NDVI composite over the year. A threshold (NDVI > 0.75) is applied to the maximum NDVI to map likely irrigated agricultural areas, outputting raster layers for visual interpretation and spatial analysis.

The script estimates land surface temperature (LST) using Landsat 8 thermal infrared data and the Split-Window algorithm from the sofiaermida/landsat_smw_lst package. It computes auxiliary variables including total column water vapor (TCWV), fractional vegetation cover (FVC), and emissivity, applies cloud filtering (CLOUD_COVER < 20%), and generates mean composite images over the study area. Outputs include mapped layers of TCWV, FVC, emissivity, brightness temperature, and LST in both Kelvin and Celsius, along with a natural color RGB composite for visual context.

The script classifies land cover types in Córdoba using a multi-temporal Sentinel-2 composite based on seasonal greenest pixel (NDVI) selection. It computes NDVI for spring, summer, autumn, and winter, creates a stacked composite, and applies Random Forest classification with training samples from five classes: meadows, tall vegetation, water, artificial surfaces, and bare soil. The classification is run multiple times with different random seeds to assess accuracy stability, and the final output is a mode-combined classified raster map of land cover with an accuracy assessment including overall accuracy, kappa, and producer/consumer accuracies.

The script analyzes vegetation health in Germany before and after a specific drought period using NDVI derived from Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery. It computes median composites for pre-drought (2015 to year before target date) and post-drought (target period) conditions, applies cloud masking and filtering by month and year, and generates RGB and NDVI visualizations. Outputs include pre- and post-event composite images for change analysis, focusing on provincial-level features in Germany, with the intent of assessing drought impact on vegetation.
task_name: Compare NDVI before and after drought

task_description: The script analyzes seasonal variations in land surface characteristics using Sentinel-1 VV/VH backscatter and Sentinel-2 optical imagery over a region of interest. It creates mosaics of dual-polarized SAR data (VV and VH) from descending passes, composites multi-temporal VV medians for three winter months (Oct–Jan), and generates RGB composites from four cloud-filtered Sentinel-2 scenes spanning June to January. Outputs include visualizations of SAR intensity layers, a false-color seasonal composite from VV time slices, and true-color RGB mosaics for different seasons, enabling visual interpretation of land cover dynamics.

The script classifies land cover types in a user-defined area using Landsat 8 Surface Reflectance imagery from 2019. It applies a cloud and shadow mask using the pixel_qa band, filters valid pixels based on reflectance values, and computes the median image. A Random Forest classifier is trained on labeled sample points (forest, rice paddy, garden, settlement, water, bare land) using spectral bands B1–B7. The output is a classified land cover map with six classes, along with accuracy assessments including overall accuracy, kappa coefficient, and producer’s/consumer’s accuracy derived from a confusion matrix.

The script calculates the weighted spatial centroid of a raster variable 'CE1' over a region defined by geometry JJJ, using longitude and latitude as weighting coordinates. It first clips and reprojects the CE1 raster and coordinate layers to EPSG:4326 at 500m scale, then computes pixel-wise products of CE1 with longitude (a) and latitude (b). Regional sums of a, b, and CE1 are extracted via reduceRegion, and the centroid coordinates (x, y) are derived by dividing sum_a and sum_b by sum_CE. The outputs are two printed numerical values representing the x (longitude) and y (latitude) of the weighted centroid.
task_name: Compute weighted centroid of CE values

task_description: The script classifies land cover types in a defined study area using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery from July to November 2021. It applies cloud masking via the QA60 band, computes mean composite imagery, and extracts spectral bands (B2, B3, B4, B8) as covariates for classification. A CART classifier is trained on labeled sample points representing impervious and pervious surfaces, vegetation, water, and buildings, then applied to generate a classified land cover map. The accuracy is assessed using both training confusion matrix and an independent validation dataset, producing overall accuracy metrics and an error matrix.

The script performs a supervised classification to map land cover classes including Water, Bare, Cropland (Vegetation), OilPalm (Mangrove), and Rubber (Reef) using manually defined training samples. It computes a confusion matrix from a classifier (assumed pre-defined as 'classifier'), evaluates accuracy metrics (overall, producer’s, and user’s accuracy), and calculates the area of each classified class within the AOI using pixel counting at 30m scale. Outputs include accuracy assessment results and a grouped area summary by classification.

The script classifies land cover types across a multi-country West African region using Landsat 7 Surface Reflectance imagery from the year 2000. It computes multiple spectral indices (NDVI, NDWI, NDBI, MNDWI, EVI, BSI, NDTI) and integrates auxiliary datasets including SRTM elevation, GHSL built-up layer, and VIIRS nighttime lights. A Random Forest classifier is trained on stratified sample points with land cover labels, using a 70/30 train-test split. The output is a classified land cover map generated by applying the trained model to the full feature stack.

The script computes NDVI from Sentinel-2 Surface Reflectance imagery over a specific region (roi) for multiple dates between May 2020 and March 2021. It manually selects 33 individual images, calculates NDVI using bands B8 and B4, clips each image to the region of interest, and computes mean and standard deviation of NDVI within the region using reduceRegion at 10m scale. The outputs are printed NDVI statistics (mean and std) for each date, enabling temporal analysis of vegetation dynamics.

The script refines the geographic positions of dam locations by filtering out invalid or incomplete entries, manually adjusting coordinates through translation (x,y offsets), and snapping adjusted points to optimal locations using a custom snapDams function. It outputs a cleaned and spatially corrected feature collection of dam locations saved as a GEE asset.

The script classifies land cover types in the Norquinco department using a Random Forest classifier trained on spectral indices (NDVI, NDWI, SAVI), Landsat 8 bands, topographic variables (TWI, TPI), and JRC surface water metrics. It computes mean, standard deviation, and percentiles (p50, p95) of time-series indices, combines them into a feature stack, extracts training samples from labeled regions, and trains a model to classify wetland and surrounding land cover types, outputting a classified raster and sample data for accuracy assessment.

The script classifies land cover types including built-up areas, crops (alfalfa, apple and pear, grapes, sugar beet, wheat and barley), fall irrigated vegetables, bareland, other vegetation, and water in the study area using multi-season Landsat 8 surface reflectance and Sentinel-1 VH backscatter data. It applies cloud masking on Landsat imagery, computes median composites per season, integrates optical and radar features, and trains a Gradient Tree Boosting classifier using labeled field samples. The output includes a classified land cover map, accuracy assessments (confusion matrix, overall accuracy, Kappa, producer/consumer accuracies), and visualizations with a legend and ground truth overlay.
task_name: Classify agricultural and land cover types

task_description: The script identifies surface water extent using Sentinel-1 C-band SAR imagery from October 2019. It applies terrain slope correction to backscatter values (VV/VH) to reduce topographic effects, followed by the Perona-Malik diffusion filter to reduce speckle noise. A modified Otsu thresholding method (bmaxOtsu) is then applied on the VV band to derive a water mask, using a grid-based bimodality assessment to select optimal threshold values. The output is a binary water/non-water classification map derived from gamma nought corrected and filtered SAR data, with intermediate layers including layover, shadow, and incidence angle added to the final image.

The script extracts the first image from a Sentinel-2 collection clipped to an AOI, computes NDVI and NDWI, adds pixel longitude and latitude bands, and then samples raster values at point geometries within the AOI. It outputs a feature collection of sampled pixels with spectral indices, coordinate information, and metadata, printed to the console and used to center the map.
task_name: Extract Sentinel-2 pixel samples with indices

task_description: The script calculates elevation statistics for a user-defined geometry using the SRTM Global DEM. It clips the DEM to the input geometry, computes the mean elevation via reduceRegion, and also retrieves min/max elevation values, printing both dictionaries as outputs for analysis.

The script extracts weekly vegetation indices (NDVI, EVI, NRV, RedEdge-VI) for cropland areas using Sentinel-2 TOA and surface reflectance imagery from 2019 to 2020. It applies cloud masking using QA60 band, computes median composites over two-week intervals, calculates four spectral indices from specific bands (B2, B4, B5, B7, B8), and appends both TOA and SR-derived indices to a single image collection per week. The output is an ImageCollection of weekly multi-band vegetation index images, each tagged with a week number, aligned spatially to the USDA NASS CDL cropland layer.

The script classifies land cover types in the Netherlands using Sentinel-2 imagery from 2017, combined with historical ecotoop data (1997–2017) to guide training sample selection. It generates a monthly composite image for 2017, computes NDVI and NDWI if enabled, and applies stratified sampling based on land cover classes. A linear trend analysis of ecotoop changes over time filters stable areas for training data. The output includes a classified raster map styled by land cover type, training and validation point sets for machine learning, and statistical summaries per class for further modeling.

The script identifies soil preparation areas by detecting changes in NDVI between pre- and post-season Sentinel-2 imagery over a specific district. It computes NDVI using B8 and B4 bands, applies cloud masking, and clips to a district boundary. A change detection method is used where pixels with high NDVI (≥0.3) before and low NDVI (<0.3) after are classified as 'soil preparation' zones, indicating vegetation removal or land disturbance. Outputs include a binary raster map of soil preparation areas, visualizations of RGB and NDVI composites, and printed statistics on total area and affected extent in hectares.

The script identifies surface frost occurrence (FSE) using Landsat 8 Collection 2 Level 2 data from 2021 over a user-defined geometry. It computes LST, NDVI, and LSWI, then applies a multi-condition threshold-based method to detect frost presence. The result is refined using masks for water, sparse vegetation, dense vegetation, and terrain (slope and elevation), producing a final binary frost occurrence map (FSE_final) representing areas with persistent frost signals after masking out non-relevant land cover and topographic conditions.

The script computes NDVI, NDWI, and NBR indices from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery. It first scales the reflectance bands (B.*) by dividing by 10000, then calculates NDVI using B8 and B4, NDWI using B3 and B8, and NBR using B8 and B12. These indices are added as new bands to the image, resulting in an enhanced image with spectral vegetation, water, and burn ratio layers for environmental analysis.

The script creates a cloud-masked median composite from Landsat 8 TOA reflectance imagery over a specific region for the year 2019. It applies a bit-based mask using the BQA band to remove clouds and shadows, computes the median value across all valid pixels, clips the result to a user-defined geometry (table), and outputs the band names of the resulting composite image.

The script analyzes changes in vegetation condition within the Linyanti region from 2019 to 2021 using EVI derived from Sentinel-2A surface reflectance imagery. It applies cloud filtering, masks out water, wetlands, and urban areas using Copernicus Land Cover data, and computes median and maximum EVI during the dry season (April–September) for each year. The script generates annual median and maximum EVI composites, calculates interannual differences (2021 vs 2019), and performs linear trend analysis on maximum EVI over time. Outputs include mapped layers of annual EVI, EVI change, and slope of EVI trend, supporting assessment of vegetation dynamics and potential degradation or recovery.

The script analyzes land cover change dynamics between 2018 and 2020 in a defined study area using bitemporal mosaics. It computes spectral indices for both time periods using a custom 'addIndices' module, combines the index-enhanced images, and trains a Random Forest classifier on labeled training samples (stable forest, stable non-forest, loss, gain). The resulting model classifies each pixel into one of four categories: green (stable forest), yellow (gain), red (loss), or blue (stable non-forest), producing a thematic map of forest change dynamics.

The script analyzes MODIS Terra LST data from 2001 to 2010 over Australia, focusing on the 'LST_Day_1km' band. It decodes quality control bits from the 'QC_Day' band using bitwise operations to generate masks for data quality, QA confidence, and LST error. These masks are combined and applied to the LST image to produce a cleaned, masked version of daytime land surface temperature. The output includes two visualizations: the original LST and the masked LST, both clipped to Australia, using a fixed color palette for comparison.
task_name: Extract and mask daytime land surface temperature

task_description: The script identifies surface water bodies using Sentinel-1 GRD SAR imagery. It applies terrain slope correction to backscatter data, performs Perona-Malik diffusion filtering for speckle reduction, and uses an edge-guided Otsu thresholding method on the VV band to generate a binary water mask. The output includes intermediate layers (binary threshold, canny edges, edge buffer, water image) added to the map, and returns a final classified water image for further analysis.

The script identifies spatial clusters (hotspots) of high reflectance and low texture in a multispectral image, likely targeting specific land cover features such as agricultural fields or bare soil patches. It uses seeded region growing with segmentation, applying Gaussian-blurred imagery and standard deviation texture analysis to detect homogeneous regions. The workflow includes morphological operations (erode, dilate), connected component analysis, object size filtering by area (2–200 m²), and vectorization of detected objects. Outputs include a raster of segmented hotspots, object labels, object size and area maps, and vector centroids representing the locations of detected features for further spatial analysis.

The script calculates tree canopy cover for the year 2000 using the NASA GFCC TC dataset. It applies a threshold to retain pixels with at least 11% tree cover, masks out lower values, and computes the total forest area in hectares within a user-defined region (selected.geometry()). It also calculates the average area per pixel to estimate the minimum forest area used based on connected pixel count. Outputs include a map of tree cover (>=11%) reprojected to a specified projection, a printed summary of total tree cover area meeting the criteria, and the minimum forest area used in hectares.
task_name: Identify forest area with minimum canopy cover

task_description: The script evaluates ecological priority areas in Victoria, Australia by combining a ratio layer (likely representing habitat or vegetation condition) with risk of loss and climate resilience (RCP45030) layers. It multiplies the ratio layer with binary filter (>0.3 threshold), then computes composite indices: priority weighted by risk of loss and by RCP45030 resilience. The outputs include mapped layers for private land, current and proposed focal landscapes, NaturePrint scores, environmental layer, and two derived priority composites (with risk and resilience), enabling spatial prioritization for conservation planning under climate change scenarios.
task_name: Identify priority conservation areas with risk and resilience

task_description: The script calculates NDVI from a cloud-masked Sentinel-2 or Landsat image mosaic over a specified polygon and a sub-region (Siembra), then computes the total area of vegetation based on NDVI thresholds. It generates two NDVI visualizations (full polygon and Siembra region), creates binary masks for pixels with NDVI ≥ -1 and ≥0.45 respectively, and calculates the total area in hectares for both regions. The outputs include mapped layers for RGB, NDVI, binary vegetation masks, and printed area summaries.

The script estimates Land Surface Temperature (LST) over a specified geometry using Landsat 8 Collection 1 Tier 1 Surface Reflectance data from 2018. It applies cloud and shadow masking, computes NDVI to derive fractional vegetation cover (FV), estimates surface emissivity (EMM), and finally calculates LST using a radiative transfer-based expression involving brightness temperature (B10) and emissivity. Outputs include the final LST raster map, intermediate layers (NDVI, FV, EMM, thermal), and statistical summaries of NDVI min/max used in emissivity modeling.

The script extracts raw surface reflectance values from Landsat 4 imagery for a set of predefined geographic points over the year 1982. It processes the LANDSAT/LT04/C02/T1_L2 collection by applying cloud and saturation masking, computes monthly median composites, and uses neighborhoodToArray with a square kernel to extract pixel values at each point location across all months. The output is a feature collection where each feature corresponds to a month and contains the extracted spectral values from the median image at the specified point locations, intended for time-series analysis at discrete sites.

The script identifies cropland areas within specific administrative regions (Lombardia in Italy, Pernambuco in Brazil, and Jalisco in Mexico) using the ESA WorldCover land cover product. It extracts Level 1 administrative boundaries from GAUL, clips the WorldCover dataset to each region, isolates cropland (class 40), masks non-cropland pixels, and computes the total cropland area in hectares. Outputs include a binary cropland map (red for cropland) overlaid on the region, the geometry of the cropland extent, and printed area summaries for each region.
task_name: Identify cropland area in administrative regions

task_description: The script processes Landsat 5 Surface Reflectance data from 2011 over the 'encore' region, applying a cloud masking function based on pixel_qa bits to remove clouds and shadows. It filters images by date and geographic bounds, maps a year property to each image, and prints the resulting ImageCollection and its size. The primary output is a filtered, cloud-masked collection of Landsat 5 SR images intended for land cover analysis.

The script generates three median composite images from Sentinel-2A Surface Reflectance data over the NW province of Pakistan for different agricultural seasons: planting (April–May 2020), mid-season (September 2020), and harvest (December 2020–January 2021). It applies rescaling of reflectance bands by dividing by 10,000 and masks clouds and shadows using the SCL (Scene Classification Layer) band. NDVI is computed from Band 5 and Band 4 to assess vegetation health during the mid-season. The output includes three false-color composite visualizations (B8-B6-B3) added to the map for temporal comparison and a derived NDVI layer used alongside reflectance bands for potential agricultural monitoring or classification tasks.

The script classifies land cover types in Wuhan using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery from March to April 2021. It applies cloud masking via the QA60 band, computes vegetation (NDVI), water (NDWI), and built-up (NDBI) indices, then extracts median pixel values for training regions. The output is a CSV file containing mean spectral and index values per region, intended for land cover classification modeling.

The script classifies land cover types across four seasons (Summer, Fall, Winter, Spring) using Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery over a specific WRS path and row (41, 35). It creates a labeled point-based training dataset with manually defined locations and associated land cover classes (e.g., Urban, Agriculture, Forest, Water, Barren) for each season. For each point, it joins the nearest available image in time (within 30 days) from a merged seasonal image collection. The output is a feature collection where each point contains a list of matched images across time, enabling seasonal land cover classification modeling or time series analysis per location.
task_name: Classify land cover types by season

task_description: The script analyzes vegetation health in a specific region using NDVI derived from two Sentinel-2 surface reflectance images acquired on September 5 and September 10, 2020. It computes NDVI using bands B8 and B4, clips the images to a region of interest (roi), and calculates mean and standard deviation of NDVI values within a geometry (emilia) using reduceRegion at 10m scale. The outputs include mapped NDVI layers for both dates and printed statistical summaries (mean and std dev) of NDVI for each date.

The script processes Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery over a specific WRS path and row (22, 36) from 2015 to 2016 with less than 20% cloud cover. It applies cloud and cloud shadow masking using the pixel_qa band, scales the reflectance values by dividing by 10,000, selects only the spectral bands (B[0-9]*), and preserves timestamp properties. The output is a filtered and masked ImageCollection ready for time-series analysis of land surface conditions.

The script classifies land use and land cover (LULC) in Semarang using Landsat 8 TOA imagery from 2017. It filters images by cloud cover, creates a mosaic, and performs supervised classification using a CART classifier trained on user-defined training samples (Water, Vegetation, Urban, Barren). The output includes a classified raster map with a four-class color scheme and accuracy assessment via validation data, producing an error matrix, overall accuracy, and kappa coefficient for model evaluation.

The script classifies land cover types in a region of interest using Sentinel-2 imagery from January 2021. It selects the least cloudy image, extracts spectral bands (B2–B7), and trains a CART classifier using labeled training samples (Agua, Humedales, Suelo, Vegetacion, Forestal) to generate a land cover map. The classification is validated using an error matrix, and overall accuracy is computed. Outputs include a classified raster map and validation accuracy metrics.

The script extracts NDVI and MSAVI2 vegetation indices over TTP points using MODIS surface reflectance data from 2000 to 2020. It applies cloud masking using the state_1km QA band, computes NDVI and temporal variables, stacks images by date, and reduces the image collection at point locations to generate a CSV table of mean pixel values. The output is a time-series vegetation index dataset for specific ground points, intended for training or trend analysis.
task_name: Extract NDVI time series from MODIS

task_description: The script calculates the mean building height per 1km grid cell in Alabama by reducing a precomputed building height image using zonal statistics over a feature collection of 1km grids. It extracts mean height values via reduceRegions with a mean reducer and converts the result into an image for mapping. Similarly, it computes the total building count per grid cell using a sum reducer on a building count image. Outputs include a raster map of mean building height (AL_meanHeight_1km) and a feature collection of building counts per grid (AL_Count_fc), both aligned to the 1km grid framework.

The script classifies land cover types across Burkina Faso, Ghana, and Nigeria using Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery from 2020. It computes multiple spectral indices (NDVI, NDWI, MNDWI, NDBI, BSI, EVI, NDTI) and integrates elevation (SRTM), nighttime lights (VIIRS), and built-up layer (GHSL) as features. A Random Forest classifier is trained on labeled regions (TD and BFVEG) with a 70/30 training-testing split, and the final output is a classified land cover map based on the trained model.

The script analyzes the tropospheric NO2 column number density over a specified bounding box using Sentinel-5P satellite data from July to August 2022. It filters the COPERNICUS/S5P/NRTI/L3_NO2 collection by date and spatial bounds, selects the first available image, clips it to the region of interest, and computes the minimum and maximum values of NO2 concentration within that area using reduceRegion with a scale of 1000 meters. The outputs are printed statistics showing the minimum and maximum NO2 values in the region.

The script classifies land cover types within a user-defined region of interest (ROI) using the MODIS MCD12Q1 Land Cover Type 5 data from 2014. It reclassifies specific IGBP classes into aggregated categories: cropland (classes 7,8 → 99→1), natural vegetation (classes 9,10,11 → 98→2), forest (classes 1,3 → 97→3), and urban/built-up (classes 2,4 → 96→4). The resulting classification map 'ynuse' is used as a mask to extract maximum annual NDVI values from MODIS MOD13A2 for each class. For each class (i=0 to 6), it computes the mean NDVI over the ROI using reduceRegion and prints the result. Outputs include a reclassified land cover raster and printed mean NDVI values per land cover class for regional analysis.

The script generates a set of random points within specified training regions in Cambodia for cashew cultivation, where the number of points is scaled by the number of patches (100 points per patch), and overlays them on a binary cashew crop presence layer for potential use in classification or sampling.
task_name: Generate random points for cashew training regions

task_description: The script classifies Sargassum presence in coastal waters using a Random Forest model trained on Sentinel-2 surface reflectance bands and spectral indices (including FAI, SEI, NDVI variants), with post-classification filtering based on connected pixel count. It outputs a classified image mosaic where Sargassum is identified, along with accuracy assessment using a held-out test set.

The script models sequential land cover changes using a Bayesian updating framework (BULC) by analyzing event images against a base image, computing transition probabilities, and generating time-series outputs including classified maps, confidence layers, conditionals, and probability distributions for each time step.
task_name: Model land cover transitions over time

task_description: The script identifies Sargassum presence in coastal waters using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data, applying a Random Forest classifier trained on spectral bands and vegetation indices (NDVI, FAI, SEI) with post-classification filtering based on connected pixel count. The output is a classified image mosaic highlighting Sargassum areas, cloud masks, and analysis-ready composites for a specific date.

The script performs image segmentation and unsupervised clustering on Landsat MSS imagery to generate superpixels (via SNIC) and classify land cover patterns using both per-pixel and per-segment K-means clustering, with outputs including PCA-transformed images, segmented results, and clustered maps for visual analysis.
task_name: Segment land cover using SNIC and K-means

task_description: The script analyzes the spatial relationship between the Calabar Super Highway and protected areas in Nigeria using Sentinel-1 SAR imagery from 2015 to 2019, computing VV and VH backscatter means and applying focal smoothing to assess landscape changes near infrastructure.
task_name: Analyze highway impact on protected areas

task_description: The script detects edges in a median composite of Sentinel-2 imagery over the Peninsula region using Laplacian and Gaussian convolution kernels, highlighting sharp transitions in surface reflectance for feature delineation.

The script calculates and compares the NBR2 (Normalized Burn Ratio 2) index from two time periods using Sentinel-2-like band data (B6, B7, B10), creating mosaicked composites for each period and computing their difference to detect changes in vegetation condition, likely related to burn scars or vegetation stress.

The script evaluates the accuracy of a land cover classification (BULC) output by comparing it with reference burned area data from NBAC 2017 in British Columbia, using stratified sampling and generating an error matrix for validation.
task_name: Classify burned and unburned areas using BULC

task_description: The script classifies cropland areas by training an SVM classifier on NDVI time series bands (NDVI, NDVI_1, NDVI_2) from a user-provided image using labeled training polygons, then applies the model to produce a classified land cover map distinguishing cropland.

The script analyzes changes in SAR backscatter by separating Sentinel-1 GRD data into pre- and post-period collections based on VV and VH polarizations over a specific region, likely to detect land surface changes such as deforestation, urbanization, or agricultural activity.

The script identifies stable forest areas by analyzing the MODIS MCD12Q1 Land Cover Type 1 product from 2018 to 2020. It remaps land cover classes to binary forest/non-forest, computes temporal standard deviation to detect stable pixels (zero deviation), masks for stable conditions, and extracts only those forest areas that remain consistently classified over time.

The script identifies flood-affected areas using Sentinel-1 VV backscatter data by applying an Otsu thresholding method on the VV band within a geographic boundary (gn_layer), then estimates the population affected by flooding by intersecting the flood mask with the High Resolution Settlement Layer (HRSL). Outputs include a flood extent map, a histogram-based threshold value, and a CSV of population affected per administrative district.
task_name: Identify flood extent and affected population

task_description: The script classifies land cover into urban, vegetation, and water categories using a CART classifier trained on labeled sample regions from a Landsat 8 image. The output is a classified raster map and pixel count statistics within the Entre Rios province boundary.

The script identifies flooded areas by analyzing the difference between pre-flood and post-flood Sentinel-1 VH polarization SAR imagery, applying a ratio-based threshold on filtered images to detect significant backscatter changes indicative of standing water.

The script classifies land cover into six categories (Built-up, Water, Dense Vegetation, Sparse Vegetation, Barren Land, Snow) using a Random Forest classifier trained on Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from 2020, with accuracy assessment via confusion matrix and validation GCPs.

The script classifies land cover into four categories (agua, rural, urbano, semides) using a Random Forest classifier trained on spectral indices and Landsat 5 TOA reflectance bands from 1999. The output is a classified map and accuracy assessment metrics including confusion matrix, overall accuracy, Kappa coefficient, and F1 score.

The script identifies the greenest pixel composite based on NDVI values from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data over a specific agricultural field in 2021, producing a clipped NDVI map highlighting areas of highest vegetation density.

The script identifies surface water extent and calculates water area over time using NDWI derived from Landsat 5 and 7 data between 1991 and 1993, with cloud cover less than 10%, masking non-water pixels and computing water area within a specified region of interest.

The script classifies land cover into three classes (likely representing distinct land cover types such as agriculture, water, and urban or forest) using a Random Forest classifier trained on ground truth points and applied to a Landsat 8 true-color composite image clipped to a study area. The output includes a classified raster map and accuracy assessment metrics.

The script performs histogram matching between two ASTER surface reflectance mosaics from different time periods using cumulative distribution functions and random forest classifiers to harmonize spectral values, with the output being a spectrally matched image composite.
The script calculates the mean NDVI from surface reflectance data of Landsat 8 over a specific region and time period, producing a single composite image representing average vegetation greenness.

The script generates a cloud-free median composite from Landsat 5 TOA imagery for the year 1989 over two WRS rows (43 and 44) covering the Dhaka region, then applies a Tasseled Cap Transformation using L5 coefficients to derive brightness, greenness, wetness, and higher-order components. The final output is a single clipped image combining spectral bands and TCT indices for the ROI.
task_name: Generate cloud-free composite and TCT for Dhaka region

task_description: The script classifies land cover in Bishoftu using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from May 13–14, 2022. It trains a Random Forest classifier on labeled ground control points (Builtup, FarmLand, ForestLand, GrazzingLand, WaterBody, WetLand) using spectral bands B1–B8, produces a classified land cover map with six classes, and evaluates model accuracy using confusion and error matrices for both training and testing datasets.

The script analyzes vegetation and surface water conditions in Bangalore Urban district using median Sentinel-2 imagery from 2019, computing NDVI, MNDWI, and SAVI indices to assess greenness, moisture, and vegetation health.

The script classifies land cover into five categories (Water, Crop land, tree vegetation, Bare soil, Urban) using Landsat 8 surface reflectance data, NDVI and NDBI indices, and a Random Forest classifier trained on user-defined regions. The output includes a classified map and accuracy assessment.

The script selects and processes mean annual environmental covariate image collections (e.g., Heat Insolation Load, NDVI, precipitation) from 2001 to 2018 for specific U.S. states (Montana, Illinois, Ohio, Minnesota, Wyoming), clips them to state geometries, and enables user-defined selection of state-specific data sources for further analysis.

The script calculates the mean VV polarization SAR backscatter from Sentinel-1 during summer 2019, separately for ascending and descending orbits, then combines and averages them to produce a single clipped mosaic image representing average surface reflectivity in VV band over the region of interest.

The script estimates Leaf Area Index (LAI), Fraction of Absorbed Photosynthetically Active Radiation (FAPAR), and Fraction of Vegetation Cover (FCOVER) using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data and trained Random Forest regression models based on spectral bands and solar/viewing geometry.

The script processes GeoHash-based feature collections in Canada and the CONUS, filters them using random sampling and state boundaries, and links geohashes to U.S. state FIPS codes. It then loads Living Root geotiff imagery for specific states and months to derive maximum vegetation composites, focusing on land cover analysis within filtered geohashes.

The script analyzes the temporal variation of NDVI at a specific point location by extracting a time series from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data, masked for clouds, shadows, and snow, within a 400-meter buffer around the point during 2019.

The script retrieves the least cloudy Landsat-8 and Landsat-7 images for a specific point in Semarang, Indonesia, for each year from 2012 to 2022 within the first half of the year (January to July), using cloud coverage as the sorting criterion. The output consists of one image per year, primarily intended for visual inspection or further time-series analysis of land surface changes over a decade.

The script performs land cover classification by first applying cloud masking using Braaten's cloud criteria on Landsat MSS TOA images, then trains a CART classifier using training samples from 1976 and 1983 to classify vegetation, burned areas, and water. It applies both per-pixel classification and superpixel-based classification using SNIC segmentation to improve spatial coherence of the classified output.
task_name: Classify land cover using SNIC and CART

task_description: The script performs land cover classification for Bishoftu town in 2019 using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data and a Random Forest classifier trained on ground control points, producing a classified map with four categories: water body, built-up area, forest, and cropland.

The script filters large wildfires in California between December 2019 and December 2020 using the GWIS GlobFire dataset, then computes deltaNBR (dNBR) for up to three fires using a custom module 'burnS_oneFire' to assess burn severity. The output is a list of dNBR results for individual fire perimeters.
task_name: Analyze burn severity of major wildfires

task_description: The script classifies land cover into three classes—forest (class 0), water (class 1), and herbaceous vegetation (class 2)—using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data and a CART decision tree classifier. The output is a classified raster map showing spatial distribution of these classes over the study area.

The script calculates NDVI from a single Sentinel-2 image, identifies bare ground areas where NDVI is less than 0.4, masks the result to a specific region defined by 'table', and computes the pixel area of bare ground, outputting a raster with the area in square meters labeled as 'bareground'.

The script estimates the average land surface temperature (LST) for Bangui during summer 2018 using Landsat 8 TIRS bands 10 and 11, computing NDVI-based emissivity and brightness temperature, then averaging both bands' LST outputs over a cloud-filtered image collection clipped to an area of interest.

The script calculates the fraction of agricultural land within level-3 geohash cells across Europe using ESA WorldCover land cover classification, filters geohashes where agriculture exceeds 10% of total area, and outputs a feature collection of these high-agriculture geohashes.

The script models the probability of species presence using Maxent classification on Landsat 8 surface reflectance bands, trained with presence-absence field data, and outputs a classified image showing spatial probability distribution.

The script creates a pan-sharpened true-color composite by fusing the high-resolution panchromatic band (B8) with lower-resolution visible bands (B4, B3, B2) from a least-cloudy Landsat 8 image, enhancing spatial detail for visual interpretation.

The script classifies land cover into four classes (agriculture, forest, cloud, and additional forest points) using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data and a CART classifier, producing a classified land cover map.

The script performs image segmentation and classification on a Landsat image over the Puget Sound region, comparing per-pixel and superpixel-based unsupervised and supervised classification methods to produce multiple thematic maps including original bands, PCA components, SNIC superpixels, and classified outputs for land cover analysis.

The script identifies surface water extent within a specified region of interest by calculating the Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI) from the first least cloudy Sentinel-2 image in the date range, then computes the total water-covered area in square kilometers and its ratio to the total ROI area.

The script calculates the temperature difference between two thermal bands (Emis_31 and Emis_32) from MODIS data to derive the Day/Night Temperature Difference (DTB) for 2019, computes NDDI (Normalized Difference Drought Index) using near-infrared and shortwave infrared bands, and generates a median composite of visible and reflective bands for vegetation and land surface analysis over the Cafayate region.

The script performs image segmentation on historical Landsat MSS/TM imagery using the SNIC (Simple Non-Iterative Clustering) algorithm followed by K-means clustering to identify homogeneous regions in tasseled cap-transformed images. It specifically targets cloud-affected pixels by masking bright areas using brightness thresholds and dilating masks, then generates per-pixel and superpixel-based unsupervised classifications. Outputs include segmented images with cluster labels and mean band values saved to user-defined assets, focusing on vegetation-related components (Brightness, Greenness, Yellowness) derived from tasseled cap transformation.
task_name: Segment land cover using SNIC and K-means

task_description: The script classifies land cover into four categories (water, rural, urban, semiarid) using a Random Forest classifier applied to spectral bands and derived indices from a Landsat 5 image from 2009. The output is a classified raster map and accuracy assessment metrics including overall accuracy, Kappa coefficient, and producer/consumer accuracies.

The script classifies land cover into six classes (impervious building, impervious non-building, pervious tree, pervious irrigated, pervious non-irrigated, water) using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data and a CART decision tree classifier trained on manually labeled training points. The output includes a classified land cover map, training and validation accuracy assessments via confusion matrices, and an estimation of class proportions through random sampling within the study area.

The script computes the Normalized Difference Polarization Index (NDPI) using VV and VH polarization bands from Sentinel-1 GRD imagery over a specified region and time period, then clips and adds the index as a new band to each image in the collection.

The script identifies forest disturbance areas in Africa using RADD (Radar for Detecting Deforestation) alert data from January 1 to December 31, 2021, by filtering and masking alerts based on date and severity, then summarizing the number of disturbed pixels within user-defined grid regions.

The script classifies land cover into four categories—water, bare soil, green vegetation, and dry vegetation—using Landsat 9 surface reflectance data. It computes NDVI and NDWI indices, trains a Random Forest classifier on manually defined training regions, and applies the model to generate a classified map. Accuracy assessments are performed using both training confusion matrix and independent validation samples.

The script classifies land cover into categories (Water, Forest, Urban, Grassland) using a support vector machine (SVM) classifier applied to Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data. It trains the model using labeled reference samples, validates accuracy with a held-out validation set, and computes per-class areas within a defined rectangle.

The script identifies changes in vegetation around large parks near BART stations by computing the NDVI difference between 2001 and 2015 using Landsat imagery, then clipping the result to large parks within 2km of BART stations.

The script extracts quality assessment (QA) bits from the BQA band of a Landsat image to derive cloud, shadow, snow, and cirrus confidence levels. It creates binary masks for high-confidence cloud, shadow, snow, and cirrus pixels, combines them into a single mask, and applies it to the original image to remove these contaminated pixels. The output includes visualizations of the individual QA bit layers, the combined mask, and the masked image.

The script classifies wheat crop areas using multi-temporal Sentinel-2 NDVI and surface reflectance data from November 2020 to May 2021. It computes NDVI time series, creates composites, rescales values, and trains a Random Forest classifier on labeled field data to produce a crop classification map clipped to a study area.

The script classifies land cover into four classes (forest, water, cloud, shadow) using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data. It trains a CART classifier with manually labeled feature collections and applies it to generate a classified land cover map.

The script identifies supraglacial lakes on Antarctic ice shelves using Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data by applying a modified NDWI-based thresholding method that differentiates water from snow, ice, and clouds. The output is a binary raster map indicating the maximum extent of potential lakes over the study period, clipped to the Scripps ice shelves boundary.
task_name: Identify supraglacial lakes on ice shelves

task_description: The script calculates NDVI from Landsat ETM+ surface reflectance data between 2010 and 2020, aggregates it annually, and extracts temporal NDVI profiles at specified water body locations for further analysis or classification.
task_name: Extract NDVI time series for water bodies

task_description: The script classifies land cover into four categories—forest, water body, farm land, and settlement—using a CART decision tree classifier applied to a Landsat 8 TOA reflectance image from early 2015. Training samples are collected from user-defined regions of interest, and accuracy is assessed using a confusion matrix on a held-out test set.

The script detects forest change by analyzing time-series NBR (Normalized Burn Ratio) data from Landsat 8 and Sentinel-2 imagery, applying harmonic modeling to fit seasonal patterns, computing z-score-based deviation bins, and running the BULC (Bayesian Updating of Land Cover) algorithm to estimate probabilities of change. Outputs include spatial layers of change probability, confidence, classification series, and visualizations of expected vs. observed vegetation trends.
task_name: Detect forest change using NBR and BULC

task_description: The script models the habitat suitability of Cervus elaphus using Maxent across multiple 8-day periods, generating probability maps. It computes Mann-Kendall trend analysis (slope and p-value) on the time series of suitability predictions to detect temporal trends in habitat suitability.

The script performs superpixel segmentation on an orthomosaic image using the SNIC (Simple Non-Iterative Clustering) algorithm, generating homogeneous regions (clusters) based on spectral similarity in bands b1, b2, and b3. It computes cluster-level statistics including mean values, standard deviation, area, perimeter, width, and height, then combines them into a single multi-band image for further analysis or classification.

The script estimates land surface temperature (LST) using top-of-atmosphere brightness temperature from Landsat 8 Thermal Infrared Sensor (TIRS) Band 10, corrected for emissivity and vegetation contribution through NDVI-derived fractional vegetation cover (Pv) and pixel quality masking for clouds and shadows. The output includes a mean LST map, its histogram, and the mean temperature value over the region of interest.

The script estimates land surface temperature (LST) in Punjab using Landsat 8 Surface Reflectance data by computing NDVI, PVI, TOA radiance, brightness temperature, and emissivity corrections for the summer months of 2021 and 2022.

The script classifies land cover types using manually labeled training points across different classes and a Landsat 8 surface reflectance composite from 2020. It generates a combined feature collection of labeled samples for supervised classification, which can be used to train a model to predict land cover categories over the Orinoquia region.
