task_description: The script classifies land cover into four categories—forest, water body, farm land, and settlement—using a CART decision tree classifier applied to a Landsat 8 TOA reflectance image from early 2021. Training samples are collected from user-defined feature collections, and accuracy is assessed using a confusion matrix on a held-out test set.

The script performs edge detection on a high-resolution SkySat RGB orthorectified image using the Canny Edge Detector and custom convolution kernels to highlight sharp intensity changes, likely for feature delineation or texture analysis.

The script performs supervised land cover classification using Landsat 8 surface reflectance data from January to March 2021 over a polygon area (likely Bishoftu town). It trains a CART classifier on labeled samples for six classes—Water body, Built-Up Area, Forest, Cultivated land, Crop Land, and Bare land—using spectral bands B2–B7, then applies the model to classify the image and evaluates accuracy with a confusion matrix. The output includes a classified map with a legend and accuracy assessment.

The script performs superpixel segmentation using the SNIC (Superpixel Non-Iterative Clustering) algorithm on Sentinel-2 imagery, followed by unsupervised clustering at both pixel and segment levels. It outputs segmented clusters, cluster means, seed points, and visualizations of classified land cover patterns within a specified study area.

The script identifies pixels in Landsat 8 surface reflectance band 7 (SR_B7) with values less than -1000 or greater than 1000 within the specified region and time period, converts the resulting binary threshold images into vector polygons, and outputs a flattened feature collection of these polygons, each tagged with the image acquisition date.
The script processes MODIS NDSI Snow Cover data to generate binary layers indicating areas with snow cover above 20%, 30%, and 40% thresholds, then clips the results to a specified AOI.

The script performs land cover classification using Sentinel-2 imagery by computing spectral indices (NDVI, MNDWI, SPI) and applying SNIC superpixel segmentation followed by a Random Forest classifier trained on user-defined feature classes (Urban, Water, Vegetation, SolarPanels). The output is a classified image map with four land cover categories.

The script maps land cover types in Adamawa State using MODIS MCD12Q1 data from 2018 to 2020, calculates the area of each land cover class within the region, and specifically identifies and quantifies built-up (urban) areas.

The script selects a specific monthly Planet basemap composite for May 2021, applies a threshold-based cloud detection algorithm using blue and NIR bands, refines the cloud mask using focal operations and reprojection at 30m resolution, inverts the mask to preserve clear pixels, and outputs a cloud-masked version of the Planet mosaic. The result is a visually improved composite with clouds removed.

The script identifies urban impervious surface areas using Tasseled Cap Transformation and multi-temporal classification on Landsat and Sentinel-2 data, applying a temporal smoothing function to refine ISA estimates over Dhaka, Narayanganj, and Gazipur regions in Bangladesh.

The script performs image segmentation using SNIC on a Landsat MSS image, applies PCA transformation, conducts per-pixel and per-segment unsupervised clustering (K-means), and trains supervised classifiers (gmoMaxEnt) using training points to classify land cover. It outputs segmented images, cluster means, and classified maps for both unsegmented and segmented approaches, with results saved to user assets. The primary purpose is land cover classification using superpixel segmentation and machine learning.
task_name: Classify land cover using SNIC and supervised learning

task_description: The script creates a false-color composite RGB image from Sentinel-1 VH backscatter values during three specific time periods (2017-01, 2018-07, and 2020-12) over the area defined by 'alap', with each layer representing the median VH polarization intensity. This composite is used to visually analyze temporal changes in surface structure and moisture, particularly sensitive to urban development, agriculture, and deforestation.

The script detects forest change by analyzing time-series Normalized Burn Ratio (NBR) data from Landsat 8 and Sentinel-2, fitting harmonic models to expected NBR values, computing deviations in the target year (2020), binning residuals into z-scores, and applying the BULC algorithm to estimate probabilities of change. Outputs include maps of mean and standard deviation of NBR, fitted vs observed values, change probability layers, and final BULC-derived change masks highlighting areas of significant NBR decline.
The script calculates the total soil organic carbon stock in gigatons for Brazil by multiplying a specific band from a soil carbon dataset by pixel area and summing the values across the country.

The script identifies recent forest disturbance alerts in Africa using RADD (Radar for Detecting Deforestation) data, extracts the latest alert and isolates disturbances from 2021, overlays them on a baseline forest cover map, and computes the number of disturbed pixels per grid unit.

The script performs unsupervised land cover classification using KMeans clustering on Sentinel-2 surface reflectance bands, masking out permanent water bodies using the JRC Global Surface Water dataset, and assigns a distinct class label (5) to non-water areas outside the original segmentation mask.

The script assigns U.S. county FIPS codes to agricultural field polygons in Iowa by spatially joining field geometries with TIGER/2018 county boundaries, using centroid containment and buffer-based intersection logic, and filters counties that contain at least one field.

The script calculates the frequency of snow cover over the specified region (WS) using MODIS NDSI data from 2001 to 2020, producing a continuous map representing the proportion of days with snow cover relative to valid observations.

The script classifies mangrove areas using a Random Forest model based on spectral indices and original bands from a user-provided satellite image, producing a land cover map with validation accuracy assessment.

The script computes a comprehensive set of spectral vegetation, moisture, soil, and atmospheric indices from Sentinel-2 data over a specific region of interest (parcelas) between August 2020 and October 2021. It applies cloud masking and scales reflectance values, then adds multiple derived bands including NDVI, EVI, SAVI, OSAVI, NDWI, MSI, BSI, ARVI, and others to each image in the collection. The output is a time-series ImageCollection enriched with these indices for monitoring land surface conditions, particularly vegetation health and soil properties.

The script creates annual median composites from Landsat surface reflectance data (1982–2020) for a user-defined study area, applying cloud masking and band normalization across sensors (TM, ETM+, OLI), with output including per-year image counts and temporal analysis.

The script estimates Leaf Area Index (LAI) and Fraction of Photosynthetically Active Radiation (FPAR) using a Random Forest regression model trained on Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data, with topographic and angular corrections, and outputs classified raster maps of LAI and FPAR for a specific date range and region.
task_name: Estimate LAI and FPAR from Sentinel-2

task_description: The script creates true-color and false-color composite images from Landsat 8 surface reflectance data over Pokhara Metropolitan City, clipped to the administrative boundary, for visual interpretation of land cover and urban extent.

The script estimates Land Surface Temperature (LST) from Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data using NDVI, fractional vegetation cover, and emissivity modeling, with thermal band B10 and a radiative transfer-based expression for LST computation.

The script performs a binary classification of mining vs. non-mining areas using a Random Forest classifier trained on 33 spectral, textural, and topographic predictors derived from satellite imagery and auxiliary data. The output includes a classified map, accuracy assessments (confusion matrix, overall accuracy, user's and producer's accuracy, kappa), and variable importance metrics.

The script calculates Land Surface Temperature (LST) from Landsat 5 Thermal Infrared data using radiative transfer equations, incorporating NDVI-based emissivity correction and brightness temperature conversion. It also computes NDVI, WET, SI, IBI, and NDBSI indices for vegetation, moisture, and built-up analysis as part of the LST derivation workflow.

The script classifies tree cover loss (tcl) by training a Random Forest model on PlanetScope imagery using labeled polygons derived from tcl bands across 54 images. It evaluates classification accuracy with a confusion matrix and performs spatial partitioning for training and testing.

The script analyzes the quality of actual evapotranspiration (ET) and its associated quality control (ET_QC) layers from MOD16A2, masking invalid pixels based on the ET band's mask, counting valid pixels within a protected area (Parque), and computing the percentage of good-quality pixels in the first image of the collection. It also generates a histogram of ET_QC values to assess pixel quality distribution.

The script estimates the methane (CH4) emission rate from a landfill by analyzing a PRISMA hyperspectral image of a methane plume, combining it with wind speed data from GEOS-CF to compute an effective wind speed and integrating the column density over the plume area to derive the emission flux in kg/h.

The script detects potential mudflow events by computing spectral anomalies between consecutive annual median Landsat images, identifying significant negative changes in blue, green, and red bands as diagnostic indicators, and classifying post-anomaly regions using a CART classifier trained on land cover features. Outputs include anomaly maps, binary change detection layers, and pixel counts per year within a defined polygon.
task_name: Detect mudflow changes using spectral anomalies

task_description: The script calculates and compares maximum NDVI values from Landsat 8 images in January 2021 and February 2016, then computes their difference to identify changes in vegetation greenness over the five-year period within a specified region of interest.

The script extracts daily maximum 2m air temperature, dewpoint 2m temperature, and total precipitation values from the ERA5 dataset for specific point locations between 1979 and 2019, using a 27.75 km resolution buffer around the points.

The script classifies land cover into four categories—dense forest, sparse forest, no vegetation, and water—using a Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier applied to Landsat 5 surface reflectance data. It computes classification accuracy metrics (overall accuracy, kappa coefficient, producer's and consumer's accuracy) using a confusion matrix and calculates the area (in sq.km) for each class within a specified geometry.

The script calculates NDVI from a single Landsat 8 TOA image, extracts maximum NDVI values within agricultural and urban regions using reduceRegions, labels them by land use, and generates an ROC curve to evaluate NDVI's ability to distinguish between agricultural and urban areas. It computes the optimal NDVI cutoff based on the closest point to (0,1) in the ROC space and outputs the AUC as a measure of classification performance.

The script maps forest type coverage from Copernicus Global Land Service data and overlays it with a natural color Landsat 5 image from June to September 1984, clipped to a user-defined area of interest. The output includes visualizations of the forest classification and the historical satellite imagery for comparative land surface analysis.
task_name: Map forest coverage and land surface

task_description: The script classifies land cover into categories (e.g., buildup, water, barren, vegetation) using a CART classifier applied to surface reflectance bands from a single Landsat 8 image. The output includes a classified map, accuracy assessment via confusion matrix, and area statistics per class within a specified region.

The script calculates Land Surface Temperature (LST) from Landsat 8 Surface Reflectance data using a radiative transfer-based algorithm that incorporates NDVI-derived emissivity and thermal band brightness temperature. Outputs include LST map and its statistical summary (min, max, mean, median, standard deviation) over a specified geometry.

The script retrieves a 2019 global land cover dataset from Proba-V at 100m resolution, reduces it using mean aggregation, and reprojects it to EPSG:4326 at 10m scale. It also processes Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8 imagery by resampling to higher resolution using bicubic interpolation, with the intent of aligning multisource data (land cover, precipitation, temperature, MNDWI, NDVI) for potential integration in land use/land cover analysis.
task_name: Extract and resample land cover data

task_description: The script identifies and calculates the total area of 'developed high intensity' land cover (class 24) in Chicago using the NLCD 2016 land cover dataset, masking and summing pixel areas classified as such.

The script performs image-to-image registration by computing pixel displacement between two SkySat red band images, then applies the computed geometric correction to align the second image with the first using bicubic resampling and displacement fields derived from cross-correlation. The output includes the georegistered image, offset magnitude, and flow angle layers.

The script registers multiple historical Landsat MSS images from 1973–1975 to a modern reference image (Landsat 8) using image displacement based on band correlation, enabling accurate spatial alignment for change analysis over time.

The script detects forest change by analyzing time series of Normalized Burn Ratio (NBR) from Landsat 8 and Sentinel-2 data, applying harmonic modeling and the Bayesian Updating of Land Cover (BULC) algorithm to identify significant decreases in vegetation condition, indicating potential deforestation or disturbance.
task_name: Detect forest change using NBR and BULC

task_description: The script identifies dark surface water features in a specified lake region using top-of-atmosphere reflectance from Landsat 8, applying a ratio of blue to near-infrared bands (B2/B4) and refining the result by excluding areas with high thermal infrared brightness and low blue-to-ultraviolet reflectance. The output is a vector feature collection of small water bodies (<100,000 m²) masked from shadows.
task_name: Identify dark water bodies in lake region

task_description: The script filters the MOD10A1 Terra dataset to extract NDSI Snow Cover images for a specific date range, month, and day of the month, returning the filtered image collection for analysis.

The script analyzes vegetation health, surface moisture, soil brightness, and urbanization patterns using multispectral indices (NDVI, NDWI, SAVI, BSI, IBI_A) derived from Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-1 data over the Annamites region between September 2019 and April 2020. Outputs include median composites of optical and radar data, resampled bands, and multiple spectral indices for land surface characterization.
task_name: Analyze vegetation and land surface properties

task_description: The script estimates the surface elevation of Lake Como using GEDI L2A elevation data, corrects it with the EGM2008 geoid model, computes statistical metrics (mean, standard deviation, NMAD), and removes outliers beyond 3 standard deviations. It also extracts the lake's boundary from JRC Global Surface Water data and analyzes the distribution of GEDI shots within the lake.

The script detects agricultural field boundaries by analyzing monthly NDVI variability from Landsat 8 TOA data in mid-year 2021 over a specific region in Brazil. It computes median composites per month, calculates NDVI, identifies temporal NDVI variation (range between max and min), enhances edges using Canny edge detection on the deviation image, and applies a ring convolution to locate field centers, ultimately mapping potential agricultural field locations based on spatial patterns of vegetation change.

The script processes Sentinel-1 GRD data to compute gamma0 terrain-corrected VV and VH backscatter bands (VV_Gamma, VH_Gamma) and their ratio (DPOL), applies angular and edge masking, and performs multitemporal despeckling using a neighborhood-based filtering approach over a specified time window. The output is a cleaned, multitemporal stack of dual-polarization SAR imagery corrected for terrain and speckle effects.

The script models the habitat suitability of Cervus elaphus over time using MaxEnt based on environmental variables derived from MODIS 8-day composites, and applies Mann-Kendall trend analysis to assess temporal changes in suitability probability.

The script identifies urban areas in Dhaka, Bangladesh by applying Tasseled Cap transformation to Landsat data from 1989 to 2018 and computing spectral indices such as NDBI, NDWI, EVI, and brightness-greenness contrast to delineate built-up regions.
task_name: Identify urban areas using Tasseled Cap transformation

task_description: The script identifies potential flooding areas by comparing Sentinel-1 SAR imagery from dry and wet periods, computing a false-color composite (RGB) where changes in surface water are highlighted using VV polarization backscatter differences over time.

The script identifies surface water, flooding, moderate drought, and severe drought conditions using NDWI derived from Sentinel-2 imagery between 2019 and 2020, applying threshold-based classification on maximum NDWI composite.

The script detects and analyzes high sargassum presence in coastal waters using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data and a suite of vegetation and water indices (NDVI, SAVI, FAI, AFAI, SEI), with cloud masking and nearshore region filtering applied.

The script reconstructs the ice shelf surface topography by modifying the REMA mosaic using morphological operations and masking, then computes the difference between the original and reconstructed surfaces to identify elevation changes in coastal Antarctica.

The script analyzes surface reflectance properties of lakes using Landsat 8 TOA imagery from May to October 2015, filtering images by cloud cover, computing HSV (Hue, Saturation, Value) from visible bands, and extracting mean, median, and standard deviation statistics for each lake. The output is a flattened CSV file containing per-lake spectral statistics across multiple cloud-filtered images.

The script validates the accuracy of a burned area classification (BULC) against NBAC reference data using an error matrix and overall accuracy assessment, focusing on fire-affected regions in British Columbia.

The script evaluates the accuracy of three different land cover classifications—Glob30, adaptive classification, and Dynamic World—by generating confusion matrices and accuracy metrics (overall accuracy, user's accuracy, producer's accuracy) using validation samples extracted from a reference dataset. The classifications are compared against ground truth points in the 'Validation' feature collection.

The script calculates the frequency of cloud-free observations from AVHRR surface reflectance data over the Amery Ice Shelf between 1999 and 2005 by extracting QA bits, identifying clear pixels, and computing a percentage of clear observations across the time series.
The script computes NDVI, MNDWI, and SAVI indices from Sentinel-2 imagery to analyze vegetation and surface water conditions in Dhaka city using cloud-masked, median-composited images from 2020.
task_name: Analyze vegetation and water in urban area

task_description: The script classifies land cover types in the Annamite region using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from September 2019 to April 2020. Training samples are derived from manually labeled feature collections for six classes: dirt roads (car and motorbike), pavement roads, forest, settlement, and water. A Random Forest classifier is trained on median-composited imagery and applied to generate a classified land cover map for 2019.

The script classifies land use and land cover (LULC) for three time periods (2015–2016, 2017–2018, 2019–2020) using Sentinel-1 VH polarization data over a user-defined study area. It trains random forest classifiers on labeled training samples (forest, road, settlement, water) for each period, produces classified LULC maps, and computes LULC change between periods (2015–2017 and 2017–2019). Accuracy is assessed via confusion matrices using a train-test split of samples. Additional layers include protected areas, 10km buffers, and major roads.

The script identifies recent deforestation alerts within African logging networks using RADD radar-based alert data from 2021, generates a heatmap of alert density, and creates a stratified random sample of points across risk strata for monitoring or validation purposes.
task_name: Identify deforestation alerts in logging networks

task_description: The script extracts Sentinel-2 top-of-atmosphere reflectance values for specific optical and near-infrared bands over field parcels during a cloudy-filtered period, outputting the first observed pixel value within each parcel as a CSV file.
task_name: Extract Sentinel-2 spectral bands for field parcels

task_description: The script computes the median composite of Sentinel-2 surface reflectance images with less than 10% cloud cover over a specified area and time period, then calculates the NDVI using bands B8 and B4, outputting the result as an NDVI image.

The script classifies land cover types using a Random Forest classifier trained on ground truth points and applied to a cloud-optimized Landsat 8 surface reflectance image, producing a classified map with three categories: red, blue, and yellow, representing different land cover classes within the study area.

The script identifies burned forest areas in the Republic of Congo by analyzing z-score anomalies from time series data and integrating MODIS active fire detections to mask and refine burn maps for the year 2015.

The script calculates the total pixel area of a feature collection named 'DAM_irri' by clipping and reducing Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery from May to June 2021, using bands B8, B4, and B2. The output is a dictionary containing the summed pixel area in square kilometers derived from ee.Image.pixelArea().

The script filters protected areas in Costa Rica using the WDPA dataset, selects those with ISO3 code 'CRI', extracts their establishment year from the 'STATUS_YR' attribute, sets it as a temporal property, and finally filters for protected areas declared in 2020.

The script performs supervised land use/land cover classification using a Random Forest classifier on satellite imagery. Training samples are generated from user-defined polygon geometries representing five classes: bosque (forest), agua (water), urbano (urban), cultivo (agriculture), and pastizal (pasture). For each class, 1,000 random points are generated within the respective geometry to extract spectral values from the input image. The dataset is split into 70% training and 30% testing for model validation. The output includes a classified land use map with five categories and accuracy assessments via confusion matrices, overall accuracy, kappa coefficient, and producer/user accuracies for both training and test datasets.

The script classifies land cover into six classes (water, tall vegetation, bare soil, low vegetation, buildings, and main roads) using Sentinel-2 imagery from 2018 to 2019. It computes spectral indices (NDVI, EVI, NDBI), trains a Random Forest classifier on manually labeled sample regions, evaluates accuracy on validation and test sets, and produces a classified land cover map.

The script calculates the area of land cover classes within a 10 km buffer around the BR-319 highway in the Brazilian Amazon by clipping a land cover classification image (AM_TC_2014) to the buffered road geometry, then computing the total area per class in square kilometers using pixel area summation.
task_name: Map land cover area along BR-319

task_description: The script analyzes land surface temperature in specific regions of Indonesia, including Sumatera Barat province and Kota Bandung, using MODIS LST data for the first half of 2018 and Landsat 8 thermal band (B11) to generate a time series and visualizations.

The script classifies land cover into six specific classes—Builtup, Bareland, Cropland, Wetland, Grassland, and Water—using a Random Forest classifier trained on Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data. The output is a classified raster map clipped to a user-defined polygon, along with accuracy assessments including overall accuracy, Kappa coefficient, and producer/user accuracies derived from a confusion matrix.

The script classifies land cover into four classes (forest, urban, agriculture, waterbody) using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data, training a Random Forest classifier on manually labeled sample points and polygons, then applying it to generate a land cover map and assess classification accuracy with validation data. Outputs include classified raster, accuracy metrics (error matrix, overall accuracy, kappa), and area calculations per class.

The script classifies land use into crop and non-crop categories using a Random Forest classifier trained on NDVI time-series features (NDVI, NDVI_1, NDVI_2) extracted from a precomputed image and labeled with training polygons. The output is a classified land use map based on spectral-temporal signatures.

The script estimates methane emission rates from a plume detected near a landfill by analyzing S3/OLCI radiance data and applying a physical dispersion model using wind speed, column density enhancement, and plume length.

The script classifies land cover types using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from October to December 2021, applying a Random Forest classifier trained on user-defined sample regions with classes including deforested areas, various forest types, saltpans, shrublands, and aquatic vegetation. The output is a classified raster map clipped to the study area.

The script analyzes the availability and temporal distribution of Sentinel-2 Level-1C images over a coastal region in Quintana Roo, Mexico, filtered by date, cloud cover, and spatial location. It outputs a collection of images, distinct acquisition dates, and MGRS tile histograms for temporal and spatial coverage assessment.

The script classifies land cover into urban, vegetation, and water classes using a CART classifier trained on Sentinel-2 surface reflectance bands B2, B3, B4, and B5. The output is a classified raster map derived from a median composite of cloud-masked Sentinel-2 images from 2017 to 2019.

The script creates a median-combined SAR intensity composite from Sentinel-1 VV and VH polarization data, using ascending and descending orbits to enhance surface structure and moisture information for land observation.
task_name: Create SAR composite for land observation

task_description: The script classifies land cover into categories such as eucalyptus, crops, water, and other vegetation using a Random Forest classifier trained on Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data, including spectral bands and TCI, with NDVI as an additional band.

The script classifies land cover into five categories (bosque, agua, suelo, isla, nube) using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data. It trains a CART classifier with manually defined training samples and outputs a classified raster map at 10m resolution.

The script identifies vegetation areas by computing NDVI from near-infrared and red bands of a NAIP image, applies a threshold to create a binary vegetation mask, and cleans the mask using a mode filter over a 1-meter square neighborhood to reduce noise.

The script analyzes monthly and annual NDVI patterns using Landsat 8 imagery from September 2015 to June 2016 over a specific polygon (J20poli), generating time-series visualizations, median and maximum composites, and mapping vegetation health across the region.
The script computes and compares median NDVI values from Sentinel-2 imagery for two different time periods in 2018 and 2017, creating a multitemporal NDVI composite for change analysis.

The script generates 100 random sample points within a defined polygon, extracts mean elevation values from an ALOS World 3D digital surface model (DSM), and performs kriging and inverse distance weighted (IDW) interpolation to create continuous elevation surfaces from the sampled points.

The script analyzes multi-temporal land cover changes by combining reclassified images from different years (1973, 1975, 1980, 1985, 2013) and integrating them into composite sets (set1–set6), then computing pixel counts and proportions for each class. It uses reclassified BULC outputs and Hansen forest/water masks to assess land cover dynamics across decades, with outputs including combined classification images, pixel count statistics, and proportional distributions.
task_name: Analyze land cover change over time

task_description: The script computes NDVI from Sentinel-2 imagery over a specific region and time period, then applies the SNIC (Superpixel Neighborhood Iterative Clustering) algorithm to segment the image into homogeneous regions. It compares segmentation results with and without reprojection to assess spatial consistency, focusing on vegetation-based land surface patterns.

The script classifies land cover into seven classes (water, plantation, agricultural land, habitation, sandy area, deep plantation) using Sentinel-2 imagery and NDVI within the Jorhat boundary. It trains a CART classifier on sampled regions and produces a classified land cover map.

The script classifies land cover into four categories—Water, Bareland, Forest, and Grassland—using a Random Forest classifier trained on Sentinel-2 surface reflectance bands. The classification is applied to a cloud-masked median composite image from July to August 2022, clipped to a specified AOI.

The script identifies wheat cultivation areas in Uzbekistan using NDVI analysis from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data between May 15, 2020, and January 15, 2021, by generating cloud-filtered mosaics and computing NDVI to assess vegetation health.

The script calculates the mean tropospheric NO2 column number density from Sentinel-5P satellite observations within specified geographic regions (table) for the period from January 1, 2020, to March 25, 2020. It outputs a flattened feature collection where each feature corresponds to a region and contains the mean NO2 value and acquisition time.

The script analyzes NDVI variability within buffered agricultural field polygons by computing standard deviation, mean, median, and min/max statistics using Sentinel-2 imagery from April 2018. The output is a feature collection with per-field NDVI summary statistics.
task_name: Analyze NDVI variability in agricultural fields

task_description: The script classifies land cover using a trained model applied to a satellite image composite, producing a classified map with seven distinct classes based on spectral characteristics from the scene and training points collected over the study area.

The script identifies urban areas in Dhaka, Bangladesh by analyzing Landsat-derived Tasseled Cap Transformation (TCT) components and spectral indices such as NDBI, NDWI, EVI, and ndTC12. It processes yearly cloud-minimized composites from 1989 to 2018, with final output focused on 2018 land cover classification emphasizing urban extent.
task_name: Identify urban areas using TCT and indices

task_description: The script extracts time series properties of forest tracts including canopy cover, canopy index, forest proportion, NDVI, and associated dates and image IDs from a precomputed table (table2), and filters forest tract features by TRACTNAME and UID from a feature collection (Hume_forest). It retrieves metadata and property values for specific forest tracts such as 'Burra' and UID 0, focusing on temporal vegetation dynamics.

The script processes GEDI L2A monthly data to filter high-quality observations, mosaics the elev_lowestmode band, samples points within a region of interest, and interpolates the sampled points using kriging and inverse distance weighting to generate a digital elevation model (DEM).

The script analyzes the temporal variation of NDVI values derived from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data over a study area in Vietnam, specifically extracting NDVI time-series at road points to monitor vegetation dynamics between September 2016 and April 2020.
task_name: Analyze NDVI time series along roads

task_description: The script classifies land cover types in Bostanliq district, Uzbekistan using Landsat 5 surface reflectance data from 1994–1995. It trains a Random Forest classifier on ground control points (GCPs) for eight classes—water, glaciers, urban, rocks, bare land, forest, rangelands, and agriculture—and validates the classification accuracy using a confusion matrix and accuracy metric.
The script calculates the difference in NDVI between 2001 and 2015 using Landsat ETM+ data, focusing on Dominica, to identify areas of vegetation change.

The script calculates NDVI from Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data, applies cloud and land masks, computes median composites for 2019 over BaliNusra, extracts minimum values for red and NIR bands, and applies a Dark Object Subtraction (DOS) correction to estimate surface reflectance for bands B4 and B5.

The script processes MODIS MYD09GA surface reflectance data to generate true-color visualizations while applying a series of masks to filter out pixels affected by clouds, cloud shadows, and high sensor zenith angles within the Parque Nacional Palo Verde (PVNP) region. It focuses on spatial subsets around specific ground stations and wetland polygons, producing masked image collections and visual layers for analysis.
task_name: Analyze surface reflectance with cloud masking

task_description: The script identifies urban areas in Dhaka, Bangladesh by analyzing Landsat-derived Tasseled Cap Transformations (TCT) and spectral indices (NDBI, MNDWI, TDVI) from 1989 to 2018, with final urban classification applied to the 2018 image. Outputs include a normalized multi-year composite with brightness, greenness, wetness, and urban probability layers, clipped to the region of interest.
task_name: Identify urban areas using TCT and spectral indices

task_description: The script classifies built-up land cover changes in Zambia for the years 2000, 2010, and 2015 using both supervised and unsupervised BULC (Batch Urbanization Land Cover) methods. It integrates base images from RCMRD and GFSAD with event images derived from Landsat data to generate classification and probability outputs for urban expansion analysis.

The script classifies land cover into predefined classes (permukiman, vegetasi, Industri) using a CART classifier applied to surface reflectance bands from Landsat 8. The output is a classified image map with distinct color-coded land cover categories.

The script retrieves the most recent NAIP image covering a specified point, applies a smoothing filter using a uniform kernel, detects edges using a Laplacian kernel, and computes standard deviation in a local neighborhood to analyze texture. Outputs include the original image, smoothed image, edge-enhanced image, and spatial variability (texture) layer for visual interpretation and feature extraction.
task_name: Detect land cover edges and texture

task_description: The script performs image segmentation on historical Landsat MSS imagery using the SNIC (Superpixel Neighborhood Iterative Clustering) algorithm followed by K-means clustering on both per-pixel and per-segment bases. It applies tasseled cap transformation, normalizes bands, masks bright pixels (e.g., clouds), and generates unsupervised classifications to analyze land cover patterns over time at a specific focal point in Quebec. Outputs include segmented images, cluster maps, and visualizations stored in user-defined assets.
task_name: Segment land cover using SNIC and K-means

task_description: The script classifies land cover types in the Bishoftu region using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from May 13–14, 2022. It trains a CART classifier on labeled regions (BareLand, CropLand, Forest, GrazingLand, Builtup, WaterBody, WetLand) using spectral bands, performs image classification, and evaluates accuracy with a confusion matrix on training and testing partitions.

The script identifies cassava cultivation areas by classifying field data into cassava and non-cassava categories, assigning binary class IDs (1 for cassava, 0 for others), merging them into a single feature collection, and converting it into a raster where each pixel represents the presence (1) or absence (0) of cassava based on the nearest field observation.

The script analyzes dry season Landsat 8 EVI data from July to October 2014 to compute maximum, mean, and standard deviation of vegetation index values, then identifies areas with EVI greater than or equal to 0.6 within a specified region in Brazil, likely targeting dense or persistent vegetation cover.

The script identifies the earliest burn dates from a sequence of fire events using a time-series of classified images, remapping class values to days of burn and masking non-continuous burns based on a maximum anomaly threshold. It outputs the minimum burn date image and a masked version excluding non-continuous burns, both clipped to a specific fire region in British Columbia.
task_name: Identify burn dates from fire events

task_description: The script analyzes temporal changes in VH-polarized Sentinel-1 SAR backscatter over a defined region, computing median images before and after mid-2019 to detect agricultural or land cover changes. It also calculates the range (85th minus 15th percentile) of 2020 VH backscatter as a measure of temporal variability, potentially indicating crop type or land use intensity.

The script mosaics five pre-defined images (image1 to image5) and applies a series of mask operations to isolate areas of selective logging based on driver and confidence layers. It generates a composite image where pixels are filtered to exclude certain drivers (values 2 and 3) and low-confidence classifications (confdriver and conftcl equal to 2), resulting in a refined map of high-confidence selective logging areas.

The script identifies dark regions in a lake area using Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data by computing the ratio of blue (B2) to near-infrared (B4) bands, then filters these regions based on their spatial relationship with radar-dark areas derived from Sentinel-1 HH backscatter. It specifically isolates persistent dark features in optical imagery that are not coincident with SAR-derived shadows, likely targeting ice or turbid water bodies while excluding radar shadow artifacts.

The script extracts carbon monoxide (CO) column number density values from Sentinel-5P satellite data for a specific date range and geographic region defined by 'geome', then samples these values at specific point locations in 'geometryPoi' with a spatial resolution of 1000 meters, returning a flattened feature collection of sampled points with CO measurements.

The script estimates tree cover loss (TCL) within concession areas excluding roads using RADD alert data, aggregated at a coarser resolution and adjusted with a multiplier to account for detection sensitivity. It outputs a mapped layer showing the percentage of tree cover loss derived from aggregated RADD alerts.

The script analyzes temporal and spatial backscatter characteristics of three wetland areas using Sentinel-1 GRD data from July 2017, computing VV, VH, and their ratio (Ratio) to compare ascending and descending orbits, generating RGB composites of multi-temporal stacks for visual analysis of wetland surface scattering dynamics.

The script maps the temporal variation in surface area of glacial lakes using Landsat and Sentinel-2 imagery from 1984 to 2022, combining NDVI, NDWI, NDSI, and topographic indices with Random Forest classification to identify water bodies and compute their area over time.

The script downscales MODIS Land Surface Temperature (LST) from 1km to 240m resolution using a random forest regression model trained on SRTM-derived elevation, Koeppen-Geiger land cover, MODIS reflectance bands, NDVI, and LST at 960m, applied per land cover class to improve accuracy. The output is a mosaic image of predicted LST at 240m resolution.

The script identifies snow-covered areas in the Alpuri region by calculating the Normalized Difference Snow Index (NDSI) from a Landsat 8 surface reflectance image, using green and SWIR bands, and applying a threshold (NDSI > 0.05) to classify snow pixels.

The script estimates Suspended Particulate Matter (SPM) concentration in water bodies using the red band (B4) from surface reflectance-corrected Landsat 8 imagery, applying a custom empirical algorithm based on reflectance transformation.

The script performs superpixel segmentation (SNIC) on a land surface image (LSM) to generate homogeneous regions (clusters) based on spectral characteristics, specifically using mean values from band 'b1_mean' and assigning cluster IDs. The output is a segmented image with clusters used for further land cover analysis or classification.

The script calculates monthly maximum NDVI values over Goiás, Brazil, from August 2014 to July 2015, composites them into a multiband image, and computes temporal statistics (min, max, mean) and standard deviation across the time series to assess vegetation dynamics.

The script estimates Land Surface Temperature (LST) using thermal infrared data from Landsat 7, incorporating NDVI-based emissivity correction and gap-filling of cloudy pixels through spatio-temporal regression. The output includes a filled Landsat image, NDVI, vegetation fraction, emissivity, and final LST in Celsius.

The script identifies vegetation and water areas using NDVI and NDWI indices derived from Sentinel-2 L1C imagery between 2019-01-01 and 2023-02-11, applying cloud masking and binary land/water classification over a specified region of interest.

The script identifies surface water bodies by calculating MNDWI from Landsat 5 SR data, applying Otsu's thresholding method on the MNDWI histogram to dynamically determine a water/non-water threshold, and producing a binary water mask which is then mapped.

The script analyzes changes in vegetation health and burn severity over time using Sentinel-2 imagery from August 2019, 2020, and 2021. It computes NDVI, NBR, and EVI indices to assess pre- and post-fire vegetation conditions within the IBRA region, with visualizations of RGB composites and NDVI layers.
task_name: Analyze vegetation and burn severity changes

task_description: The script calculates HSV (Hue, Saturation, Value) components from red, green, and blue bands of top-of-atmosphere reflectance in Landsat 8 imagery over selected lakes, then computes mean, standard deviation, and median values within lake boundaries for cloud-filtered images between June 1–30, 2014. The output is a CSV file containing per-lake spectral statistics used for water appearance analysis.
task_name: Extract lake water color and brightness statistics

task_description: The script analyzes Sentinel-2 MSI imagery over selected lakes between May and October 2016, filtering images by cloud cover, computing HSV (Hue, Saturation, Value) from RGB bands, and extracting mean, median, and standard deviation statistics for each lake. The output is a CSV file containing per-lake spectral and derived HSV band values across multiple cloud-filtered images.

The script classifies land cover into forest, bushes, and open areas using Landsat 7 surface reflectance data, then analyzes annual forest cover percentage changes from 2000 to 2021 in Tesso Nilo National Park, correlating it with fire occurrences, DMI, and SOI climate indices.

The script classifies forest areas affected by wind damage using PCA components and fractional cover data from 2015 and 2017, applying a Random Forest classifier on selected spectral bands to distinguish between wind-damaged and non-damaged regions.

The script filters a feature collection of lakes within a region of interest (roi), extracts various aggregated properties such as Hylak_id, country count, elevation statistics, and generates random points around Montreal. It also computes histograms, products, and distinct counts of lake attributes, while mapping area and centroid features for watersheds. Outputs include printed summaries and map visualizations of processed lake and watershed data.
task_name: Extract lake properties and generate random points

task_description: The script creates a cloud-minimized, true-color composite mosaic from Sentinel-2 imagery for two regions of interest in 2019 by selecting the least cloudy image and combining them into a single seamless image.

The script masks an MVI (likely Moisture Vegetation Index) image using SRTM elevation data, restricting the analysis to areas below 50 meters in elevation. It then calculates the mean, minimum, and maximum values of the masked MVI within a specified region.

The script calculates mean winter (December-February) land surface temperatures from MODIS Terra and Aqua daily data, distinguishing between daytime (11h, 13h) and nighttime (22h, 2h) over a specific rectangular region in the Iberian Peninsula. It applies quality filtering (QC bit 0–1) and converts digital values to Celsius, then clips results to a predefined geometry.

The script analyzes and compares the spectral bands, spatial resolutions, and temporal coverage of multiple Earth observation datasets (MODIS, MSS, TM, NAIP, Landsat, Sentinel-2) over a specific geographic point, primarily focusing on band names, image counts, projection scales, and temporal series for multi-sensor comparison.

The script validates the accuracy of a burned area classification (BULC) result against NBAC 2017 reference data for British Columbia, using an error matrix to compute overall accuracy. It compares pixel-level classifications from BULC output with independent fire perimeters and NBAC burned/unburned labels within a specific region.

The script computes NDWI from Sentinel-2 imagery for seven monthly composites between November 2020 and May 2021, applies the Canny edge detector to identify water body boundaries, and sums the resulting edge maps to highlight persistent or changing surface water edges within the region of interest.
task_name: Detect water body changes using NDWI and edge detection

task_description: The script identifies RADD (Radar for Detecting Deforestation) alerts in Africa for 2021, masks them by date, and overlays them on a mosaic of Sentinel-1 images. It then analyzes the impact of spatial resolution aggregation (from 10m to 50m and 100m) on the representation and summation of low tree canopy cover areas (tcl == 1), computing frequency histograms and cell counts across scales.
task_name: Identify deforestation alerts and analyze spatial aggregation effects

task_description: The script classifies land cover types using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from 2015 to 2020, applying a Random Forest classifier trained on user-defined sample regions with 7 spectral bands. The output is a classified raster map of 12 land cover classes within a specified watershed boundary.

The script analyzes multi-temporal land cover changes by combining reclassified images from different years (1973, 1975, 1980, 1985, 2013) into composite sets and computing pixel counts and proportions. It integrates Hansen forest change data with user-classified Landsat-derived land cover maps to assess temporal transitions in land cover classes across the study area.
task_name: Analyze land cover change over time

task_description: The script analyzes population density and its changes over time in Africa using multiple high-resolution population datasets (WorldPop, GHSL, and Facebook/HRSL). It computes population density for a given year and calculates both absolute difference and relative percent change between two time points. The analysis is masked by user-defined thresholds to focus on areas above minimum population density. Outputs include raster images of population density, density difference, and percent change, which can be used for regional demographic studies and urbanization monitoring.

The script processes Landsat 5 Surface Reflectance data to compute the Tasseled Cap Brightness (TCB) index, applies cloud and shadow masking using pixel quality bands, and extracts time-series spectral and TCB values at specific point locations. It outputs CSV files containing sampled pixel values (Blue, Green, Red, NIR, TCB) over multiple point geometries (p0–p7) for long-term land surface monitoring and agricultural or land cover change analysis.
task_name: Extract Tasseled Cap components for land cover analysis

task_description: The script processes MODIS MCD43A4 surface reflectance data to generate temporal composites and spectral mixture analysis (SMA) products. It selects specific reflectance bands, renames them for consistency, applies SMA using a custom package, and computes annual and multi-year median composites from 2000 to 2023. The outputs include various temporally reduced ImageCollections (monthly, yearly, and long-term medians), SMA-transformed imagery, forest cover collections, and scaled percentage images, intended for land surface monitoring and vegetation change analysis.

The script maps mangrove forest extent using multi-temporal Sentinel-1 C-band VV backscatter data over a tropical coastal region. It retrieves ascending-orbit, slice-filtered GRD imagery from specific relative orbits, computes median composites for selected dates (2016–2019), and combines them into multitemporal RGB visualizations. The analysis integrates JAXA ALOS PALSAR annual mosaics (2007, 2010, 2017) for historical context and applies a mangrove mask derived from the LANDSAT/MANGROVE_FORESTS dataset to focus on mangrove areas. Outputs include layered visualizations of S1 VV time series, PALSAR HH/HV composites, and masked multitemporal S1 composites for change and extent analysis.
task_name: Map mangrove forest extent using SAR

task_description: The script classifies forest disturbance stages (healthy spruce, mixed forest, infested spruce, post-beetle outbreak) using Landsat 8 surface reflectance and Tasseled Cap components. It computes brightness and greenness from surface reflectance bands, trains Random Forest classifiers on three different feature sets (Tasseled Cap only, surface reflectance only, and combined), and generates three classified land use maps. Accuracy assessment is implied through classifier explanation output.

The script performs a supervised classification of land cover using a CART classifier on multispectral imagery. It computes PCA on the input image combined with HSV-transformed bands, extracts training samples from labeled polygons, trains the classifier, and applies it to generate a classified land cover map. The output includes the classified raster, accuracy assessment via confusion matrix, and a mode-filter-smoothed version of the classification for visual improvement.

The script classifies land cover types using NDVI percentile and interval-mean features derived from a Sentinel-2 surface reflectance image collection over a specified region and time period. It computes NDVI from B8 and B4 bands, applies cloud masking using QA60, and generates a composite with multiple percentile and interval-mean statistics. This composite is combined with a MODIS land cover map (test4) to train a Random Forest classifier. The trained model is applied to classify the full study area, and accuracy is assessed using a confusion matrix on a held-out test set. Outputs include the classified land cover map, training/testing datasets, and classification accuracy metrics.
task_name: Classify land cover using Sentinel-2 NDVI percentiles

task_description: The script identifies vegetated areas in Aruba using NDVI derived from Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data for June 2020. It computes NDVI from bands B5 and B4, selects the greenest pixel composite based on maximum NDVI, applies a threshold (NDVI > 0.2) to classify vegetation, and calculates the mean vegetation fraction within the region. Outputs include a clipped NDVI mosaic map, a binary vegetation mask, and the average vegetation coverage value printed to the console.

The script classifies forest health conditions in a mountainous region using Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery from July to August 2020. It applies cloud and saturation masking, computes median composites, and trains a Random Forest classifier on labeled training points (healthy spruce, mixed forest, grey stage, post bark beetle) to generate a land cover classification map with four classes. The output includes the classified raster map, training and validation accuracy assessments via confusion matrices, and overall accuracy statistics.

The script classifies land cover types using Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data from October 2019 over a study area. It applies cloud masking based on the BQA band, filters images by date and cloud cover, computes a median composite, and extracts training and testing samples from labeled regions (c1–c9) for supervised classification. The output includes stratified training and testing datasets with land cover labels, sample counts, and a clipped median mosaic used for classification, enabling model development and accuracy assessment.

The script identifies burned areas in the Beira Corridor region using Landsat imagery from 2013 to 2019. It processes collections of Landsat 7 and 8 surface reflectance images, applying a threshold on the near-infrared band (B5 for Landsat 8, B4 for Landsat 7) to detect potential burned pixels. Annual burned area layers are generated by summing binary masks across images per year, then applying a frequency threshold. A final cumulative burned area map from 2014 to 2019 is produced by combining annual binary burned area rasters. Outputs include annual and total burned area visualizations using a color palette, clipped to the study area.

The script classifies three types of tree plantations—eucalyptus, fir, and pine—using summer Sentinel-2 imagery over defined regions of interest. It applies cloud masking, selects red edge and NIR bands (B6, B7, B8, B8A, B11), computes median composite, and extracts labeled training samples by clipping class labels (1: eucalypt, 2: fir, 3: pine) to respective geometries. The output is a CSV file of sampled pixels with spectral values and class labels, intended for use in supervised classification model training.

The script processes a collection of Landsat 8 surface reflectance images over a defined polygon in China, filtering for images from May to August 2020 and selecting only the blue band (B2). It then mosaics images taken on the same date into single composites, assigning each mosaic a timestamp corresponding to its acquisition date. The output is a daily-mosaicked ImageCollection of the blue band, intended for temporal analysis of surface reflectance, with metadata preserved for time-series use.
task_name: Mosaic Landsat 8 blue band by date

task_description: The script computes the Vegetation Health Index (VHI) over a user-defined AOI using Landsat 8 and 9 surface reflectance and brightness temperature data from January to June 2022. It first applies scale factors and cloud masking, then calculates NDVI to derive the Vegetation Condition Index (VCI), uses thermal band ST_B10 to compute the Temperature Condition Index (TCI), and finally combines VCI and TCI into VHI. The output is a VHI time-series image collection mapped over the area, with each image containing the VHI band for its respective date.

The script computes the Radar Vegetation Index (RVI) from Sentinel-1 VV and VH polarizations over Zhejiang Province for 2020. It calculates RVI using the formula '4*VH/(VV+VH)', applies a Savitzky-Golay time-series smoothing filter to reduce noise, clips results to the ZJ boundary, and adds temporal bands (date, month, day of year). The output is a smoothed, time-continuous RVI image collection with reconstructed values named 'd_0_constant', suitable for monitoring vegetation dynamics using radar backscatter.
task_name: Estimate crop vegetation condition using SAR-derived RVI

task_description: The script compares mean tropospheric NO2 column number density over a 30-day period in 2019 and the same period in 2020 (one year apart) using Sentinel-5P data. It applies cloud masking (pixels with cloud fraction < 25%) and computes monthly averages, then highlights areas where NO2 exceeds 50 µmol/m². The output is a split-panel interactive map showing spatial patterns of NO2 for both periods with synchronized viewing, along with a legend and time labels for comparison.
task_name: Compare NO2 levels before and after lockdown

task_description: The script calculates MSI, ARVI, and SAVI vegetation indices from VIIRS surface reflectance data, then computes VCI (Vegetation Condition Index) and TCI (Temperature Condition Index) using NDVI and LST composites, and finally derives VHI (Vegetation Health Index) as a weighted combination of VCI and TCI. It processes a time series of VIIRS images over a specified region and date range, generating multi-band imagery with derived indices for drought or vegetation health monitoring.

The script identifies water bodies in a specified region using the Automated Water Extraction Index (AWEI) derived from Landsat 5 surface reflectance imagery. It applies a cloud masking function to filter out clouds and shadows, computes median composite imagery, calculates AWEI2 to detect water, classifies pixels with AWEI2 >= 0 as water, masks non-water areas, and computes the total water surface area in square kilometers using pixel area summation within a given geometry.

The script analyzes soil properties in Java, Indonesia by combining mean sand and water content from SoilGrids datasets. It computes a composite index (sand + water) and classifies it into liquefaction risk categories using an SLD-based interval classification. The output includes layered visualizations of sand content, water content, their sum, and a classified risk map with custom legends for each variable, focused on selected provinces in Java.
task_name: Assess soil sand and water content

task_description: The script calculates mean aboveground biomass values from two biomass datasets (globBiomass and WHRC) stratified by land cover classes from either MapBiomas or stability14 classifications. It masks biomass layers using a stability layer (stability14.gt(0)), then combines them with land cover maps before computing grouped mean statistics per class via reduceRegion. Outputs are printed dictionaries showing mean biomass per remapped land cover class for four combinations: MapBiomas-globBiomass, stability14-globBiomass, MapBiomas-WHRC, and stability14-WHRC.
task_name: Analyze biomass by land cover class

task_description: The script computes a comprehensive list of spectral indices (e.g., NDVI, EVI, MSAVI) from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery over Malta using a custom spectral library. It retrieves the first available image from the specified date range, scales the bands via the 'spectral' package, and prepares to calculate all indices listed in the INDICES collection. The output is intended to be a multi-band image where each band represents a different spectral index, enabling detailed land surface analysis related to vegetation, water, soil, and built-up features.

The script extracts pixel values from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery for specific bands (B2, B3, B4) during a narrow date range in July 2017, using minimum value compositing. It samples these values at predefined feature locations labeled with 'Height' to create a training dataset for classification or regression modeling. The data is then partitioned into training (70%) and testing (30%) sets based on a random column, enabling model validation. Outputs include the full sampled collection, and the split training and testing partitions, which are printed for inspection.
task_name: Extract training samples for land classification

task_description: The script classifies forest disturbance stages (healthy spruce, mixed forest, grey stage, post bark beetle) using Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery from June 2015. It applies cloud masking and scaling factors, then trains a Random Forest classifier on labeled training points within user-defined geometries. The output includes a classified land cover map with a four-class palette, training and validation accuracy assessments via confusion matrices, and overall accuracy statistics for both training and validation datasets.

The script identifies monthly surface water extents from January to December 2022 (with December 2021) using Sentinel-2A/B SR harmonized imagery. It computes NDWI (Normalized Difference Water Index) based on green and near-infrared bands, applies SCL-based cloud masking, calculates median NDWI composites per month, classifies water bodies using a threshold (NDWI > 0), combines selected months into a maximum water occurrence image, and generates vector polygons of persistent water zones. Outputs include binary water masks for each month, a yearly maximum water extent raster, and vectorized water body zones clipped to the study area.

The script generates a minimum value composite of cloud-masked Landsat 5 surface reflectance imagery over a user-defined boundary. It applies a cloud masking function using pixel_qa bits for cloud and water, combines it with the existing image mask, and computes the minimum pixel value across the time series within the region of interest, then clips the result to the boundary. The output is a single multiband raster representing the temporal minimum surface reflectance, which may be used for surface characterization or as input for further analysis.

The script computes a time series of maximum NDVI values using a moving window convolution (MVC) over Sentinel-2 imagery. It first calculates NDVI from B8 and B4 bands, filters images by date, region, and cloud cover, then applies a 10-day sliding window to compute the maximum-value composite for each center pixel in the window. The output is a daily ImageCollection where each image represents the maximum NDVI over a 10-day window, with timestamps advanced accordingly.
task_name: Compute NDVI time series with moving window

task_description: The script classifies land cover types (built-up area, slum, water, vegetation, agriculture) using Landsat surface reflectance imagery from 2013 to 2020. It merges labeled training samples for five classes, applies cloud masking for Landsat 5, 7, and 8, computes spectral indices (NDVI, EVI, LSWI), and trains a Random Forest classifier on median-composited imagery from 2020. The output is a classified land cover map clipped to the study area and an area calculation in square kilometers per class, derived from pixel counts.

The script identifies urbanized areas in Africa using the Global Human Settlement Layer (GHSL) SMOD population dataset from 2015. It filters the GHSL SMOD image to extract pixels with an urban code (3), creates a binary urban/non-urban mask, and vectorizes the resulting urban regions into polygons. The output includes a raster mask of urban areas and a vector feature collection of urban polygons, which are filtered by label value corresponding to urban density. Additionally, it prepares building density and population layers from Facebook HRSL data for further analysis.
task_name: Identify urban areas from GHSL data

task_description: The script classifies land cover types in the Upper Ganga region using Sentinel-2 imagery from December 2016 to February 2017. It computes NDVI, NDBI, and NDWI indices, applies cloud masking, and trains a Random Forest classifier on labeled ROIs (agriculture, water, sandbar, baresoil, vegetation, builtup). The output includes a classified raster map with a color palette for six classes, along with accuracy assessments (error matrix, overall accuracy, kappa, user's and producer's accuracy, F1-score) based on test samples.

The script compares surface reflectance in California before and after a wildfire event in 2020 using MODIS MOD09GA imagery. It processes two image composites: one from late July (pre-fire) and one from late October (post-fire), applying median reduction, scaling by dividing pixel values by 10000, and clipping to the California state boundary. The output consists of two visual layers on the map showing true-color-like composites (using bands b01, b02, b06) for the pre- and post-fire periods, enabling visual assessment of landscape changes due to wildfires.
task_name: Compare pre- and post-fire surface reflectance

task_description: The script identifies flood-affected areas by comparing dry and wet season water extent using Landsat 8 TOA imagery from 2020. It computes NDWI from green and NIR bands for both periods, applies a threshold (0.1) to classify water in the wet season, and generates masked flood extent maps. The outputs include true-color composites for dry and wet seasons, NDWI visualizations for both periods, a binary flood area map, and comparison with BPBD flood reference data, supporting flood impact assessment.

The script analyzes the temporal pattern of NDVI over a region of interest using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from 2020. It applies cloud masking using the QA60 band, computes NDVI from bands B8 and B4, and aggregates the image collection by day of year (DOY), computing mean NDVI values per DOY across the year. The output is an array of NDVI values indexed by DOY, representing the phenological trend for the year 2020 over the specified region.
task_name: Analyze NDVI time series by day of year

task_description: The script assesses wildfire burn severity in Kalimantan Timur, Indonesia, using pre- and post-fire Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery from 2013–2014 and 2018–2019. It computes the Normalized Burn Ratio (NBR) for both periods, calculates the difference (dNBR), scales it by 1000, and classifies burn severity into eight categories (e.g., high regreening, unburned, low to high severity burns) using a custom SLD-based legend. The output includes pre- and post-fire RGB composites, NBR maps, dNBR raster, classified dNBR map with a visual legend, and an interactive map centered on the study area.

The script evaluates the accuracy of water class predictions in France using LUCAS ground truth data and COPERNICUS Land Cover data from 2018. It filters predicted water points with high confidence scores (≥0.95), compares them to actual LUCAS labels, and separates correct and incorrect classifications. The output consists of two feature collections styled as green (correct) and red (incorrect) points on the map for visual assessment of classification performance.

The script identifies surface water bodies in a specified region using the Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI) derived from Sentinel-2 imagery collected between January 12 and January 28, 2022. It applies strict cloud filtering (less than 1% cloud cover), computes median pixel values, and clips to a user-defined geometry. NDWI is calculated using Green (B3) and NIR (B8) bands. An Otsu thresholding method is applied to the NDWI histogram to automatically determine an optimal threshold for separating water from non-water pixels. The result is a binary water mask mapped in blue. Outputs include the NDWI raster, its histogram, the computed Otsu threshold value, and the classified water body map.

The script performs a supervised land cover classification using a Random Forest classifier on satellite imagery. It splits the sample data into training (70%) and validation (30%) sets based on a random column, trains the classifier using spectral bands and a class property 'id', then evaluates accuracy via a confusion matrix. The output includes the confusion matrix and overall classification accuracy.

The script assesses liquefaction risk potential in Nusa Tenggara Barat by analyzing soil sand and water content derived from WorldClim soil texture layers. It computes mean sand (OLMS) and water (OLMW) content, combines them into a composite index, and categorizes the result into liquefaction risk levels (Sedang to Sangat Tinggi) using an SLD-based interval classification. The output includes layered maps of sand content, water content, their sum, and classified risk zones, along with two colorbar legends for sand and water content and a categorical legend for liquefaction risk.

The script computes multiple vegetation and land surface indices (NDVI, SAVI, LAI, NDWI, GCI, NDRE, DYI) from Sentinel-2A/B SR data over a user-defined region of interest. It applies cloud masking using the QA60 band, filters images by date and cloud cover, and maps index calculations across the image collection. Outputs include layered visualizations of NDVI and DYI, an RGB composite of a filtered image, and the point/table geometry on the map for spatial context.
task_name: Compute vegetation and crop health indices

task_description: The script processes Landsat 5 and 7 surface reflectance imagery over a specific WRS path/row (118/32) from 2002 to 2006, focusing on cloud-masked, seasonally filtered images. It applies a focal mean filter to simulate gap-filling of the Scan Line Corrector (SLC) failure artifacts in Landsat 7 imagery. The output includes visual comparisons of original and filled Landsat 7 images, alongside a Landsat 5 image for resolution comparison, enabling assessment of gap-filling performance.

The script detects land cover changes using Sentinel-2 imagery by comparing pre- and post-event median composites. It computes spectral indices (NDVI, NDSI, NBR) and change metrics (CV, RCV) between time periods, applies thresholding based on z-score statistics to identify significant changes, and generates a binary change mask. The output includes a classified raster map of change areas and vector polygons delineating changed regions for further analysis.

The script classifies six different forest types in a study area using Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery, terrain attributes (elevation, slope, aspect), and GLCM-based texture features. It computes multiple vegetation indices (NDVI, EVI, SAVI, etc.), applies cloud masking, and normalizes the composite image before training a Random Forest classifier on labeled training samples. The output includes a classified raster map of forest types, variable importance scores from the Random Forest model, and accuracy assessment metrics (confusion matrix, overall accuracy, kappa, producer's and consumer's accuracy) based on an independent validation dataset.
task_name: Classify forest types using spectral and terrain features

task_description: The script analyzes multi-temporal Landsat surface reflectance data (Landsat 5, 7, and 8) from 1984 to 2021 over a specific WRS path/row region. It applies consistent preprocessing including cloud and snow masking using pixel quality bands, scales reflectance values, renames spectral bands for uniformity, and merges collections across sensors. The output is a unified, masked, and sorted image collection suitable for time series analysis of land surface conditions, particularly vegetation dynamics using Red and NIR bands. The script also samples pixel values over user-defined geometries (e.g., watersheds, streams, administrative regions) for validation or further analysis, indicating a focus on regional land surface monitoring.

The script identifies burned areas in New Mexico using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery from April to August 2019. It applies cloud masking using the QA60 band to remove pixels with high probability of clouds, cirrus, and opaque clouds, then computes a median composite. Training labels are created from polygon features labeled as 'Burn', which are converted into a binary label image. The script generates 256x256 pixel image patches centered on random sample points within the burn sites, extracts RGB and label bands, and outputs TFRecord files containing these image chips for machine learning training.

The script calculates the mean downward shortwave radiation at the surface from the TerraClimate dataset for the year 2020. It selects the 'srad' band, computes the annual mean, divides the result by 10 to convert units (from W/m² to a scaled value), and then extracts the mean radiation value over the 'chaidamu9' geometry using reduceRegion. The output is a dictionary containing the mean radiation value for the specified region.

The script estimates sub-pixel fractions of photosynthetic vegetation (PV), non-photosynthetic vegetation (NPV), and bare soil using spectral unmixing on MODIS MCD43A4 surface reflectance data. It applies a linear unmixing model with predefined endmember spectra for PV, NPV, and bare soil, masks water pixels using the Hansen global forest change dataset, and generates monthly SMA (Spectral Mixture Analysis) composites from 2003 to 2020. Outputs include false-color visualizations of SMA results mapped over the area of interest, with layers for specific months (e.g., December 2019 to April 2020) and annual medians, supporting temporal analysis of land surface composition changes.

The script maps land surface characteristics in the Batu region using median surface reflectance from Landsat 8 OLI/TIRS imagery collected in 2021. It applies cloud and shadow masking via the pixel_qa band, computes a median composite, and clips the result to the administrative boundary of Batu. A second image collection from 2020–2021 is also processed similarly but filtered to a smaller AOI (aoi1), though it is clipped to the same Batu boundary. Two true-color (B4-B3-B2) visualizations are added to the map for comparison, indicating the focus on visual interpretation of land surface features over time.

The script calculates the percentage of vegetation cover within the Bangalore city boundary using a pre-classified land cover image. It extracts the vegetation class (class value 3) from the classified raster, computes its area in square kilometers using pixel area multiplication and reduction over the city geometry, and derives the proportion relative to total city area. The output is a single rounded percentage value representing vegetation coverage.

The script analyzes land surface changes over time using atmospherically corrected Landsat surface reflectance data from 1984 to 2020. It processes Landsat 5, 7, and 8 imagery for a specific WRS path/row, applies scaling factors to optical and thermal bands, masks clouds and shadows using QA_PIXEL bits, and merges the collections into a single time series. The output is a cleaned, continuous dataset of surface reflectance images suitable for long-term land surface monitoring and change detection analysis, with visualizations of training or reference points across multiple locations.

The script analyzes the distribution of land cover classes in a region of interest using GlobCover 1992 data. It extracts the 'landcover' band, clips it to a vector boundary (elc_gdc_10), computes a frequency histogram over that area using reduceRegion with a scale of 1000 meters, calculates relative proportions by normalizing counts, and outputs both the raw frequency dictionary and the normalized class proportions for analysis.

The script assesses the severity of a wildfire by computing the difference between pre- and post-fire Normalized Burn Ratio (NBR) using Sentinel-2 imagery. It calculates median composites for pre-incendio (2019-01-01 to 2019-01-20) and post-incendio (2020-01-01 to 2020-01-11) periods, masks clouds with less than 10% cloud cover, and derives NBR from B8 and B12 bands. The difference (NBRPreIncendio - NBRPostIncendio) produces a burn severity index map. Additionally, NDVI is computed for both time periods to evaluate vegetation health before and after the fire. Outputs include visualizations of pre- and post-fire false-color images, NBR maps, NDVI maps, and a burn severity map using a custom color palette.

The script computes multiple vegetation and water-related indices (NDVI, EVI, RVI, GCVI, LSWI, NDTI) from Sentinel-2 imagery over a region of interest. It applies cloud masking using the QA60 band, filters images by date and cloud cover, maps index calculations across the image collection, and generates a composite (maximum value) image clipped to the ROI. The output is a multi-band raster asset containing spectral bands and derived indices, suitable for vegetation monitoring and land surface analysis.

The script calculates Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) using Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery from January 2018 to April 2022 over a user-defined geometry. It processes the image collection by applying the normalizedDifference function on bands B5 (NIR) and B4 (red), renames the result as 'ndvi', and adds it as a new band to each image in the collection. The output is an ImageCollection with an additional NDVI band for each scene, suitable for vegetation monitoring and time-series analysis.

The script analyzes Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery from 2020 over a specified region to identify vegetation and built-up (urban) areas. It applies cloud masking using pixel quality bands, computes NDVI and NDBI indices, and applies thresholding: NDVI > 0.275 for vegetation and NDBI between 0.1 and 0.3 for built-up areas. The outputs include three visual layers: a binary NDVI-based vegetation mask, an NDBI-based built-up area mask, and a true-color composite of the mean annual image, all clipped to the study area.

The script analyzes tree cover extent in the year 2000 using the Global Forest Change (GFC) dataset, distinguishing areas with at least 60% canopy density. It computes spatial layers for forest loss and gain, masks them to high-canopy tree cover, and calculates pixel-area-weighted statistics. The workflow includes masking and layer multiplication to derive surface area in square meters. Regional statistics are extracted for two sets of geopolitical regions: the Southern United States (e.g., Alabama, Georgia) and South American countries (e.g., Brazil, Argentina), producing a tabular summary of forest loss, gain, and original tree cover area per region.
task_name: Identify tree cover and forest loss gain

task_description: The script evaluates the quality of Landsat 8 surface reflectance images over a specific WRS path/row region by comparing their NDVI values with temporally proximate MODIS MCD43A4 NDVI. For each Landsat image, it computes NDVI, finds matching MODIS images within ±16 days, calculates median MODIS NDVI co-located with the Landsat scene, computes absolute NDVI differences, and flags the Landsat image as 'bad' if more than 10% of 2000 sampled points show NDVI differences exceeding 0.25. The output is a list of system:index values for flagged (poor-quality) Landsat images based on spectral inconsistency with MODIS.
task_name: Flag Landsat images by NDVI consistency with MODIS
