The script evaluates and maps high-priority grassland areas for bird habitat in Middlebury, Vermont by combining scored criteria including grassland size, soil quality, and parcel protection status, producing both scored and threshold-based composite maps that integrate land cover, soil, and parcel data to prioritize conservation areas.
task_name: Identify priority grasslands for bird habitat

task_description: The script classifies land cover into urban, bare, water, and vegetation categories using a random forest classifier trained on Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from 2019 over Bangalore, producing a classified map for that region.

The script classifies land cover into six classes—Water, Secondary Forest, Shrub and Scrub, Oil Palm Plantation, Bare Land, and Built-up Area—using Sentinel-2 spectral indices and Random Forest classification, with post-classification masking for water and oil palm using SAR data.

The script classifies land cover types in the Kyiv region by training a Random Forest model on multi-temporal Sentinel-1 VV and VH backscatter data, with training samples derived from buffered polygons. The output is a classified raster map clipped to the Kyiv region boundaries.

The script extracts the Fraction of Absorbed Photosynthetically Active Radiation (FAPAR) from the NOAA AVHRR CDR dataset over a specified geometry between April 1, 2017, and October 30, 2017. It composites the data into 16-day median images, formats each with a date-stamped band name, and merges them into a single multi-band image stack clipped to the region of interest.

The script generates median and mosaic composites from Sentinel-2 imagery for two different years (2019 and 2020) over a specific point location, using cloud-filtered images to produce clear-sky representative images for visual analysis in RGB bands.

The script generates a cloud-masked median and mosaic composite of Landsat 7 Surface Reflectance data from 2009 to 2012, clipped to a region of interest, for visual interpretation using true-color rendering.

The script analyzes vegetation health and change over time using NDVI derived from Landsat 8 and Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data for Smolensk Oblast, Russia. It computes median NDVI for 2020 and 2021 from cloud-masked image collections, applies percentile-based masking to filter extreme values, and calculates the difference between years to identify spatial patterns of vegetation change.

The script classifies the probability of vicugna presence using Random Forest based on environmental variables derived from Landsat 8 surface reflectance, bioclimatic temperature (bio01), and precipitation (bio12) data, training the model with presence points and generating a continuous probability map output.

The script classifies land cover types in the Kyiv region using multi-temporal Sentinel-2 optical data and time-series Sentinel-1 SAR data, combining cloud-masked imagery with Random Forest classification trained on buffered ground truth polygons.

The script analyzes Sentinel-1 SAR time series to compute a cumulative sum (CUSUM) of the VH-VV polarization ratio deviation from dry season baseline, enabling detection of surface water changes and potential flooding events in the North Rupununi region.

The script creates a cloud-free mosaic of Landsat 8 TOA reflectance images by filtering for low cloud cover, mosaicking the collection, and clipping to a study area. The output is a single composite image representing surface reflectance over the region during the specified period.

The script computes multiple vegetation and water indices (NDVI, NDWI, MNDWI, AWEI, EVI, LSWI, MSAVI, SB, WRI, SWIR, NIR) from Landsat surface reflectance data, masks clouds and cloud shadows, and extracts pixel statistics (min, max, stdDev, median, 10th–90th percentile mean) at specified point locations for the year 2014.
task_name: Extract spectral indices for land analysis

task_description: The script corrects surface reflectance imagery for topographic illumination effects using the SCS+c correction method on Landsat 8 SR data, computing illumination conditions (solar zenith, solar azimuth, slope, aspect) from SRTM DEM and applying per-band linear regression to reduce terrain-induced radiometric distortions.

The script creates a median composite image from Sentinel-2 data between January and June 2017, masking clouds and cirrus using the QA60 band, filtering images by cloud cover, and reducing the collection using the 50th percentile. The output is a surface reflectance mosaic used for visual interpretation in RGB bands (B4, B3, B2), which can support land surface monitoring such as vegetation or land cover analysis.

The script analyzes the spatial relationship between wildland fires and road infrastructure across different GDP-based regions, calculating road lengths within buffered fire perimeters to assess human exposure and environmental impact.

The script processes Sentinel-1 SAR imagery to create daily mosaics of VH and VV polarization backscatter over a specified region, focusing on ascending orbit data at 10-meter resolution. It outputs an image collection composed of daily mosaic images spanning from January 1, 2015, to October 30, 2018, enabling temporal analysis of surface structural and moisture characteristics using radar backscatter.
task_name: Map land surface with Sentinel-1 SAR mosaics

task_description: The script classifies land cover into tidal flats, water, and other classes using a CART classifier applied to surface reflectance bands from Landsat 8. The output is a classified image map with three categories: water (blue), tidal flats (red), and others (green).

The script generates a cloud-corrected, atmospherically scaled, and clipped true-color composite image from Landsat 9 OLI-2 data for a user-defined region of interest, using the red, green, and blue bands (SR_B4, SR_B3, SR_B2) averaged over 2022 with less than 10% cloud cover.

The script classifies built-up areas using PlanetScope imagery by training a Random Forest classifier on building point labels, applying NDVI, NDWI, and RGDIFF indices, and excluding floodplain and zero-value pixels within the MecBa region in Ethiopia.

The script identifies flooded areas by comparing MNDWI (Modified Normalized Difference Water Index) derived from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data before and after a flooding event in February–March 2022, applying a water mask difference to detect newly inundated regions within Kyiv Oblast, Ukraine.

The script classifies land cover types using a time-series stack of Sentinel-1 SAR imagery, applying a Refined Lee filter for speckle reduction and training a Random Forest classifier on labeled regions to produce a classified land cover map.

The script prepares training and validation datasets by merging three feature collections (Stadium_Golf, Non_Trees, Grass), assigning random values to split them into 80% training and 20% testing samples for a land cover classification task.
The script identifies and masks cloud and cirrus pixels in a Sentinel-2 image using the QA60 band, then applies a cloud-free mask to produce a filtered image with improved atmospheric clarity.

The script analyzes long-term Landsat imagery to compute water and vegetation indices (AWEI, NDWI, MNDWI, NDVI) and generates temporal statistics (min, max, median, percentiles, interval means) for modeling surface water occurrence and land cover characteristics. It also incorporates topography (ETOPO1) and global surface water occurrence data to support environmental monitoring.
task_name: Analyze surface water and vegetation dynamics

task_description: The script identifies surface water bodies using the Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI) derived from MODIS MYD09A1 data, applies a quality mask based on StateQA bits, reclassifies NDWI values to binary water presence, and computes the cumulative cost distance to water for each pixel within the area of interest between 2014 and 2017.
task_name: Map water extent and distance to water

task_description: The script detects edges in Sentinel-2 satellite imagery over a specified region and time period using the Canny Edge Detector algorithm, with images filtered for low cloud cover.

The script computes a time series of NDVI values from May 2020 to December 2020 and January 2021 using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data, generating monthly median composites over a specified geometry. It calculates NDVI from bands B8 and B4, scales the values by multiplying by 10,000, and combines them into a multi-band image collection representing monthly vegetation indices. Additionally, it creates a stacked reflectance image (refl) containing full spectral bands across the same period for further analysis.
The script creates a median composite image from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data filtered by date, region, and cloud coverage for visual analysis using true-color (B4, B3, B2) bands.

The script calculates the mean slope value from a terrain dataset within a specified geometry at two different scales (30m and 1m), and also computes the total area where elevation exceeds 500 meters by summing pixel areas. Outputs are printed as dictionary results from reduceRegion operations.

The script estimates Land Surface Temperature (LST) using thermal infrared data from Landsat 8, incorporating NDVI-based Fractional Vegetation Cover (FVC) and Emissivity (EM) calculations to refine the LST model. Outputs include NDVI, FVC, emissivity, and LST maps within a user-defined polygon.

The script analyzes Sentinel-1 SAR time series to compute CUSUM and Z-score transformations on VH or VV backscatter for detecting surface moisture dynamics, particularly identifying wetting and drying patterns over the Forth catchment region in Scotland using change detection methods.

The script identifies surface water bodies using VV-polarized Sentinel-1 SAR imagery by applying terrain slope correction, Perona-Malik diffusion filtering, and an edge-guided Otsu thresholding method on backscatter values. The output is a binary water mask derived from the VV band, with non-water pixels masked out based on edge connectivity and histogram analysis.

The script constructs a comprehensive feature stack for land cover classification or environmental modeling by computing spectral indices (EVI, SAVI, IBI, ND and R ratios), tassled cap components and angles, terrain features, and integrating static layers such as distance to roads, buildings, streams, protected areas, eco-regions, tree canopy height, water occurrence, and JRC water history. The output is a multiband image combining optical bands, derived vegetation indices, topographic variables, and ancillary geospatial datasets for predictive modeling.
task_name: Model land cover with spectral indices and topography

task_description: The script detects active fire alerts using thermal infrared data from the FIRMS dataset, filters them by date and geographic area (Guatemala), converts pixel counts to vector points representing fire locations, and outputs the number of detected fire points.

The script calculates the spectral ratio of ASTER band B7 to B5 over a region in Madagascar between January 1 and January 10, 2022, to identify locations with potential kaolinite mineral presence based on reflectance characteristics.

The script identifies tree cover areas within a 3000-meter buffer around a specific GPS point using the ESA WorldCover land classification dataset from 2020–2021. It calculates the percentage of tree cover (class 40) relative to the total land cover area within the region.

The script calculates the total precipitation volume for polygon features by multiplying the sum of precipitation (in mm) from DAYMET data by the area of each feature, then identifies the top 5 regions with the highest precipitation volume.

The script calculates the total area of tree cover in the year 2000 (with canopy cover ≥51%) and quantifies annual forest loss from 2001 to 2014 in the Philippines using the Hansen Global Forest Change dataset. Outputs are printed as square meters of forest cover in 2000 and annual forest loss per year.

The script compares forest loss and gain detected by MapBiomas land cover transitions (2008–2021) with results from LT-NDFI change detection models (loss and gain) in two study areas (Apui and Horta) in the Brazilian Amazon, computing user's and producer's accuracy through pixel count comparison within AOIs.
task_name: Compare forest loss and gain detection

task_description: The script filters cloud and shadow pixels from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance images over Primorsky Krai, Russia, between January and February 2019, producing a cloud- and shadow-masked composite image for improved visual analysis.
task_name: Filter clouds and shadows in S2 imagery

task_description: The script identifies forested areas in the NLCD 2016 land cover dataset by selecting classes 41 to 43 (deciduous, evergreen, and mixed forests), computes the area of forest in acres per pixel, and aggregates the total forest area per U.S. county using a reduceRegions operation.
task_name: Map forest area by land cover classification

task_description: The script generates a multi-temporal composite of Landsat 8 TOA reflectance and derived vegetation indices (NDVI, GRVI, GBVI, EVI, GCVI) over a specified region in Tanzania for the year 2017, applying cloud masking and percentile-based reduction to produce a median and percentile summary image stack for agricultural monitoring.

The script extracts land cover classification for the Gulbarga district in Karnataka, India, using ESA WorldCover data from 2020–2021. It clips the classification to the administrative boundary and computes the area (in km²) of each land cover class within the region, then prints a dictionary mapping class names to their respective areas.

The script performs terrain slope correction on Sentinel-1 GRD data using volume and surface scattering models, then trains Random Forest classifiers on corrected and uncorrected VV/VH backscatter to classify land cover types. It evaluates classification accuracy using stratified sampling and outputs classified maps for uncorrected, volume-corrected, and surface-corrected imagery.

The script identifies and monitors surface water pixels over time using the Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI) derived from green and near-infrared bands of Landsat 8 Surface Reflectance data, applying cloud and terrain shadow masking, and filtering for land pixels before generating a time series of water pixel counts within a specified region.

The script computes MNDWI, EVI, MSAVI, and SB indices from Landsat surface reflectance data, masks clouds and cloud shadows, and extracts min, max, stdDev, median, and interquartile statistics per point location to generate a CSV dataset for model training and validation.
task_name: Extract vegetation and water indices for training data

task_description: The script classifies land cover into six categories (water, urban, mangrove, tambak, veglain, lahanterbuka) using a CART classifier on median composite Landsat 8 TOA reflectance from August 2014, then evaluates classification accuracy with an error matrix and computes area per class in square kilometers.

The script calculates the Band-Standardized Chlorophyll Index (BSCI) using Landsat 8 surface reflectance data to assess vegetation structural complexity over a specific region during July 2016. It computes the mean BSCI across the time period and extracts mean BSCI values for user-defined feature collection sites.

The script detects edges in a land cover image (image1) using a custom 9x9 convolution kernel with zero weights, then clips a MODIS surface reflectance band for a specific date and region. The primary output is the result of convolving image1 with the defined kernel, intended for edge detection or pattern recognition in land cover data.

The script analyzes seasonal patterns of vegetation, water, and soil brightness using Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data over a rural polygon from 2018 to 2022. It computes NDVI, NDWI, and BSI indices, identifies greenest, bluest, and brownest pixels using quality mosaics, maps the day of year (doy) for phenological seasonality, and fits harmonic regression models to NDVI time series for both rural and urban areas to detect temporal trends and seasonal cycles.
task_name: Analyze seasonal vegetation and water dynamics

task_description: The script quantifies forest gain in Colombia by extracting pixel values from the UMD Hansen global forest change dataset, masking for gain areas, and summarizing the total gain per administrative region using zonal statistics. The output is a CSV file containing summed forest gain values for each region in the Colombian boundary feature collection.

The script analyzes annual NDVI composites from Landsat surface reflectance data between 2013 and 2018 to detect temporal changes in vegetation using the LandTrendr algorithm, producing a time-series segmentation image collection that identifies breakpoints and trends in vegetation condition.

The script calculates Pearson correlation coefficients between various spectral indices (including NDVI, SAVI, ARVI, and their variants using green, SWIR1, and SWIR2) derived from Landsat 8 surface reflectance data and a vegetation volume variable (VT_1ha) in Quintana Roo, Mexico. It first creates a median composite for 2017, extracts training and validation sample sets from the dependent variable, computes spectral bands and indices, and then evaluates their linear relationship with the vegetation volume metric over the training region.

The script identifies and maps the frequency of water and vegetation occurrence in a specified region using Landsat 8 surface reflectance data from 2017. It applies cloud masking, computes multiple spectral indices (MNDWI, EVI, NDVI, LSWI, AWEIs, etc.), and uses a decision tree to classify water and vegetation across the time series. The final outputs are water and vegetation frequency layers derived from the sum of classified images divided by the total count.

The script prepares a median composite from Landsat 5 surface reflectance data over the Emalahleni region for 1990, computes spectral indices (NDVI, NDBI, NDWI) to distinguish land cover types such as urban, water, coal mine, vegetation, and bare land, and combines these with SRTM elevation data to create a multiband feature stack for potential supervised classification of land cover.

The script applies a cloud masking function to Landsat 5 and Landsat 8 surface reflectance data, computes median composites per year for the period 1984–2011 (Landsat 5) and 2014–2020 (Landsat 8), and adds them to a list with year and product metadata. The final output is a time-series collection of annual median images over a specified region, intended for land cover analysis.

The script calculates the number of days in 2019 when the maximum 2m air temperature exceeded 32°C by converting Kelvin to Celsius and applying a threshold, then sums the binary results over the year and clips to Africa.

The script calculates and maps the distance to surface water by first computing NDWI from Landsat 8 TOA data, masking clouds and cloud shadows, classifying water pixels (NDWI ≥ 0), and then computing the cumulative cost distance from non-water to water pixels within the area of interest.

The script computes a cloud probability score for Sentinel-2 images using multiple spectral thresholds on blue, RGB, coastal blue, water vapor, and cirrus bands, then masks pixels above a cloud threshold of 25. The output is a median composite of cloud-masked Sentinel-2 imagery over Guyana from 2018 to 2019.

The script detects algal blooms in Taihu Lake by calculating the Floating Algae Index (FAI) from atmospherically corrected MODIS surface reflectance data, applying thresholds to identify bloom-affected areas, and summing binary occurrence maps over time to produce a frequency map of algal blooms.

The script identifies urbanized areas with significant nighttime light intensity (stable lights > 30) within a 40km buffer around cities in India using DMSP-OLS data from 2013, masking out darker regions to focus on illuminated city zones.

The script performs topographic correction on Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery using the SCSc method, incorporating solar geometry and SRTM-derived terrain attributes (slope, aspect) to reduce illumination effects in mountainous areas. It computes illumination conditions (IC), applies per-band correction for blue, green, red, NIR, SWIR1, and SWIR2 bands, and outputs corrected median composites with NDVI time series analysis over multiple years.

The script calculates the total area of forest loss in the Gondia region by identifying pixels with forest loss in 2012 from the Hansen Global Forest Change dataset and summing their area using pixel area multiplication and reduction over the Gondia boundary.

The script calculates the number of days with clear or water conditions (cfmask ≤ 1) for each pixel by analyzing Landsat Surface Reflectance data from 2014, producing a yearly clear observation count map.

The script identifies the least cloudy Landsat 8 image within a study area by sorting the collection based on 'CLOUD_COVER' and selecting the first image. It also creates a median composite of images from January to May 2023, clipped to the study area, for visual analysis using false-color rendering (B5, B4, B3). Outputs include the least cloudy single scene and a cloud-reduced median composite for the region.

The script identifies newly constructed buildings by analyzing a pre-computed classified image of building presence in the Awabel and Aneded districts (AnAw) of Ethiopia, then applies a Gaussian kernel convolution to compute a smoothed density map of these buildings. The output includes a binary classification layer of buildings and a kernel density estimation layer for spatial pattern analysis.
task_name: Identify new buildings using classified image

task_description: The script calculates the number of tropical nights (days with minimum temperature ≥ 20°C) per year from 1985 to 2019 using PRISM and DAYMET climate datasets, focusing on San Diego County. It generates a histogram showing the frequency distribution of tropical nights within the county boundary.
task_name: Count tropical nights from minimum temperature

task_description: The script identifies areas of potential flooded vegetation by analyzing temporal changes in Sentinel-1 VV and VH backscatter. It computes ratio and difference metrics between wet and dry season composites, applies thresholds to detect significant increases in radar return, and generates masked layers highlighting regions with flood signatures based on SAR response characteristics.
task_name: Detect flooded vegetation using SAR ratios

task_description: The script computes radar-based backscatter ratios (CR), normalized difference ratio index (NDRI), and difference indices (DRI) from Sentinel-1 VV and VH polarizations over Tanzania during a training period from 2019 to 2020, using percentile reductions to characterize surface scattering behavior for agricultural or land cover monitoring.

The script calculates EVI anomalies by comparing median EVI values from a baseline period (1984–1994) against subsequent images (1994–2012), highlighting areas of positive and negative vegetation change over time using Landsat 5 surface reflectance data.

The script classifies land cover into five categories—urban, forest, water, agriculture, and grassland—using a Random Forest classifier trained on mean surface reflectance values from Landsat 8 imagery from 2017. It evaluates classification accuracy using validation points and outputs a classified land cover map along with an error matrix and overall accuracy.

The script filters U.S. counties by a specified state name ('Califonia', likely intended as 'California') using the TIGER/2018/Counties dataset, retrieves the corresponding STATEFP code, and populates a dropdown menu with sorted county names within that state for interactive selection.

The script identifies surface water extent in the Massingir reservoir using NDWI derived from Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data on a specific date (2019-07-11), applies a threshold to classify water, masks non-water areas, clips to the region of interest, and calculates the total water-covered area in square kilometers.

The script identifies and maps the frequency of canola cultivation (crop code 153) from 2012 to 2019 using annual crop type data from AAFC/ACI, generating three visualizations: crop frequency for 2012–2015, 2016–2019, and combined 2012–2019 periods within a user-defined region of interest.

The script classifies land cover into categories such as forest, non-forested vegetation, non-vegetational areas, and water using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data. It computes spectral indices (NDVI, NDWI, SAVI), trains a Random Forest classifier on labeled sample regions, and applies it to generate a classified land cover map.

The script classifies land cover types in the Miombo region using Landsat 5 TM surface reflectance data from 2005 by computing NDVI thresholds, training a Random Forest classifier on labeled sample points, and applying post-classification corrections. The output includes a classified land use map with six categories: Forestland, Cropland, Grassland, Wetlands, Settlements, and Otherland, along with accuracy assessment metrics and visualizations.

The script identifies areas of Rabi crop cultivation and detects changes between 2019 and 2020 using NDVI thresholds from Sentinel-2 data, focusing on persistent and newly cultivated agricultural land within buffered regions of interest.

The script analyzes the spatial and temporal impact of wildfires on wildland and forest areas, quantifying affected population within buffer zones, burned area extents, and proximity to critical infrastructure such as roads and power grids across continents from 2001 to 2015.
task_name: Analyze wildfire impact on population and infrastructure

task_description: The script models Net Ecosystem Exchange (NEE) of carbon by combining MODIS-derived land surface temperature, emissivity, LAI from a precomputed image, PAR data, and derived variables including Rd, α, Fcsat, and PPFD. The output is a raster representing NEE in µmol/m²/s.
task_name: Model NEE from vegetation and temperature

task_description: The script analyzes seasonal vegetation dynamics by computing 20th percentile NDVI and true color composites from Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8 data during dry and rainy seasons (2018–2020) over a defined geometry, producing layered visualizations of surface reflectance and vegetation health.

The script identifies the frequency of water and vegetation presence using a decision tree approach applied to cloud-masked Landsat 7 surface reflectance data from 2017. It computes multiple spectral indices (AWEIs, EVI, NDVI, LSWI) to classify water and vegetation, then calculates their temporal frequency and maps intertidal and non-vegetated tidal flat zones.

The script analyzes changes in vegetation health by computing NDVI from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data over a coastal region in California, comparing median NDVI values between 2019 and 2020 to detect potential forest disturbance or degradation, such as from fire or drought.
task_name: Analyze NDVI change in forest area

task_description: The script processes a Sentinel-2 image collection by filtering for moderate cloud cover (10–30%), adding cloud and shadow masks, applying mask-based filtering, and performing topographic correction using the SCS+C method on blue, green, red, and NIR bands over a specified terrain (isok). The output is a topographically corrected image collection suitable for analysis in rugged terrain.
task_name: Correct topographic effects on Sentinel-2 imagery

task_description: The script identifies flooded areas by analyzing the difference in VV-polarized backscatter from Sentinel-1 SAR imagery before and after a flood event, applying focal median smoothing and a threshold to detect significant changes.

The script calculates the median Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) from cloud-filtered Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery over a specific point in northeastern Brazil between January 2020 and March 2023, producing a single composite NDVI image for vegetation assessment.

The script classifies different land cover types in Quintana Roo, Mexico, using a Random Forest and CART classifier trained on NDVI values derived from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data. Training data consists of labeled feature collections for mangroves, ferns, non-forest areas, swamp forests, semi-evergreen forests, and other vegetation types. The output includes classified raster maps and accuracy assessments for both classifiers.

The script calculates multiple vegetation and plant health indices (NDVI, NDMI, SAVI, EVI2, EVI, ARI) using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data for a specific date and region, then extracts mean and median values within a defined geographic boundary.

The script classifies land cover types (Forestland, Grassland, Cropland, Wetland, Settlement, Otherland) using a Random Forest classifier applied to Landsat 7 surface reflectance and NDVI data from the year 2000, with training and validation points derived from labeled feature collections. The output includes a classified land use map, accuracy assessment metrics (overall accuracy, kappa, producers/consumers accuracy), and a visual legend.

The script identifies areas of change in the land surface by computing the squared difference between each image in a cloud-masked Sentinel-2 collection and the median image, then creating a mosaic based on minimum values across time. The output is a composite image highlighting spectral differences over time, primarily using visible and NIR bands.
task_name: Detect land surface changes using Sentinel-2

task_description: The script identifies areas of high vegetation density (NDVI ≥ 0.7) within 3.5 km buffers around Kamchatka volcanoes using Sentinel-2 imagery from July to September 2020, and classifies each volcano region based on whether the masked NDVI pixel count exceeds 200,000.
task_name: Identify high NDVI vegetation near volcanoes

task_description: The script generates a multi-temporal composite of Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 optical imagery with derived vegetation indices (NDVI, GNDVI, GRVI, GBVI, EVI, GCVI) and statistical reductions (median, min, percentiles, stdDev) over a buffered agricultural zone in Tanzania for use as input features in crop monitoring or insurance modeling.
task_name: Extract S1-S2 vegetation and radar predictors

task_description: The script generates median composite images from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data for each month of 2021, filtered by low cloud cover and clipped to a user-defined geometry, then combines June through December composites into a multi-band image for temporal analysis of land surface properties.

The script calculates NDVI using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from July 2020, selecting cloud-free images within a specified geometry, and generates a mosaic to derive a final NDVI layer for vegetation analysis.

The script filters Landsat 8 TOA reflectance images by multiple spatial and temporal criteria, including point locations, a polygon ROI, WRS path/row, system index, and day of year, to identify specific scenes within the collection. It does not perform analysis on the imagery but prepares subsets for potential downstream use.
task_name: Filter images by region and date

task_description: The script generates a median composite true color image of Trinidad and Tobago for the year 2000 using Landsat ETM+ TOA reflectance data, applying cloud masking with the simpleCloudScore algorithm and clipping to the country boundary.

The script classifies the presence of fishponds in a specific region using Sentinel-2 or Landsat satellite imagery, training a Random Forest classifier on spectral indices (NDVI, NDMI, NDWI, MNDWI) and reflectance bands (B2, B3, B4, B6, B8, B11). Training and validation are performed using labeled point datasets for fishponds and unclassified areas. The output is a classified raster map showing predicted fishpond locations within the region of interest, with accuracy assessment metrics derived from test samples.

The script calculates land surface temperature in Celsius from Landsat 8 thermal band ST_B10 using a radiance-to-temperature conversion formula, computes the median temperature over 2020–2021, and extracts mean temperature values for regions in a user-defined study area in Chile.

The script classifies land cover change and regrowth dynamics between 2010 and 2015 using ground-truthed sample points, categorizing them into reference strata for forest, non-forest, degradation, deforestation, and regrowth conditions, then validates map outputs against these references.

The script classifies land cover into three categories—water, vegetation, and urban—using Landsat 8 surface reflectance data from 2019 over the Kumasi region. It trains a Random Forest classifier using 60% of labeled ground control points, validates with the remaining 40%, and outputs a classified land use map along with an accuracy assessment via confusion matrix and overall test accuracy.

The script classifies agricultural land cover using Planet Labs satellite imagery by training a Random Forest model on spectral indices and ground truth samples in Tanzania. It outputs a classified land cover map, training and validation confusion matrices, and sampled pixel values for accuracy assessment.

The script estimates Land Surface Temperature (LST) from a single Landsat 8 image by first computing NDVI to derive fractional vegetation (Fv), then estimating emissivity (EMM), and finally applying a radiative transfer-based formula using brightness temperature (B10) and emissivity. Outputs include NDVI, NDWI, NDBI, Built-up Index (BI), emissivity, and LST layers, all clipped or calculated for the region of interest.

The script classifies land cover into forest, shrubs, agriculture, crater (likely bare soil or disturbed land), and building classes using manually labeled training points, with the output being a supervised classification task based on spectral characteristics from Landsat 5 imagery within a specific region of interest.

The script fills voids in the SRTM elevation data below 3000 meters by merging it with mosaicized ALOS AW3D30 DSM data, producing a gap-filled digital elevation model for regions including Spain, France, Andorra, and Portugal.
task_name: Fill SRTM elevation holes with ALOS DSM

task_description: The script classifies land cover into three categories—vegetation, sea, and urban—using a CART classifier applied to median composite Landsat 8 surface reflectance data within a specified polygon. The output is a classified image map with green for vegetation, blue for sea, and red for urban areas.

The script identifies and classifies vegetation density levels (very sparse, sparse, moderate, dense, very dense) within a specific polygon using median-composited, cloud-masked Landsat 8 surface reflectance data from January 2022, applying NDVI calculated from bands B4 and B5.

The script filters Sentinel-2 Level-1C and Level-2A satellite image collections for images with less than 20% cloud cover, acquired between January and May 2022, over a specific point near Juja, Kenya. It counts the number of images before and after filtering to assess data availability, but does not perform further analysis such as vegetation or land cover assessment.

The script filters the Sentinel-2 satellite image collection to include only images with less than 20% cloud coverage, acquired between January 1, 2022, and May 31, 2022, within the spatial bounds of a specified point geometry. The output is the count (size) of the filtered image collection.
task_name: Filter Sentinel-2 images by cloud cover and date

task_description: The script analyzes Landsat 8 surface reflectance data to compute NDWI over time, derives the percentage of time pixels are wet, and identifies persistent shallow water features (reefs) by thresholding the percent wet image between 25% and 75%, masking out open water and land. Outputs include visualizations of true color composites, NDWI standard deviation, percent wet, wave presence, stack depth, and vectorized reef boundaries.
task_name: Identify reef areas using water frequency

task_description: The script analyzes JRC Global Surface Water data to identify permanent water bodies in Belize using a seasonality threshold and detects areas of new water occurrence between 2018 and 2022 by analyzing the transition year band.
task_name: Identify permanent water and recent water gain

task_description: The script identifies areas where cocoa cultivation overlaps with forest degradation by analyzing a land use map and a degradation map, then quantifies the percentage of cocoa areas affected by degradation between 2000 and 2019.

The script calculates the number of days with clear or water conditions (cfmask ≤ 1) for each pixel by compositing daily mosaics from Landsat surface reflectance data between 2014-01-01 and 2014-12-31, then outputs a raster showing total annual clear observations over a specified region.

The script classifies land cover into urban, vegetation, and water classes using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from a median composite for July 2019. It trains a CART classifier and evaluates a MaxEnt classifier using sample regions from feature collections, producing a classified land cover map and a confusion matrix for accuracy assessment.

The script performs basic operations with Earth Engine data types such as String, Number, List, and Dictionary, focusing on creating and manipulating variables to represent city names and population values. It calculates the sum of populations between Niterói and Rio de Janeiro using both direct addition and EE methods, demonstrating scalar arithmetic in GEE. The primary outputs are printed strings and numbers showing concatenated text, population totals, and list/dictionary queries.

The script analyzes multi-temporal Landsat surface reflectance data from 2014 to 2018 over a coastal region in Florida to derive water-related indices (AWEI, NDWI, MNDWI) and their statistical summaries (min, max, median, percentiles, interval means). It also incorporates terrain (ETOPO1) and long-term surface water occurrence (JRC Global Surface Water) to support hydrological analysis, likely focused on mapping surface water dynamics and identifying persistent vs. seasonal water bodies.
task_name: Analyze water occurrence and elevation in coastal region

task_description: The script assesses riverbank erosion risk in Bangladesh by analyzing temporal changes in water occurrence from the JRC Global Surface Water dataset, computing distance-to-water trends over time, and combining the latest distance map with negative trend values to derive an erosion risk index using normalized difference. Outputs include mapped layers of water extent (2019–2021), distance-to-water evolution, 3- and 6-year trend rates, and composite erosion risk indicators for the Jamuna River region.

The script classifies land cover into vegetation, water, and bare soil in Floresta do Araguaia using a Random Forest classifier applied to a median composite of Landsat 8 imagery from 2018, with training samples collected from three classes.

The script identifies surface water bodies by computing the Modified Normalized Difference Water Index (MNDWI) from Sentinel-2 imagery, applying cloud masking, and analyzing the maximum MNDWI value over a filtered image collection to highlight persistent water areas.

The script identifies and maps the frequency of pea and lentil cultivation over time using annual crop type classification data from AAFC/ACI, aggregating occurrences across years within a specified region in Saskatchewan, Canada.
task_name: Map pea and lentil cultivation frequency

task_description: The script classifies crop areas within a buffered insurance zone in Tanzania using a Random Forest classifier trained on a composite of Sentinel-1 backscatter (VV), NDWI, and GCVI indices. It evaluates classification accuracy with training and validation datasets and outputs a masked crop classification map.
task_name: Classify crop areas using SAR and vegetation indices

task_description: The script extracts monthly total precipitation values from the ERA5 dataset for the period May to September between 1998 and 2021 at a specific point location (−106.56583, 52.06603), clips the images to the point, and computes zonal mean statistics using reduceRegion. It also attempts to extract a time-series list of precipitation values and prints specific May values from 1999 to 2019, although the indexing logic contains an error.

The script classifies land cover types for the year 2021 using Landsat 8 surface reflectance data and a Random Forest classifier trained on user-defined sample regions, producing a classified land cover map with six classes: water, urban, forest, croplands, grass, and barren.

The script identifies the greenest pixel composite based on NDVI from Sentinel-2 imagery between March and May 2018, using cloud-masked images to generate a high-quality NDVI mosaic for vegetation analysis.

The script creates a classified land cover map for the year 2020, focusing on forested areas with over 75% tree cover in 2000, detects water and urban areas from custom classifications, and identifies deforestation in 2020 using Hansen's forest loss data. It combines these layers into a final discrete classification map where values represent different land cover types: forest (1), deforested area (2), urban (3), and water (4), clipped to Peru.
task_name: Map deforestation and land cover change

task_description: The script classifies land cover into three categories (Forest, Water, Soil) in the Islamabad Capital Territory using a CART classifier trained on Landsat-8 TOA reflectance data from 2016. It evaluates classification accuracy with an error matrix and computes the area per land cover class within the region.

The script classifies land cover types in Trinidad and Tobago for 2015 using Landsat 8 surface reflectance data, trained with user-defined regions of interest, and validates the classification accuracy using an error matrix. It outputs a classified land cover map and accuracy assessment metrics including overall accuracy, producer's and consumer's accuracy, and Kappa value.

The script identifies areas where vegetation has significantly declined between 2000 and 2014 by calculating the difference in maximum annual NDVI from Landsat ETM+ data, applying a threshold (>0.5) to highlight strong decreases, and masking non-declining areas. The output is a binary map of significant vegetation loss, clipped to a user-defined area of interest.

The script classifies land cover types using Sentinel-1 GRD data, applying terrain slope correction (volume and surface models), generating temporal statistics (mean, min, max, median, stdDev) for VV and VH polarizations, and training Random Forest classifiers on stratified samples to produce classified land cover maps before and after correction.

The script generates a composite image of temporal statistics (percentiles and ranges) for optical vegetation indices (GCVI, NDWI) from Sentinel-2 and radar backscatter (VV, VH) from Sentinel-1 over an insurance zone in Tanzania, used as predictors for agricultural monitoring or modeling.
task_name: Extract agricultural vegetation indices and radar metrics

task_description: The script creates a land cover classification map for forest and cerrado (savanna) ecosystems in Mato Grosso, Brazil, using a median composite of low-cloud Landsat imagery from 1987, masked by MapBiomas classes 3 (forest formation) and 4 (cerrado), then classified via Random Forest using training samples. The output is a classified image with three categories: forest, cerrado, and other.

The script maps land cover strata (classes 1–4) within a property boundary, excluding an intervention site, using a precomputed 'remapped' classification image. It calculates the area (in m² and ha) per class, prints total Horta area, and computes the percentage of conserved landscape (class 1) relative to the total area, including uncertainty bounds.
task_name: Map land cover strata and calculate area

task_description: The script calculates the number of days with clear or water conditions (cfmask ≤ 1) over a specific region and time period using Landsat surface reflectance data, producing a summed clear observation count image.

The script identifies areas of pea and lentil cultivation by remapping land cover classifications from the AAFC/ACI dataset within a specified geometry, then calculates the frequency of these crops over time by summing binary layers for each year where the land cover corresponds to peas (code 162) or lentils (code 174), producing a cumulative count map.

The script computes the maximum Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) within specific agricultural region boundaries for the year 2013 to 2016 by combining Landsat 8 and Sentinel-2 data. It prioritizes fused Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8 results where available, otherwise falls back to Landsat-only data, then calculates mean and standard deviation of NDVI per year over the respective region geometries.
task_name: Compute maximum NDVI for agricultural regions

task_description: The script models Net Ecosystem Exchange (NEE) of carbon by combining MODIS-derived land surface temperature and emissivity, LAI from a user-provided image, and PAR data to compute photosynthetic active radiation. It calculates intermediate biophysical parameters including Rd (respiration), α (quantum efficiency), Fcsat (light-saturated gross canopy photosynthesis), and PPFD, then applies an exponential light-response model to estimate NEE in µmol/m²/s.
task_name: Model NEE from vegetation and temperature

task_description: The script analyzes surface water dynamics within a watershed using elevation, drainage accumulation, and multiple water-related metrics derived from the JRC Global Surface Water dataset, including total water extent, recurrence, seasonality, and change over time, all clipped to a HydroSHEDS-defined basin.
task_name: Analyze water occurrence and accumulation in watershed

task_description: The script classifies land cover types using multi-temporal Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 optical imagery over the Kyiv region, combining radar backscatter time series with cloud-masked optical composites to train a Random Forest classifier on labeled training data, producing a classified land cover map clipped to the region of interest.

The script applies topographic correction to Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery using the SCSc method, which adjusts for solar illumination variations caused by terrain slope and aspect. It computes illumination conditions (solar zenith, azimuth, slope, aspect) and performs per-pixel correction on optical bands to reduce topographic shadows and enhance surface reflectance consistency.

The script identifies potential water bodies by applying a threshold mask on the Landsat 8 Band 5 (SWIR) reflectance values, analyzing the histogram of B5, smoothing the band with a convolution kernel, and validating the masked result within a region of interest. The output includes a binary water mask derived from B5 reflectance ≤ 0.05, a count of valid pixels in the masked region, and visualizations of the original, smoothed, and masked data.
task_name: Identify water bodies using B5 threshold

task_description: The script classifies forest and water areas around the Ubinas volcano using Landsat 8 surface reflectance data from July to August 2018. It computes NDVI, NDSI, NDWI, NDII, and EVI2 indices, then applies threshold-based rules: pixels with NDVI > 0.44 are classified as forest, and pixels with NDWI > 0.2 and NDVI < -0.1 are classified as water. The final output is a classified image layer where forest is coded as 10, water as 20, and other areas as 0.

The script classifies land cover into four categories (Water, Vegetation, Urban, Barren) using a supervised classification (CART) on Landsat 7 surface reflectance data from 2003 to 2005. It computes the area in square kilometers for each class within a specified region of interest.

The script classifies land cover in Quintana Roo using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from January to June 2019. It trains a Random Forest classifier on labeled training regions (water, non-forest, mangroves, flooded forest, dry forest) and produces a classified map with four classes, evaluating accuracy using a validation set. The output is a classified image and an accuracy assessment.

The script estimates forest degradation in Laos between 2015 and 2019 by combining stratified reference data from CEOSampling with classified map outputs, using a ratio estimator to compute area estimates for different forest types (mixed, dipterocarp, evergreen) based on sampled regions and strata totals.

The script classifies land cover into agriculture, vegetation, and water using supervised classification with Landsat 8 surface reflectance data and training samples. The output is a classified raster map labeled 'Classified'.

The script filters CHIRPS precipitation data for June 2020 within the Maharashtra region of India, computes the maximum precipitation value over the period, clips it to the state boundary, and then extracts the maximum precipitation per district using reduceRegions. The output is a feature collection with maximum precipitation values for each district in Maharashtra.

The script analyzes multi-temporal Landsat surface reflectance data from 1999 to compute water indices (NDWI, MNDWI, AWEI) and combines them with topographic (ETOPO1) and global surface water occurrence (JRC/GSW1_0) datasets to generate a composite for modeling surface water presence. It applies cloud masking, spatial filtering, and statistical reduction (e.g., percentiles, interval means) across the time series to derive robust water presence indicators, particularly focusing on areas within elevation and coastal proximity masks.

The script detects land cover changes using CCDC (Continuous Change Detection and Classification) algorithm on Landsat time series data from 2000 to 2020 over a region in Rondônia, Brazil. It analyzes spectral breakpoints in GREEN, RED, NIR, SWIR1, and SWIR2 bands to identify the timing and probability of changes, then maps the number of detected breaks masked by change probability and year range.

The script calculates the area of cashew cultivation in Cambodian provinces using a binary threshold on a cashew probability image. It compares pixel-based area estimates derived from Earth Engine with reported agricultural statistics for validation across multiple provinces.

The script classifies land cover in Novo Progresso using a random forest classifier trained on labeled samples of vegetation, water, and soil, applied to a median composite of Landsat 8 imagery from 2018.

The script computes a weighted rainfall layer by analyzing multi-scale mean curvature from ALOS DSM data, combining it with WorldClim bio12 and bio16 variables, and applying a slope mask to produce a modified climate surface emphasizing topographic influence on precipitation patterns.
task_name: Analyze mean curvature for terrain weighting

task_description: The script identifies the frequency of water and vegetation presence using a decision tree algorithm applied to cloud-free Landsat 8 surface reflectance data from 2017. Water is detected using MNDWI and EVI thresholds, while vegetation is identified based on EVI, NDVI, and LSWI criteria. The output is a composite showing the annual frequency of water and vegetation occurrence over the region.

The script retrieves the first image from the ESA WorldCover dataset, clips it to the boundary of Colombia, and calculates the total area (in square meters) for each land cover class within the country using pixel area summation. The output is a grouped reduction result listing each land cover class with its corresponding area.

The script generates 500 random point samples within each of 11 predefined pasture geometry regions, assigns a class label (0–10) to each set of points, merges them into a single feature collection, and extracts pixel values from a multi-year composite image (2016–2018) at these points for potential classification or training purposes.
task_name: Generate random samples for pasture classes

task_description: The script calculates Pearson correlation coefficients between various spectral bands, ratios, and vegetation indices (e.g., NDVI, SAVI, EVI) derived from a 2017 satellite image and field-measured forest volume data (VT_900) within modeling polygons in the Laguna Om-Caobas area. The output includes mean values of spectral features per polygon and their correlation with forest volume.
task_name: Analyze spectral indices for forest volume modeling

task_description: The script creates multi-temporal Sentinel-1 SAR composites to analyze surface and vegetation changes over time in Madre de Dios, Peru, using VV and VH polarization backscatter and the Radar Forest Degradation Index (RFDI) derived from co-polarized ratios.

The script filters Sentinel-2 imagery over a specific point in Morocco during May 2017, then selects the least cloudy image based on 'CLOUDY_PIXEL_PERCENTAGE' for further use, printing both the filtered collection and the selected image.

The script analyzes Sentinel-1 SAR backscatter (VH and VV bands) time series to monitor industrial activity at specific automotive manufacturing plants in Europe between 2018 and 2020, with a focus on detecting changes during the 2020 COVID-19 lockdown period by comparing pre-, during, and post-lockdown VV backscatter means.

The script corrects terrain-induced illumination effects on Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery using the SCSc (Sun-Canopy-Sensor corrected) method, producing a median-composited image with improved radiometric accuracy for hilly or mountainous regions.

The script identifies surface water extent in Pune by combining NDVI and NDWI thresholds from Sentinel-2 imagery, masking non-water areas, and converting the result into vector polygons labeled as 'water'. It also calculates the total area of the detected water features.

The script computes the maximum NDVI values from 32-day Landsat composite images for the years 2000 and 2014, then calculates the difference between them to identify areas of significant vegetation decline. It highlights regions where the NDVI in 2000 was more than 0.5 units higher than in 2014, indicating substantial loss in vegetation greenness.

The script calculates a linear transformation of the SWIR1 band mean values to estimate a derived surface property, likely related to surface reflectance or biomass, using a predefined slope and intercept. The result is clipped to the Deramakot boundary and used to compute mean and standard deviation values over that region.

The script classifies forest and non-forest land cover using Sentinel-2 TOA reflectance data, applying cloud and shadow masking, NDVI computation, and a Random Forest classifier trained on sample regions. The output includes classified images for multiple dates and a difference analysis between classifications.

The script classifies urban land cover into seven classes (agua, gramineas, arbustiva, arvore, pavimento, casa, edificio) using a Random Forest classifier applied to a PlanetScope-like satellite image (CBERS-4A fusion). It generates a classified map, computes per-class areas, and evaluates classification accuracy with a confusion matrix, overall accuracy, producer/consumer accuracies, and Kappa coefficient.

The script analyzes the spatial relationship between wildland fires and power grid infrastructure by calculating fire-affected wildland areas and measuring the length of power grids exposed to fire per continent. It outputs tabular data containing continental statistics on wildland fire extent and associated power grid lengths for different buffer distances around fires.
task_name: Assess wildfire impact on power grids

task_description: The script classifies land cover types using median surface reflectance from Landsat 9 and Dynamic World data, training a Random Forest classifier on clipped imagery over a specified region to produce a land cover map with multiple classes including forest, cropland, urban, and water.

The script assesses the state of crops over multiple years (2013–2017) by computing NDVI from both Landsat 8 and Sentinel-2 imagery, fusing the best available data per year, and classifying crop health into three categories: good, poor, and moderate. The output includes classified maps and mean/std statistics across regions.

The script calculates the Chlorophyll Index (CI) using the red and blue bands from Landsat 8 surface reflectance data and generates a quality mosaic based on CI values to highlight vegetation. It also computes a cloud score to filter out cloudy pixels during the compositing process.

The script classifies land and lake areas using NDVI and a Random Forest classifier applied to Sentinel-2 imagery from July to October 2018, producing a classified map based on training polygons within a specified boundary.

The script calculates the difference between daytime and nighttime land surface temperature (LST) from MODIS Terra data on a specific date, computes the mean difference over the Kaza region, classifies pixels into above and below mean categories, and performs variance and pixel count analysis for each class to evaluate within-class variability. It also tests Otsu-like thresholding by comparing the original difference image with the computed within-class variance.

The script processes Landsat 4–8 surface reflectance data over a defined region to compute multiple vegetation and water indices (NDVI, NDWI, MNDWI, AWEI, EVI, LSWI, MSAVI), brightness (SB), water ratio (WRI), and SWIR/NIR bands. It also extracts topographic elevation (from ETOPO1) and surface water occurrence (from JRC Global Surface Water) for each point in a feature collection. The output is a flattened table joining these time-series statistics with static geophysical covariates per location.
task_name: Extract spectral indices and topographic features for land analysis

task_description: The script classifies land cover types using a random forest classifier trained on satellite imagery and reference sample points. It selects the first image from a filtered Landsat collection between mid-2010 and mid-2012 within a specified geometry, uses band values as predictors, and trains the model with labels from 'LC4_ID' in the provided table. The output is a classified raster map where each pixel is assigned a land cover class based on the training data.

The script classifies land cover into five categories (Water, Vegetation, Fallow, Builtup, Crop) using a CART decision tree classifier trained on ground truth points and applied to a median composite of Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery from early 2020. The output is a classified raster map and a confusion matrix for accuracy assessment.

The script prepares a cloud-masked median composite of Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery from 2019, clipped to the Quintana Roo region, using specific optical bands (B2, B3, B4, B8) for visual interpretation and further classification. It loads multiple labeled feature collections (e.g., Manglar, Helecho, SB_Inundable) suggesting the intent is to train or validate a land cover classification model focused on differentiating forest and non-forest vegetation types, particularly subtropical and mangrove forests.

The script calculates NDVI to analyze vegetation conditions in Daan Park and Tianmu Baseball Field in Taipei for the years 1984 and 2021 using Landsat 5 and Landsat 8 surface reflectance data, comparing changes in greenness over time.

The script analyzes vegetation health using NDVI derived from Sentinel-2 imagery within the Barguzinskyi protected area in August 2019, computes maximum NDVI values via reduction, and overlays fire detections from FIRMS for August 2015, providing spatial analysis of vegetation and prior fire occurrence.

The script maps and quantifies land cover classes by renaming classification values from a pre-existing classified image (classified_correct2) into meaningful land cover categories (e.g., Soja, Pastura, trigo), then calculates the area in hectares for each class within a defined study area using pixel count and pixel area multiplication.

The script classifies land cover types (forest, grassland, cropland, sugarcane, core area) in St. Kitts using a Random Forest classifier applied to a Landsat 7 surface reflectance composite from 2008–2011. It trains the model on labeled feature collections, validates accuracy with error matrices, and applies post-classification filtering using connected pixels and focal mode to improve map quality.
task_name: Classify land cover using random forest

task_description: The script classifies land cover types for the year 2005 using Landsat 7 surface reflectance data, training a Random Forest classifier on labeled feature collections (forest, grassland, cropland, sugarcane, core area) and producing a classified land use map with accuracy assessment including error matrix, overall accuracy, Kappa value, and producer/consumer accuracies. It also computes NDVI and identifies high-NDVI regions likely corresponding to dense vegetation such as sugarcane fields.

The script creates a median composite from Sentinel-1 GRD imagery, combining ascending and descending passes, computing mean VV and VH backscatter values, and applying a focal median filter for smoothing. The output is a two-band image where the first band is the mean VV (from both orbits) and the second band is the mean VH (descending only), used for land surface analysis such as agriculture, land cover, or surface moisture monitoring.

The script computes multiple biophysical and thermal parameters including NDVI, EVI, SAVI, LAI, albedo, emissivity, and land surface temperature (LST) from Landsat 5, 7, and 8 surface reflectance data. It applies cloud masking, spectral index calculations, and physical modeling to derive vegetation health and surface energy properties over a specified region and time period.

The script identifies building locations in MecBa, Ethiopia by classifying PlanetScope imagery and remapping classification results to distinguish buildings from non-buildings, producing a binary map of building presence.

The script applies terrain correction and gamma nought normalization to Sentinel-1 GRD data over a specific tile geometry, computing improved backscatter values (gamma0) while correcting for topographic effects such as layover and shadow. It also applies a refined Gamma Map filtering to reduce speckle and outputs the corrected image collection for analysis.
task_name: Apply terrain correction to SAR imagery

task_description: The script creates a binary mask identifying the spatial extent of water bodies by clipping a constant image to the geometry of a FeatureCollection representing Denver's NHD (National Hydrography Dataset) water features, then masks and renames the image to represent water presence.

The script classifies land cover types using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data, computing vegetation indices (NDVI, NDWI, SAVI), and applying a Random Forest classifier trained on user-defined samples. The output is a classified land cover map with accuracy assessment metrics including overall accuracy, kappa coefficient, and confusion matrix.

The script calculates the pixel-wise difference between a user-provided image band and a clipped MODIS MOD09GQ surface reflectance image from January 13, 2017, over a specific geographic region, likely to detect changes or discrepancies in surface reflectance values.

The script filters a satellite image collection by location, date, and cloud cover (less than 20%), then computes the median pixel value across the time series to produce a clean composite image for the specified period and region.

The script calculates annual median surface reflectance from Landsat 8 Collection 1 Tier 1 Surface Reflectance data for a region of interest (shp) from 2013 to 2021, masks clouds and cloud shadows using the pixel_qa band, computes NDVI using near-infrared (B5) and red (B4) bands, and extracts yearly minimum, maximum, and mean NDVI values within the study area. The outputs are printed statistics for each year's NDVI distribution.

The script analyzes surface reflectance and thermal properties from Landsat 8 data over Baringo and Nakuru counties in Kenya between January and April 2020, applying radiometric calibration to derive surface reflectance and land surface temperature for visual interpretation using a false-color composite (SWIR1, NIR, Red).
task_name: Analyze vegetation and land surface properties

task_description: The script performs supervised land cover classification using Random Forest and SVM classifiers on Landsat 8 surface reflectance data. Training samples are defined for five classes—water, urban, forest, agriculture, and vegetation—using polygon geometries. The output is a classified raster map showing spatial distribution of these land cover types, along with accuracy assessment metrics including confusion matrix and overall accuracy for both classifiers.

The script classifies land cover into three categories (TC_Reclass: 3 likely representing a specific land cover class such as urban or deforested areas) using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data, training a Random Forest and CART classifier on sampled regions, and evaluates classification accuracy with validation data. Outputs include classified land cover maps and accuracy assessments.

The script calculates daily NDMI (Normalized Difference Moisture Index) values from Landsat surface reflectance data over forested areas within a specified polygon between March 1, 2018, and December 31, 2018. It masks non-forest pixels using a preprocessed forest mask, mosaics images by day, computes NDMI per image using NIR and SWIR bands, merges them into a single multi-band image, scales and rounds the values, and applies the forest mask to retain only forested areas. The output is a masked, time-composite NDMI dataset focused on forest moisture dynamics.

The script compares two land cover classifications—one generated without spectral indices and another with spectral indices—by extracting classification values at stratified random sample points. It outputs a feature collection of sampled points with classification labels from both models for accuracy assessment or comparison.
task_name: Classify land cover with and without indices

task_description: The script calculates the proportion of pixels with NDVI values greater than 0.3 (scaled to 3000) for each month from January 2015 to December 2019 using MODIS MOD13A1 data. It outputs a monthly composite image collection representing the fraction of valid NDVI observations exceeding the threshold within each month, clipped to a specified geometry.
task_name: Calculate NDVI proportion above threshold by month

task_description: The script performs a supervised land cover classification using Sentinel-2 imagery and training data composed of seven classes (solar, vegetation, urban, bare, home, road, water). It trains a Random Forest classifier on a mosaic of two Sentinel-2 images, then applies the model to classify a third image, producing a thematic map of classified land cover types.

The script estimates Total Suspended Solids (TSS) in water bodies using a band ratio model applied to MODIS MYD09GA surface reflectance data, specifically using the red and green bands. It applies QA-based cloud and land masking, filters for valid observations, and merges with meteorological temperature data from GRIDMET for potential environmental correlation analysis.

The script analyzes dual-polarization Sentinel-1 SAR data (VV and VH) to compute polarization differences and create composite images before and after Hurricane Florence in September 2018. It generates masked layers based on backscatter thresholds to detect potential flooding and inundated areas, and compares them with pre-event conditions. Additionally, it incorporates Sentinel-2 optical imagery to provide multispectral context for land surface analysis during the same period.
task_name: Analyze SAR polarization differences for flood and inundation mapping

task_description: The script identifies water bodies by applying a threshold to NDVI values, creating a binary water mask and masking NDVI pixels below the threshold to highlight non-water areas.
task_name: Identify water bodies using NDVI threshold

task_description: The script analyzes land cover and surface water dynamics by combining ESA WorldCover 2020 land classification with JRC Global Surface Water data to map cropland, built-up areas, and their interaction with permanent and seasonal water extent, occurrence, and seasonality within a user-defined AOI.
task_name: Map cropland and built-up areas with surface water dynamics

task_description: The script calculates NDVI values from Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data over a user-defined area of interest between 2014 and 2020, applies cloud and shadow masking, and generates a time-composited median image clipped to the AOI for vegetation analysis.

The script filters Sentinel-2 surface reflectance images from the past year relative to the current date, selecting those with less than 10% cloud coverage and overlapping a specific point location. The output is an ImageCollection of filtered Sentinel-2 images.
task_name: Filter Sentinel-2 imagery by cloud cover and date

task_description: The script creates mosaicked Sentinel-1 VV and VH polarization images from October 14 to November 27, 2021, clipped to a study area, for analysis of surface structure and moisture, likely supporting land cover or land use classification.

The script calculates per-pixel vegetation proportion (Pv) from NDVI derived from Landsat 8 surface reflectance data, then computes land surface emissivity for thermal bands 10 and 11 (em10 and em11), and finally derives the mean and difference of these emissivities. The primary output is the vegetation proportion (Pv) layer mapped over the AOI.

The script performs supervised land use/land cover classification using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from January to July 2018, applying a cloud-masked image composite over a region of interest (roi). Training and testing samples are drawn from merged feature collections (tree, water, crop, urban), labeled by 'class', and classified using an SVM (libsvm) classifier. The output includes a classified land use map and an accuracy assessment via confusion matrix and overall accuracy.

The script classifies land cover into three categories—water, human-impacted areas, and forest—using a Random Forest classifier trained on Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data. It evaluates classification accuracy with an error matrix and reports overall accuracy, consumer's and producer's accuracy, and kappa coefficient using independent validation samples.

The script identifies non-forested areas in Latin America by combining land cover data from ESA CCI and MODIS with tree cover, loss, and gain layers from the Hansen global forest change dataset. It creates binary masks to exclude water, urban, snow/ice, and barren areas, then defines non-tree areas based on tree cover thresholds and forest change dynamics, producing multiple masked outputs for comparison across different land cover classifications.

The script classifies land cover types using Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-1 data from 2020, training a Random Forest model on sample points within a defined region (Ca), and outputs a classified image map along with accuracy assessments including confusion matrix, overall accuracy, kappa, and variable importance.

The script processes Sentinel-1 GRD SAR data over the Porbandar district in Gujarat, applying calibration to natural units, performing Refined Lee speckle filtering, and converting back to decibels. The output is a filtered time-series of dual-polarized (VV/VH) radar backscatter imagery for January 2020, intended for analysis of surface structural and moisture characteristics.

The script computes the Normalized Difference Built-up Index (NDBI) from median surface reflectance imagery of Landsat 5 after masking clouds and valid pixels, aiming to identify built-up or urban areas within a specified boundary for the year 2001.

The script classifies land cover types in Madagascar using Sentinel-2 imagery and Dynamic World model outputs from October to November 2021, generating a median classified image and a mode-composite mask to identify dominant land cover classes including trees, grass, flooded vegetation, shrub/scrub, and bare ground.

The script generates a multi-band image composite containing minimum, percentiles (10, 25, 50, 75), and standard deviation values for Landsat 8 TOA reflectance bands and derived vegetation indices (NDVI, GNDVI, GRVI, GBVI, EVI, GCVI) over a specified region and time period, used as predictor variables for agricultural monitoring.

The script filters Sentinel-2 imagery for low cloud cover and a specific date range, selects all optical bands (B.*), computes the temporal mean across the image collection, extracts the first image, and calculates per-band mean values both globally over the image and within a specified geometry at 100m scale. It outputs the size of the filtered collection, the global mean image, and the mean value of band B4 within the region.

The script classifies land cover into urban, water, vegetation, and soil classes using a CART classifier applied to surface reflectance bands from Landsat 8. The output is a classified image map with four land cover categories.

The script classifies land cover into four categories—Water, Vegetation, Urban, and Barren—using a supervised classification (CART) on Landsat 8 surface reflectance data from 2015. Training points are merged from user-provided feature collections, and the output includes a classified land cover map and area calculations in square kilometers for each class within the ROI.

The script performs terrain slope correction on Sentinel-1 GRD SAR imagery using SRTM elevation data to produce gamma0 terrain-flattened backscatter values, specifically mosaicking and clipping VV-polarized corrected imagery over a mountainous region in the Alps for improved radar analysis.
task_name: Correct SAR backscatter for slope effects

task_description: The script predicts tree volume (VT_900) in a forested area using a regression model (CART) trained on spectral indices, band ratios, texture features, and reflectance values from a 2017 satellite image. It evaluates the model's accuracy using validation data and generates a classified map of predicted volumes with a legend.
task_name: Predict tree volume using satellite imagery

task_description: The script compares terrain-corrected Sentinel-1 SAR backscatter values (VV, VH) and incidence angle across multiple processing methods (Gamma, SNAP, ISCE, pseudo-RTC) over forested areas. It computes statistical metrics including mean, standard deviation, coefficient of variation (CV), and angular sensitivity (linear fit slope) for each dataset and location, focusing on evaluating RTC consistency and radiometric behavior.

The script generates cloud- and shadow-free median composite images from Landsat 8 Surface Reflectance data for two years (2019 and 2020) over a specific WRS path and row, selecting visible and near-infrared bands to create true-color imagery for visual analysis.

The script assesses the state of crops over multiple years (2013–2017) by computing NDVI from Landsat 8 and Sentinel-2 imagery, selecting the best available data per year, and classifying the condition into three categories: high vegetation (1), low vegetation (2), and intermediate (3). The output includes classified maps and mean/std statistics across regions.

The script identifies flooded areas by analyzing the difference between pre-flood and post-flood Sentinel-1 VH polarization SAR imagery, applying a ratio-based threshold to detect significant backscatter changes indicative of surface water inundation.

The script analyzes the impact of wildfires on human populations by calculating road lengths and population density within buffered wildfire perimeters in Africa, using MODIS land cover, JRC wildfire data, and GPW population density datasets for specific years.

The script analyzes the spatial relationship between annual wildfire perimeters and land cover types (wildlands and forests) across continents, calculating burned areas, population exposure within buffer zones, and summarizing these metrics by continent for multiple years.
task_name: Analyze wildfire impact on wildland and forest areas

task_description: The script calculates a z-score of human modification by comparing local deviations from neighborhood means using the Global Human Modification dataset. It generates a binary mask identifying areas with significantly lower human modification than surrounding regions and attempts to compute a weighted spatial aggregation of quality and distance, though the latter part contains undefined variables and errors.

The script identifies flooded rice fields by applying Otsu thresholding on VH-polarized Sentinel-1 SAR imagery to detect water extent, then masking permanent water and rice-growing areas in Quang Ninh, Vietnam, during a specific flood event in July 2018.

The script classifies land cover types (Bareland, Settlement, Water, Vegetation, Mining) in the Emalahleni area using median-composite Landsat 5 surface reflectance data from 1990 to 1999, calculating spectral indices (NDVI, NDBI, NDWI) and incorporating SRTM DEM for terrain analysis. The output is a stacked image with reflectance bands, indices, and elevation for use in supervised classification training.

The script computes multiple vegetation and soil-adjusted indices (NDVI, SAVI, ARVI, and their variants with green, SWIR1, SWIR2) from a 2020 Landsat image over Quintana Roo, and uses training samples from 2009–2014 field data to create a merged dataset for model training and validation. The primary output is a classified land cover map focused on vegetation analysis using time-series sampled training data.
task_name: Classify vegetation types using spectral indices

task_description: The script identifies and maps surface water extent in the Nhecolândia region using MNDWI derived from atmospherically corrected Landsat 8 SR data, with masking of clouds and cloud shadows, and calculates the total water-covered area in square kilometers during rainy periods.

The script models the seasonal patterns of NDVI using harmonic analysis on Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data for the years 2019 and 2020 over the Katavi region in Tanzania, producing visualizations of phase, amplitude, and vertical shift as RGB composites derived from harmonic coefficients.

The script calculates NDVI from Landsat 8 imagery between May and September 2016, computes mean NDVI over a region centered on a point in Georgia (42.10, 42.76), classifies SRTM elevation into five zones (0–4 corresponding to >1000m intervals), and then computes the mean NDVI grouped by these elevation zones within a 20km buffer around the point.
