The script calculates Burned Area Recovery Ratio (BRR) by comparing Normalized Burn Ratio (NBR) values before and after a fire event, using Landsat surface reflectance data. It computes pre-fire and post-fire NBR means, then evaluates annual recovery from 2007 to 2009 by computing the ratio of recovery in NBR to the initial burn severity.

The script calculates the difference in Normalized Burn Ratio (dNBR) from Landsat 5 surface reflectance data before and after a specified date to detect wildfire-affected areas. It identifies connected components of significantly burned regions (dNBR > 0.1) and labels them for spatial analysis.

The script identifies wheat and rapeseed (youcai) cultivation areas using Sentinel-1 SAR data, specifically the VH polarization band, masked by rice land cover classification from WorldCover and thresholding on backscatter values. Wheat is identified as pixels with VH < -15.5 dB within rice-classified areas, while rapeseed is identified as pixels with VH > -15.5 dB but still above -15 dB in the same masked region.

The script calculates the 5th and 95th percentile values of NDVI from MODIS MOD13A1 data for the year 2010, masked to soybean cultivation areas, to analyze vegetation health and variability within those regions.

The script updates land use and land cover (LULC) maps for Jiangsu, Anhui, Zhejiang, and Shanghai regions by integrating annual water occurrence data from 1992 to 1995. It identifies permanent water bodies using a threshold (>=3 months) from a mode-composited image collection, masks them, and reclassifies the corresponding pixels in the LULC rasters to class 6 (water). The output is a series of corrected LULC images where persistent surface water areas are explicitly mapped for each year.

The script filters a Sentinel-1 Ground Range Detected (GRD) image collection to retain only VV-polarized, IW-mode images from March 1–15, 2015, and masks out pixels with values below -30 dB to remove processing artifacts along image edges. The output is a filtered ImageCollection suitable for further analysis of land surfaces using C-band SAR backscatter.

The script calculates the mean terrestrial water storage anomalies (lwe_thickness_csr) from GRACE satellite data over Kruger National Park (KNP) for the year 2020, providing a spatially averaged time-series reduction of groundwater equivalent water thickness.

The script identifies newly developed built-up areas and newly established vegetation areas by comparing Dynamic World land cover probabilities and Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery from March 2020 and March 2022, using thresholds on built and tree probability bands to detect significant changes.
task_name: Identify new built-up and vegetation areas

task_description: The script calculates the Remote Sensing Ecological Index (RSEI) by combining NDVI, LST, WET, and NDBSI derived from MODIS data. It performs PCA on these indicators to generate a composite ecological index for specific regions over multiple time periods (2001–2021), with outputs including time-series RSEI images and their mean values, used to assess ecological condition changes.

The script applies a classification mask from a user-provided image to identify grassland areas by setting pixels equal to class 30 to zero and masking them out, using MODIS NDVI data within the昭通市 region for analysis.

The script calculates and maps the annual surface water occurrence frequency (in percent) for the year 2010 across the United States using the JRC Global Surface Water dataset. It identifies pixels with at least one observation and computes the proportion of time they were classified as permanent water (water class = 2), then masks zero values and clips the result to the US boundary. Additionally, it computes the total area where water presence is observed at least 60% of the time within the US region.
task_name: Map surface water frequency in US

task_description: The script performs superpixel segmentation using the SNIC algorithm on a Landsat 8 surface reflectance image clipped to a specific village in Yunnan Province, with and without reprojection, to generate segmented regions for fine-scale land cover analysis.

The script selects the least cloudy Landsat 8 surface reflectance image from May to June 2016 over a specified region of interest, then extracts training samples for four land cover classes (urban, water, forest, agriculture) using six spectral bands (B2–B7). The output is a feature collection of labeled training data for supervised land cover classification.

The script analyzes the NDVI distribution for soybean (crop type 3) using MODIS MOD13A1 data from April 22, 2010, to October 1, 2010. It computes maximum and minimum NDVI values at the 95th and 5th percentiles within the soybean-growing region, updates the image with these statistics as properties, and masks the MODIS NDVI data to only include areas classified as soybean. The final output is a masked, scaled NDVI image with associated min/max NDVI metadata.

The script estimates Land Surface Temperature (LST) for the Qinghai region using Landsat 8 TOA and surface reflectance data from June to July 2020, incorporating atmospheric correction with NCEP Reanalysis water vapor data and emissivity modeling based on NDVI and ASTER GED data.

The script calculates a 5-day running mean of 2-meter air temperature from ERA5-Land daily data for 2015, clips it to a defined geographic region (China), converts units from Kelvin to Celsius, and identifies the day of year with the lowest mean temperature during October–December 2015.

The script computes the Cloud Distortion Index (CDI) for Sentinel-2 images over a specific tile (T50TMK) in June 2017, selects the least cloudy 20% of images based on CDI, and generates a composite mean image from bands B7, B8A, and B8. The output is a reduced-image composite representing spectrally consistent surface reflectance with minimal cloud contamination.
task_name: Compute mean spectral index from least cloudy Sentinel-2 images

task_description: The script classifies land cover types using a CART decision tree classifier trained on Landsat-8 surface reflectance data and NLCD 2016 land cover labels, producing a classified land cover map around San Francisco for 2016.

The script masks cloud and cloud shadow pixels from Landsat 8 Surface Reflectance data over a specific region (Yellow River basin) for June 2020, then mosaics the images into a single cloud-cleared composite.

The script classifies land cover types (Buildup, woody cover, grass cover, water, bare surface, agriculture) using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from January to October 2023 by training a classifier with labeled regions of interest and generating a classified image based on spectral bands B2, B3, and B4.

The script calculates long-term average daily precipitation from CHIRPS data (2001–2021) and computes daily precipitation anomalies for each day of the year by comparing individual year composites to the climatological mean, producing cumulative anomaly images over time within a specified region of interest.

The script analyzes land cover characteristics in three distinct regions—near Cusco (AOI), the Ausangate glacier region, and Sincelejo city—using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data. It generates cloud-masked median and maximum composites for visual interpretation and band-specific analysis in RGB and false-color composites, focusing on urban areas, agriculture, vegetation, and snow/ice surfaces.
task_name: Analyze urban and agricultural land cover

task_description: The script identifies potential tea cultivation areas by analyzing percentile thresholds of biophysical indicators (GSL, GUD, GUS, SDPS, SS) derived from an image in a collection. It computes 5th and 95th percentiles within known tea and crop regions, then applies these thresholds spatially to classify suitable areas for tea based on spectral properties.

The script classifies land cover into three categories—water, vegetation, and non-vegetation—using a CART classifier trained on labeled sample points and applied to a cloud-cleared, median-composited Landsat 8 image over a region of interest.

The script classifies land cover for the years 2019 and 2001 using Landsat TOA reflectance data, trains CART and MaxEnt classifiers on labeled regions (water, vegetation, buildings), performs accuracy assessment via error matrices, and computes the difference between the two classified maps to detect land cover change from 2001 to 2019.

The script identifies and masks cloud-covered and shadowed pixels in a Landsat 8 surface reflectance image collection from 2017 over the Matopiba region using pixel QA bands, Fmask, sun angle geometry, and thermal-based dark pixel analysis to improve image quality for further land surface analysis.
task_name: Detect and mask clouds and shadows

task_description: The script processes Sentinel-2 imagery for tile 34TCS in 2016 with strict cloud filtering, masks clouds using QA60, computes NDVI, NDWI, and NDSI indices, and outputs a masked, scaled image collection with these spectral indices for analysis over a specified region.

The script calculates the total area of forest loss and annual forest loss by year in hectares within three specific protected areas—AFDC operational area, Sai Yok National Park, and Erawan National Park—using the Global Forest Change dataset from 2000 to 2020. It outputs total loss in hectares and a dictionary of yearly loss from 2001 to 2020 for each region.

The script fits a double logistic function to time-series LAI data using the Levenberg-Marquardt optimization algorithm to estimate phenological parameters such as greenup and dormancy timing, amplitude, and growth rates. The output is an array image containing optimized model parameters for vegetation dynamics modeling.

The script classifies land cover types using a CART classifier trained on ground truth points and applied to a cloud-cleared, mean Landsat 7 surface reflectance composite from August to October 2003, clipped to the MatNorth region.

The script identifies burned areas by calculating the Normalized Burn Ratio (NBR) from multispectral imagery, applying cloud and shadow masking, detecting pixels with NBR values below -0.23 (or -0.1 for later years), and performing superpixel segmentation (SNIC) to group binary burn detections into spatially contiguous regions. The output is a binary raster indicating potential burned areas, refined through region grouping.

The script processes a time series of EVI images to detect and smooth vegetation dynamics specific to rice cultivation by applying temporal filtering, masking, and correction algorithms based on dasarian (10-day) composites from 2021–2022. It outputs a smoothed EVI time series optimized for identifying rice cropping patterns.

The script processes MODIS surface reflectance data to compute and temporally smooth the Normalized Difference Moisture Index (NDMI) specifically over corn cultivation areas identified by a feature with index 295. It applies cloud, shadow, and snow masking, computes NDMI using NIR and SWIR1 bands, clips to a regional boundary (shp), performs linear interpolation, and applies Whittaker smoothing to produce a clean, continuous NDMI time series for 2019.
task_name: Smooth NDMI time series for corn areas

task_description: The script extracts 2-meter temperature data from the ERA5 monthly climate dataset for the period April to October between 2014 and 2020, converts it from Kelvin to Celsius, and samples the pixel values within administrative regions (MEGYE) of Hungary using a mask and reprojection. The output is a feature collection of point samples with temperature time series per region.

The script identifies flooded areas by comparing Sentinel-1 SAR imagery before and after a flood event in Greater Accra, using VH polarization and applying speckle filtering (Refined Lee) to improve image quality. Outputs are mosaicked and clipped radar intensity images before and after the flood for visual and analytical comparison.

The script identifies persistent water bodies by analyzing the maximum VH polarization backscatter from Sentinel-1 SAR data, applying morphological operations (erosion and dilation) to refine land-water separation, and removing small isolated segments based on size thresholds.
task_name: Identify water bodies using VH backscatter

task_description: The script extracts a time series of multiple vegetation and land surface indices (including NDVI, kNDVI, EVI, NDMI, PSRI, NIRv, RENDVI, NVIA, SMMI, NDDI, NDWI, NDDI2, BSI11, BSI12) from Sentinel-2 data for a specific field (ID: 20086852) in 2022, using predefined dates between March 1 and October 1. The output is a CSV file containing daily values, with missing dates filled as 100, representing the mean index value over the field geometry.

The script classifies land cover types using a CART decision tree model trained on Landsat 8 TOA reflectance bands and MODIS MCD12Q1 Land Cover Type data. The output is a classified image map where each pixel is assigned a land cover class based on the training from MODIS-derived labels.

The script identifies vegetation areas within the Teochew Cemetery in Bangkok using NDVI analysis from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data between 2021-01-01 and 2022-06-06, calculates the total vegetation-covered area in square kilometers, and prints it alongside a scaled value based on a custom multiplier.

The script extracts land cover class values and names from the CORINE Land Cover dataset for the year 2000, then computes the fractional coverage (as percentages) of each of the 44 land cover classes by reprojecting and aggregating the data to match MODIS resolution and projection. It creates a multi-band image where each band represents the areal proportion of a specific land cover class within MODIS pixels, focused on a defined geographic region (FORSEE).

The script analyzes optical and radar satellite imagery from August to September 2020 to monitor land surface changes, using Sentinel-2 (B2, B3, B4), Landsat 8 (B3, B4, B5), and Sentinel-1 VV polarization data. It generates cloud-filtered composite images for visual interpretation of surface dynamics over time.

The script classifies snow cover in North Sikkim using Sentinel-2 imagery and a supervised Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier. Training data is derived from user-defined regions of ice and non-ice, and the final output is a binary snow cover map with accuracy assessment via confusion matrices for training, testing, and total datasets.

The script estimates daily total NOx emissions from agricultural fires by combining MODIS FRP data, crop dominance maps, and emission factors derived from land cover and crop area data. It outputs a time series of daily NOx emissions aggregated over a boundary for specific days in December 2015.
task_name: Estimate daily NOx emissions from crop fires

task_description: The script identifies areas of significant vegetation decline in March 2019 by comparing the greenest pixel composite NDVI of that year to a multi-year (2016–2018) mean and standard deviation, classifying pixels into zones based on deviations from historical norms.

The script evaluates the accuracy of deforestation detection by comparing satellite-derived high-frequency disturbance alerts (from FreqH) against manually validated deforestation alerts within a specific grid cell. It performs spatial intersection analysis between buffered detected alerts and validated alerts, computes an error matrix, and derives accuracy metrics including precision, recall, F-score, and user/producer accuracies.
task_name: Identify deforestation alerts using frequency data

task_description: The script processes a time series of EVI images from 2021 to 2022 over agricultural areas, specifically targeting rice cultivation dynamics. It applies multiple correction and smoothing steps using phenological metrics (min, max, mean, median EVI), masking with paddy fields, and temporal segmentation based on dasarian periods (10-day intervals). The output is a smoothed and corrected EVI time series optimized for detecting crop growth patterns in irrigated lowland agriculture.
task_name: Smooth EVI time series for rice monitoring

task_description: The script evaluates 30-day cumulative precipitation and counts days with maximum temperature above 31°C to identify periods meeting drought-like conditions: less than 10mm of total precipitation over 30 days and at least 15 days with daily max temperature exceeding 31°C. It outputs a binary image indicating where both conditions are met, focusing on a specific time window in 2018.
task_name: Identify dry periods with high temperature

task_description: The script classifies land cover types (Tree, Herbaceous, Concrete, Water, Buildings) in the Irvington neighborhood using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data and a CART classifier trained on manually labeled sample points collected in 2023.

The script identifies and evaluates forest change detections from the CODED-at algorithm by comparing satellite-derived change patches with ground-validated alerts within a specific grid cell (CHSA) over a given fortnight. It performs spatial filtering based on object size, generates vector polygons for detected changes, buffers them and validated points, computes spatial overlaps, and produces a confusion matrix to assess detection accuracy, including precision, recall, and F-score.
task_name: Identify forest change alerts using CODED

task_description: The script processes MODIS surface reflectance data to compute multiple vegetation and water indices, applies cloud masking and linear interpolation over time, and specifically analyzes the temporal profile of EVI2 over three corn classes (early, full, late season) within a defined region (NYQ with CHANGE=9). It extracts mean EVI2 values over these areas through time to support phenological analysis of corn growth stages.
task_name: Analyze corn phenology using EVI2 time series

task_description: The script classifies land cover into water, nonvegetation, and vegetation using Landsat 5 surface reflectance data and a Random Forest classifier trained on user-provided labeled regions. It also computes vegetation indices (NDVI, EVI, SAVI) and analyzes temporal NDVI trends from 1987 to 2000.
task_name: Classify land cover using Random Forest

task_description: The script creates a multi-temporal composite of Sentinel-1 VV polarization SAR images from June 2020 to March 2021 over the Nilanga region in India, specifically targeting descending IW mode acquisitions. The output is a 24-band image where each band represents the median VV backscatter during a ~3–4 day window, used for monitoring temporal changes in surface structure, likely for agricultural phenology analysis—particularly wheat cultivation.
task_name: Monitor wheat growth using VV backscatter

task_description: The script classifies land cover types using a Random Forest model trained on labeled sample points, with the classification applied to a composite image masked to non-forest areas. The output includes a classified land cover map, variable importance analysis for feature bands, and accuracy assessment via confusion matrix.

The script analyzes vegetation health, water content, and moisture stress using Sentinel-2 data by computing NDVI, NDWI, and NMDI indices. It generates a composite image with mean NMDI, VCI (Vegetation Condition Index), and mean NDWI as outputs for the specified time period and region.

The script identifies flooded areas and soil moisture conditions by analyzing Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data using NDVI, NDWI, and B11 (SWIR) thresholds, combined with land cover and cloud-masked classifications to produce a flood extent map for a specific date in 2018.
task_name: Identify flooded areas using spectral indices

task_description: The script identifies corn cultivation areas by isolating pixels with a value of 10 in the gyep2021 land cover image, then applying a neighborhood count filter over a 3x3 pixel window to detect fully surrounded 3x3 blocks of corn pixels, resulting in a masked output where only such compact corn patches remain.
task_name: Identify corn fields using pixel neighborhood

task_description: The script monitors rice crop growth over the planting season by analyzing time-series Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI) values derived from Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8 satellite data, applying compositing, masking, and moving average smoothing techniques to generate phenological profiles for agricultural monitoring.

The script predicts surface water frequency (SWF) using a random forest classifier trained on Landsat-derived spectral indices and DSWE classes, producing a time series of SWF maps and a median inundation map for a region in Canada between 2015 and 2020.

The script identifies water bodies within a region of interest by computing NDWI (McFeeters), NDWI (Gao), and MNDWI (Xu) indices from a median composite of Sentinel-2 imagery collected in December 2020. The outputs are three thematic layers highlighting surface water features based on different spectral band combinations.
task_name: Extract water bodies using NDWI and MNDWI

task_description: The script calculates the precipitation anomaly for April 2022 by comparing it to the long-term average of March-April-May precipitation from 2000 to 2021, using summed images from March, April, and May each year. It outputs three rasters: the anomaly (2022 minus mean), the total precipitation for March-May 2022, and the percentage of 2022 precipitation relative to the historical average, all clipped to a region of interest.

The script calculates the frequency of precipitation events exceeding four thresholds (0.1 mm/day, 1 mm/day, 10 mm/day, and 25 mm/day) over 4-day intervals for each year from 2003 to 2021, aggregating results at sample locations. It outputs CSV files containing mean values of binary occurrence indicators per 4-day window across the year for each threshold level.

The script applies the Refined Lee speckle filter to VV-polarized Sentinel-1 GRD imagery in decibel scale, converting it to natural units, performing adaptive filtering to reduce noise while preserving edges, and then converting back to dB. The output is a filtered ImageCollection of SAR images suitable for high-quality land surface monitoring, particularly for agriculture, vegetation, or surface moisture analysis.
task_name: Filter SAR imagery for surface analysis

task_description: The script creates a multi-temporal composite of Sentinel-1 SAR imagery over the Nilanga region, using VV and VH polarization bands from descending IW mode acquisitions between June 2020 and March 2021. The output is a 24-layer image where each layer represents the median backscatter (VV and VH) for a specific 3-day period, enabling analysis of temporal changes in surface structure and moisture, particularly for agricultural monitoring.

The script computes the greenest pixel composite of MODIS NDVI over a specific period, calculates long-term mean and standard deviation of historical greenest NDVI values, and classifies drought severity in 2018 by comparing that year's greenness to historical baselines. It outputs a classified raster map showing levels of drought stress and regions with non-cropland or masked crop types.

The script identifies waterlogged areas and wetland inundation by analyzing Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data, computing multiple spectral indices (NDVI, NDWI, NDMI, NDSI, NMDI), and applying rule-based classification to detect zones of open standing water, saturated soil, and flooded vegetation within a region of interest. It outputs two thematic maps: one based on multi-index thresholds ('zones') and another using a specialized Water in Wetlands (WIW) index ('WIWzones'), both masked for clouds and terrain artifacts.
task_name: Identify waterlogged areas using spectral indices

task_description: The script computes the median NDVI from MODIS MOD13Q1 imagery between March 2000 and May 2015 over the Democratic Republic of Congo, and extracts NDVI values at randomly generated points within a specified rectangle, adding a date attribute to each point for time-series analysis.
task_name: Extract NDVI time series at random points

task_description: The script analyzes NDVI time series from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data to monitor vegetation dynamics over rice fields in Kabupaten Serang during 2019. It generates maximum NDVI composites at ten-day, fifteen-day, and monthly intervals, along with a median RGB composite for visual interpretation, all clipped to the administrative boundary of Kabupaten Serang.

The script calculates the accumulated sum of daily mean 2m air temperature (converted from Kelvin to Celsius and masked below 10°C) over China for the year 2019, representing a thermal accumulation metric potentially used in agricultural or ecological studies.

The script creates a pansharpened RGB image by combining the high-resolution panchromatic band (B8) of Landsat 8 with the hue and saturation components of the visible-infrared bands (B7, B6, B4), resulting in a higher spatial resolution color composite image over a user-defined area of interest.

The script identifies wheat cultivation areas in Cangzhou using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data and NDVI analysis from April to May 2022. It generates a time-series composite using geomedian aggregation, masks clouds and water, clips to the region of interest, and performs stratified sampling on classified wheat areas for validation or modeling input.

The script computes the greenest pixel composite of NDVI from MODIS Terra and Aqua 250m data for August, then compares the target year's greenness to a multi-year reference mean and standard deviation to classify drought severity into eight categories, including non-supportable areas, resulting in a spatial drought zonation map.

The script calculates Tasseled Cap transformation components (brightness, vegetation, wetness) from surface reflectance values of Landsat 8 TOA imagery after masking clouds and cloud shadows, then computes median composite and regional statistics over an AOI for the year 2022.

The script computes mean VV polarization SAR backscatter from descending and ascending orbits over a watershed during three seasonal periods in 2016, generating multi-temporal composite images to analyze surface moisture or structural changes across spring and summer.

The script identifies the bluest county in Pennsylvania by computing a greenest pixel composite based on NDWI (Normalized Difference Water Index) from NAIP imagery between 2017 and 2018, then calculates mean NDWI values per county to determine the water-richest and water-poorest counties.

The script computes the greenest pixel composite of MODIS NDVI from both Terra and Aqua satellites for a specific day range across multiple years, calculates the long-term mean and standard deviation of these composites, and compares the 2017 greenest NDVI to this baseline. It then classifies drought severity into eight categories based on deviations from the mean, incorporating land cover and water body masks, and outputs a spatial map of drought conditions.

The script analyzes vegetation health in Zaveh County during winter 2020–2021 using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data, computing a median composite and generating an NDVI time series with spatial averaging over the region.

The script performs supervised land cover classification using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from August to December 2020 over a user-defined region of interest (PurbaBDN). Training and validation samples are collected from manually labeled polygons representing four classes: water, urban (city), forest, and other (likely agriculture or bare land), with classification performed using a CART decision tree classifier. The output is a classified land cover map and an accuracy assessment including an error matrix and overall accuracy.

The script generates a median surface reflectance composite from Landsat 5 SR data, applies topographic correction using SRTM DEM and illumination modeling (SCSc method), computes NDVI and BSI indices, and derives per-pixel maximum, mean, and standard deviation statistics for NDVI and BSI over the time series. Final outputs include a multi-band image asset with reflectance bands, NDVI, BSI, and their statistical summaries clipped to the Borkena region.
task_name: Generate surface reflectance composite with terrain-corrected vegetation and bare soil indices

task_description: The script identifies wheat cultivation areas using NDVI time series analysis from Sentinel-2 data between April and July 2022, applying cloud-masked composites and temporal smoothing to detect vegetation patterns characteristic of wheat growth in the Cangzhou region.

The script performs Principal Component Analysis (PCA) on a cloud-masked, NDVI-enhanced Landsat 8 surface reflectance image collection over the Bac_Can watershed, computing and returning the first principal component (PC1) for each image to highlight dominant spatial patterns in multispectral data.
task_name: Extract PCA component from Landsat imagery

task_description: The script processes a collection of EVI images by correcting anomalies, smoothing noise, and applying iterative filtering based on temporal patterns and thresholds. It specifically targets rice cultivation areas (implied by 'sawah') using multi-temporal EVI statistics (Max, Min, Mean, Med) and outputs a corrected and smoothed EVI time series for the planting season from dasarian September 2020 to October 2021.
task_name: Correct and smooth EVI time series

task_description: The script retrieves the top-of-atmosphere (TOA) reflectance image with the least cloud cover from a specified date range and geographic region, selecting visible and near-infrared spectral bands for further analysis.
task_name: Extract TOA reflectance with minimal clouds

task_description: The script estimates Land Surface Temperature (LST) from Landsat 8 Surface Reflectance data using NDVI, fractional vegetation cover, and emissivity modeling, with a focus on temporal analysis through charting LST time series over a specified geometry.

The script calculates the maximum NDVI value from a 10-day composite PROBAV surface reflectance dataset for August 2018, using NIR and RED bands, clipped to a region 'mo', resulting in a single-band image representing peak vegetation greenness for that month.

The script identifies and segments vegetated areas within a boundary using NDVI derived from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data, applying an Otsu thresholding method on a specified region (largeshrubarea) to distinguish vegetation cover, and outputs the segmented binary vegetation map along with pixel statistics.

The script computes the greenest pixel composite of NDVI from MODIS 250m and 1km data for specific days in a year, then compares the 2012 greenest NDVI with a multi-year mean and standard deviation (2004–2006, 2008, 2010) to classify zones of vegetation change, excluding water bodies using a mask. The output is a classified raster map indicating areas of significant decline, moderate decline, stable, above-normal, and much-above-normal vegetation conditions.

The script classifies flooded areas by training a CART classifier on median-reduced Sentinel-1 VH and VV backscatter values, using manually labeled wet and dry points, and applies a flood probability mask to refine the output.

The script analyzes vegetation health using NDVI and EVI from MODIS, along with evapotranspiration (ET) and precipitation (CHIRPS), over a specific region between October 2019 and May 2020. It computes cumulative ET and rainfall, masks them using an NDVI image, converts ET to a scaled integer format, and generates a quality mosaic of EVI and DayOfYear. Outputs include layered visualizations of NDVI in January and March, accumulated precipitation, raw and converted ET, and the MODIS EVI-DOY composite.

The script identifies permanent surface water areas by calculating the Modified Normalized Difference Water Index (MNDWI) using the Green and SWIR bands from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data over a specified geometry for the year 2020, then masks pixels below a threshold (MNDWI >= 0.0) to extract water bodies and computes the total water area in square kilometers.

The script classifies land cover types in the Irvington area using a CART classifier trained on Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data, with training samples derived from manually labeled points. The output is a classified land cover map based on spectral signatures from selected Sentinel-2 bands.

The script identifies rice cultivation areas by analyzing time-series EVI composites from Sentinel-2 and Landsat (5,7,8,9) data over the 2021–2022 planting season, applying masking, resampling, and quality mosaicking to detect vegetation dynamics specific to paddy fields in Kabupaten Serang.
task_name: Detect rice cultivation using EVI time series

task_description: The script calculates the total area of forest loss and annual forest loss distribution from 2000 to 2020 within two specific administrative areas in Thailand using the Hansen Global Forest Change dataset. It outputs the total forest loss in hectares and a yearly breakdown of forest loss by calendar year.
task_name: Analyze forest loss area and year distribution

task_description: The script analyzes interannual variations in cropland NDVI from MODIS data (2014–2021), masked by annual cropland maps, computes a long-term mean and standard deviation at coarse resolution using reduceResolution, and calculates yearly deviations from the mean to assess vegetation dynamics and stability in agricultural areas.

The script classifies land cover into six classes (urban, dense forest, water, moderate forest, degraded forest, agriculture) using a Random Forest classifier applied to Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data, with EVI and NDVI as derived spectral indices. The output is a classified raster map of land cover types.

The script calculates Land Surface Temperature (LST) for Uganda using Landsat 8 Collection 2 Level 2 data from 2018. It applies radiometric scaling to surface reflectance and brightness temperature bands, computes NDVI, derives vegetation fraction (Fv), estimates emissivity (EM), and finally computes LST using a split-window approximation via a thermal radiation expression. The output is a median composite image of LST over Uganda with a visual palette applied.

The script analyzes vegetation and water conditions by computing FDI, NDVI, and NDWI from Sentinel-2 data, combined with SAR backscatter (VV, VH) and ratio from Sentinel-1, focusing on dates matching ground observations in Tokushima. The output is a matched, cloud-masked, mosaicked ImageCollection with key spectral and radar bands for multi-temporal analysis.

The script classifies land cover into five categories—Hyacinth, Vegetation, Water, Built-up, and Bare Land—using Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data and a Random Forest classifier trained on user-defined training regions. The output includes a classified land cover map and a confusion matrix for accuracy assessment.

The script maps rice cultivation areas by analyzing time-series EVI from Sentinel-2, Landsat 8, Landsat 9, and Landsat 7 data over the 2021–2022 growing season in Kabupaten Serang. It applies masking, compositing, noise correction, and temporal smoothing to generate a clean EVI time series for agricultural monitoring.

The script classifies land cover types in Shenzhen using Landsat 5 TM imagery from 1986 by computing spectral indices (MNDWI, NDBI, NDVI, RVI, DVI) and applying a Random Forest classifier trained on labeled sample regions. The output includes a classified land cover map, confusion matrix, overall accuracy, and kappa coefficient for validation.

The script processes Sentinel-1 GRD imagery by applying terrain correction using SRTM DEM and a refined Lee filter to reduce speckle noise, producing corrected VV and VH backscatter images along with derived indices such as the VV/VH ratio, local incidence angle, and layover/shadow masks for October 2020.
task_name: Apply terrain correction and refined Lee filtering to Sentinel-1 SAR data

task_description: The script classifies land cover types using Sentinel-2 imagery from 2020, computing multiple spectral indices (NDVI, MNDWI, NDWI_McF, NDWI_Gao) and applying a Random Forest classifier trained on labeled sample regions for classes including water, urban, wetland, vegetation, bare soil, and cropland, producing a classified land cover map.

The script analyzes the cumulative NDVI anomaly over time by applying quality masking and temporal accumulation on MODIS MOD09Q1 surface reflectance data from April to October 2018, producing a time series of masked NDVI images and computing their cumulative sum for vegetation dynamics monitoring.

The script estimates dry biomass (kg/m^2) by combining Sentinel-1 SAR data (VV, VH polarizations) and Sentinel-2 multispectral data to derive vegetation indices (NDVI, LAI, FAPAR) and crop water content (CWC), then models dry biomass using a threshold-based formula applied to these variables over a specified region of interest.
task_name: Estimate dry biomass in agricultural areas

task_description: The script identifies anomalous vegetation conditions in 2018 by comparing the greenest pixel composite of MODIS NDWI from January to March 2018 against a multi-year baseline (2004–2016), classifying areas into deviation categories based on mean and standard deviation, while excluding non-vegetated and built-up areas using land cover masks.

The script identifies corn cultivation areas in Hungary for the year 2015 using TNDVI and MODIS data, applying masking and classification techniques to isolate maize fields from satellite imagery and validate them against agricultural parcel data with damage claims.

The script evaluates the classification accuracy of soybean areas in two different land cover datasets (before and after adjustment) by comparing pixel classifications within sampled regions intersecting a boundary. It calculates and prints the precision (proportion of correctly classified soybean pixels) for both the original and changed classification maps, and estimates the total area of soybean cultivation in acres.

The script filters Sentinel-1 C-band SAR imagery from June to November 2019 within the LNKOMA region, selecting images with less than 30% cloudy pixel percentage, and prints the resulting image collection for inspection.
task_name: Filter Sentinel-1 imagery by cloud cover and date

task_description: The script computes the maximum NDVI value over multiple 16-day periods in August across years 2004–2018 using MODIS 250m and 500m data, applies cloud and water masking, and generates a difference map between the greenest pixel composite of 2018 and the mean of reference years (2004, 2005, 2006, 2008, 2010, 2014, 2015, 2016) to assess vegetation change.

The script analyzes 30-day cumulative precipitation and temperature data to identify areas where precipitation is below 10mm and below 25mm combined with high temperatures (above 31°C) over a specific period. It outputs two maximum occurrence maps: one for the 10mm precipitation threshold and another for the combined 25mm precipitation and 31°C temperature condition, both clipped to a region of interest. Additionally, it filters agricultural damage claims related to drought for corn fields in 2018.
task_name: Identify drought conditions with precipitation and temperature thresholds

task_description: The script identifies corn cultivation areas in Huantai using time-series Sentinel-2 NDVI, MNDWI, and LSWI data from January to July 2022, applying phenological thresholds and growing season length filtering based on 75th percentile NDVI values.

The script identifies cloud-free Sentinel-2 image mosaics over an agricultural stratum in Austria between August 1–20, 2020, filters them by tile coverage (greater than 90%), and calculates the spatial coverage of valid pixels for each mosaic to ensure high data availability for land cover analysis.

The script identifies the largest contiguous water body within a specified polygon by applying a water mask from Landsat 8 surface reflectance data collected in January 2017, then computes its area, perimeter, and shape density index (SDI), returning the largest water feature as a vector.

The script identifies maize (kukorica) cultivation areas in 2021 using NDVI analysis from Sentinel-2 data, reprojects the mask to MODIS grid for consistency, and samples kNDVI and NDVI values within a buffered polygon (geometry3) to analyze temporal vegetation patterns via charted time series at random points.

The script identifies flood extent by analyzing changes in SAR backscatter from Sentinel-1 data during and before a flood event, combining hydrobasin data, forest cover, and multi-temporal radar statistics to mask and refine the flooded areas. The output includes a binary flood extent map and catchment-level flood magnitude.

The script calculates the greenest pixel composite of NDVI from MODIS Terra and Aqua (MOD09GQ/MYD09GQ) for a specific period, computes long-term mean and standard deviation of historical greenest NDVI values (2004–2016), and compares 2020's greenest NDVI against this baseline to classify drought severity levels. It integrates land use masks (non-supportable areas, cropland masks) to refine output zones. The final output is a classified raster map with 10 categories ranging from 'No data' to 'Much better than average', including agricultural exclusion zones.

The script calculates per-band black-sky and white-sky albedo composites for all seven Landsat 8 OLI bands, then computes a weighted sum of band-specific albedo values to derive a final composite albedo index named 'albedoSUM' normalized by a total weight factor and divided by 1000. The output includes individual albedo layers for each band and the final aggregated albedo layer.
task_name: Compute weighted albedo from BSA and WSA bands

task_description: The script identifies and analyzes corn cultivation areas (coded as value 10 in gyep images) over 2014–2020 by computing kernel NDVI (kNDVI) from MODIS surface reflectance data, reprojecting to a coarser grid for consistency, and comparing annual kNDVI values against a long-term mean to detect deviations. Outputs include masked kNDVI images for each year over corn areas, CMG-gridded kNDVI means, standard deviations, and interannual difference maps.

The script identifies burned areas by computing multiple spectral indices (NDVI, NBR, NBR2, NDMI, MIRBI, SAVI, BAI, GEMI) from Landsat 8 surface reflectance data and classifying them using a Random Forest model trained on fire-affected and non-fire regions. The output includes probability-based classification maps of burn scars.
task_name: Identify burned areas using spectral indices

task_description: The script monitors rice cultivation dynamics in Kabupaten Serang by analyzing time-series EVI from Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8 data, applying masking, compositing, correction, and smoothing methods to generate a phenologically consistent vegetation index time series for agricultural monitoring.

The script calculates NDVI from surface reflectance data of Landsat 8, then computes the standard deviation of NDVI in a 7-pixel radius circular neighborhood to analyze spatial texture and variability of vegetation in a specific region in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) for the year 2016.
The script analyzes NDVI values over rice fields in Serang Regency using atmospherically corrected Sentinel-2 imagery from 2018, applying cloud masking and spatial clipping to the region of interest.

The script classifies land cover into Water, Grassland, Woodland, Forest, Rock outcrop, and Cropland using a CART classifier applied to surface reflectance bands from Landsat imagery within the MatNorth region, producing a classified image with distinct color-coded land cover categories.

The script analyzes the temporal NDVI profiles from MODIS for different land cover types (P.Denso, P.Ralo, Cultivo_verano, Cultivo_invierno, pradera) during 2016–2017, using randomly sampled points from a feature collection to extract time series data.
task_name: Analyze NDVI temporal patterns by land cover type

task_description: The script identifies snow-covered areas using Sentinel-2 imagery from June 2019 by calculating the normalized difference snow index (NDSI) based on B3 and B11 bands, applying a threshold (>0.4), and computing the area of detected snow within a polygon.

The script identifies corn fields affected by drought in Hungary between May 2018 and November 2019 using Sentinel-2 NDVI time series analysis. It filters agricultural damage reports for specific corn types and drought events, computes pre- and post-damage NDVI values from cloud-masked Sentinel-2 imagery, and determines whether fields were likely harvested based on low post-event NDVI thresholds.

The script calculates the difference in Normalized Burn Ratio (dNBR) between two Landsat 8 images acquired before and after a potential fire event in July 2016 to assess burn severity. It also processes Landsat 5 and 7 surface reflectance collections for median compositing, likely for comparative land surface analysis over time.

The script compares mean surface reflectance in the red, green, and blue bands over a defined region for summer months of 2021 and 2022 using Sentinel-2 data, producing two RGB visualizations clipped to the region of interest.

The script computes multiple vegetation and environmental spectral indices (NDVI, OSAVI, NDRE, GNDVI, TDVI, LCI, NDWI, EVI, PSRI, RVI) from Sentinel-2 imagery over a buffered region of interest, mosaics images by date, and extracts median pixel values within the region for each index across time. Outputs are CSV files containing time-series data of these indices per feature in the region, used for monitoring vegetation condition and land surface dynamics.
task_name: Analyze vegetation health using spectral indices

task_description: The script extracts hourly air temperature at the surface skin level (Tair_f_inst) from the GLDAS NOAH model dataset for a specific time range around the year 2000, focusing on temporal filtering and manipulation of image collection timestamps. It does not perform spatial analysis or generate new derived products beyond subsetting the dataset.

The script retrieves the top-of-atmosphere reflectance image with the least cloud cover between 2020-07-01 and 2020-08-01 over Palo Verde, CA, determines its acquisition timestamp, and extracts the corresponding NLDAS-specific humidity data from one hour prior to the satellite overpass.
task_name: Extract specific humidity at overpass time

task_description: The script processes Sentinel-2 imagery corrected with the SIAC atmospheric correction method, filters it for June–July 2016 over a region containing agricultural fields (specifically corn), and computes zonal statistics (mean values) of selected bands (B2, B3) within 30-meter buffers around sample points. The output is a feature collection where each point contains time-series band values and image metadata from overlapping Sentinel-2 images.
task_name: Extract Sentinel-2 reflectance for buffered points

task_description: The script generates a median true-color composite image using scaled surface reflectance bands 4, 3, and 2 from Landsat 8 OLI sensor data collected between January 1, 2022, and August 16, 2022, clipped to a specified area of interest (aoi).

The script identifies flood extent by calculating Z-scores from Sentinel-1 GRD time series data before and during the flood event, applying thresholds on VV and VH backscatter, and generating a flood map for March 24, 2019, over Beira, Mozambique.

The script calculates the Normalized Burn Ratio (NBR) from Landsat 7 surface reflectance data, identifies potential burned areas by thresholding NBR values below -0.1, and applies image segmentation (SNIC) to group pixels into clusters. It then generates a binary mask of these clusters and analyzes the temporal distribution of minimum NBR values within clustered regions to detect and characterize fire-affected areas over the year 2018.

The script calculates the median VV polarization backscatter from Sentinel-1 GRD data over a specified region and time period, converts it to decibels, and generates a histogram showing the frequency distribution of Sigma naught (dB) values.

The script calculates the area of center pivot irrigation systems in Dundy County, Nebraska, and analyzes the distance from these agricultural fields to major stream networks, identifying proximity patterns and computing average and minimum/maximum distances.
task_name: Analyze center pivot irrigation distance to streams

task_description: The script identifies flood extent by analyzing Sentinel-1 SAR backscatter changes, combining forest cover, hydrobasins, and multi-level thresholded images to model inundation in forested and low-lying areas. It outputs a binary flood extent map, catchment-level event magnitude, and a smoothed mask of flooded regions.
task_name: Identify flood extent using SAR and hydrology data

task_description: The script monitors rice cultivation dynamics by analyzing time-series EVI from Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8 data over Kabupaten Serang, Indonesia, applying masking, compositing, correction, and smoothing methods to generate a smoothed EVI time series at a specific point for phenological analysis.

The script analyzes surface temperature variation in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania by computing the brightness temperature from Landsat 8 Band 10, identifying the hottest areas using a quality mosaic based on NDWI, and calculating deviations from the regional mean temperature within county boundaries.

The script calculates land surface temperature (SST) from Landsat 7 thermal band data using radiative transfer corrections and emissivity parameters, focusing on specific buffered point regions in central Chile.

The script analyzes a time series of EVI from a custom image collection to detect and refine rice cultivation patterns by applying temporal filtering, masking with paddy fields, and correcting anomalies using minimum EVI thresholds and moving averages. The output is a corrected and smoothed image collection representing updated EVI dynamics for the growing season, specifically tailored to rice phenology in the target region.

The script calculates, for each daily ERA5 image between April 10 and October 1, 2018, the sum of total precipitation over the preceding 30 days. It identifies areas where this 30-day cumulative precipitation is less than 10mm and adds this binary condition as a new band to the original precipitation image. The output includes a time-series collection with this derived band and a maximum composite of the 30-day low-precipitation condition across the period, clipped to the region 'mo'.

The script classifies land cover into categories such as water, urban, wetland, vegetation, bare soil, and field using Sentinel-2 imagery from 2020, computing NDWI and applying a Random Forest classifier trained on user-provided sample regions.

The script calculates NDWI using Sentinel-2 bands B11 and B4, and two versions of EVI using bands B8/B4/B2 and B8A/B4/B2, over Vietnam with a 1km buffer, generating time-series image collections of these water and vegetation indices clipped to the region.
task_name: Compute NDWI and EVI for Vietnam

task_description: The script calculates the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) using near-infrared (B5) and red (B4) bands from a single Landsat 8 TOA reflectance image captured on 2019-07-31, with additional filtering of a Landsat 8 collection by date, geometry, and cloud cover for potential time-series analysis, although only one image is ultimately used for NDVI computation.

The script identifies maize (corn) cultivation areas in Central Europe by masking MODIS Terra surface reflectance data with a crop-specific mask (o2015==10) and computes vegetation indices (NDVI, TNDVI, EVI2, kNDVI) over the period 2016–2021. The output is a time-series collection of masked vegetation index images clipped to the target region.

The script classifies tea cultivation areas using Sentinel-2 Level 1-C data, incorporating spectral bands, vegetation indices, and GLCM texture features. It trains a Random Forest classifier on labeled training points and applies it to produce a binary classification map (tea vs non-tea) over a specific region in Turkey.

The script identifies areas of continuous maize cultivation from 2014 to 2020 by analyzing annual maize maps derived from the gyep20XX datasets, masking for maize (class 10), reprojecting to MODIS grid to ensure spatial consistency, and detecting pixels classified as maize in all seven years. The output is a binary map of persistent maize fields and a count of such pixels within a specified region (mo).

The script identifies vegetation health zones for the year 2018 by computing the greenest pixel composite of MODIS NDVI data from DOY 16 to 32, comparing it against a long-term mean and standard deviation of NDVI, and classifying pixels into 10 distinct zones based on deviations from expected vegetation conditions, with additional masking using land use and water/land flags.

The script computes the greenest pixel composite of NDVI from MODIS Terra and Aqua data for specific years, calculates long-term mean and standard deviation of NDVI (2004–2016), and compares 2019 and 2020 conditions against this baseline to classify drought severity levels across time. The output is a categorized raster map showing spatial patterns of drought stress relative to historical norms, including zones of improved vegetation condition and non-eligible agricultural areas.

The script computes a combined index from red-blue and SWIR2-SWIR1 bands, resembling a dual-index analysis for vegetation and surface moisture using median-composited Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data over a specific region, clipped to a polygon in East Africa.

The script calculates the median NDVI within the Lincoln watershed (HRU ID 6803530) using Landsat 8 surface reflectance data from July 1 to August 1, 2020, and computes the mean NDVI value over this area.

The script calculates a soil moisture stress index (gama_sm) by combining surface and root zone soil moisture from GLDAS data, comparing it with permanent wilting point thresholds, and generating a time-averaged moisture stress map. The output is a mean image representing spatial patterns of soil moisture availability relative to plant stress levels over July 2002.

The script calculates and smooths the Radar Vegetation Index (RVI) using VV and VH polarizations from Sentinel-1 GRD data, applying spatial filtering and median smoothing to reduce noise, then computes a mean smoothed RVI image over a specified geometry and time period for vegetation analysis.
task_name: Analyze smoothed RVI from SAR data

task_description: The script analyzes vegetation dynamics over center pivot irrigation systems in Dundy County, Nebraska, using NDVI time series derived from Landsat 7 and 8 surface reflectance data between 2010 and 2015. It generates a clickable map interface to inspect annual NDVI patterns at user-selected points within the center pivots.

The script processes and combines three components—CODEDat (change magnitude), freqH (frequency of change), and deforestation classification (ndfi_clas)—to generate a categorical deforestation alert map (C3Alg) for two regions (CHH and CHSA). The output classifies pixels into high (3), moderate (2), or no (0) deforestation alert levels based on thresholding the summed scores from the input layers.
task_name: Detect deforestation alerts using CODEDat and frequency analysis

task_description: The script classifies land cover types by computing 30-day maximum NDVI composites from Landsat imagery between 2019 and 2021, then trains a Random Forest classifier on these temporal NDVI features using ground truth data to produce a land use/land cover map with validation metrics and variable importance analysis.
task_name: Classify land cover using NDVI time series

task_description: The script computes the median composite of Sentinel-1 GRD imagery, specifically calculating mean VH band values for ascending and descending orbits, mean VV and VH across both orbits, and combining them into a single median image representing multi-orbit, dual-polarization radar backscatter over the period.

The script evaluates the accuracy of satellite-detected deforestation alerts (from CODED algorithm) in the Chaco Semiárido region by comparing them with ground-validated alerts. It generates a confusion matrix to compute precision, recall, and F-score, assessing how well the satellite-derived alerts match the validated ones during a specific fortnight (Q10) in 2021.
task_name: Identify deforestation alerts using satellite data

task_description: The script computes a monthly composite of 10th percentile reflectance from Landsat 7, Landsat 8, and Sentinel-2 imagery over Perm Krai in 2018, then calculates multiple vegetation and moisture indices (NDVI, NBR, SIPI, EVI, RDVI, SRI, MSR, SAVI, OSAVI) for each month to analyze vegetation condition and biophysical properties.

The script maps cocoa cultivation areas and other land cover types (rubber, closed forest, open forest, grass, shrub, built-up, water) in Côte d'Ivoire using high-resolution satellite imagery composites and manually labeled training samples. It integrates JRC radar-optical time series data with reference datasets for classification and analysis.
task_name: Map cocoa and land cover classes

task_description: The script filters a collection 'cl' for the first image between January 1, 2015, and December 31, 2015, within day of year 200 to 210, then clips it to a geometry defined by 'table'. The output is a single clipped image from the filtered temporal and seasonal window.
task_name: Extract image by date and clip

task_description: The script evaluates deforestation detection performance by comparing satellite-derived alerts from the CODED algorithm against manually validated reference alerts within a specific grid cell (147) and quincena (Q11). It computes spatial overlaps using buffered polygons, constructs a confusion matrix, and calculates accuracy metrics including precision, recall (exhaustividad), F-score, and overall accuracy.

The script performs land cover classification using a set of environmental and spectral variables, including elevation, Sentinel-1 SAR bands (VV, VH), Sentinel-2 optical bands (B8A, B9, B11, B12, etc.), bioclimatic variables, texture metrics, and vegetation indices like DIFNDVI and LSWI. It trains multiple classifiers (Naive Bayes, CART, SVM, Gradient Tree Boost, Random Forest) on labeled training points to classify a dataset into 12 land cover classes, primarily focused on forest types (e.g., fir, pine, oak) and non-forest areas. The output is a classified map with accuracy assessment via confusion matrix, overall accuracy, Kappa, user’s and producer’s accuracy, and F-measure based on an independent test point set.
task_name: Classify forest and non-forest land cover

task_description: The script computes the greenest pixel composite of NDVI from MODIS Terra and Aqua data for specific years, calculates long-term mean and standard deviation of historical greenest NDVI, and classifies drought severity in 2020 by comparing it against historical variability. The output is a classified raster map showing levels of drought severity including areas with no data, strongly to slightly drought-affected zones, average conditions, better-than-average vegetation, non-supportable land, and cropland mask (wheat/sunflower).

The script computes 6-year temporally averaged hourly temperature, solar radiation, wind speed, surface pressure, specific humidity, and soil moisture for the top 30cm of soil from ERA5-Land and GLDAS datasets between January 1, 2015, and February 1, 2015, by combining current year data with five prior years' same-day observations. Outputs include time-series ImageCollections mapped to single-band composites per hour, used for climatological baseline modeling.

The script classifies solar panel installations using Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 satellite imagery by training a Random Forest classifier on labeled regions, producing a binary classification map where 'solar' and 'non-solar' areas are distinguished based on spectral and radar features.

The script calculates and compares NDVI values optimized for snow detection using Landsat 8 and Sentinel-2 imagery over the same geographic area and time window, computes their difference, and analyzes the absolute difference through summation and standard deviation reduction. The output includes visualizations of NDVI_snow, NDVI_snow_s2, their difference, and statistical summaries of the discrepancy.

The script computes the span ratio from dual-polarized Sentinel-1 SLC imagery after terrain normalization, speckle filtering, and masking of zero values, combining ascending tracks (paths 44 and 117) over a specific region to generate a time-series of SAR-derived surface scattering metrics.

The script analyzes long-term Leaf Area Index (LAI) trends from 2003 to 2019 over Sichuan, China, using MCD15A3H data. It computes inter-annual LAI changes for each IGBP land cover class (e.g., evergreen needleleaf forest, croplands), applies temporal outlier detection using interquartile range on neighborhood-smoothed LAI residuals, and fills outliers with modeled values based on linear regression. Outputs include corrected LAI images and intermediate statistical layers such as mean, standard deviation, coefficient of variation, and trend significance.
task_name: Analyze LAI trends by land cover type

task_description: The script extracts MODIS surface reflectance data for Togo, specifically selecting bands 1, 3, and 4 to create a true-color composite image from the median of an ImageCollection spanning June 9–13, 2005, clipped to the Togo administrative boundary.

The script evaluates deforestation detection performance by comparing satellite-derived alerts from the CODED algorithm against manually validated reference alerts within a specific grid cell (CHT) for a given fortnight. It computes spatial overlaps using buffered vectorized detections and validations, then generates a confusion matrix to calculate accuracy metrics including precision, recall, F-score, and overall accuracy.

The script calculates the proportion of valid pixel coverage (after cloud masking and clipping) within a specific stratum (STRKOD 33) for Landsat 5 SR data in 2011, returning the non-masked area in km² and the percentage coverage ('tile_cover') for each mosaicked image by date.

The script classifies land cover into four categories—trees (cay), houses (nha), rice fields (ruong), and water (nuoc)—using Landsat 8 surface reflectance data and a Random Forest classifier trained on manually labeled sample points. The output is a classified raster map of Hau Giang province with accuracy assessment metrics including confusion matrix, overall accuracy, and kappa coefficient for both training and validation datasets.

The script identifies cropland areas (class 10) from annual land cover data and analyzes NDVI values from MODIS MOD09Q1 during late August to early September (day of year 24–31) between 2014 and 2020. It reprojects and aggregates the NDVI data to a coarse CMG grid (0.05°), computes long-term mean and standard deviation, and calculates annual deviations from the mean to assess vegetation health variability over time.
task_name: Analyze NDVI trends in cropland areas

task_description: The script processes a time series of EVI images from 2021 to 2022 over agricultural areas, specifically targeting rice cultivation dynamics. It applies multiple stages of filtering and correction including noise masking, temporal smoothing using moving averages with minimum and maximum composites, and iterative correction based on seasonal metrics. The output is a smoothed EVI time series optimized for detecting crop growth patterns in irrigated lowland agriculture.
task_name: Smooth EVI time series for rice monitoring

task_description: The script computes the greenest pixel composite of NDVI from MODIS Terra and Aqua data for specific years, calculates long-term mean and standard deviation of historical greenest NDVI values, and compares 2017 conditions against this baseline to classify drought severity levels across a region. The output is a classified raster map showing zones of drought stress, including categories from severely dry to much better than average, with masking for non-eligible areas.

The script calculates the difference between total tree carrying capacity and actual tree cover in 2000 to estimate forest restoration potential, masking out agricultural and non-vegetated areas using CCI Land Cover data and Hansen tree cover.

The script classifies land cover types (other vegetation, water body, mangrove, building, bare ground) in the Coastal region of Benin using a CART and Maxent classifier trained on Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data from 2019. It outputs a classified LULC map and evaluates model accuracy with a confusion matrix.

The script classifies land cover into categories such as water, urban, wetlands, vegetation, bare soil, and cropland using Sentinel-2 imagery from 2020. It computes NDVI and NDWI indices, trains a Random Forest classifier on sampled regions, and produces a classified land cover map.

The script maps grassland areas using kNDVI derived from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data between 2018 and 2021, masked with annual grassland presence layers (2018–2021) to analyze temporal vegetation dynamics within defined regions of interest.

The script identifies non-vegetated surfaces and buildings within a defined urban area by masking NAIP imagery using NDVI thresholds and reflectance values, then applies this mask to height-above-ground (HAG) data to set non-vegetated areas to zero.

The script classifies land use types (built-up, herbaceous vegetation, forest, water, mine) in Gembloux, Belgium, using a Random Forest classifier trained on Sentinel-2 imagery from May and September 2016. The output is a classified land use map and accuracy assessment via confusion matrix and overall accuracy.

The script calculates the Biophysical Composition Index (BCI) using Tasseled Cap transformation components (brightness, vegetation, wetness) derived from Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data. It normalizes these components and computes BCI as a ratio of transformed brightness and wetness to vegetation, providing an output image and regional statistics (mean, min, max) over the AOI.

The script computes the maximum CO column number density from Sentinel-5P data over a user-defined region (mo) for weekly intervals between September 23, 2019, and October 28, 2019, producing a time-series of weekly maximum carbon monoxide levels, with each image in the collection representing the peak CO concentration for that week.

The script computes multiple spectral indices (NDVI, NDWIg, NDSIg, NDWI, NDMI, BSI, GLAI, PSRI, kNDVI) from Sentinel-2 imagery to analyze vegetation health, moisture, soil brightness, and plant stress over a specific region and time period. The output is a single mean-reduced image composite representing average index values across the selected dates.
task_name: Analyze vegetation and land surface conditions

task_description: The script identifies vegetation anomalies in August 2018 by comparing the greenest pixel composite NDVI of that year with a multi-year reference (2004–2016), computing mean and standard deviation from the reference period, and classifying areas into seven zones based on deviations from expected NDVI values.

The script computes the difference between each digital elevation model (DEM) image and the minimum value across a stack of four DEM images, producing four difference rasters that highlight deviations from the lowest elevation surface.

The script detects vegetation degradation by comparing current NDFI values against a historical 5th percentile baseline from Landsat data, generating binary alert maps where significant drops in NDFI exceed a threshold, specifically within a predefined ecological region and grid cell.

The script analyzes the impact of a cyclone by comparing pre- and post-event Sentinel-1 VV and VH backscatter intensity over a region of interest, generating mean composite images for both polarizations before and after the event to detect surface changes.

The script identifies areas classified as cropland (code 10) in a 2021 land cover dataset, reprojects and thresholds them to a MODIS grid, then analyzes time-series NDVI data from MODIS at these locations aggregated to a climate modeling grid (CMG). It extracts regional statistics for a selected Hungarian county (mKOD), generating pixel samples and computing temporal means of NDVI across the year 2021. The output includes masked NDVI images on cropland, gridded composites at 0.05° resolution, sample points, and per-pixel time series used to compute mean NDVI values by day of year.
task_name: Identify cropland extent using MODIS NDVI

task_description: The script calculates the VH/VV backscatter ratio from Sentinel-1 SAR data over a specified region of interest and uses it to derive a threshold dry biomass value through a linear scaling expression. The outputs include a map of the VH/VV ratio and a mapped threshold dry mass value, both clipped to the region of interest.

The script classifies the magnitude and duration of land surface changes using a precomputed change detection image (BigDelta), reclassifies magnitude into discrete intervals, combines it with duration, computes frequency distribution within Uruguay, and extracts values to vector features. Outputs include classified rasters, pixel counts per class, and regional reduction results.
task_name: Classify land change magnitude and duration

task_description: The script processes a time series of EVI images to detect and correct anomalies in vegetation dynamics over agricultural areas, specifically targeting rice cultivation periods between October 2021 and September 2022. It applies temporal smoothing and correction functions to refine EVI values using dasarian (10-day) composites, with masking applied to paddy fields (sawah), and outputs corrected image collections for analysis.
task_name: Smooth EVI time series for rice monitoring

task_description: The script analyzes changes in coastal vegetation using multispectral and radar satellite data from Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-1, combining optical indices (NDVI, NDWI, FDI) with SAR backscatter (VV, VH, Ratio) over specific field observation dates near Beppu. Outputs include a time-series of co-registered, cloud-masked, and mosaicked multiband images for selected dates, enabling spatiotemporal monitoring of vegetation and water conditions.

The script identifies flood-affected areas by analyzing changes in VH backscatter between pre-flood and post-flood Sentinel-1 SAR images, applying a refined Lee filter, computing the ratio of filtered images, masking permanent water and small noisy patches, and outputting a binary map of flooded regions.

The script detects vegetation anomalies in May 2020 by comparing NDVI values from Sentinel-2 with the mean NDVI of the same period in 2017–2019, applying cloud-masked composites and temporal filtering to identify significant deviations in vegetative health.

The script evaluates a flood probability raster (1-in-1000 year floodplain) against a set of reference points to determine which points are captured (flood probability above threshold) or missed (below threshold), then calculates the hit rate using random points for accuracy assessment.

The script evaluates the clearness of a Landsat 8 image by analyzing the BQA (Band Quality Assurance) band to generate cloud and shadow masks, then calculates the percentage of clear pixels (not obscured by clouds or shadows) within the region of interest. It outputs an image with added mask bands for clear clouds, clear shadows, and overall clear areas, along with a 'percentage_clearness' property derived from the mean of the clear mask over the geometry.

The script identifies surface water extent by applying the Refined Lee filter to Sentinel-1 GRD data, converting VV backscatter to dB, and using Otsu's method on a histogram of VV values masked by Canny edge detection and HAND terrain data to determine an optimal threshold for water classification.
task_name: Identify surface water extent using SAR

task_description: The script analyzes a time series of EVI (Enhanced Vegetation Index) images to detect and correct anomalies in vegetation dynamics, specifically targeting rice cultivation patterns over two growing seasons (2021–2022). It applies temporal filtering, masking, and correction algorithms to identify key phenological events such as planting and harvesting by analyzing maximum and minimum EVI values across dasarian (10-day) intervals. The output is a smoothed and corrected EVI time series optimized for detecting agricultural cycles in irrigated rice fields.

The script classifies land cover types using a random forest classifier trained on spectral indices (NDVI, NDBI, MNDWI) and surface reflectance bands from Landsat 8 SR data, producing a classified land cover map for the Gansu region in 2021.

The script processes Landsat 8 Surface Reflectance data from April to June 2019 over a point in Indiana (39.77, -86.07), applies a cloud and cloud shadow mask using the pixel_qa band, creates a custom mask using a ratio of B2 (blue) and B10 (thermal infrared), and generates both unmasked and masked median composites for visual comparison. The primary outputs are masked and unmasked false-color images and intermediate masking layers used to assess data quality and improve composite clarity.
task_name: Mask clouds and generate median composite

task_description: The script maps rice field vegetation health using maximum NDVI and median RGB composites from Landsat 8 and Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data over Kabupaten Serang during March 2020, focusing on agricultural areas within a specified boundary.

The script analyzes textural features derived from TNDVI (Transformed NDVI) in agricultural regions using Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data, specifically focusing on dissimilarity, variance, and contrast metrics. It reprojects and resamples a precomputed TNDVI-based image to MODIS resolution for area calculation, suggesting an analysis of spatial heterogeneity in vegetation patterns.
task_name: Analyze TNDVI dissimilarity in agricultural areas

task_description: The script combines original NDVI values from an HLS-derived dataset with their 13-period moving average (MAVG1) values into a single ImageCollection, enabling comparison between raw and temporally smoothed vegetation index time series for the same locations and dates.

The script computes a greenness index using Tasseled Cap transformation coefficients applied to a median surface reflectance composite of Landsat 8 OLI data from May to September 2021, clipped to six Chinese provincial regions, with the purpose of analyzing vegetation characteristics.

The script classifies land cover into five categories—very wet hyacinth, water, vegetation, built-up areas, and bare land—using a Random Forest classifier trained on labeled samples and applied to a composite image. It outputs a classified map, accuracy assessment via confusion matrix, and pixel area statistics within an AOI.

The script analyzes vegetation health, moisture content, and soil brightness using Sentinel-2 data by computing NDVI, NMDI, NDWI, and BSI indices. It generates a composite image of maximum NMDI, VCI (Vegetation Condition Index), and maximum NDWI for a specific month (April 2020), masked by cloud-free pixels, to assess agricultural and environmental conditions.

The script calculates the total area of classified pixels and computes the area for each land cover class, specifically identifying open forest (class 3), within a defined region of interest using a pre-classified optical and SAR image. It outputs the total classified area, open forest area, and individual areas for all classes in square kilometers.
task_name: Classify land cover and compute area per class

task_description: The script classifies land cover into distinct categories (e.g., urban, vegetation, water) using surface reflectance and brightness temperature bands from Landsat 8 OLI/TIRS data. It trains a CART classifier on labeled sample points and applies it to generate a thematic land cover map.

The script filters the Landsat 8 TOA reflectance collection from 2020, selects the least cloudy scene within a specified geometry by sorting on 'CLOUD_COVER', and retrieves the first (least cloudy) image. The output is a single cloud-optimized Landsat 8 image for visual or analytical use.

The script estimates land surface temperature (LST) from Landsat 7 TOA reflectance and brightness temperature data in 2021, using NDVI, proportion of vegetation (Pv), fractional vegetation cover (fv), and emissivity correction over Bandarlampung city, Indonesia.

The script identifies glacial lakes by applying a series of band ratios, spectral indices (NDWI, NDSI, TIRBLUE), and threshold-based masking on Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data. It first computes indices, masks out sea and cloud pixels, then applies thresholds on NDWI and visible band differences (B3B4, B2B3) to detect lake pixels, resulting in a binary lake map.
task_name: Detect glacial lakes using spectral indices

task_description: The script performs Savitzky-Golay filtering on a synthetic time series of length 364 by computing the impulse response from a polynomial fitting matrix and applying a moving window smoothing operation. The output is a smoothed version of the input sequence using pseudoinverse-based convolution weights.

The script identifies the greenest vegetation period by computing the maximum NDVI from MODIS 250m and 500m data (MOD09GQ/MYD09GQ and MOD09GA/MYD09GA) for specific days in August across multiple years, then compares a target year (2022) against a historical baseline to detect anomalies in vegetation health using z-scores. The output is a classified image showing zones of vegetation deviation.

The script analyzes absolute crop yield within a specific agricultural perimeter by integrating multi-source Earth observation data, including precipitation (CHIRPS), evapotranspiration (GLDAS), and vegetation dynamics (MODIS EVI). It masks yield data based on the current campaign year, computes accumulated environmental variables over a defined growing season, converts and normalizes day-of-year values from MODIS to align phenological stages, and calculates regional statistics for time of peak vegetation. The output includes mapped layers of yield, rainfall, ET, and EVI composites, along with the mean day-of-year at peak greenness.
task_name: Analyze crop yield and climate impacts

task_description: The script calculates the percentage of forest cover within MODIS pixels by aggregating high-resolution forest classification data (from nosztep) to the coarser MODIS spatial resolution, using mean reduction and reprojection. It outputs a continuous map of forested area proportion at MODIS scale in percent.

The script estimates chlorophyll-a concentration in Lago Lanalhue using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data by applying a custom vegetation index expression derived from red, green, and near-infrared bands.
