It processes MODIS Terra and Aqua imagery from 2019 to 2020, computes EVI and Fc, combines them with day/night Gsoil models, and applies an ERA5-driven G function to produce time-sorted ImageCollections for both daytime and nighttime soil heat flux.
task_name: Estimate daytime and nighttime soil heat flux

task_description: The script processes Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-1 data over the Lizhou District in China for 2019 to generate a time series of cloud-cleared, gap-filled, and smoothed monthly composites of multiple vegetation and moisture indices (NDVI, BSI, LSWI, EVI, GCVI, NDWI, NBR) along with VV and VH backscatter from Sentinel-1. These are merged into a single multiband image asset for machine learning or phenological analysis.

The script extracts the first image from the MOD11A1 collection, selects its first band (land surface temperature), and computes the mean temperature values within regions defined by elevation mask (ETOPO1 > -100m), converting the results into vector polygons globally between ±80° latitude.

The script creates cloud-masked mosaics of Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery before (April–June 2021) and after (July–August 2021) a specific period, using true-color bands (B4, B3, B2), to visually compare land surface changes over a defined polygon. Outputs include two mosaicked images clipped to the region of interest, intended for change detection analysis.
task_name: Compare land surface before and after event

task_description: The script identifies the timing of maximum red snow algae presence (via RGND index) on glaciers in North America, stratified by elevation (high vs low), using MODIS Terra and Aqua data from 2000 to 2022. Outputs include regional and pixel-level statistics on the day of year with peak RGND values, masked by glacier and snow algae extent, and aggregated over user-defined regions.
task_name: Identify snow algae timing by elevation

task_description: The script identifies forest fragments by applying a threshold (>30%) on the year 2000 tree cover data from the UMD Hansen global forest change dataset, then performs connected component labeling to detect and label individual forest patches within a specified region.
task_name: Identify forest fragments from tree cover

task_description: The script estimates land surface temperature by applying atmospheric correction to thermal infrared data using emissivity derived from ASTER GED, water vapor, and radiative transfer parameters. It computes a corrected surface temperature image using band 13 and band 14 emissivity, vapor content, and model coefficients.

The script trains a Random Forest classifier using labeled feature collections (extr30 to extr180) to classify land cover based on surface reflectance bands from Landsat, evaluates the model's accuracy using a test set, and prints the overall classification accuracy.

The script computes a mean composite of Sentinel-1 GRD imagery filtered by date, study site, instrument mode (EW), and resolution (H), then isolates images by relative orbit number (specifically 119 or the first in the list) to create orbit-specific mean composites. Outputs include a mean backscatter composite across all orbits and two orbit-specific mean images, one using a hardcoded orbit number (119) and another using the first orbit from the histogram of available orbits.
task_name: Compute mean SAR composite by orbit

task_description: The script identifies potential winter wheat cultivation areas in Henan Province, China, by analyzing temporal changes in NDVI and EVI from MODIS MOD13Q1 data across three time periods. It detects pixels that show low vegetation index in September–October 2019, high index in March 2020, and a decline by May–July 2020, consistent with winter wheat phenology. Two separate masks (wheat1 using NDVI, wheat2 using EVI) are generated and masked to highlight likely wheat zones. Total area in hectares for both criteria is computed and printed.

The script calculates the mean HV polarization backscatter values from Sentinel-1 SAR imagery over large lakes (greater than 250 km²) in southern Greenland between October 2018 and April 2019, producing a time-series table of per-lake radar reflectance used for cryospheric or hydrologic analysis.

The script calculates the mean evapotranspiration (ET) for different land cover types (crop, forest, grass, water, barren, city, wetland) using a classified land cover map and a median ET image derived from a time-series of 24 input images. It computes regional means over a specified ROI and outputs them per land cover class.
task_name: Estimate ET by land cover type

task_description: The script identifies urban expansion and changes in built-up areas by analyzing Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data and applying threshold-based classification on a predicted urban probability layer. It compares urban development between December 2018, March 2020, and September 2021 using normalized difference change detection and morphological filtering to highlight pre- and post-COVID urban growth patterns in Queen Creek.

The script identifies surface water extent by calculating the modified Normalized Difference Water Index (mNDWI) from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data, using green (B3) and shortwave infrared (B11) bands, for a specific region and time period with strict cloud cover filtering.

The script detects changes on the ice surface of the Larsen C ice shelf by analyzing temporal differences in HH-polarized Sentinel-1 SAR backscatter between a winter reference period and a summer observation period, applying speckle filtering and entropy-based masking to improve change detection accuracy.

The script filters a Landsat 8 TOA reflectance image collection for images that intersect a specified region of interest (roi) and fall within the date range from January 1, 2018, to January 1, 2019. It outputs the filtered image collection to the console.
task_name: Filter Landsat images by region and date

task_description: The script classifies land use and land cover types using median-composite Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery from 2017 to 2019, applying a Random Forest classifier trained on user-defined feature collections (cropland, forest, water, bareland, bush, Town) within a specified polygon region near coordinates (16.9142, -17.5809). The output is a classified raster map of six land cover classes.

The script analyzes vegetation recovery in the Cameron Peak fire region using Sentinel-2 imagery from May to June 2021 by computing MSAVI, SAVI, and NDVI indices to assess vegetation health and density after wildfire disturbance.

The script classifies soil erosion risk levels (Very Low, Low, Medium, High) using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data and a CART-trained classifier applied to a feature collection of labeled points. The output is a classified raster map of soil erosion risk.

The script analyzes land degradation in Ecuador by integrating land cover, productivity dynamics, soil organic carbon, fire recurrence, precipitation trends, and terrain data. It evaluates degradation status using QM mapping units, identifies direct causes and degradation types, and generates hotspot maps based on multi-criteria analysis combining ecological, socio-economic, and biophysical indicators.

The script checks whether at least one Landsat image is available within a specified geographic extent and temporal window in the year 2000, specifically around day-of-year 195–199. It outputs a message 'yay' if an image exists, otherwise 'boo'.

The script calculates the water area within Chennai using the NDWI index derived from a single Landsat 8 TOA image, applying a threshold to classify water pixels and computing the total water-covered area in square meters.

The script normalizes Sentinel-1 HV polarization backscatter values across different relative orbits to reduce orbit-dependent variability, then extracts time-series mean HV backscatter values over lake vectors in the CW region for the 2014–2015 winter season. Outputs include a CSV of per-lake, per-image backscatter values and metadata of the processed image collection.

The script computes the Jeffries-Matusita (JM) distance for each spectral band in a Sentinel-2 image to evaluate class separability among land cover types using training points. It generates a median composite from Sentinel-2 imagery (2020–2021), calculates vegetation and moisture indices, and assesses spectral discrimination between six land cover classes.
task_name: Analyze spectral separability for land cover classification

task_description: The script calculates daily water balance components including soil moisture storage change, net recharge, and precipitation surplus using GLDAS NOAH model data over the specified region and time period. Outputs are summed total Surplus, Net_Recharge, and Balance layers clipped to the study area.

The script identifies surface water bodies in the Amazon region using hue thresholding on a median-composited Landsat 8 image, applying cloud masking and spatial clipping to a user-defined feature collection.

The script merges multiple user-generated feature collections of training data points, each labeled with a land cover class, converts polygon features to centroids if necessary, and joins them with Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery within a 30-day temporal window. It applies pixel value extraction at the point locations to generate a final training dataset for supervised land cover classification. The output is a flattened feature collection containing spectral values from Landsat bands matched to labeled training points, intended for use in a land cover classification model.

The script identifies water bodies by computing the Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI) from Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data, applying a cloud-masked quality mosaic based on NDWI values, and clipping the result to a rectangular polygon. The output is a single composite image where maximum NDWI pixels are selected over the time period, used to map surface water extent.

The script classifies land cover types, specifically distinguishing onion, grape, wheat, maize, built-up areas, wasteland, and water bodies within an AOI using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from 2021 and 2022. It trains an SVM (libsvm) classifier on spectral bands and evaluates accuracy using a confusion matrix for both training and testing partitions.

The script classifies land and water areas using a cloud-score-weighted Landsat 7 TOA composite from mid-2014, computing NDVI and NDWI to train a CART classifier on a user-defined region in western Canada, producing a classified land-water map.

The script identifies deforestation by comparing NDVI-masked vegetation cover between two Sentinel-2 image dates, computing binary differences to highlight areas of vegetation loss, and additionally analyzes burn scars using NBR differencing to detect fire-affected regions.

The script identifies urban expansion between 2019 and 2021 by combining spectral indices from Sentinel-2 (NDTI, NDVI, NDBI) and backscatter changes from Sentinel-1 (VV), applying morphological filtering and thresholding to detect built-up areas and their change over time. The output is a binary map of urban change validated against ground truth labels.
task_name: Identify urban change using Sentinel data

task_description: The script calculates fire severity metrics (dNBR, RBR, RdNBR) with offset corrections using pre- and post-fire Sentinel-2 NBR and NDVI values, specifically analyzing burn severity for individual fire perimeters in 2020. Outputs include corrected dNBR, rbr, and rdNBR images clipped to fire boundaries and masked for water.
task_name: Assess wildfire severity using satellite indices

task_description: The script computes a time series of monthly median Sentinel-2 surface reflectance images from 2020, masked for clouds, and adds multiple vegetation and water indices (NDVI, EVI, RVI, DVI, ARVI, NBR1, NBR2, NDVIre1-3, CTre, NDre1-2 and modified versions, MTCI, IRECI, mNDVI, NDWI, SAVI, OSAVI) to assess vegetation condition and biophysical properties over a region of interest.

The script classifies land cover types using a pre-trained land cover image (2020) and uses manually defined polygon regions representing different land cover classes (e.g., cultivated land, forest, grassland, wetland, water bodies, artificial surfaces) to potentially train or validate the classification. It also processes Sentinel-2 imagery for visual verification by applying cloud masking and computing a median composite for the first half of 2020.

The script identifies potential ice sheet melt areas in South Greenland using Sentinel-2 imagery by computing NDWI with blue and red bands (B2 and B4), creating a maximum NDWI pixel composite, and generating a binary difference mask between pixels with NDWI > 0.5 and NDWI > 0.25 to highlight surface water changes likely associated with melting ice.

The script creates a cloud-masked Sentinel-2 surface reflectance composite for China during summer 2018 using the quality mosaic method, prioritizing pixels with low QA60 values to minimize cloud contamination.

The script calculates the Near-Infrared Reflectance of Vegetation (NIRv) for January 2020 using Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data, combining bands B3, B4, and B5 through a spectral index expression. The output is a single-band image representing NIRv values derived from the median composite of January 2020 imagery.

The script calculates the difference between two C-band HH-polarized Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images from the Sentinel-1 mission acquired six months apart, highlighting surface changes through backscatter intensity differences in urban, agricultural, or natural landscapes.

The script classifies rice cultivation areas in Heilongjiang Province using a trained SVM classifier applied to spectral indices (ndvi, lswi, EVI, GCVI, PSRI, bsi) derived from a composite image. The output is a classified raster map of rice extent, masked and clipped to the Heilongjiang boundary, with validation performed on an independent test dataset.

The script classifies land cover into four categories (building, water, crop, and an additional class implied by palette) using Landsat 8 surface reflectance data from mid-2019. It computes MNDWI, NDBI, and NDVI indices, trains an SVM classifier on sampled regions, and produces a classified land cover map with accuracy assessment including confusion matrix, overall accuracy, and kappa coefficient.

The script creates a quality mosaic of Landsat 8 TOA reflectance images from early summer 2013, using the 'system:time_start' metadata to select the image with the earliest acquisition time at each pixel location within the specified spatial extent.

The script retrieves the first Sentinel-2 image within a specified geometry and extracts pixel values from the blue spectral band (B2) by sampling at the region defined by the geometry, resulting in a feature collection of sampled points with B2 reflectance values.

The script creates two binary images by painting geometries, applies a mask from a third geometry on the second image, combines them into an image collection, computes a count composite to identify areas where images overlap, samples the result at a specific location, and filters the collection by another geometry. The output is a count of overlapping painted images and sampled pixel values, demonstrating spatial masking and compositing logic.

The script classifies land cover into vegetation, soil, and water classes using a random forest classifier trained on Sentinel-like spectral bands from a median composite of cloud-filtered satellite imagery over the APATX region in 2019. The output is a classified raster map labeled 'APATX'.

The script classifies industrial land cover in South African provinces using a Random Forest classifier trained on Sentinel-2 imagery masked by ESRI Land Use/Land Cover data, with final output focusing on the Western Cape region.

The script detects land cover changes in the Imperial, CA region by analyzing the difference in Landsat 8 SWIR1 (B5) band values between three time periods (2013–2018 and 2018–2021), masking for clouds using pixel QA bits, and applying a threshold based on mean and standard deviation to identify significant change. The output is binary change maps indicating areas of detected surface change.

The script identifies open water and vegetated water bodies using Sentinel-1 VV backscatter thresholds and adaptive thresholding based on mean and standard deviation within the area of interest. It also implements a supervised Random Forest classification model trained on sample points to classify water types, with outputs including classified water maps and threshold values as image bands.
task_name: Identify open water and submerged vegetation

task_description: The script creates a cloud-filtered minimum value composite from Sentinel-2 imagery for January to March 2018, selecting bands B8, B4, and B2 to form a high-resolution true-color-like image suitable for land surface observation, with minimal atmospheric interference.

The script processes a sugarcane farm feature collection by computing plantation and monitoring periods for each farm, then generates 10 random points per farm for potential remote sensing monitoring. It also prepares a cloud-masked Sentinel-2 image collection filtered to the farms' spatial and temporal extent for vegetation analysis.

The script identifies forest loss events in Guangxi, China by analyzing time series of Landsat imagery using the Continuous Change Detection and Classification (CCDC) method. It generates a classified raster output indicating predicted land cover change (SRP: stable reference period; NSRP: non-stable reference period), validated against sample points, with outputs including yearly land cover classifications, breakpoint detection, and post-processed change maps.

The script identifies areas of potential surface melt on the Greenland ice sheet by analyzing Sentinel-2 imagery during summer 2016, using a normalized difference water index (NDWI) thresholding approach. It generates binary masks for NDWI > 0.5 and NDWI > 0.25, then computes their difference to highlight regions with moderate melt signal, focusing exclusively on the ice sheet via a GIMP ice mask.

The script analyzes forest change using the Hansen Global Forest Change dataset to identify areas of forest loss between 2005 and 2009, detects persistent tree cover (not affected by gain or loss) above 20% canopy density, and generates stratified sample points from stable forest regions. It also enables interactive time series analysis at clicked locations using Landsat-derived vegetation and soil indices for monitoring forest dynamics.
task_name: Identify forest loss and stable tree cover

task_description: The script generates a median composite of Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery from 2017, masked for clouds and cirrus using the QA60 band, filtered by low cloud cover, and clipped to a specified geometry. It outputs a true-color (B4, B3, B2) RGB image and includes near-infrared and shortwave infrared bands (B8, B11, B12), suitable for land surface monitoring and vegetation analysis.
task_name: Extract cloud-masked Sentinel-2 RGB and SWIR imagery

task_description: The script generates a median composite of Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery for the Guairá department in Paraguay, filtered for low cloud cover during the second half of 2019, and clipped to the administrative boundary.

The script analyzes the temporal evolution of NDVI and EVI vegetation indices at a specific point in Córdoba, Argentina, using MODIS data, and generates a cloud-minimized composite image from Sentinel-2 with NDVI for visual assessment of greenest pixels over the region.
task_name: Analyze NDVI and EVI time series

task_description: The script classifies land cover types in an urban area of Córdoba using Sentinel-2 imagery by computing NDSV indices and applying a Random Forest classifier, producing a classified map and accuracy assessment from ground truth data.

The script analyzes vegetation conditions using the Normalized Burn Ratio (NBR) derived from Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data and overlays NLCD land cover classification to assess land cover types in a specific region during May 2017.

The script calculates multiple spectral vegetation and land surface indices from a Sentinel-2 image, including NDVI, EVI, MSAVI, NBR1, NBR2, NDVIre1, NDVIre2, NDVIre3, CTre, NDre1, NDre1m, NDre2, NDre2m, MTCI, IRECI, GNDVI, NDWI, and OSAVI, for detailed biophysical and vegetation analysis over a specified region of interest.
task_name: Compute vegetation and land surface indices

task_description: The script identifies surface water extent in a reservoir using NDWI derived from Landsat 8 TOA data, calculates the total water-covered area within a specified region, and generates vector polygons representing water zones. Outputs include a maximum NDWI image, a binary water mask, and vectorized water boundaries.

The script identifies areas of winter-emergent crops in California by analyzing Sentinel-2 NDVI time series between January and March 2019, applying dynamic NDVI thresholds (minimum and maximum) based on acquisition date to detect fields exhibiting expected vegetation growth patterns for winter emergence.

The script classifies urban areas by training a model using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data and labeled urban training samples. It processes NAIP imagery for visual reference and applies cloud masking to Sentinel-2 images from 2019–2020 over a defined ROI, then extracts spectral band values at training locations for subsequent classification.

The script processes Landsat 8 surface reflectance data from 2017 over a user-defined region of interest to generate a median composite image. It applies cloud and cloud shadow masking using pixel_qa, then computes multiple spectral indices (NDVI, MNDWI, NDBI, Green, Wetness, Brightness) to enhance vegetation, water, built-up, and soil features. The final output is a multispectral composite used for land cover classification analysis.

The script calculates the total forest area in 2000 within the geographic range of a specific species using the UMD Hansen global forest change dataset and a species distribution image. It computes two results: one using vectorized species range polygons and another using raster masking, both yielding forest area in square kilometers.
task_name: Estimate forest area within species range

task_description: The script calculates NDVI using top-of-atmosphere (TOA) reflectance values derived from raw Landsat 8 band data by manually applying scaling and offset coefficients for bands 4 and 5, then compares the result with the pre-computed TOA NDVI from the Landsat 8 TOA dataset to evaluate differences in computation methods.

The script generates a training dataset for mangrove classification by collecting random and existing sample points from annual regions between 1986 and 2020, assigning each point a 'mangrove' label and corresponding year, then filtering these samples within a defined ROI. It also prepares and composites annual median surface reflectance images from Landsat 5, 7, and 8 for the same period, clipped to the ROI, to support time-series analysis of mangrove dynamics.

The script detects the melt state (melt vs. unmelt) of snow using time-series Sentinel-1 SAR imagery by analyzing HH backscatter changes between a reference winter period and a target March month, applying a threshold-based change detection method, and classifying results using SVM with training and validation points. Outputs include classified melt maps and validation accuracy metrics (overall accuracy and kappa) for four regions.

The script classifies rice cultivation areas in Heilongjiang Province using a trained SVM classifier on spectral indices (LSWI and GCVI) derived from a composite image. It evaluates classification accuracy using a confusion matrix, reporting user accuracy, producer accuracy, overall accuracy, and kappa coefficient based on test samples.

The script classifies land cover into five categories (Water, Pasture, Forest, Agriculture, ImpermeableSurface) using Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data and a Random Forest classifier, then validates the classification accuracy using an error matrix, overall accuracy, user accuracy, producer accuracy, and kappa coefficient.

The script computes monthly median NDVI from Sentinel-2 imagery after cloud masking using QA60, aggregates it into seasonal composites for five years (2016–2020), and performs a spatiotemporal change analysis by comparing forecasted and true NDVI values using convolution with a 7x7 averaging kernel. The final output is a vegetation change layer (b3) highlighting deviations between expected and actual vegetation conditions.

The script calculates the Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI) using red, near-infrared, and blue bands from a median-composited Landsat 5 SR image over a rectangular region in northern China for January 2011.

The script identifies burned areas by calculating the Normalized Burn Ratio (NDBR) from Landsat 8 surface reflectance data, applying a threshold (NDBR < -0.18) to detect fire-affected regions, and generating a binary fire mask. It also analyzes land cover types (e.g., rock, evergreen forest, shrub) using NLCD 2016 data within a specified region, computing area statistics for each class.

The script identifies surface water bodies using NDWI calculated from Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data, applying a threshold of 0.25 to mask non-water areas, and uses the resulting lake mask to filter Sentinel-1 SAR imagery for lake surface analysis.

The script computes a median composite NDVI image using Landsat 8 surface reflectance and TOA data, applying a percentile-based mask on the BQA band to filter pixels, then combining normalized surface reflectance with panchromatic masking for vegetation analysis.

The script classifies land cover into cover crop, pasturegrass, and stover based on seasonal NDVI thresholds derived from Sentinel-2 imagery over a specific region of interest. It computes median NDVI for October 2017, May 2018, and December 2017–January 2018, then applies logical conditions to distinguish vegetation types.

The script identifies burned areas by calculating the Normalized Burn Ratio (NDBR) from Landsat 8 surface reflectance data between August 1 and September 15, 2020, applying a threshold of -0.2 to detect fire-affected regions, and generating a binary mask highlighting those areas in red.

The script calculates the mean CH4 column volume mixing ratio in dry air from Sentinel-5P data over São Paulo state between May and July 2019, samples the values, and performs kriging interpolation to generate a continuous surface of methane concentrations.

The script performs supervised land cover classification to distinguish limestone from other land areas using ASTER satellite imagery and machine learning classifiers (CART, Random Forest, Naive Bayes, SVM). It trains models on labeled samples, classifies the image, and evaluates accuracy using error matrices.

The script classifies land cover into seven classes (耕地, 林地, 草地, 灌丛, 水体, 不透水层, 裸地) using seasonal median composites of Landsat 8 surface reflectance data from 2020, with NDVI, NDBI, and NDWI indices. Training samples are collected from user-defined regions, and a Random Forest classifier is applied to generate a classified land cover map.

The script extracts the first available NDVI image from the MODIS MCD43A4_NDVI collection and masks it using specific land cover classes (classes 1 to 8) derived from the MCD12Q1 land cover product. The output is a masked NDVI image showing only pixels corresponding to these selected land cover types.
task_name: Extract NDVI for specific land cover classes

task_description: The script computes the Remote Sensing Ecological Index (RSEI) for a region of interest by combining NDVI, LST, WET, and NDBSI indices derived from MODIS data. It performs PCA on these normalized indices to generate a composite ecological condition index (RSEI) over time, with outputs including annual RSEI images, trend analysis, and visualizations. The final output is a time series of RSEI maps indicating spatiotemporal ecological changes.

The script performs image co-registration of two ASTER satellite images by calculating pixel displacement between a reference and target image using normalized difference analysis on specific bands, then applies the displacement to align the second image with the first. The output includes offset magnitude, angle, and the final co-registered image.

The script classifies land cover into water, tree, and soil classes using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data. It trains a CART classifier on sampled regions and applies it to produce a classified image with three categories: water (blue), soil (yellow), and vegetation (green).

The script analyzes pre- and post-wildfire Landsat 8 imagery to compute Burn Area Index (BAI) and Normalized Burn Ratio Thermal (NBRT), then calculates the difference in NBRT before and after the Rim Fire to assess burn severity.

The script classifies land cover into seven categories (Cropland, Forest, Grassland, Shrubland, Water, Impervious Surface, Bareland) using multi-temporal Sentinel-2 surface reflectance composites from four seasons in 2019–2020. It trains a Random Forest classifier on fishnet-based training samples and validates the model using independently labeled validation polygons, producing a classified land cover map and accuracy assessment including confusion matrix, overall accuracy, and producer/consumer accuracies.

The script updates a 2016 land use and land cover (LUCC) map by integrating change information derived from image collections and applying spatial overlays for specific land cover transitions, using Landsat surface reflectance data and multiple static transition maps. The final output is a refined LUCC image for 2016 that reflects updated classifications based on detected changes and user-defined conversions such as crop to grass, city to desert, etc.
task_name: Update 2016 land cover with change detection

task_description: The script classifies land cover by training random forest models on biomes using spectral indices (NBR, NDVI, BAI, NBRtwo) derived from Landsat TOA data. The output is a classified mosaic image where each biome is processed separately, trained on labeled samples, and combined into a final byte-scaled result representing classification confidence above 60%.
task_name: Classify land cover using NBR and vegetation indices

task_description: The script pansharpen a Landsat 8 TOA reflectance image by fusing the panchromatic band (B8) with the RGB bands (B4, B3, B2) using an HSV-based color transformation to enhance spatial resolution of the visible bands.

The script calculates the annual sum of Gross Primary Productivity (GPP) and canopy evaporation (Ec) from the PML_V2 model over the Tarim River region for the year 2001, then computes their ratio as an array output. The result represents the proportion of photosynthetic carbon uptake relative to transpired water loss by vegetation canopy at the regional scale.
task_name: Calculate annual GPP to Ec ratio

task_description: The script generates monthly RGB composites and NDVI maps from Sentinel-2 imagery between 2016 and 2021, masked for clouds and cirrus, to visually monitor land surface changes over time within a specific administrative boundary (processo).
task_name: Monitor vegetation and land cover with RGB and NDVI

task_description: The script detects changes in vegetation conditions associated with cheatgrass presence by computing and analyzing differences in multiple spectral indices (NDVI, EVI, MSAVI, NDWI, TCB, TCW, TCG) derived from Sentinel-2 imagery before and after a fire event in June–July 2021. The output is a multiband image of index differences (e.g., dNDVI, dEVI) masked for non-water areas, used to identify cheatgrass-invaded regions affected by the Cameron Peak fire.
task_name: Detect cheatgrass disturbance using spectral indices

task_description: The script identifies flood extents by processing Sentinel-1 GRD SAR imagery through time-series mosaicking, K-means clustering for unsupervised classification, and post-classification filtering. It generates a multi-year flood frequency map by combining classified flood events from 2017, 2018, and 2019 with two historical Landsat-based flood maps from 2000 and 2011. Outputs include a summed flood occurrence image and a CSV file listing all detection dates.
task_name: Identify flood extents using radar imagery

task_description: The script identifies breakpoints in forest areas using time series segmentation from CCDC analysis, combining Landsat-based image collections to detect changes in NDFI and classify land cover annually, with post-processing to extract and smooth forest loss events.

The script classifies land cover into 19 distinct classes using a Random Forest classifier trained on manually labeled regions and a set of environmental covariates derived from a 2018 composite image. The output is a classified land cover map with pixel-level labels across the study area.

The script identifies surface water extent using Sentinel-1 SAR data by computing the SDWI (Synthetic Aperture Radar-Derived Water Index) and applying a threshold to classify water bodies in the Yangtze River Delta region (Chongming area) for April 2019.

The script computes a shaded relief model using elevation data, incorporating light source direction, viewer perspective, and surface normals to simulate realistic 3D terrain illumination with specular and diffuse lighting components.

The script applies Local Incidence Angle (LIA) correction to Sentinel-1 GRD images over a specified ROI by using SRTM DEM and terrain geometry to correct radiometric distortions due to topography, outputting corrected VV and VH backscatter bands along with layover and shadow masks.
task_name: Apply local incidence angle correction to SAR imagery

task_description: The script computes median VV and VH polarization composites from Sentinel-1 SAR data over a region of interest, generating single-band layers for VV and VH, as well as three-season temporal composites (early, mid, late year) to analyze seasonal variations in radar backscatter, likely for land cover or agricultural monitoring.

The script analyzes land cover changes between the years 2000 and 2018 in Guyana by comparing two classified land cover maps (Guyana2000 and Guyana2018). It computes a transition matrix using stratified sampling based on the earlier classification to quantify changes between classes such as water, urban areas, cropland, dense canopy, and wetlands. The output includes mapped classifications for both years, sampled points for accuracy assessment, and a printed transition matrix with overall accuracy representing the percentage of unchanged samples.

The script performs topographic correction on a Landsat 8 image by modeling solar illumination based on terrain slope and aspect, then applies a C-correction model to adjust reflectance values in bands B4, B3, and B2 to reduce topographic effects. The output is a corrected image composite with adjusted offsets.
task_name: Correct surface reflectance using illumination modeling

task_description: The script identifies areas where vegetation significantly decreased between late April and early June 2019 by comparing NDVI values from Sentinel-2 imagery, specifically detecting pixels that transitioned from high vegetation (NDVI > 0.6) to low vegetation (NDVI < 0.5), then calculates the total area of this change within a user-defined boundary.

The script identifies the greenest pixels by computing a quality mosaic based on NDVI from Landsat 8 surface reflectance data over a single year (2019), then creates a binary mask where NDVI exceeds 0.5, indicating dense vegetation. The output includes a clipped NDVI maximum composite, a greenest pixel composite, and a thresholded result for high-vegetation areas.

The script identifies water bodies by computing a Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI) using green and near-infrared bands from Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data, creating a cloud-masked composite, and applying a threshold to extract surface water extent within a defined polygon.

The script calculates NDVI from Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data for a specific path/row and low cloud cover, then extracts median NDVI values per polygon in a given geometry collection over the year 2017.

The script identifies the impact of Typhoon Fitow on paddy rice fields in Shanghai and Zhejiang by analyzing changes in NDVI from MODIS data before, during, and after the typhoon event, classifying damage into five types based on thresholds and temporal NDVI differences.
task_name: Identify typhoon impact on rice fields

task_description: The script generates 100 random points over a global glacier dataset (GLIMS), then filters the dataset to Iceland and generates 100 random points within that region. The output is a feature collection of random spatial points constrained by glacier geometry.
task_name: Generate random points on glacier data

task_description: The script identifies the greenest pixel composite based on NDVI from cloud-cleared Landsat 5 surface reflectance imagery during spring months (July–November) between 1983 and 1988 over a specific catchment area, producing a cloud-free mosaic image for vegetation analysis.

The script calculates the mean of 2-meter air temperature from ERA5 data for July and August, identifies pixels where the temperature is not greater than 270 Kelvin, and masks out areas above this threshold. The output is a binary masked layer highlighting regions with relatively low air temperatures during summer months.
The script identifies regions in Pakistan with elevations between 1500 and 2500 meters using SRTM elevation data, creating a binary mask that highlights these areas on the map.

The script filters the Landsat 8 Surface Reflectance dataset to extract cloud-filtered images (less than 80% cloud cover over land) within a specific catchment boundary (RRD_Catchment_full) during the spring months (January to March) from 2013 to 2017. The output is an ImageCollection of seasonal surface reflectance data suitable for land surface monitoring in the study area.

The script calculates Land Surface Temperature (LST) using Landsat 8 TIRS bands 10 and 11, applying a split-window algorithm that incorporates NDVI-derived vegetation cover, emissivity corrections, and at-sensor brightness temperatures. The output is a mean LST image for January 2020, masked to a user-defined geometry.

The script calculates the annual water balance for São Paulo state by computing the difference between total accumulated rainfall from TRMM and actual evapotranspiration from MOD16A2, resulting in a spatial layer representing net water availability (precipitation minus ET) for the year 2010.

The script fuses Sentinel-1 SAR data (VV, VH) and Sentinel-2 multispectral bands (B1–B12) through Principal Component Analysis after preprocessing, generating a fused image product that integrates radar and optical information for enhanced land surface characterization.
task_name: Fuse Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 for PCA analysis

task_description: The script analyzes temporal NDVI patterns at field points with high and low cheatgrass presence using Planet satellite imagery from April to early June 2021, comparing vegetation dynamics between cheatgrass-dominated and non-cheatgrass areas within the Cameron Peak Fire boundary region.

The script calculates the ratio of VV to VH polarization backscatter from Sentinel-1 GRD data, likely to analyze surface structure and moisture characteristics in agricultural or land cover monitoring. Outputs are multi-temporal mean images for ascending and descending orbits, masked to remove noisy edges.
task_name: Compute VV/VH ratio for SAR analysis

task_description: The script identifies surface water extent using a combination of NDVI, mNDWI, and EVI indices derived from Landsat 8 surface reflectance data between 2018-01-01 and 2018-12-31. It applies cloud masking and calculates spectral indices to detect water bodies, producing a binary surface water map where water is classified as value 2 and non-water as 0.

The script calculates a vegetation index (difference between near-infrared and red bands) from MODIS MOD09A1 surface reflectance data over a global extent for the period 2012–2014, then computes the median value per pixel across the time series and extracts the maximum median value within the defined region.

The script calculates the NDVI growth trend of winter wheat by comparing current-phase Sentinel-2 NDVI with historical median NDVI over a user-defined year range, applying a cloud-masked time-series analysis within a specified region. Outputs include current NDVI, past NDVI median, relative NDVI difference, and reclassified anomaly layers, masked to winter wheat distribution areas.

The script classifies land cover into builtup, vegetation, waterbody, and wasteland using a CART and Random Forest classifier trained on Landsat 7 TOA reflectance data from 2005. It outputs a classified LULC map and evaluates accuracy using training and testing partitions with confusion matrices.

The script estimates monthly NOx emissions by combining fire radiative power (FRP) data from MODIS with crop dominance, land cover, and phenology information. It calculates emission factors (EFs), peak FRP contributions, and hourly fire emissions to derive monthly maximum NOx emission images weighted by crop-specific emission factors.
task_name: Estimate monthly NOx emissions from crop fires

task_description: The script analyzes anomalies in cyanobacteria levels using NDCI from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data between 2016 and 2020, focusing on summer-fall seasons (July–October), generating standardized anomaly images for each year relative to the mean and standard deviation.

The script identifies flooded areas by comparing Sentinel-1 VV backscatter before and after a flood event in October 2020, applying a threshold on the difference of focal median-filtered images to detect significant drops in radar signal indicative of surface water inundation.

The script computes monthly mean VV and VH backscatter from Sentinel-1 GRD data, applies terrain flattening and Refined Lee filtering, then derives temporal statistics (mean, standard deviation) and percentiles for 2017 and 2018 over a region of interest. Outputs include gamma-nought calibrated, filtered, and decibel-scaled backscatter images, as well as percentile composites for interannual comparison of radar signal behavior.

The script generates cloud-masked, clipped, and median-composited surface reflectance images from Landsat 5, 7, and 8 for the Netherlands on a yearly basis from 1998 to 2018, producing an ImageCollection of annual mosaics filtered to valid 11-band outputs.

The script computes a median NDVI composite from surface reflectance data of Landsat 7, applying cloud masking, scaling factors, and gap-filling using temporal linear regression to mitigate data gaps caused by SLC-off. The output includes a filled surface reflectance mosaic and NDVI composite for agricultural or land surface monitoring.

The script calculates changes in Tasseled Cap Brightness (TCB) and Greenness (TCG) from Landsat 8 TOA imagery before and after the Cameron Peak Fire to assess burn severity, producing difference images (dTCB and dTCG) that highlight vegetation and surface structural changes due to fire.
task_name: Detect burn severity using TCB and TCG

task_description: The script filters and merges Landsat 4, 5, 7, and 8 surface reflectance or top-of-atmosphere collections based on spatial location, time range (2015–2019), seasonal window (May–September), cloud cover threshold (<100%), and WRS row constraint (<234), then standardizes band names across sensors for consistent spectral analysis over a point of interest.

The script classifies land cover types by training a CART classifier on clipped NDVI images from Landsat 5 surface reflectance data, using USDA cropland data as training labels, and applies the model to classify the first image in the NDVI time series over a region in southern California.
task_name: Classify land cover using NDVI and USDA training data

task_description: The script calculates the total annual precipitation from daily CHIRPS data for the year 2019, then computes the median precipitation value within each feature of a user-defined region FeatureCollection using zonal statistics at 5km scale.
task_name: Calculate annual precipitation median by region

task_description: The script identifies ice sheet areas in Greenland by creating a maximum NDWI pixel composite from Sentinel-2 imagery, masking clouds and non-ice areas, and applying a threshold to isolate ice surfaces based on spectral characteristics.
task_name: Identify ice sheet areas using NDWI

task_description: The script extracts Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD) at 550 nm wavelength from MODIS MCD19A2 granules for specific time periods in 2019, applies a mask based on internal quality flags from the AOD_QA band, and selects data within a defined geometry. It produces two image collections: one with quality masking applied and one without.

The script calculates hourly fire radiative power (FRP)-based emission rates for rice residue burning, using MaxFRP from a MODIS image collection, and applies empirical coefficients (B, O, H) and emission factors (EF) to estimate NOX emissions over time. The final output is a time-aggregated emission raster (NOX_rice) representing total NOx emissions from rice straw burning.
task_name: Estimate NOx emissions from rice burning

task_description: The script identifies the presence of red snow algae using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data by applying a trained classifier and masking non-algal areas, then computes the mean algal RGND index within a region of interest.

The script analyzes flood extent from radar and optical imagery, calculates water-covered areas over time, and extracts the maximum floodwater surface elevation by combining flood masks with SRTM DEM data. It outputs a CSV table of flood elevations and area statistics over the study period.

The script calculates the total area of mud by multiplying an image (presumably representing mud) with pixel area and summing the values within a specified polygon region (site0), then outputs the result to the console.

The script processes MODIS MOD09GQ and MOD09GA data to generate a combined reflectance product by fusing 250m red and NIR bands with 500m blue and green bands using a ratio-based adjustment method, resulting in a higher spatial resolution multispectral dataset.

The script classifies land cover types—specifically forest, water, crop, urban, and plantations—using Sentinel-2 imagery from 2017 over Vietnam. It trains a Random Forest classifier on reference data, applies it to the image, and evaluates classification accuracy using a confusion matrix, overall accuracy, producers' accuracy, consumers' accuracy, and kappa coefficient.

The script classifies land cover into water, tree, and soil classes using supervised classification (CART) on Landsat 8 surface reflectance bands. It trains a classifier with labeled regions, applies it to an image, and identifies water extent by masking classified water pixels, counting them within a region of interest.

The script calculates the covariance matrix of spectral bands from a single Earth Engine image after subtracting the mean, using a specified scale and CRS, to analyze noise or spectral variability characteristics in the image.

The script calculates the total potential evapotranspiration (PET) for the year 2016 in the Sta. Barbara region by summing MOD16A2 PET data and applying a unit conversion (multiplying by 0.1), then computes the mean PET grouped by land cover classes derived from MCD12Q1. The output is a grouped regional reduction showing mean PET values per land cover type.

The script identifies algal blooms on ice surfaces using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data by applying a machine learning classifier trained on spectral bands and redness indices, with cloud masking and spatial smoothing to refine detection.

The script calculates NDVI using Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data for January 2017, clips it to a feature collection of drainage networks (vaos), computes median NDVI values within each feature, and adds a metadata field 'produto_id' before outputting the resulting feature collection.
task_name: Extract median NDVI from agricultural areas

task_description: The script processes MODIS Terra and Aqua MOD11A2 and MYD11A2 Collection 6.1 data to extract day and night land surface temperature (LST) values, applies quality filtering using QC bitmasks for valid observations, converts Kelvin to Celsius, and clips results to a user-defined shapefile boundary for the period 2003–2020.

The script identifies surface water extent by applying Otsu's thresholding method on median-filtered VV-polarized Sentinel-1 GRD imagery from March 2016, producing a binary water mask and calculating water area per polygon in square kilometers.
task_name: Identify water bodies using SAR thresholding

task_description: The script computes the pixel-wise covariance matrix of visible and near-infrared bands (B2–B4) from top-of-atmosphere Landsat 8 imagery over a region in Valencia, Spain, after cloud masking and temporal filtering between April 2015 and May 2016. The output is a composite sum of covariance matrices across all images, intended for multivariate spectral analysis such as principal component transformation or texture-based land cover characterization.
task_name: Analyze spectral covariance in agricultural areas

task_description: The script computes median NDVI and surface reflectance values for dry and wet seasons using Landsat 8 data, comparing vegetation conditions over time by applying cloud masking and temporal filtering to generate composite images for each season.
task_name: Analyze dry and wet season vegetation

task_description: The script calculates the annual water balance for the Cerrado region in 2010 by computing the difference between precipitation and evapotranspiration, then subtracting surface runoff. The output is a clipped raster showing spatial variation of net water availability (surplus or deficit) across the Cerrado biome.

The script calculates NDVI from satellite imagery to generate a forest mask (NDVI > 0.5), then computes the total forest area within a specified geometry in square meters and converts it to square kilometers.

The script analyzes dual-polarization Sentinel-1 SAR imagery (HH band) from two dates to compute a backscatter difference image, highlighting changes in surface moisture conditions. It generates histograms over defined regions (Dry, wet, Percolation) to characterize reflectance distributions and their changes, supporting analysis of hydrological dynamics such as wetting or drying trends.

The script estimates daily NOx emissions in Hubei Province by modeling fire radiative energy from MODIS and MYD satellite data, applying emission factors and diurnal cycles for different land cover types (rice, other crops, urban), and aggregating results monthly for January, February, March, April, November, and December 2015.
task_name: Estimate NOx emissions from fire radiative power

task_description: The script identifies the greenest pixel composite from Landsat 8 surface reflectance data using NDVI as a quality metric over a summer period in 2013, and compares it with a custom median-quality mosaic and a band-wise median composite for a region in southern Nevada.

The script calculates and compares NDBI (Normalized Difference Built-up Index) from MODIS and Landsat 8 TOA data to analyze built-up or impervious surface areas in Philadelphia for summer months of 2018, producing median composite images and histograms for NDBI values within the city boundary.
The script selects the least cloudy Landsat 8 image within a specified date range and geographic region for potential use in land cover analysis or as input for further processing.

The script analyzes Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data over Wuhan to compute NDVI and NDRI indices, masks water using NDWI, estimates fractional vegetation cover (FVC) and rockiness (Fr), classifies rocky desertification severity into six levels (from no to extreme), and generates a legend, histogram, and area statistics for each class.

The script detects active fire occurrences in Hubei province, specifically within urban land cover areas, using MODIS Fire Mask data from 2013 to 2016. It analyzes monthly fire frequency by applying a threshold (FireMask > 8) and masks results with urban land cover derived from MCD12Q1. Outputs are regional fire counts per month for 2013, and composite fire maps for January 2014 and February 2016.
task_name: Detect fire occurrences in urban areas

task_description: The script identifies cultivated areas by analyzing Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data using NDWI and NDVI indices, applying cloud masking and neighborhood smoothing, with temporal filtering across multiple seasonal periods between 2018 and 2020, focusing on a region around Chongming Island.
task_name: Identify cultivated areas using spectral indices

task_description: The script identifies high tide water extent and generates median composite imagery using Landsat and Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from 2021, applying percentile filtering and MNDWI-based quality mosaicking over the JJiang region.

The script analyzes surface soil moisture from SMAP data and compares Normalized Burn Ratio Index (NBI) with NDVI derived from Sentinel-2 to assess land surface conditions, specifically focusing on soil moisture and vegetation-burn ratio relationships in April and November 2020.
task_name: Analyze soil moisture and vegetation index

task_description: The script analyzes surface water dynamics at Jagersfontein using NDWI derived from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data between August and September 2022, generating temporal composites including mean, median, and mode images to assess water presence and variability within a defined area of interest.

The script calculates the total area of a region (roi_AF) in square kilometers and maps burned areas within that region for the year 2020 using the FireCCI51 dataset. It computes the spatial extent of fire occurrence by binarizing the BurnDate band (values >1 set to 1), mosaics the images, clips to the region of interest, and calculates the total burned area in square kilometers through a grouped reduction by pixel class.

The script detects snow/ice melt states using SAR imagery from Sentinel-1 by analyzing changes in HH backscatter between winter reference and melt period images, applying a threshold-based change detection method, and classifying the results using SVM with training and validation points. The output is a classified mosaic indicating 'Melt' and 'Unmelt' areas for region 3.

The script analyzes vegetation health using NDVI derived from Sentinel-2 imagery, creating both a median composite and a quality mosaic based on maximum NDVI values over the specified period and region.

The script classifies land cover into water and vegetation using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data and supervised machine learning classifiers (Random Forest and SVM). It trains on user-defined feature collections of water and vegetation polygons, then generates a classified land cover map for the region of interest.

The script calculates NDVI from NAIP imagery using near-infrared and red bands, thresholds the NDVI to identify vegetated areas (NDVI > 0.25), labels connected components to group contiguous vegetation patches, and converts the labeled regions into vector features for mapping.

The script classifies land cover types for the year 2019 using a percentile composite of Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data and a CART-trained random forest classifier, based on training samples from ROI, producing a predicted land cover map styled with specific color-coded classes including tree cover, shrubland, cropland, built-up, water, and others.

The script calculates mean elevation from the NED 10m dataset within HUC06 watershed boundaries, interprets it as a proxy for precipitation (labeled 'prcp'), computes the total water volume per watershed by multiplying area and precipitation depth, then identifies the top three watersheds with the highest estimated volume. The output includes a list of names of these high-volume watersheds.

The script identifies winter wheat cultivation areas by analyzing time-series NDVI data derived from MODIS surface reflectance, applying Savitzky-Golay filtering and phenology-based thresholds using heading, seeding, and harvesting dates estimated from latitude and elevation. The output is a binary map indicating the presence of winter wheat.

The script calculates and masks the difference between DSM and DEM data to identify above-ground structures, specifically buildings, by remapping GHSL data to isolate built-up areas and applying a height threshold mask where elevation difference is greater than zero.

The script identifies surface water extent using AWEI_nsh, AWEI_sh, and mNDWI water indices derived from top-of-atmosphere reflectance Landsat 8 imagery over a specific region and date range, masking clouds and calculating water area per pixel.

The script classifies land cover into urban, bare soil, water, and vegetation categories using a Random Forest classifier applied to spectral indices (NDVI, NDBI, MNDWI, BSI) derived from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data over a selected urban area for the year 2019.

The script identifies and maps burned areas within the subhumid deciduous forest of Chiquitania by analyzing MODIS MCD64A1 fire data from 2000 to 2020, applying uncertainty filtering (≤25), temporal segmentation, masking, and vectorization to extract persistent fire-affected regions not overlapping with prior burns.
task_name: Identify burned areas in subhumid forest

task_description: The script classifies land cover into 10 distinct categories using a pre-trained AI model (blindspot_hype_ensemble2) applied to atmospherically corrected Landsat 8 surface reflectance data. The classification is based on spectral, temporal (seasonal), elevation, and latitude features, with cloud and cloud shadow masked out. The output is a single mean-predicted land cover image where each pixel represents the most frequent predicted class across the time series.

The script identifies winter wheat cultivation areas by analyzing time-series NDVI data derived from Sentinel-2, applying Savitzky-Golay filtering and phenology-based thresholds using seeding, heading, and harvesting stages modeled from latitude and elevation.

The script classifies rice cultivation areas in Heilongjiang Province using a precomputed composite image (compositeEppf) and a support vector machine (SVM) classifier trained on labeled regions of interest. The output is a binary classification map where rice areas are identified (class 0), and the total area of rice cultivation is computed in square kilometers within a specified geometry (haerbin).

The script downscales annual winter precipitation data from PRISM climate datasets using SRTM and NED elevation data as predictors through a regression-based neighborhood resampling method, producing a high-resolution precipitation map clipped to a specified boundary.

The script identifies pest-infected and healthy tree areas by generating training points from stratified sampling and spectral-temporal metrics derived from CCDC analysis, using forest change and tree cover data to label tree health status, then extracts time-series coefficients for model training. The output is a labeled geospatial dataset of tree points (pest vs. healthy) with spectral predictors for classification modeling.

The script computes an Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI) composite using Landsat surface reflectance data for the state of Wyoming in the year 1984, applying cloud masking and quality-based mosaicking to generate a single cloud-cleared image representing peak vegetation conditions.

The script models land use and land cover (LUCC) changes for the year 2013 by analyzing Landsat 8 surface reflectance data, applying cloud masking, and using transition rules between classes (e.g., city to water, crop to grass) based on predefined spatial masks. The output is a classified LUCC map for 2013 with updated transitions stored as an Earth Engine asset.

The script analyzes changes in cheatgrass-dominated vegetation using pre- and post-fire Sentinel-2 imagery by computing spectral indices (NDVI, EVI, MSAVI, NDWI) and tasseled cap components (TCB, TCW, TCG), then calculates difference images to assess fire-induced vegetation change within the Cameron Peak Fire region.

The script maps the spatial extent of marshlands annually from 1986 to 2020 using Landsat surface reflectance data, applying NDVI and NDWI for vegetation and water detection, with manual polygon feature collections representing marsh areas for each year.

The script estimates Land Surface Temperature (LST) from Landsat 8 Surface Reflectance data using NDVI, fractional vegetation cover, and emissivity modeling, with thermal band brightness temperature and atmospheric correction via a radiative transfer equation.

The script classifies land cover into three categories—likely agriculture (yellow), vegetation (green), and water (blue)—using a Random Forest classifier trained on Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from 2019, with training samples collected from user-defined points and applied to a median composite image clipped to a municipal boundary in Pará, Brazil.

The script filters a Landsat 8 TOA reflectance image collection based on SUN_ELEVATION, applying a multiplication factor of 2 to images with sun elevation less than 40 degrees, while leaving others unchanged, then merges the processed subsets. It also performs mathematical operations (squaring, multiplication, odd number filtering) on a numeric list as a demonstration of client-server computation logic in Earth Engine.
task_name: Process Landsat collection by sun elevation

task_description: The script generates a median RGB composite image from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data for summer months (June–September) of 2016, masked for clouds and scaled, over a defined region in North America.

The script calculates the NDVI growth trend of winter wheat in selected cities of Shandong Province by comparing current-phase Sentinel-2 NDVI with historical median NDVI from a user-defined year range, producing a classified growth status map (very poor to very good) based on NDVI difference masked by a winter wheat distribution layer.

The script estimates water quality parameters including Total Suspended Solids (TSS), Chlorophyll-a (chl_a), and Colored Dissolved Organic Matter (CDOM) using Sentinel-2 imagery from 2018, applying band math and masking cloudy pixels and non-water areas via Automated Water Extraction Index (AWEI).

The script combines multiple DSM images into a mosaic, clips it to a specified geometry, and uses GHSL classification data to mask the DSM for built-up areas and specific building types. It then remaps building heights and identifies areas with buildings (ID=1) to create masked DSM layers. Finally, it calculates the mean DSM value within regions defined by 'floor' features, likely representing administrative or land-use units, focusing on built land and specific building categories.

The script identifies vegetated areas by computing NDVI from NAIP imagery using near-infrared and red bands, applying a threshold (NDVI > 0.25), labeling connected components, and converting the result into vector polygons representing contiguous vegetation patches.

The script filters MODIS MCD43A4 data for 2018 and applies a bitmask to exclude pixels with poor quality (quality values 3 or 255) in the BRDF_Albedo_Band_Mandatory_Quality_Band1 band, specifically targeting unreliable surface reflectance observations due to BRDF processing issues.

The script calculates the aridity index for Sri Lanka in 2011 by dividing annual accumulated CHIRPS precipitation by annual summed potential evapotranspiration (PET), scaled appropriately, and clipping to the country boundary. The output is a mapped aridity index layer with values classified into a color palette ranging from dry (red) to wet (blue).
task_name: Calculate aridity index from precipitation and PET

task_description: The script identifies areas with low vegetation density by computing NDVI from Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data, applying a threshold (NDVI < 0.2), removing isolated pixels through connected component analysis, and producing a cleaned binary mask of low-vegetation regions within a specified polygon.

The script classifies soybean cultivation areas using a Random Forest classifier trained on multi-temporal Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data, with spectral indices (NDVI, EVI, GCVI, LSWI, BSI, PSRI) and bands (B11, B12) derived from four time periods in 2018 and 2019. The output is a classified raster map of soybean presence (remapped to class 1) within the Nenjiang region, validated using accuracy metrics including confusion matrix, user accuracy, producer accuracy, overall accuracy, and kappa coefficient.

The script calculates NDVI from Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data, clips the first NDVI image to a feature collection of irrigation perimeters (VAOs), and computes the median NDVI value within each perimeter using reduceRegions. The output is a printed FeatureCollection with median NDVI values for each VAO.

The script identifies surface water extent in the Arkavathy basin using Sentinel-1 SAR imagery by applying a refined Lee filter for speckle reduction and thresholding on the VH polarization band in decibel units.

The script evaluates the accuracy of fire detection by comparing FireMask values from two MODIS collections (MOD04 and MYD04) against a predicted fire image, computing confusion matrix metrics (true positives, false positives, false negatives, true negatives), and deriving accuracy, precision, sensitivity, and specificity within the Australian region.

The script extracts daytime and nighttime land surface temperature (LST) values from both Terra and Aqua MODIS sensors, filtered by a user-defined shapefile boundary and a date range from 2003 to 2020, including quality control bands for day and night observations.

The script calculates the depth distribution within a future reservoir by subtracting a specified water level (103 meters) from SRTM elevation data, clips it to the reservoir geometry, and computes the mean depth. It also generates histograms of elevation and depth values for analysis.

The script identifies potential flooding areas by comparing median-filtered VV polarization backscatter from Sentinel-1 GRD images before and after a flood event in October 2019, using a threshold on the difference to detect significant decreases in radar signal indicative of surface water increase.

The script classifies the presence of algae in a water body using Landsat 8 surface reflectance data, applying NDSI and RGND indices to mask non-water and non-algae pixels, then trains and applies an SVM classifier on labeled polygon samples to distinguish algae from non-algae areas.

The script analyzes seasonal vegetation dynamics in Cameroon by computing and comparing median NDVI values from Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8 surface reflectance data during dry and wet seasons (2019–2020), applying cloud masking and temporal compositing to generate true-color and NDVI-enhanced visualizations for change detection.

The script classifies the probability of disease cases using a random forest model trained on NDVI from Landsat 8, elevation from SRTM, and land surface temperature from MODIS, with case locations as training data. The output is a continuous probability map derived from the classification.

The script classifies land cover into four categories—water, forest, plantations (mislabelled as urban), and cities (mislabelled as crops)—using Sentinel-1 SAR data. It applies sigma-to-gamma correction, spatial filtering with a boxcar kernel, and trains a Random Forest classifier on manually defined training regions, producing a classified raster map and accuracy metrics including confusion matrix, overall accuracy, and kappa coefficient.

The script classifies land cover types by training a Random Forest model on dNBR (difference Normalized Burn Ratio) values derived from satellite imagery, using reference points labeled as 'stable' and 'burn'. The output includes the trained classifier, confusion matrix, overall accuracy, consumer's accuracy, producer's accuracy, and kappa coefficient for model evaluation.

The script classifies land cover into urban, water, and vegetation classes using a Random Forest classifier trained on Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data from 2016, producing a classified land cover map and evaluating classification accuracy with a confusion matrix and holdout validation.

The script analyzes vegetation dynamics by computing NDVI and generating a quality mosaic from Sentinel-2 imagery over multiple time periods between April and November 2021, combining mean reflectance composites from specific dates with an NDVI-based optimal pixel selection to create a synthesized multi-temporal image stack for agricultural or land cover monitoring.

The script identifies the first image from a Sentinel-2 surface reflectance collection in the blue band (B2), creates a mask of pixels with values greater than 1000 in the most recent image, and computes the pixel-wise maximum between the first image and the masked layer. The output is a composite image highlighting areas of high reflectance in the blue band, potentially indicating bright surfaces such as clouds, snow, or urban features.
task_name: Identify high-reflectance pixels in blue band

task_description: The script computes Tasseled Cap transformations (brightness, greenness, wetness) from Landsat 5 surface reflectance data for three time points (1990, 1997, 1999), calculates change magnitudes between consecutive periods, and classifies land cover changes into four types: regrowth, deforestation, biomass loss, and burning or water-related changes based on thresholds in brightness and greenness differences.
task_name: Detect land cover change using Tasseled Cap

task_description: The script classifies land cover into categories including Vegetation, Built-up Areas, Water Bodies, and Agriculture using multi-temporal Landsat surface reflectance data, NDVI, NDWI, and Random Forest classification. It also computes area statistics per class within a study region.

The script calculates the mean sea surface temperature (SST) for a specific date (June 27) across multiple years (1982–2020) within a defined geographic region (geomTOres), using NOAA OISST data. The output is a time-series of mean SST values printed for each year on that date.

The script calculates the maximum NDVI value from Landsat 8 32-day composite images in 2014, then computes the mean NDVI over the state of Gujarat using reduceRegion, outputting the average NDVI value.

The script estimates daily NOx emissions in Hubei Province by analyzing MODIS and MYD fire radiative power (MaxFRP) data, combining it with land cover types (rice, other crops, urban), temporal emission profiles, and crop-specific emission factors. The output includes monthly summed NOx emissions (in metric tons) for May through October 2015.
task_name: Estimate NOx emissions from fire radiative power

task_description: The script computes a median NDVI composite from Landsat 5 Surface Reflectance data within a user-defined area and time period, applying cloud masking and filtering by maximum cloud cover. The output is a clipped NDVI median image collection used for vegetation analysis.

The script analyzes wildfire burn severity by computing Normalized Burn Ratio (NBR) from pre- and post-fire Landsat 8 surface reflectance images within the Mad River Complex fire perimeter, comparing vegetation condition before and after the event.

The script evaluates the accuracy of a pre-trained land cover classification map for the Arkavathy region using ground control points. It splits the GCPs into training and validation sets, samples the classified image with validation points, and computes a confusion matrix, overall accuracy, producer's and consumer's accuracies, and kappa coefficient to assess classification performance.

The script computes long-term averages and standard deviations of near-infrared (nir) and shortwave infrared (swir1) bands from satellite imagery over a buffered region around Laos' administrative boundary, generating a composite image representing mean and variability of these spectral bands from 2000 to 2010.

The script analyzes long-term Landsat surface reflectance data to compute NDVI anomalies by comparing post-2010 observations against a 2002–2005 reference period, identifying areas with significant vegetation decline trends through cumulative anomaly detection.

The script performs supervised land cover classification using Sentinel-2 imagery over Luang Prabang province, training a CART classifier on user-defined regions of water, teak forest, other forests, and other lands, then classifying the image into these four land cover categories.

The script detects time periods with active fires within a specified region by analyzing thermal anomalies (T21) from the FIRMS dataset between June and September 2022. It aggregates fire pixel counts in 5-day intervals and outputs dates where fires were detected.

The script calculates the Clumping Index (CI) using MODIS BRDF albedo parameters, FCOVER data, and GLC2000 land cover classification. It processes daily, monthly, and yearly composites of CI with quality filtering, angular correction, and phenology-based smoothing using Savitzky-Golay filtering, outputting masked and calibrated CI images.
task_name: Estimate clumping index from MODIS BRDF

task_description: The script estimates daily NOx emissions from agricultural and urban fire radiative power (FRP) using MODIS and MYD data over Hubei Province between May and October 2016. It calculates emissions by applying emission factors and combustion rates to FRP values, partitioned by land cover types (rice, other crops, urban), and outputs monthly aggregated NOx emissions in gigagrams.

The script analyzes vegetation health in a region of Colorado, USA, using Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI) derived from both Landsat 8 and Sentinel-2 satellite data for June 2021. It generates true-color composites and EVI maps to compare vegetation conditions, with specific focus on a clipped region of interest (ROI) near the Front Range.

The script identifies surface water extent using NDWI (Normalized Difference Water Index) derived from Landsat 5 SR data, applying a threshold of -0.3 to classify water pixels for the years 2000 and 2011 within a study area.

The script maps annual forest loss due to fires in Europe from 2001 to 2021 using a custom-generated image collection, clips the data to a user-defined study region, applies spatial smoothing with median filters, and generates a histogram of fire-related forest loss values within the region. Outputs include visualizations of the original and smoothed fire loss layers and a statistical histogram for analysis.

The script classifies coniferous forest types (gaoshansong and yunnansong) using a fusion image masked by 'imageyls', computing a spectral index (NDVIre3) based on B8 and B7 bands, then applying Otsu's method to threshold the index values within a region of interest (roi), resulting in two binary classes representing different forest types.

The script generates a monthly time series of maximum NDVI values by aggregating MOD13A1 data from January 2000 to December 2021, producing one image per month where each pixel represents the highest NDVI value observed in that month. The output is an ImageCollection with images labeled by their start date in milliseconds.

The script classifies land cover types using a random forest classifier trained on spectral indices and Landsat 8 surface reflectance bands, with validation performed on labeled training polygons. Outputs include classified imagery, accuracy metrics (overall accuracy, kappa, user's and producer's accuracy), and an error matrix.

The script classifies land cover types in Jorhat using Sentinel-2 imagery by computing NDVI and NDBI indices, training a Random Forest classifier on labeled regions, and generating a classified map with accuracy assessment via confusion matrix.

The script calculates spatially explicit, crop-specific emission factors by combining land cover dominance data with agricultural area statistics and crop-specific emission factors, producing a per-pixel weighted emission factor map for major crops across Chinese provinces.

The script calculates mean, standard deviation, and pixel count of EVI values within forest-type (land cover classes 1–6) and grass-type (land cover classes 7–10) areas inside a defined study region using MODIS land cover classification and MCD43A4 EVI data from a single date.
task_name: Analyze EVI for forest and grass types

task_description: The script computes a refined Lee filtered mean SAR image from Copernicus Sentinel-1 GRD data in HH polarization for December 2015, applying despeckling to enhance surface texture interpretation over a user-defined region of interest.
task_name: Filter SAR imagery for surface texture

task_description: The script fuses Sentinel-1 SAR data (VV, VH) and Sentinel-2 multispectral data (12 bands) through Principal Component Analysis (PCA), using the first principal component to create a fused image product that integrates structural and spectral information for land surface analysis.
task_name: Fuse Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 for PCA

task_description: The script classifies urban land cover into six classes—water, high vegetation, exposed soil, low vegetation, built-up areas, and roads—using Sentinel-2 imagery and a Random Forest classifier. It computes NDVI, EVI, and NDBI indices, trains the model using labeled feature collections, evaluates accuracy with validation and test sets, and outputs a classified map with a legend.

The script calculates top-of-atmosphere (TOA) reflectance from Landsat 8 raw digital numbers for the Ankara province between October 25 and October 28, 2018, and attempts to add random albedo calculations on points, though with a logical error in implementation. The output includes metadata of filtered Landsat images and visualizations of TOA reflectance and erroneous albedo layers.

The script identifies red snow algal blooms on glacier surfaces using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data, applying a multi-step filtering and masking workflow based on spectral indices (NDSI, RGND, GBND), saturation thresholds, cloud/snow conditions, solar geometry, and spatial despeckling to isolate valid algal bloom pixels. The output is a feature collection of sample points representing likely red snow algae occurrences.
task_name: Identify red snow algae on glaciers

task_description: The script calculates NDVI for a Landsat 7 5-year composite (1999–2003) to assess vegetation conditions, computes the difference and squared difference between two Landsat 7 composites (1999–2003 and 2008–2012) for change detection, and calculates EVI from a Landsat 8 TOA image (2014) to evaluate vegetation health using a spectral index.
