It selects optimal pre- and post-fire images based on cloud coverage, temporal lag, and suitability scoring, then calculates NBR for reference images and derives dNBR for each fire event within a specified region and time frame.

The script computes maximum NDVI values from Landsat 8 surface reflectance data for two time periods (2013-04-11 to 2015-12-31 and 2016-01-01 to 2018-03-12), then calculates the difference between the two resulting composites to assess changes in vegetation greenness over time. Outputs include visualizations of max NDVI for each period and their difference.

The script calculates soil field capacity (FC) in mm by combining soil moisture content at 33 kPa and bulk density across multiple depth layers, then derives the water holding capacity (WHC) by subtracting temporary wilting point (TLP) from FC, all resampled to 250m resolution and clipped to Indonesia's provincial boundary.
task_name: Estimate field capacity and water holding capacity

task_description: The script classifies land cover in Exmoor National Park using Dynamic World v1 surface reflectance data from April to June 2021, computes a mode-reduced land cover composite, extracts built areas (class label 6), and calculates the percentage of built area within the region by comparing masked and total pixel counts. It also outputs per-class pixel counts with formatted labels for analysis.
task_name: Classify land cover and quantify built area

task_description: The script detects land cover changes by applying spectral mixture analysis (SMA) to Landsat data, computing fractional components (green vegetation, non-photovoltaic vegetation, soil, shade), generating a Cloud Shadow Fraction (CSF), and combining it with probability-based classification to identify changes between two time periods. Outputs include classified change maps, probability layers, and training samples for water-related classes.
task_name: Detect land cover change using spectral unmixing

task_description: The script estimates tree cover density by training a Random Forest regression model using Landsat 8 surface reflectance data and ALOS PALSAR SAR backscatter (HH and HV) as input features, calibrated with the UMD Hansen tree cover data for year 2000, then applies the model to classify tree cover density over a region in South America.

The script extracts median surface reflectance values from Sentinel-2 MSI bands B2, B3, and B4 at 10 specified point locations within a region of interest after cloud masking and temporal compositing for July–August 2019. The output is a CSV file containing point IDs, coordinates, and corresponding spectral values.
task_name: Extract surface reflectance values at sample points

task_description: The script analyzes monthly nighttime light intensity from VIIRS DNB data over a global latitudinal range between 78°N and 58°S for the year 2016, computing the sum of radiance values and identifying areas with average radiance greater than 50. It also calculates the difference between peak annual radiance and individual monthly images, mapping these differences along with the month of acquisition and radiance deviation.

The script classifies land cover into three classes (urban, rural, and native vegetation) using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data within defined parcels. It trains a Random Forest classifier on sampled regions and applies it to generate a classified land cover map.

The script identifies snow-covered bare soil areas by combining NDSI from MOD09GA, snow cover from MOD10A1, and reflectance thresholds on MODIS bands to mask non-bare surfaces and detect snow presence.

The script classifies land use and land cover (LULC) for Dharan in 2001 and 2019 using Landsat imagery, trains CART and MaxEnt classifiers with training samples, evaluates accuracy via confusion matrices, and computes LULC change between the two years by combining classified images.

The script classifies land cover types in the United States using a Random Forest classifier trained on NDVI from Landsat, meteorological variables from ERA5, soil moisture and temperature from FLDAS, and GFSAD1000 for labels. The output is a classified land cover map and accuracy assessments via confusion matrices.
task_name: Classify land cover using satellite and climate data

task_description: The script classifies oil palm plantations by analyzing Sentinel-2 and Landsat-8 surface reflectance data, using NDBI, EVI, and NDWI indices to distinguish built-up areas, vegetation, and bare land, with additional masking from terrain slope and radar data. Output includes classified land cover maps, RGB composites, and build-up detection layers.

The script computes the ratio of VV to VH polarization from Sentinel-1 SAR data, generating a median composite of this ratio over the study area for the year 2020. It processes ascending orbit data, masks out noisy pixels below -30 dB, and outputs a multi-temporal median image with the derived VV/VH band.

The script identifies areas with high vegetation density by computing the maximum NDVI from Landsat 8 images over a one-year period, then classifies these into zones based on NDVI thresholds within a 30km radius around a point in southern Spain.

The script performs land cover classification using Landsat surface reflectance and top-of-atmosphere data from 1987 to 2020, focusing on the GRID1 region in Egypt. It computes NDVI and MSAVI2 vegetation indices and applies a custom classification algorithm (PINO1) to map land cover types such as water, clouds, shadows, bare soil, and vegetation. The primary outputs are median composite images of MSAVI2 and NDVI, along with a time-series analysis of classified imagery for the year 2015.
task_name: Classify land cover using spectral indices

task_description: The script creates a median composite image from a cloud-masked Landsat 8 TOA reflectance collection over a specified region and time period, applying a BQA-based cloud mask to improve data quality before compositing.

The script identifies burned areas by calculating the Normalized Burn Ratio (NBR) from Landsat 8 surface reflectance data, applying a cloud masking function, and classifying pixels based on NBR thresholds to detect fire-affected regions within specific map sheets in Brazil.

The script creates a land mask using the SWIR band (B11) to exclude water pixels from a Sentinel-2 surface reflectance image, then demonstrates different unmasking techniques: filling masked areas with a constant value, restoring the original footprint, and replacing masked pixels with data from another Sentinel-2 image taken on a different date.

The script classifies land cover types by training a Random Forest model on monthly maximum NDVI, B8 (NIR), and LCI (Leaf Chlorophyll Index) values derived from Sentinel-2 imagery. The classification uses a merged feature collection of various agricultural, forest, water, barren, built-up, and other land cover classes, with temporal stacking of monthly composites from 2018 to 2020 for multi-temporal analysis.
task_name: Classify land cover using time-series indices

task_description: The script calculates the area (in hectares) of each Natural Habitat (NNH) class (1 to 4) within 50km buffers around point features by rasterizing ecoregions, computing pixel areas, and summarizing regions using reduceRegions. Outputs include classified habitat rasters, buffered geometries with area, and zonal statistics of habitat areas per buffer.
task_name: Calculate NNH ecoregion area in buffers

task_description: The script calculates NDVI and a Soil-Adjusted Residual Index (SRI1) from Landsat 8 surface reflectance data over Juazeiro in 2019, then derives a Crop Condition Estimate (CE) using a polynomial function of SRI1. It outputs time-series NDVI data, single-date reflectance layers, and spatial visualizations of NDVI, SRI1, and CE for agricultural monitoring.
task_name: Estimate crop condition using NDVI and SRI1

task_description: The script retrieves the first Sentinel-2 image with the least cloud cover between February and March 2018 within a specified point, selects its B4 (red band) reflectance, and extracts the pixel's longitude and latitude values along with the B4 value at that location.

The script identifies surface water areas by applying a threshold of -14 dB on the VV polarization band from Sentinel-1 GRD imagery, using maximum value compositing over a 21-day period in January 2019. The output includes a binary water mask and mosaicked VV and VH backscatter images clipped to the study area.

The script models the seasonal dynamics of Leaf Area Index (LAI) using a double-logistic function fitted to MODIS MOD15A2H data from 2001, comparing original and reconstructed LAI values at a specific point within the region of interest.

The script identifies intersections between farm points buffered by farm area and protected areas from the WDPA dataset, mapping which farm locations potentially overlap with designated protected polygons.

The script identifies rubber plantations in Cambodia by training a Random Forest classifier on a multi-band composite image from 2018, including spectral indices, topography, JRC water data, and vegetation metrics, then outputs a probability-based land cover classification map clipped to Cambodia.

The script detects the timing of forest disturbances in the Amazon using CCD (Continuous Change Detection) results derived from Landsat time series, applying post-processing masks based on magnitude, intercept ratios, and spatial consistency to refine change year estimates. The output is a mapped year of first detected disturbance between 1989 and 2019, masked by multiple criteria for accuracy improvement.

The script analyzes temporal changes in SAR backscatter and computes a VH/VV ratio (SAR Vegetation Index) over Iloilo, Philippines, using Sentinel-1 GRD data from 2019. It generates a three-period composite image stack (April–May, June–August, September–November) for visual interpretation and enables interactive time series inspection of VH, VV, and VH/VV ratio at user-clicked locations.

The script classifies mangrove forest areas using Landsat TOA reflectance data and a Random Forest classifier trained on sampled regions. It evaluates classification accuracy with confusion matrices and computes precision, recall, F-score, and specificity. The final output is a classified image for the year 2016 centered on a specified point.

The script identifies surface water extent in Argentina by analyzing minimum backscatter values from Sentinel-1 GRD data, applying thresholds on VV (less than -15 dB) and VH (less than -21 dB) polarization bands over the period from October 2018 to May 2019.
task_name: Identify surface water extent using Sentinel-1 VV and VH

task_description: The script calculates mean monthly evapotranspiration (ET) from MOD16A2 data within a specified grid cell over the period 2000–2015, generating a multi-band image where each band represents the monthly average ET for a specific month and year, clipped to the 'SC-24-V-D' grid cell in the Caatinga biome.

The script analyzes the number of valid observations in a daily NDVI time series over agricultural fields in Trentino, Italy, by masking clouds and shadows from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data and counting non-masked pixels across the composite period.
task_name: Analyze valid pixel count for NDVI time series

task_description: The script corrects rice field data for Serang District (AOI) by reclassifying the maximum EVI values derived from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance images. Pixels with EVI less than 0.41 are classified as non-rice areas and masked out to enhance accuracy of rice field mapping.
task_name: Reclassify EVI max for rice fields

task_description: The script classifies land cover types using spectral unmixing, NDFI, and a decision tree applied to Landsat 8 surface reflectance data over a specific grid in Peru for the year 2018. Outputs include a classified map with categories such as forest, water, clouds/shadow, and other land covers, along with a composite image containing multiple vegetation indices, fraction layers, terrain attributes, and masks.

The script classifies land cover into four categories—bare soil, urban, vegetation, and water—using a random forest classifier trained on Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data from 2015, then applies the model to classify both 2015 and 2016 images.

The script quantifies forest loss within and around Mt. Malindang by analyzing the Global Forest Change (GFC) dataset, calculating total forest loss in hectares inside the protected area and in 1000 m, 2000 m, and 3000 m buffer zones surrounding it.
task_name: Quantify forest loss around protected area

task_description: The script generates a cloud-free Sentinel-2 image composite for February 2022 over the Sundarbans by applying cloud masking, percentile-based band selection (VNIR at 35th percentile, NDVI at 90th percentile), and computes enhanced vegetation index (EVI) and NDVI. The output is a surface-reflectance mosaic with optimized vegetation indices for analysis.
task_name: Generate cloud-free composite with NDVI and EVI

task_description: The script classifies land cover into categories including land, snow, vegetation, and water using NDVI, NDWI, and NDSI indices derived from satellite imagery. It processes images with less than 10% cloud cover between April and December 2013 over a region in China, generating a mosaic for each image where different land cover types are encoded by distinct pixel values based on thresholded spectral indices.

The script calculates the Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI) at monthly and 16-day intervals using CHIRPS precipitation data, generating time series image collections for drought monitoring over Ninh Thuan province, Vietnam.

The script classifies land cover into six categories (built-up, water, sea, vegetation, bare land, agricultural) using a CART classifier applied to a median composite of Landsat 8 surface reflectance bands and NDVI in Seoul for autumn 2017.

The script classifies land cover types in Guarulhos, São Paulo, using Sentinel-2 imagery and machine learning (Random Forest), producing a classified map with seven classes: Forest, Water, Exposed Soil, Urban, Field, Industrial, and Main Roads, validated with accuracy assessment and error matrix.

The script calculates and compares NDVI values from two Landsat images acquired in different years (1989 and 2018) over a specific location, generating NDVI maps for each date and computing their difference to assess changes in vegetation greenness over time.

The script analyzes time series of Sentinel-1 VH and VV backscatter from ascending passes over burned and unburned forest areas in Montiferru, Sardinia, to assess post-fire vegetation changes using median values extracted from sampled polygons.

The script computes and analyzes the Green Chlorophyll Vegetation Index (GCVI) and Land Surface Water Index (LSWI) from Sentinel-2 imagery over a one-year period, generating weekly composites to derive temporal statistics (mean, median, standard deviation, percentiles) for vegetation and moisture conditions. It outputs a single composite image asset containing these statistical summaries, masked by cloud-filtered data and clipped to a geographic boundary.

The script extracts sea salinity at 0-meter depth from the HYCOM ocean model dataset for the period December 28 to December 31, 2020, converting the time-series image collection into a band-wise composite image where each band represents a daily salinity observation.

The script identifies plantation areas by combining and comparing two land cover classifications: one from a CCDC-SMA forest disturbance map and another from an RLCMS land cover product for 2018, generating maps showing overlapping and individual plantation detections.

The script estimates aboveground biomass density (AGBD) in the Amazon rainforest using GEDI full-power waveform LiDAR observations filtered by date and region, then spatially aggregates the point measurements into a gridded image mosaic at 30m resolution using Landsat 8-derived projection as reference.

The script creates a median false-colour composite image using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data with bands B11, B8, and B2, masked for clouds, covering Iloilo, Philippines, from March 2019 to March 2020.

The script generates a median composite of cloud-cleared, top-of-atmosphere reflectance imagery from Landsat 8 for a specified region and time period, filtered to low cloud cover, intended for land surface analysis.
task_name: Generate median composite of Landsat imagery

task_description: The script calculates NDVI from Sentinel-2 imagery during the mid-year period (day of year 153–273) over a 2-year span (2016–2017), focusing on a buffered point location, and generates a median NDVI composite image for that region and time frame.

The script identifies compound climate extremes by detecting regions with extreme high temperature (lowest 3rd percentile rank) and extreme low precipitation (highest 3rd percentile rank) annually from 2001 to 2022, then analyzes the impact of these extremes on vegetation (via kNDVI anomalies) across major land cover types, producing spatial blobs of compound events and scatterplots of temperature-kNDVI relationships.

The script extracts and processes administrative sub-district (Kecamatan) boundaries from a custom feature collection for Indonesia in 2010, filters them by PLU_ID or name, converts them to raster format, and generates metadata such as centroid, ID, and name. It also creates an interactive UI panel for selecting provinces, districts, and sub-districts.

The script identifies changes in vegetation between two time periods (2014–2015 and 2019–2020) using NDVI derived from Landsat 8 TOA imagery, computing the difference to classify areas with positive change, negative change, or no change within the Ocaso sector. Outputs include a classified change mosaic map (green for increase, red for decrease, white for no change), a continuous NDVI difference layer, and the total area (in hectares) of each change category.

The script calculates the mean NDVI value within a specified polygon for the years 2002 and 2008 using MODIS MOD13Q1 data, comparing vegetation conditions between these two years by computing regional averages through reduceRegion.

The script creates a median composite image from Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data within a specified region and time period, filtering scenes by date and low cloud cover to produce a clean, representative surface reflectance image.

The script extracts a 60-day backward time series of daily precipitation values ending on a specific acquisition date derived from a feature's 'acq_date' property, formats the date, and samples the precipitation data at the feature's geometry to count the number of consecutive zero-precipitation days starting from the end of the period.

The script identifies the year of forest disturbance in the Amazon between 2000 and 2019 by comparing multiple datasets: a custom-coded disturbance map, JRC TMF degradation year, UMD forest loss year, and CCD-based tBreak change detection, all masked to intact forest areas and overlapping time range.

The script computes a median surface reflectance composite from Landsat 5 TM data between 2000 and 2001 over Vietnam, applying Bidirectional Reflectance Distribution Function (BRDF) correction to reduce angular illumination effects, masking clouds and poor-quality pixels using pixel QA and a cloud scoring algorithm, resulting in a visually enhanced true-color image suitable for surface analysis.

The script calculates annual mean, standard deviation, coefficient of variation (CV), and IPSE (a derived vegetation stability index) from MODIS NDVI data between 2000 and 2020, then computes interannual mean and standard deviation of IPSE. Outputs include multi-band images of annual metrics and final reduced images representing interannual patterns of vegetation dynamics over a defined region.

The script detects changes in benthic green vegetation using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from 2017 to 2020, applying atmospheric correction, water masking via NDWI, depth normalization using a reef depth model, and temporal differencing between two composites (2017–2020 and extended to April 2020), with final outputs masked by benthic presence and brightness thresholds.

The script classifies land cover into seven categories (urban, vegetation, sawah, tubuh_air, lahan_basah, tanah_terbuka, ladangtegalan) using Landsat 8 surface reflectance data from two seasons (dry and wet), computing spectral indices (NDVI, MNDWI), incorporating SRTM elevation data, and applying a Random Forest classifier trained on labeled sample points.

The script identifies areas of tree cover loss from 2001 to 2005 using UMD Hansen forest change data and overlays 2018 GLAD deforestation alerts (from two different datasets: 00_00_SA and 01_01_SA) over a region in Brazil, calculating tree cover extent in 2000 and quantifying forest loss during the first five years of the 21st century in hectares per pixel.
task_name: Identify tree cover loss and GLAD alerts

task_description: The script computes the Built-up Index (CBI) using Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and spectral indices on Sentinel-2 imagery to extract urban/built-up areas. It applies Otsu thresholding to create a binary map of built-up vs non-built-up areas, validates the result using reference points, and evaluates classification accuracy with an error matrix.

The script computes multiple vegetation and land surface indices (NDVI, BSI, NDWI, ARVI, SAVI, EVI, IPVI, REDNESS_INDEX, VDVI, ratio, RERNDVI) from Sentinel-2 data, combines them into a stacked image, and trains a Random Forest classifier to classify land cover types. It evaluates model accuracy using training and validation datasets derived from region-based sampling.
task_name: Classify land cover using vegetation indices

task_description: The script generates a cloud-masked, noise-reduced mean composite of Landsat 7 surface reflectance imagery for summer months (June–August) between 2016 and 2018, focusing on removing shadows, clouds, and pixel-level noise to produce a clean spectral image stack for further analysis.

The script calculates the Vegetation Condition Index (VCI) from Landsat 8 SR data by computing NDVI, SRI1, and CE indices over a defined area and time period. It classifies vegetation health into five degradation scores (UD to ESD), computes the area (in km²) for each class, and calculates a Global Degradation Index (GDI) to assess the overall level of land degradation.

The script identifies and corrects isolated temporal classification errors in a land cover time series by applying a 3-year median filter logic, ensuring that single-year misclassifications surrounded by consistent classifications are adjusted to maintain temporal consistency.

The script analyzes changes in VV and VH backscatter from Sentinel-1 SAR data before and after a wildfire event (August 2021) to detect its impact on the land surface. It computes mean pre- and post-event images for both polarizations, calculates the difference (post - pre), and generates a binary change mask highlighting significant changes in VH polarization, likely indicating structural vegetation damage or surface alterations due to the fire.

The script processes Sentinel-1 GRD data over a user-defined region (TJROIboundary) to generate terrain-corrected, speckle-filtered VV and VH polarization images using the Refined Lee algorithm, focusing on ascending orbit data between September 10–14, 2019. The output includes mosaic images of backscatter intensity in decibels, clipped to the region of interest, for analysis of surface structural and moisture characteristics.

The script classifies land cover types using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data and a CART classifier trained on labeled sample points representing different land cover classes such as bofedales, construction, matorrales, and water bodies. The output is a classified raster map with distinct color-coded land cover categories.

The script classifies land cover in Dubai using Sentinel-2 imagery from January to May 2020. It trains a CART classifier on labeled training samples (Water, Vegetation, Urban, Sand, Rocks) and applies it to the first image in the filtered collection, producing a classified land use/land cover map with five classes. The result is validated using independent validation points, and an error matrix, overall accuracy, consumer's accuracy, producer's accuracy, and kappa coefficient are computed.

The script maps canopy cover distribution across a study area in Midnapore by analyzing Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data. It computes a median composite from cloud-masked images (2018–2020), calculates multiple vegetation and structural indices (NDVI, EVI, SAVI, NBR, etc.), and likely classifies or analyzes areas based on canopy density using predefined feature collections for different canopy ranges (below 10%, 10–30%, 30–70%, 70–100%) clipped to the study region.

The script analyzes the column density of carbon monoxide (CO) from Sentinel-5P satellite data over Paraguay for July and August 2020, producing a visual comparison of monthly mosaicked and clipped CO concentrations using a split-panel swipe interface in the map viewer.

The script calculates multiple spectral indices (EVI, MSAVI2, MNDWI, SR) for Mongolia using multispectral satellite imagery, focusing on vegetation health, biomass, and surface water presence. The output includes mapped layers for each index derived from band math operations.

The script performs image segmentation using the SNIC algorithm on a normalized stack of environmental and socio-economic variables to generate landscape units (clusters) within a specified region. The output includes a segmented image, cluster seeds, and vectorized segments representing homogeneous regions based on multi-thematic input layers.
task_name: Segment landscape units using environmental variables

task_description: The script calculates the maximum NDVI from Landsat 8 surface reflectance data over a one-year period, groups it by elevation zones derived from SRTM data, and computes mean NDVI values for each elevation zone within a buffered region of interest.

The script filters Landsat 8 surface reflectance images within the Republican watershed boundary for the year 2016, likely preparing for land surface or vegetation analysis using spectral indices, though no explicit index or classification is computed in the provided code.

The script calculates NDII (Normalized Difference Infrared Index) from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data to assess vegetation moisture content, standardizes it into a standardized vegetation index (SVI), and reclassifies pixels with SVI < -1.5 into a binary layer to identify areas of abnormally low vegetation moisture within the AOI.

The script classifies land cover types using Landsat 8 imagery from late August 2015 by computing NDWI, NDVI, and NDBI indices and applying a classification function to distinguish land cover classes within a defined polygon in Turkey. The output is a single classified image representing land cover categories.

The script identifies glacier zones by analyzing the median NDSI (Normalized Difference Snow Index) from Landsat 8 imagery between August and September 2013–2015, reclassifying values into non-glacier, low-confidence glacier, and high-confidence glacier areas, then masking out non-glacier regions.

The script downscales MODIS surface reflectance data to Landsat resolution using linear regression between MODIS and Landsat bands, then computes high-resolution NDVI from the fused data for improved vegetation monitoring.

The script calculates the median NDVI values within buffered pivot irrigation fields using a cloud-filtered Landsat 8 TOA image, clipping the image to the pivot areas and computing NDVI from bands B5 and B4, then summarizing the mean NDVI per pivot via reduceRegions.
task_name: Analyze median NDVI in pivot irrigation areas

task_description: The script downloads Sentinel-1 C-band SAR GRD float images in IW mode for April 2019, clipped to a specified region of interest, with backscatter values preserved as floating-point numbers.

The script analyzes Sentinel-2 imagery before and after a hail event on July 27, 2020, to assess vegetation and water content changes in a specific agricultural field (Rzepak_Hail_1520) using NDVI and NDWI differencing. Outputs include pre- and post-event false-color images, NDVI and NDWI maps, and their difference layers to detect potential crop damage.
task_name: Assess crop damage from hail event

task_description: The script identifies almond cultivation areas using the USDA NASS Cropland Data Layer for 2016, masks these areas, generates random sampling points within them, and extracts OpenET ensemble evapotranspiration and another ET dataset (Eta_Jun20) values at those points for June 2016. The final output is a CSV file of sampled points with combined ET values.

The script calculates broadband albedo and estimates snow grain size using MODIS surface reflectance and angular data, applying a radiative transfer model (ART1) and a logarithmic inversion method on snow-covered regions identified by NDSI thresholds.
task_name: Estimate snow grain size from albedo

task_description: The script creates a mosaic of selected optical bands (B2, B3, B4) from a filtered image collection over a specific region and time period, resulting in a composite image representing surface reflectance for visual analysis or download.

The script generates a median and percentile-based RGB composite from Sentinel-2 imagery over Italy for 2020, applying both cloud percentage filtering and cloud masking using QA60 band to improve image quality. Outputs include clipped true-color visualizations using B4, B3, B2 bands for both median and 25th percentile reductions.

The script classifies land cover types using Sentinel-2 imagery from November 2017, training a CART classifier on manually labeled sample regions representing different land cover classes such as fruit orchards, urban areas, forest, and horticultural zones. The output is a classified raster map showing distinct land cover categories across the study area.

The script computes an NDWI (Normalized Difference Water Index) based binary classification to identify water bodies, where pixels with NDWI ≤ 0.05 are classified as non-water (0) and others as water (1). The resulting mosaic is clipped to a region and evaluated for accuracy using validation point collections from three regions: Gambia, Canada, and Tibet. Accuracy metrics including overall accuracy, kappa coefficient, producers' and consumers' accuracy are computed and printed.

The script analyzes time-series Sentinel-2 imagery to compute and extract EVI, NDVI, NDBI, and NDWI indices over ganja cultivation locations in Indonesia from 2019 to 2022, generating monthly composites and spatial statistics for temporal vegetation monitoring.

The script accesses a MapBiomas Collection 5.0 land cover classification image, selects the 2002 classification band, and masks it to retain only pixels classified as class 5, which corresponds to forest areas. The output is a masked image layer showing forest coverage for the year 2002.
task_name: Extract forest areas from land cover map

task_description: The script calculates NDVI, EVI, and LSWI indices from Landsat 8 surface reflectance data for January 2018 over a defined region in southern Asia, likely focusing on vegetation and surface water conditions using masked imagery to exclude clouds and shadows.

The script retrieves a collection of Sentinel-2 images within a specific date range and geographic region, then performs list-based manipulations to explore image metadata and structure. It converts the image collection to a list, accesses individual images, and prints them for inspection, focusing on data handling rather than spectral analysis or feature extraction.

The script calculates the mean evapotranspiration in Fresno County, California, using OpenET data filtered by date and geographic boundary for the year 2021. The output is a raster layer representing average evapotranspiration values over the region.

The script processes the US mTPI (multi-scale Topographic Position Index) dataset by clipping it to a user-defined AOI, then resampling and reprojecting it from its original resolution to 10 meters using bilinear interpolation. The output includes visualizations of the original and resampled mTPI layers for comparison.

The script analyzes Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data before and after the Proenca-a-nova wildfire event in September–October 2020 to generate median composite images for visual assessment of burn areas and post-fire recovery using shortwave infrared, near-infrared, and red bands (B12, B8, B4).

The script identifies almond cultivation areas in 2016 by extracting cropland data from the USDA NASS CDL 2016 dataset, isolating pixels classified as almonds (code 75), remapping them to a distinct value, and clipping to a specified region (sa). It then generates random sample points within a polygon (alm_poly) to extract time series of evapotranspiration components (Ec, Es, Ei) from the PML_V2 dataset for those locations.

The script calculates the area in square kilometers of two buffered points (10 km radius) around specific geographic coordinates and also retrieves precomputed areas from a feature collection for features with IDs 206 and 1, using geometry.area() and unit conversion.

The script analyzes vegetation polygons in Rocky Mountain National Park, computing statistics such as count, total extent, mean, median, and standard deviation of patch sizes in acres. It also calculates weighted mean patch size using a weighted feature collection and performs class-specific and grouped-class analyses for specific vegetation types and groups.

The script computes median composite images from Landsat 8 Surface Reflectance data annually between 2013 and 2020, then calculates NDVI for each year to analyze vegetation dynamics over time within a specified geometry.

The script computes the Tasseled Cap Wetness (TCW) index from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data over a specific region between April and October 2018, generates a median TCW composite, and extracts TCW values at specified point locations to analyze surface wetness conditions, serving as an indicator of surface water presence and moisture.

The script calculates the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) from Landsat 8 surface reflectance data over a user-defined geometry between 2016 and 2017, then computes the pixel-wise maximum NDVI value across the time series to highlight areas of peak vegetation greenness during that period.

The script applies temporal smoothing to a land cover classification image collection by correcting isolated classifications over time using 3-year and 4-year consistency windows. It identifies pixels that revert after one or two years (e.g., class X → not X → X) and corrects intermediate years back to the stable class, producing a temporally filtered land cover sequence from 1985 to 2020.

The script computes daily mosaics of Sentinel-2 surface reflectance images, calculates NDWI using bands B8 and B12, generates a median NDWI composite over the growing season, and extracts NDWI values at specific point locations to assess surface water presence and variability.
task_name: Extract daily NDWI medians for water detection

task_description: The script calculates the Normalized Snow and Ice Index (NSMI) from Sentinel-2 data over a specific buffered field region on April 6–7, 2020, masks clouds using QA60, computes median NSMI values, and extracts mean NSMI per field for analysis. Output includes a median NSMI image and regional statistics.
task_name: Analyze recent NSMI in agricultural fields

task_description: The script identifies historical flood extents by processing Sentinel-1 GRD imagery from 2015 to 2020, applying a VV polarization-based thresholding method with median filtering and mosaicking the results into a single flood map clipped to the study area.

The script extracts metadata from a filtered Landsat ImageCollection over Suriname, including spacecraft ID, WRS path/row, acquisition date, and cloud cover, for the purpose of generating a CSV file containing image metadata relevant to surface water monitoring.

The script analyzes the difference between OpenET ensemble evapotranspiration and observed February 2016 evapotranspiration (eta_feb) over almond cultivation areas within the Firebaugh Study Area, masking for almond crops using USDA NASS CDL 2016 data and computing a monthly average ET deficit.

The script identifies high-intensity and mid-low intensity vegetation pixels using Sentinel-2 data by computing NHISWIR and NHISWNIR spectral indices and applying threshold-based classification over a specific date range and area of interest near coordinates [-75.32, 4.89].

The script performs supervised land cover classification using Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data and a Random Forest classifier. It trains the model with labeled samples (forest, water, sand, cropland, settlement, barrenland), applies it to classify the entire study area, and evaluates accuracy using a validation dataset. Outputs include a classified land use map and accuracy assessment metrics such as confusion matrix, overall accuracy, kappa coefficient, and producer/consumer accuracies.

The script calculates the total area of forest loss per year within a 10 km buffer around a point, using the Global Forest Change dataset. It outputs a dictionary mapping each year (formatted as '20XX') to the corresponding lost area in square meters, along with separate prints for areas that were lost, not lost, and total area.
task_name: Quantify forest loss area by year

task_description: The script classifies land cover types in Trinidad and Tobago using cloud-masked Landsat 7 TOA reflectance data from 2019. It trains a Random Forest classifier on user-defined training regions (Water, Grassland, Forest, Cropland, Wetland, Settlement, Otherland) and applies the model to generate a classified land cover map. The output includes the classified image, accuracy assessment via error matrix, overall accuracy, consumer's and producer's accuracies, and Kappa value based on validation samples.

The script extracts mean EVI values over two specific regions (dry and elder) from an EVI image collection, mapping each region with its corresponding EVI mean and timestamp, then flattens the result into a feature collection of triplets (region, EVI mean, time).
task_name: Extract EVI time series from regions

task_description: The script classifies irrigated agricultural areas in the United States using NDVI, evapotranspiration, and land surface temperature data from 2000–2001, training a CART classifier on MIRCA2000 irrigation extent data, and evaluates model accuracy through stratified sampling and confusion matrices.

The script computes NDVI from Landsat 4 and 5 surface reflectance data over Nunavik between July 1 and August 31, 1984, after masking clouds and filtering for low cloud cover, producing a time-series image collection for vegetation analysis.

The script analyzes temporal changes in Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI) over the Riau province in Indonesia using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from 2019 to 2022, generating a multi-year composite image for annual EVI monitoring.

The script analyzes changes in Sentinel-1 VV polarization radar backscatter between August 2020 and August 2021 using median composites from ascending orbit passes, with speckle filtering applied by masking extreme low values (-30 dB), to detect surface structural or moisture changes over time.

The script calculates mean and individual land surface temperature values from MODIS MOD11A1 data, applying cloud masking using QC_Day bits for clear-sky observations between September 2016 and September 2019.

The script classifies land cover into three categories—urban, natural, and agricultural—using median composite Sentinel-2 imagery from October 2018. It computes spectral and vegetation indices (e.g., NDVI, SAVI, EVI2, GCVI, PRI, LAI, entropy) and their statistical metrics (min, max, amplitude, mean, median) across red, green, blue, NIR, and derived bands. A Random Forest classifier is trained on labeled sample regions (urban, rural, native vegetation), and the resulting model is applied to produce a classified land cover map clipped to the study area.

The script classifies land cover into forest, non-forest, and water classes using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from 2020. It computes spectral indices (NDVI, NDBI, NDWI, NDUI), trains a Random Forest classifier on labeled polygon samples, and generates a classified land cover map with accuracy assessment including confusion matrix, overall accuracy, and producer's/consumer's accuracy.
task_name: Classify forest cover using satellite imagery

task_description: The script creates a median true-color composite image from atmospherically corrected Landsat 5 surface reflectance data for the year 2011, using bands 3, 2, and 1 (red, green, blue), clipped to a user-defined geometry, for visual interpretation of land surface features.

The script analyzes time series of Landsat-derived CCD (Continuous Change Detection) results to detect and map the timing of forest disturbances in the Amazon, applying multiple post-processing masks based on magnitude, intensity, and individual segment properties to refine change detection. Outputs include maps of first detected break year, masked by different thresholds, and final combined masks saved to an asset.

The script calculates the total area of forest loss and forest gain in Senegal using the Hansen Global Forest Change dataset from 2014, reporting the results in square meters through zonal statistics over the country's geometry.
task_name: Quantify forest loss and gain area
